sections.heading: Why TOK feels unteachable to Mumbai parents, and why it is not
paragraphs: The feeling has a real cause. Every other subject in the diploma hands a parent something to check: a chapter list, a set of past papers, a formula sheet, a vocabulary list. TOK hands over a prescribed title and a prompt and nothing else. There is no content to revise, so the ordinary machinery of Indian academic support, which is built on covering a syllabus and then testing recall of it, has nothing to grip. Parents conclude the subject is either trivial or impossible, and students pick up whichever conclusion is in the air at home.

What that machinery misses is that TOK does have a curriculum. It is a curriculum of moves rather than of facts, and moves are taught the way a tennis serve is taught: demonstrated, attempted badly, corrected, attempted again. A student can be shown how a knowledge question differs from a topic question in twenty minutes and still need six weeks to produce one unaided. That gap is not a sign the subject is unteachable. It is the normal distance between understanding a technique and owning it, and it is exactly the distance a tutor is useful across.

This is also why effort without method stalls so visibly in TOK. A hardworking DP2 student in Bandra West will read four articles, fill eight pages and produce something that still reads as a description of the articles. More reading does not fix it, because the problem is not a shortage of material but the absence of a question the material is answering. The same student given one page and told to write a claim, an example and the objection to it will produce more usable text in forty minutes than the eight pages contained. Parents who respond to a weak TOK draft by buying more hours of the same activity get a longer weak draft.

So the first sessions have a specific job, and you should expect to see it done. Session one establishes what the student already thinks knowing means, in their own words, and diagnoses whether they can hear the difference between a claim and an example. Session two produces one knowledge question the student can defend for five minutes. Session three puts a counter-case in front of that question and makes them write the reply. By the end of the third session there should be a page with a position on it, however rough. If there is only a plan, something is wrong with the match. The best IB tutor in Mumbai for your child is the one who got that page written in three sessions, not the one with the longest list of subjects on their profile.
bullets: No syllabus to cover means the usual cover-and-test support model has nothing to grip
The curriculum is moves, not facts, and moves are drilled rather than explained
Expect a long gap between understanding a technique and using it unaided
More reading does not fix a descriptive draft; a sharper question does
By session three expect a written position, not another plan

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks, progress is a change in how your child talks. They should be able to state a knowledge question and say why it is a question about knowledge rather than about a topic, and they should flinch slightly when they catch themselves describing instead of arguing. There is unlikely to be a finished anything. If a tutor shows you polished prose in month one, ask who wrote it, because that is a question worth asking early rather than after submission.

At one term, there should be a complete piece of the student's own writing that has been worked against the published criteria at least twice, with the second version visibly different from the first in structure rather than in vocabulary. A term is also long enough to see whether the student now generates counter-cases without being prompted. That habit, more than any grade indicator, is what carries into the second year, and it is the clearest signal that TOK home tuition is doing its job.

Across a full exam cycle, the realistic claim is consistency rather than transformation. The student who could write one good paragraph in September can sustain a position across a full piece by February, holds the counter-argument seriously instead of dismissing it in a clause, and no longer treats the word limit as an obstacle. Where the gain often shows up unexpectedly is in the Extended Essay and in subject internal assessments, because the habit of justifying a claim transfers.

The limits deserve stating plainly. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor can. TOK assessment is externally moderated, the criteria are applied by people who have never met your child, and a tutor who promises a specific outcome is either inexperienced or selling. A student who will not put words on a page cannot be helped by any tutor at any price, and if that is the real problem, more sessions are the wrong purchase. Tell us and we will say so.
bullets: Four weeks: the student can state a knowledge question and defend why it is one
One term: a complete self-written piece, restructured at least once against the criteria
One term: counter-cases generated unprompted, which is the habit that lasts
One cycle: a position sustained across a whole piece, with the objection taken seriously
Externally moderated assessment means outcomes are never guaranteed by anybody

sections.heading: Getting started with a TOK tutor in Mumbai this week
paragraphs: Prepare four things before the first session and you save a fortnight. The prescribed titles list if the school has issued it. Any handout the TOK teacher has given out, including the prompt list for the exhibition. The last piece of written feedback on anything the student has produced for the core, even if it is two lines in a margin. And the school's internal deadline dates for the year. A tutor with those four can plan the term in the first twenty minutes instead of spending two sessions reconstructing them.

The first session itself should be diagnostic and slightly uncomfortable. Expect the tutor to ask your child what they think knowing something means, to push back on the first answer, and to get a sentence written down before the hour ends. Expect them to leave with one task that takes under thirty minutes. A first session that consists of an overview of the course and a promise to start properly next week is a wasted session, and you should say so.

On money, we quote nothing on this page because fees here are not a single number. What IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on is the board and level, how scarce the subject specialism is, whether the tutor travels to you and how far, the session length and whether you are booking a term or a crisis fortnight. Core subjects like TOK sit at the scarce end, and a travelled evening slot in South Mumbai in the monsoon costs the tutor more time than the same slot in Kharghar. Ask for the rate and the travel assumption together.

After that it is logistics. Agree a fixed weekly hour, tell the society office the tutor's name so the gate pass is standing rather than negotiated weekly, and set a four-week review date in your own calendar. If the review is honest, the arrangement either continues with confidence or ends without drama. Either outcome is better than drifting to February.
bullets: Bring the prescribed titles list, school handouts and the last written feedback
Bring the school's internal core deadlines, not the external ones
Expect a sentence on paper and one short task in session one
Ask for the hourly rate and the travel assumption in the same message
Register the tutor at the society gate once, then set a four-week review

faqs.question: What does an IB DP Theory of Knowledge tutor actually do in a session?
faqs.answer: They drill four moves, because TOK has no content to revise. A session takes the student's own sentence, asks which part is a claim and which is an example, supplies a counter-case the student must answer in writing, and pushes for precise wording. Alongside that, the tutor reads the prescribed title with the student until it is clear what is being asked. What they do not do is lecture about knowledge in general. If you listen in from the next room and hear the tutor talking for forty minutes, the session is going wrong.

faqs.question: Can a TOK home tutor travel to our building in Bandra West for an evening slot?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if we match within the Western Suburbs rather than across the city. A tutor already living between Khar West and Andheri West can hold a 6pm or 7pm slot in Bandra West through the year. The arrangements that fail are the ones where a tutor crosses from Chembur or Thane in the evening peak; those survive a month and then start arriving late. Tell us your preferred two windows and your building's visitor rules, and we will shortlist from your own corridor first.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 and has not really started TOK. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: No, it is the best time to start. DP1 is when there is nothing due, which is exactly when the four moves can be built without a deadline distorting them. A student who learns to frame a knowledge question in the first term of DP1 spends DP2 writing rather than panicking. Starting in DP2 is still worth doing, but the work becomes triage: one title, one structure, one usable set of examples, and less room to discover what the student actually finds interesting.

faqs.question: Will a tutor write or fix up the TOK essay for us?
faqs.answer: No, and you should end the arrangement with anyone who offers. The work must be the student's own. A tutor may question choices, teach the technique on a different example, mark a draft with questions in the margin and explain why a paragraph fails against the criteria. A tutor may not write, redraft or supply any part of the essay or the exhibition commentary. The prescribed title is used exactly as set and never reworded, and any use of artificial intelligence is declared under your school's own rules. Schools investigate these cases and the consequences land on the student.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during home tuition sessions?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole hour, but someone should be in the flat. We ask that an adult is at home when a tutor visits, which protects both the student and the tutor, and that the session happens in a shared room rather than behind a closed bedroom door. A dining table works better than a desk anyway, because TOK is argued out loud and needs space to spread two pages. Many parents listen to the first ten minutes of session one and then leave them to it, which is about right.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for a core subject like TOK?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we will not invent a figure for any of them. The board and level, the scarcity of the specialism, whether the tutor travels and how far, the session length, and whether you are booking a term or a late rescue. TOK sits at the scarce end because fewer tutors have taught it inside the Diploma Programme. A travelled evening slot in Walkeshwar in the monsoon costs the tutor more unpaid time than the same hour in Vashi, and rates reflect that. Ask every tutor for the rate and the travel assumption together.

faqs.question: Is online TOK tutoring as good as home classes?
faqs.answer: For draft work it can be better; for early DP1 argument practice it is usually weaker. Marking a paragraph in a shared document, with objections appearing beside the student's own sentences, is genuinely easier on screen. Being pressed on a shaky claim is easier in a room, because a tutor can see hesitation that a video call flattens. Most families here end up mixing the two: home sessions for the hard decisions about a title or an object, online for marking. The sibling page on online TOK tutoring goes into the remote format in detail.

faqs.question: A month in and nothing has changed. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the written evidence first, then decide. There should be a knowledge question the student can defend, at least one page of their own argument, and marginal comments on it. If all three exist and the student is still slow, that is normal and worth continuing. If there is only a plan and a folder of notes, the match is wrong and we will re-shortlist. Tell us within the first month rather than at the term's end; the whole point of a four-week review is that it happens before a deadline makes the decision for you.

faqs.question: Can a tutor commute to Kharghar or Thane for a weekday evening session?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the tutor is sourced locally. In Navi Mumbai we match node to node, so a Kharghar slot is filled from Kharghar, Belapur or Panvel rather than from the island city, because a tutor crossing the creek twice a week stops being reliable by the second month. In Thane the deciding factor is Ghodbunder Road: a Kasarvadavali slot is easiest for a tutor already living past Majiwada. Say which node or which stretch of Ghodbunder Road you are on and we will work outward from there.

faqs.question: Can a tutor promise a specific grade in TOK?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor will offer one, because TOK assessment is externally moderated and the criteria are applied by examiners who have never met your child. What a tutor can promise is method, regular written feedback against the published criteria and a visible improvement in the student's own drafts. If someone quotes you an outcome, treat it as information about them rather than about your child. Ask instead what the first three sessions will produce on paper.

faqs.question: How should a tutor handle a title that touches religion, politics or culture?
faqs.answer: By examining how the claims are justified and by attributing every position to the people who hold it, without taking a side. TOK titles reach into contested territory by design, and the published criteria reward a student who can set out how two communities of knowers reach different conclusions and what each treats as sufficient evidence. A tutor who uses the session to argue their own view on a religious or political question is doing the student harm as well as overstepping. The right question is always how this is known, not who is right.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to our school in any way?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, nor with the International Baccalaureate organisation. We name schools only as local context, because their internal calendars and draft deadlines shape how a term of TOK tutoring is scheduled. Your school's DP coordinator remains the authority on the current subject guide, the criteria and your child's internal deadlines, and a good tutor works to those dates rather than inventing their own.

sections.heading: How we shortlist a tutor for IB DP tuition in Mumbai without adding to the week
paragraphs: A parent asking for IB DP tuition in Mumbai usually opens with a subject and a problem: Physics is slipping, the Mathematics Analysis and Approaches grade dropped after the first mock. The first thing we ask about is the calendar instead. What time does the school bus get back to the building? Which evenings are already gone to Creativity, Activity, Service commitments? When is the next CAS interview with the coordinator? A home tutor who fits the subject but not the week gets cancelled by November, and nobody learns anything from a cancelled slot.

Once the week is on paper the shortlist narrows fast, and usually by geography before pedagogy. A DP2 student in Kasarvadavali with Saturday mornings committed to a service project in Thane does not need the strongest Chemistry tutor in the city; she needs a strong Chemistry tutor who can reach Ghodbunder Road on a Tuesday at 7.30pm and keep doing it in July. We say so plainly when the only tutor with the right component depth lives an hour away in the wrong direction, and we recommend online for that subject rather than booking a commute that will quietly fail.

Every profile we send names the board and the level the tutor has actually taught, the components they have marked or coached, and the slots they can hold for a full term rather than a fortnight. You speak to the tutor before anything is booked. That conversation is where the awkward question belongs: given what my daughter already has in her week, is this one session or two, and what should she stop doing to make room for it?

IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school, examination board or the International Baccalaureate organisation, and we do not guarantee grades. What we can do is put a specialist in front of a student at a time she can genuinely use, and tell you honestly when the problem we are being asked to solve is a timetable problem rather than a teaching one.

sections.heading: What is CAS, and why can a Mumbai DP student not quietly skip it?
paragraphs: Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) is one of the three core requirements of the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (DP), alongside the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK). It runs across both DP years, carries no grade and no marks, and a student who does not complete it does not receive the diploma. That is the whole trap in one sentence: CAS cannot raise a points total, and it can remove the diploma entirely.

The requirement has a shape worth knowing before you plan a term. CAS runs for roughly eighteen months from the start of DP1 and asks for a reasonable balance across its three strands: creativity, activity and service. The student has to demonstrate seven learning outcomes, carry out at least one CAS project lasting a month or more that involves working with others, keep a portfolio of evidence and reflection, and sit three formal interviews with the CAS coordinator, one early, one at the midpoint and one at the end. None of it is marked. All of it is checked.

Mumbai families underestimate this in a specific way. The activities themselves are rarely the problem. A student at Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC or Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu is usually already doing plenty that qualifies: football, Bharatanatyam, a Model UN committee, weekend teaching at a community centre in Govandi. What gets postponed is the evidence and the reflection. Portfolios get written in the final term from memory, which is exactly the term the student is also finishing internal assessments and starting revision. A reflection written eleven months late is both worse and slower to write than one written the same week.

The other two core pieces are at least a known quantity: a word count and a deadline. CAS is open-ended, and open-ended work expands into whatever evening happens to be free. That is why it belongs on a page about tuition rather than in a school newsletter. Any honest conversation about IB DP home tuition in Mumbai has to start from a week that already contains a non-negotiable, ungraded, eighteen-month commitment.
bullets: CAS spans both DP years and must be completed for the diploma to be awarded
Three strands: creativity, activity and service, held in reasonable balance

sections.heading: Six subjects, six internal assessments: where a DP week's hours actually go
paragraphs: A DP student carries six subjects, normally three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), plus the core. Each of those six carries at least one internal assessment (IA): a Group 4 practical investigation in Physics, Chemistry or Biology, a Mathematics exploration, an oral and a written task in Language A and Language B, a commentary portfolio in Economics, a historical investigation, a process portfolio in Visual Arts. Count them and you are looking at six separate pieces of coursework, each with a school-set draft deadline sitting ahead of the real one.

This page is not the place to learn the Mathematics exploration criteria, and we are not going to tell you how to write a Group 4 investigation here. What matters in a time budget is the hours. An HL subject takes substantially more class time than its SL version and sets correspondingly more work at home. A single science investigation does not fit into one sitting: there is the data collection, the uncertainty treatment, the write-up and at least one redraft after supervisor feedback. All IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai covers through IB Gram sit somewhere on that scale, and the scale is the thing to plan a term around.

Families often run both boards at once with two children. A Year 10 sibling at Bombay International School near Babulnath choosing between Core and Extended Mathematics is making a smaller decision with the same shape: Extended covers more ground, sets more homework and keeps more degree options open, and the right answer depends partly on how much of the week is already committed elsewhere. The DP student's week is simply the extreme version of the same calculation, with six of those decisions already made and locked in.

A tutor's job inside this ledger is to make hours shorter, not to add hours. Two focused sessions on the HL Physics investigation in October are a better purchase than four unfocused ones in February when the draft is already late. A tutor who cannot tell you which two of your student's six subjects actually need the slot, and which internal assessment is closest to trouble, is guessing with your evening.
bullets: Six subjects, three HL and three SL, each carrying at least one internal assessment
HL sets more class time and more home work than SL in the same subject

sections.heading: Home tuition across all six Mumbai zones, measured in commute minutes
paragraphs: IB DP tuition in Mumbai is a travel problem before it is a teaching problem, and the problem is different in each of the six zones. In South Mumbai the distances are short and the clocks are slow: a tutor coming from Worli to Cuffe Parade or Colaba covers single-figure kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at 7pm. That is why we match inside the island for Walkeshwar, Tardeo and Fort rather than bringing someone down the Western Line. The Coastal Road has helped the Worli to Nariman Point direction far more than it has helped anyone trying to cross east.

The Western Suburbs run in a line, so matching along the line works and matching across it does not. Khar West to Santacruz is ten minutes; Malad to Kandivali is similar on Link Road. Bandra to Andheri is quick at 4pm on the Western Express Highway and can take three times as long at 6.30pm. Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made the Dahisar to Andheri run predictable in a way the highway never was, which matters when a tutor is holding a 7pm slot in Borivali or Goregaon East twice a week through a whole term.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR in between. Powai has no station of its own, so a Hiranandani Gardens family is matched by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and a Ghatkopar tutor also has Metro Line 1 running west. In the Eastern Suburbs, from Chembur and Govandi up through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund, the Eastern Freeway has quietly changed what is possible: a Chembur tutor reaches Wadala and Parel faster than the map suggests, and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road makes a Chembur to Santacruz match workable where it once was not.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes and we match node to node. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short drive from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines and Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 covering the rest. The Atal Setu has cut the Sewri to Chirle crossing sharply, but pulling a tutor from the island city across the creek for a 7pm weekday lesson still rarely survives a full term. Thane spreads from the station along Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road, and Ghodbunder sets the schedule: the station to Kasarvadavali runs about twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak. Thane tutors cover Thane, and a Mulund tutor sometimes crosses over for a late slot.

Parents searching for IB tutors near me in Mumbai are usually right to search that way. For home tuition, proximity is the single best predictor of whether a weekly slot is still running in March. It is also why we ask about June before we ask about marks. In Mumbai, Maharashtra a heavy spell can close the Andheri subway, slow the Sion-Panvel Highway and make a Ghodbunder Road run unpredictable, and a DP student with CAS commitments on Saturday cannot easily absorb a Tuesday session pushed into the weekend. The hybrid arrangement is agreed in advance for those weeks, not improvised during them.

sections.heading: How does the Mumbai school calendar collide with CAS deadlines?
paragraphs: The collision is predictable. Mumbai IB schools run a June to May year, so internal assessment drafts cluster from September to November of DP2 and again in January, the Extended Essay falls due in the same stretch, and the final CAS interview is often scheduled in exactly that window. November to January is when an over-full week breaks, and it breaks in the same order every year.

The detail differs by school. Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off JVLR in Goregaon East, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, Singapore International School in Dahisar East and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul all set their own internal deadlines ahead of the board's submission dates. IB Gram is an independent platform and not affiliated with any of these schools or with the International Baccalaureate; they are named here as local context only.

The school day is the largest single line in the budget, and in Mumbai it is longer than the printed timetable. A student at Oberoi International School living in Andheri West, or at Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School commuting within Thane, can spend over an hour a day on the bus. That hour is real: it is not study time and it is not rest, and it comes out of the same twenty-four hours as everything else. A Kharghar or Panvel family sending a child to a BKC school is spending considerably more than that, in both directions, five days a week.

Most Mumbai schools do timetable some CAS activity inside the week, a Saturday service slot or an after-school sport, and that helps. What they almost never timetable is the reflection. So the portfolio becomes homework, and homework competes with six subjects. When the coordinator sends the midpoint interview reminder in DP1 and the student has eleven entries to write that evening, the Chemistry session booked for that week is money spent on a student who is somewhere else. Tell us those dates and a home tutor can work around them.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a DP student whose weekends are already booked
paragraphs: IB DP home tuition in Mumbai is the default for a straightforward reason: the tutor absorbs the travel instead of the student. A DP1 student with a Saturday service commitment in Chembur and football on Sunday morning has no spare block to add a commute to, so a tutor arriving at the flat at 7.15pm on a Wednesday costs the household ninety minutes and costs the student only the session itself. Home tuition also puts the tutor in the room where the work actually happens, which is how you find out that the study desk is in the living room next to the television.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai solves the problems geography creates. If a Panvel family needs HL Economics and the depth sits in Bandra, online is the only version that lasts a term. So is a 9pm slot after a CAS rehearsal, and so is the week the Ghodbunder Road run is underwater. The trade-offs are real and worth saying out loud. Screen sessions are harder for a tired student at the end of a long day, practical and diagram-heavy work loses something without a shared table, and a tutor cannot see the phone lying face down beside the laptop.

Hybrid is where most of our DP families end up, and it works when it is structured rather than improvised: one home session a week for the subject that needs a person in the room, one online session for the subject where the scarce specialist happens to live on the other side of the city, and a rule agreed in advance that monsoon weeks and clashes move online rather than cancel. All IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai can be run on that pattern. The agreement matters more than the format does.

Choose the mode from the student's week rather than from a preference. If the only free evening is Thursday and the CAS project meets on Thursday, no format fixes that and something has to give. If what actually exists is forty-five usable minutes after dinner on three nights, that is an argument for short online check-ins rather than one long home visit that runs past bedtime. The format should bend to the calendar, which is the opposite of how the decision usually gets made.

sections.heading: How are IB DP tutors in Mumbai checked, and what should you check yourself?
paragraphs: Every tutor is checked for identity, qualifications and documented IB or IGCSE teaching history before any match is offered, and we confirm which board, level and components they have actually taught rather than accepting a subject list at face value. What we cannot verify on your behalf is fit, and fit is the part to test in the first conversation.

An IB home tutor in Mumbai who says they teach Physics may have taught it at IGCSE and never at HL, or taught the HL course without ever supervising a Group 4 investigation to a school's draft deadline. So we ask for specifics: which syllabus cycle, which papers, which internal assessment criteria they have marked or coached against, and whether they have worked with a student on a CAS-heavy timetable before. References from previous families are requested where they exist. Hiring an IB private tutor in Mumbai outside a platform is a perfectly reasonable choice, but the checking then becomes your job rather than ours.

Three checks are yours either way and none of them require subject expertise. First, ask the tutor to describe your student's week back to you; if they cannot, they were not listening. Second, ask what they would remove from that week. A tutor who answers "nothing, we will just work harder" has never watched a DP2 student come apart in January. Third, check the slot against the gate: most Mumbai societies issue a visitor pass per visit, and arranging standing weekly entry with the committee or the facility manager in advance stops a 7pm session starting at 7.20pm every week.

We do not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor will offer to. What a real checking process buys is better odds that the hours spent are the right hours, and the removal of the worst outcomes: the tutor who stops turning up in February, the one working a syllabus cycle behind, and the one who sets four hours of homework to a student who already has nine.

We confirm the components taught, not just the subject name on a profile
Ask the tutor to repeat your student's weekly commitments back to you

sections.heading: The honest arithmetic of a DP week in Mumbai: add the hours up before you add a tutor
paragraphs: Take one week and spend it on paper. School is the largest single block, and in Mumbai it is longer than the timetable prints because the commute belongs to it: twenty minutes each way when the school is in the same suburb, well over an hour each way for a Kasarvadavali or Kharghar family whose child attends a school in BKC or Juhu. Then sleep, which a sixteen-year-old needs around eight hours of and rarely gets. Then meals, the travel to anything that is not school, and the ordinary friction of living in a flat with other people. Before a single piece of academic work has been counted, most of the week is already allocated.

Now add the academic load into what is left. Six subjects setting homework, three of them at Higher Level. Six internal assessments with school-set draft deadlines that do not politely space themselves out. The Extended Essay, which is an independent research project with supervisor meetings attached. Theory of Knowledge, with its own essay and exhibition. CAS, which has to be done and then has to be written up. Each of those is reasonable on its own. The point of writing them in a column is that they are not on their own, and they are not sequential.

This is where IB DP tuition in Mumbai goes wrong. A parent sees a grade drop, adds two hours of tuition a week, and subtracts nothing. The two hours come out of the only slack that existed, which was sleep, or the CAS portfolio, or the Sunday that was keeping the student functional. Four weeks later the Physics grade has moved slightly, the Economics commentary is late, the portfolio has not been touched since August, and the student is running on empty. Adding a tutor without removing something is how a student ends up doing everything badly at the same time.

So decide what goes before the first session rather than after the first crisis. The things that usually can go: a second or third tuition subject taken on in the same month, screen time and gaming, a competitive exam preparation course bolted on alongside the Diploma Programme, one of two overlapping activities that evidence the same CAS strand, and the habit of restarting homework at 11pm. The things that should not go: sleep, meals, the CAS activity that is genuinely the student's own rather than the one chosen to look good on an application, and whatever single commitment is keeping her steady. Cutting sleep buys an hour tonight and loses two tomorrow. Cutting the thing she actually enjoys produces a student who is present at every session and absorbing none of it.

Then place the sessions deliberately around the fixed points. If the service project meets on alternate Saturdays in Govandi, the tuition slot is not Saturday. If school sport runs Monday and Wednesday after class, the home tutor comes on Tuesday or Friday, and a 7.30pm start will be used where a 6.30pm start the student arrives late to from practice will not. If the CAS project is in its intensive final month, that is the month to run one subject rather than three. Tuition that collides with CAS gets cancelled, and a cancelled slot is worse than no slot, because the calendar paid for it either way.
bullets: Write the week out in hours: school, commute, sleep, meals, then what remains
Six subjects, six internal assessments, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS
Every hour of tuition added should replace an hour, not sit on top of one
Cut duplicate activities and parallel exam coaching before you cut sleep
Place sessions on evenings with no school sport and no CAS meeting
In a CAS project's final month, run one tuition subject instead of three

sections.heading: Is your DP student over-committed rather than under-taught?
paragraphs: These are two different problems with different fixes, and tuition only solves one of them. An under-taught student does not understand the material: she cannot explain the concept, her errors are conceptual and they repeat, and she improves visibly once somebody teaches it properly. An over-committed student understands it perfectly well and cannot get to it. No tutor fixes the second one.

The signals are distinguishable if you look for them. Over-commitment looks like work that is finished but late, drafts handed in at the deadline with the easy parts done well and the hard parts skipped, strong performance in the subject timetabled first thing in the morning and weak performance in the one taught after lunch, falling asleep at the desk rather than struggling at it, and a student who knows exactly what she should be doing and sounds flat about all of it. Under-teaching looks different: confident wrong answers, the same misconception surviving three corrections, and work that is on time and incorrect.

That distinction also changes what progress should look like and when. At four weeks, expect better organisation and a clear picture of the gaps rather than a grade. The honest four-week deliverable is a tutor who can tell you which two of six subjects need the hours and which internal assessment is in trouble. At one term, with a slot that has actually been kept, expect visible movement in the tutored subject and a CAS portfolio that is current instead of six months behind. Across a full exam cycle, from a mock to the real session, expect accumulated technique: question reading, timing, showing method. Expect none of it if the sessions were cancelled.

Parents ask us who the best IB tutor in Mumbai is for a given subject, and the honest answer is that the question is slightly off. The tutor who produces the most improvement is usually the one whose slot is still running in March, which is a scheduling property at least as much as a teaching one. We do not guarantee grades and we do not promise a number of points. Where the evidence says a student is carrying too much rather than learning too little, we would rather say that than sell a second session.
bullets: Under-taught: repeated misconceptions, confident wrong answers, work on time and wrong
Over-committed: work late but correct, hard parts skipped, exhaustion rather than confusion
Four weeks: a clear diagnosis and better organisation, not a changed grade
One term: movement in the tutored subject and a portfolio that is current
One exam cycle: technique and timing, provided the sessions were actually kept

sections.heading: Starting IB DP home tuition in Mumbai: what to bring to the first session
paragraphs: IB DP tuition in Mumbai starts with the week, not with the subject. Before the first session, write down the school timetable, the bus times, every CAS commitment with its day and its likely end date, the internal assessment deadlines the school has published, and the hours the student is currently sleeping. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai can be matched on subject within a day; matching on the week is the part that makes the match hold to March.

Then the paper. The last report card, the most recent mock with the marks still on it, the internal assessment brief for the subject in question and whatever draft exists, and the CAS portfolio as it stands even if it runs to three entries. A tutor who sees a marked mock knows within twenty minutes whether the problem is content, method or time in the exam hall, and those three have entirely different fixes. Without it, the first two sessions go on finding out.

The first session is diagnostic and it should produce something written: which topics are weak, which are weak only because they were rushed, what the next four weeks will cover, and what has to come out of the week to make room for any of it. If the honest answer is that nothing should be added until the CAS portfolio is caught up, a good tutor says so in that session, and a good platform does not argue with them in order to book a second one.

Practicalities worth settling the same day: the standing slot and its start time, society gate access and the visitor pass arrangement, where in the flat the session happens, who is at home, and what happens to a missed session. Settle those once and the term largely runs itself. IB Gram remains an independent platform, not affiliated with any school or examination board named on this page, and nobody here will tell you that a grade is guaranteed.
bullets: Bring the timetable, bus times, CAS commitments and published draft deadlines
Bring the last report, a marked mock paper and the current internal assessment draft
Bring the CAS portfolio as it stands, however thin it currently is
Expect a written four-week plan and an honest note on what to drop

faqs.question: Does CAS really have to be finished, or can my child let it slide?
faqs.answer: It has to be finished. Creativity, Activity, Service is a required part of the Diploma Programme core, and a student who does not complete it to the school's satisfaction does not receive the IB diploma, however good the subject grades are. It carries no marks, which is precisely why it gets deprioritised, and the part that slides is almost never the activity itself. It is the portfolio: the evidence, the reflections against the seven learning outcomes, and the interviews with the CAS coordinator. Letting those drift turns a manageable eighteen-month commitment into a crisis in the final term, sitting next to internal assessments and revision.

faqs.question: My daughter has no free evenings left. Should we add tuition anyway?
faqs.answer: Not without taking something out first. Adding two hours a week to a week with no slack means those hours come out of sleep, the CAS portfolio, or the one activity keeping her steady, and all three cost more than the tuition gains. The useful first step is to write the week down in hours and look at where the time would actually come from. Sometimes the answer is that one well-placed hour a week is the right purchase. Sometimes it is that a parallel commitment has to go before any tutor can help. We will tell you which one we think it is.

faqs.question: What should we cut first to make room for IB DP tuition?
faqs.answer: Start with duplication and parallel tracks. A competitive exam coaching course running alongside the Diploma Programme, two activities that evidence the same CAS strand, a third tuition subject taken on in the same month, and homework that routinely restarts at 11pm are the usual candidates. Screen time is the easiest hour to recover and the least painful to lose. What should not be cut: sleep, meals, and the CAS activity that is genuinely the student's own rather than the one chosen to look good on an application. Cutting the activity she actually enjoys produces a student who attends every session and absorbs nothing.

faqs.question: How do you schedule sessions around a Saturday CAS project?
faqs.answer: We schedule the tutor around the CAS commitment, not the other way round. Tell us the day and time the project meets, including the alternate-Saturday pattern many Mumbai school service projects run on, and we shortlist only tutors who can hold a different evening for a full term. If the project is in its intensive final month, the honest recommendation is often to run one subject that month rather than three. A session booked on top of a CAS meeting gets cancelled, and a cancelled slot costs the calendar whether it is taught or not.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: They depend on a short list of things rather than a published price list. The board and the level matter, because Higher Level Diploma Programme work needs a scarcer tutor than IGCSE. The subject matters, because an HL Physics or Economics specialist is harder to find than a Mathematics tutor. Then travel distance and time of day, session length, how many sessions a week, and whether the format is home, online or hybrid. Online usually sits lower than a home visit because nobody is paying for a commute across the city. We quote per match, once the subject and the week are clear.

faqs.question: We live in Kharghar and the school is in BKC. Is home tuition realistic?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the tutor is local to Kharghar rather than local to the school. A tutor travelling from BKC or Bandra to Kharghar for a 7pm weekday session will not sustain it beyond a few weeks, Atal Setu or not. We match inside Navi Mumbai node to node, across Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, so the travel is a short drive on Palm Beach Road or the Sion-Panvel Highway. Where the specialist genuinely does not exist on that side of the creek, we say so and recommend online for that one subject instead of booking a commute that fails in June.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our building on a weekday evening in Thane?
faqs.answer: Yes, and two things are worth settling in advance: the gate and the hour. Most Thane societies issue a visitor pass per visit, so arranging standing weekly entry with the committee or the facility manager saves ten minutes at the gate every single session. On timing, Ghodbunder Road is the constraint: the station to Kasarvadavali stretch runs about twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak, so a 7.30pm start is more reliable than 6.30pm. We also agree in advance which monsoon weeks move online rather than being cancelled outright.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What happens now?
faqs.answer: Tell us, and expect a diagnosis rather than a defence. At four weeks the honest deliverable is clarity, not a grade: which subjects need the hours, which internal assessment is at risk, and whether the student is under-taught or simply out of time. If the sessions have been happening and nothing has moved, we change the tutor. If the sessions have been cancelled, or she arrives from a CAS rehearsal with nothing prepared, changing the tutor fixes nothing and we will say so. We would rather lose a second session than keep billing a timetable problem.

faqs.question: Does online tuition actually work for a tired DP student at 9pm?
faqs.answer: It can, but not in a long block. A student at 9pm after school, a commute and a CAS session will get more out of forty-five focused minutes on screen than ninety, and an IB online tutor in Mumbai should be scheduling accordingly. Online genuinely works for question practice, past-paper walkthroughs and quick concept repair, and it is the only format that survives a monsoon week or a scarce Higher Level specialist living on the other side of the city. It works less well for a student who needs a person in the room to stay off her phone.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace them, without a new enquiry. You do not need a reason beyond "this is not working", though a specific one helps: the slot keeps moving, the explanations are not landing, the homework set ignores the rest of the week. We shortlist again using what the first match taught us, and the replacement starts from the plan the previous sessions produced rather than from scratch. If the real issue turns out to be that the student has no time rather than the wrong tutor, we will suggest pausing instead of swapping.

faqs.question: My son is sleeping five hours a night. Is that a tuition problem?
faqs.answer: No, that is a timetable problem and no tutor will fix it. Five hours makes every other hour of the day less productive, so adding tuition to that week buys very little and makes the sleep worse. The sequence that works is to find the hours being spent badly, usually late-night restarts and duplicated commitments, recover sleep first, then add one well-placed session. We would rather start a month later with a student who is awake than start now against a standing deficit. A tutor working with an exhausted DP2 student is being paid to watch her not absorb anything.

faqs.question: Do we need a parent at home during a home session?
faqs.answer: Not in the room for a DP student, but someone at home is sensible. A parent or another adult in the flat is the usual arrangement for a home tutor in Mumbai, with the session at the dining table or a study desk rather than in a bedroom, and the door left open. You do not need to supervise the teaching, and hovering tends to make a seventeen-year-old worse at asking questions. What helps is being available at the start and the end: two minutes with the tutor afterwards tells you more about the week than any written report will.

sections.heading: How we match an IB DP tutor in Mumbai to a subject choice, not just a subject
paragraphs: Nearly every DP1 request reaches us as a single subject name: Physics, or Maths, or Economics. By the second phone call it usually turns out the subject itself is not settled. A student picked Higher Level Physics in the first week of term because two friends did, has since sat through a month of mechanics, and has gone quiet about it at dinner. The tutor who helps here is not the one who opens the kinematics chapter on day one. It is the one who has taught that exact course and can say whether a month of discomfort is ordinary adjustment or an early signal that the level is wrong for this particular student.

So the first thing we ask is not what the student is struggling with. It is the full set of six choices, the school, the term the student is in, and where in the city you live. A Higher Level Chemistry request from a family in Chembur and the same request from a family in Kharghar are different matching problems, because the pool of people who have taught that syllabus and can reach your door on a Tuesday evening is different. The process from enquiry to a standing weekly slot runs like this.

What we deliberately do not do is put a generalist in front of a Diploma Programme subject decision. A tutor who has taught the course knows which internal assessment it carries, where the published criteria actually bite, and what the gap between Standard Level and Higher Level content feels like in week six rather than in a syllabus document. A tutor who has not taught it will tell you the student needs to work harder, which is both true and useless. If we do not have someone who has taught the specific course at the specific level, we say so rather than sending the nearest available person.

sections.heading: Six choices, a few weeks, and two years of consequences
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) asks a student of about sixteen to choose six courses, three of them at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), inside a window that is usually a few weeks long. Most schools in Mumbai hold an options evening, circulate a form, run a short settling period, and then close changes. The student making the choice has never studied any of these courses. The parent making it with them often last looked at a school syllabus twenty years ago and under a different board. That asymmetry, not a lack of effort, is what produces most of the regret we see in DP2.

The constraint nobody mentions on the options evening is the timetable. Schools build blocks, and the blocks decide which combinations are actually available. A student who wants HL Economics, HL Physics and HL Visual Arts may find two of those sit in the same block, so the honest choice is between them rather than between all three. Asking the school's timetable coordinator which combinations are genuinely offered this cycle, before filling the form, saves a conversation that is much harder to have in October.

Alongside the DP decision sits the quieter one that families with a younger child are making in the same household: whether the International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) Mathematics paper is sat at Core or Extended tier. Core caps the grade available and covers less ground; Extended is the tier that keeps the door to Higher Level Mathematics in the Diploma Programme comfortably open. Deciding Core because a term went badly is one of the few school decisions that can quietly close options two years ahead of time, and it deserves the same scrutiny as an HL choice.
The point of a tutor in this window is not to make the choice. It is to shrink the gap between what the course documents say and what the course actually asks of a student in month three.

School timetable blocks decide which HL combinations are really on offer

sections.heading: Which Mathematics course, which science, and at which level?
paragraphs: Mathematics is the choice that trips most families, because it is two separate courses rather than one course at two speeds. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-leaning route: calculus carries most of the weight, and at Higher Level the paper set includes a section where no calculator is allowed. Applications and Interpretation is modelling, statistics and data, and its assessment includes a paper built around technology use throughout. They are not harder and easier versions of each other. A student strong at statistics and weak at abstract manipulation can do better in Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level than in Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level, and the reverse is equally true.

The destination matters more than the label. Quantitative degree paths frequently expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, but which course and level any given programme expects differs by country, by institution and by individual course, and these expectations are revised between admissions cycles. No single person covers all IB and IGCSE subjects and a tutor in Mumbai who says otherwise is selling you something; equally, no tutor should be your source for what a university requires. Read the university's own admissions pages for the course the student actually wants, for the year they would apply, and treat everything else as hearsay.

The sciences carry a second variable: the internal assessment. Each science course requires an individual investigation, and what that investigation demands in practice differs between Biology, Chemistry and Physics in ways a prospectus does not show. Chemistry investigations often need laboratory access and a reaction that behaves; Physics investigations frequently live or die on whether the student can control one variable cleanly; Biology investigations can run into sample size and ethics constraints. Choosing between HL Chemistry and HL Physics partly on which investigation the student can realistically run, with the equipment their school actually has, is a more honest basis than which subject sounds more serious.

Group 2, the language group, produces the most avoidable mistakes. A student who has studied French for five years can continue it as a language acquisition course, or start Spanish from scratch as an ab initio course at Standard Level. The scratch option looks easier because it begins at zero. It is a two-year commitment to building a language from nothing while also carrying three Higher Levels, and the ceiling on the course is lower. Continuing the language already in hand is usually the safer call, and the exceptions are specific enough to be worth talking through properly.
bullets: Analysis and Approaches: algebra, calculus, proof, and a no-calculator paper
Applications and Interpretation: modelling, statistics, and technology use throughout

sections.heading: Subject choice across six Mumbai zones, and why your locality changes the shortlist
paragraphs: A good IB DP tutor in Mumbai starts by asking which zone you are in, because that answer decides who can hold a Tuesday evening slot for two years. In South Mumbai the distances are short and the clock still runs slow: a tutor crossing from Worli to Cuffe Parade covers a handful of kilometres and can lose half an hour to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. Families in Colaba, Babulnath, Tardeo and Fort are usually matched within the island rather than from the suburbs, and the Coastal Road has changed northbound timings more than southbound ones.

The Western Suburbs run along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway, so a tutor moving Bandra to Andheri is quick off-peak and slow at six in the evening. Matching along the line works: Khar West to Santacruz, Juhu to Vile Parle, Malad to Kandivali East, Borivali to Dahisar East. Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made the Dahisar to Andheri stretch workable for a tutor who would once have refused it. The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR; Powai has no station of its own, so tutors reach it by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and the Santacruz Chembur Link Road is what makes a Kurla to Chembur evening slot realistic.

The Eastern Suburbs stretch from Chembur and Govandi up through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund West, on the Central and Harbour lines. The Eastern Freeway makes South Mumbai reachable from Chembur and Wadala faster than the map suggests, which occasionally lets a SoBo specialist take one eastern slot a week. Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, and tutors are matched node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short drive from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway. The Atal Setu has shortened the island crossing, but pulling a tutor across the creek for a weekday evening lesson still rarely survives a full term. In Thane the Ghodbunder Road stretch sets the schedule: Kasarvadavali is twenty minutes from the station off-peak and close to an hour in the evening, so Thane families are matched with Thane tutors, with occasional crossover from Mulund.

Searching IB tutors near me in Mumbai returns a list sorted by nothing in particular. Families also ask for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai under one roof, and that is rarely the right shape for a DP1 subject decision: the person who can talk honestly about Higher Level Chemistry is usually not the same person who can talk about Spanish ab initio. Two tutors who each know their own course beats one who knows neither.

sections.heading: How Mumbai school calendars compress the subject-change window
paragraphs: The window in which a DP subject or level can still be changed is set by the school, not by the IB, and in Mumbai it closes earlier than most parents expect. Schools have to register candidates, order materials, build the two-year timetable and staff each Higher Level section, so the practical deadline arrives well before the formal one. An IB home tutor in Mumbai sees the same calendar from inside twenty different households and can usually tell you, in the first week of a match, whether the school you are dealing with treats the change request as routine paperwork or as an exception.

The schools families here deal with set the pressure points. Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off JVLR, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, the JBCN International School campuses at Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur, NES International School in Mulund West, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul all run their own options process, their own internal deadlines and their own tolerance for a late change.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of the schools named here. We name them because their calendars are the real constraint on a subject decision, not because we have any relationship with them. No school endorses us, no school receives anything from us, and nothing on this page should be read as a statement on behalf of a school or of the International Baccalaureate.

Practically, this means the first conversation with a tutor in DP1 should include a question about dates. If the school's change window shuts at the end of the first term, a diagnostic session in week four is worth more than a brilliant tutor starting in week twelve. If the window is already shut, the conversation changes entirely: the question becomes how to carry the Higher Level the student is now committed to, and that is a different piece of work with a different plan.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a DP1 subject decision in Mumbai?
paragraphs: For a subject and level decision, home tuition is the mode that works best, because the tutor needs to see actual work rather than hear a description of it. Most families who ask for an IB DP home tutor in Mumbai want someone at the dining table with the student's first Higher Level problem set, the first lab write-up and the first marked piece of class work spread out. A tutor reading those three things in one sitting learns more in forty minutes than a month of screen-shared slides will teach them. Home tuition also removes the commute from the student's side, which matters in a term where the evenings are already short.

The honest cost of home tuition is the tutor's travel. A tutor who crosses the Bandra Worli Sea Link twice a week for one lesson is a tutor who will eventually ask to move the slot, and that instability lands on the student. This is why we match within the zone and fix a standing weekly time rather than booking lesson by lesson. A tutor who lives in Chembur taking a Chembur or Govandi slot will still be there in DP2.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai becomes the better answer in two specific cases. The first is a scarce course: if the student has chosen a Higher Level subject that only a handful of people in the city have taught, the choice is between an online specialist and a local generalist, and the specialist wins. The second is the follow-up rhythm: once the subject decision is made and the student is working, a short online check-in between home sessions costs nobody an hour in traffic. Online is weaker for the diagnostic itself, for a student who drifts without someone in the room, and for anything involving a piece of handwritten working the tutor needs to read line by line.

Hybrid is what most of our DP1 matches settle into by the second month: one home session a week in a fixed slot, one online session shorter than the home one, and an agreement that the week before a school deadline both go online if traffic on the Western Express Highway or Ghodbunder Road is likely to eat the slot. The structure to avoid is the one where mode changes week to week by negotiation, because that is the arrangement that quietly stops happening in November.

sections.heading: How is an IB DP home tutor in Mumbai checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Before an IB DP tutor in Mumbai reaches your shortlist we verify identity with government photographic identification, confirm the degree or qualification claimed, take references from people who have actually used the tutor, and record the specific courses and levels they have taught rather than the subjects they are willing to attempt. That last distinction is the one that matters for a subject decision. Somebody who has taught Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level through a full cycle can tell you what the no-calculator paper does to a student who relies on a graphing display. Somebody who has taught Mathematics generally cannot.

An IB private tutor Mumbai families engage through us is a self-employed professional, not our employee, and we say that plainly because it changes what you should check yourself. Verification tells you a person is who they claim and has done what they claim. It does not tell you whether they will suit your child, whether they explain in a way this particular student follows, or whether they will be honest with you when the news is bad. Those are things only the first conversation and the first few sessions reveal.

So check four things yourself, in the first call and the first session. Ask which exact course and level they have taught, and in which years. Ask what the internal assessment for that course demands, and listen for whether the answer is specific or generic. Ask what they would tell a student who wants to drop from Higher Level to Standard Level, and be suspicious of a tutor who says nobody should ever drop. And ask how they will tell you if they think the student has chosen wrongly, because a tutor who will not deliver unwelcome news is worth very little in DP1.

You should also check the practical things nobody thinks to ask until they are a problem: whether the tutor can commit to the same slot for the full term, what notice they need to reschedule, and whether they are willing to be added to your society's visitor register for a standing weekly entry. Parents type best IB tutor in Mumbai into a search box when the useful question is narrower: who has taught this exact course, at this exact level, and can reach my door at the same time every week.

sections.heading: Higher Level versus Standard Level: the hours, the depth and the three-HL question
paragraphs: The IB's published guideline is 240 teaching hours for a Higher Level course and 150 for a Standard Level one. That difference understates what actually happens, because the extra hours are not padding: they are additional topics, an additional option or extension in several subjects, and in most courses an extra paper or a longer one. Higher Level is also assessed differently in kind, not only in quantity. The questions reward a student who can carry an argument across several steps without being led, and that is a different skill from doing more questions of the same type. An IB DP tutor in Mumbai who has taught both levels will describe that gap in terms of specific question types rather than in terms of difficulty.

This is why three Higher Levels, not any single Higher Level, is the real workload question. A student can almost always carry one demanding HL. Three demanding HLs taken together means three courses each running deeper content, each carrying its own internal assessment, each with its own teacher who sets deadlines without consulting the other two. The combination problem is additive in hours and worse than additive in attention. The students who struggle most in DP1 are rarely the ones who picked one hard subject; they are the ones who picked three, each defensible on its own.

The honest signals that a student should move from Higher Level to Standard Level are specific, and they are visible by about week six. The student is completing work but cannot explain what they did when asked the next day. Marks are holding up on routine questions and collapsing on the unfamiliar ones. Time spent on one subject is quietly eating the other five. The student has stopped asking questions in class, which is usually embarrassment rather than comprehension. None of those, alone, settles it. Two or three of them together, in the same subject, in week six, is a conversation worth having before the school's change window shuts.

The reverse signal exists too and is under-used. A student bored in Standard Level, finishing work early, and asking questions the course does not reach is a candidate for moving up, and that move is usually much harder to arrange late than a move down. Both decisions are the school's to make, in consultation with the counsellor and the subject teachers. A tutor contributes evidence to that conversation: a clear account of what the student can and cannot do, based on work the tutor has watched them produce. A tutor who tries to make the decision, or who lobbies for a level to keep a lesson on the timetable, has overstepped and should be replaced.

sections.heading: What should progress look like once the choices are locked?
paragraphs: At four weeks, progress on a subject decision looks like clarity rather than marks. You should be able to say which of the six courses is genuinely at risk and why, in a sentence that names a skill rather than a feeling. The student should be able to explain what the internal assessment for each Higher Level course will require of them, roughly when, and what it is marked against. If after a month nobody in the house can answer those questions, the tutoring is not working, whatever the lesson reports say.

At one term, you should see a change in how the student works rather than a jump in grades. Problem sets attempted before the lesson instead of during it. A lab write-up drafted and then revised against the published criteria rather than written once. Questions arriving by message mid-week because the student noticed something and wanted to check. Grades usually move later than behaviour does, and in a two-year programme that lag is normal rather than alarming. Over one full exam cycle, consistent work with a tutor who knows the course tends to show up as fewer unforced losses: the marks given away on process, on unanswered command terms, on an internal assessment handed in underdone.

We do not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor or platform can. A tutor controls the quality of the explanation, the structure of the practice and the honesty of the feedback. The student controls the work. The school controls the teaching, the deadlines and the level change decision. A board controls the assessment. Anyone promising a specific points total is either guessing or misleading you, and in DP1 the promise does particular damage because it discourages the level change that would actually have helped.

There is also a limit worth stating on the subject-choice question itself. A tutor can describe a course accurately, test a student against it, and report honestly on what they see. A tutor cannot know the student the way the school's counsellor and subject teachers do, cannot see the timetable blocks, and should not be the person telling a family what a university will accept. The useful tutor stays inside those lines and says so when asked to step outside them.

sections.heading: Getting started with home tuition in Mumbai after the choices are made
paragraphs: IB home tuition in Mumbai begins with a first session that is mostly listening. Have four things on the table before the tutor arrives: the student's subject and level sheet as submitted to the school, the first marked piece of work in each subject you are worried about, any written note from a subject teacher, and the school's dates for the options change window if you have them. The tutor will spend most of the session reading and asking, and should leave you with a plain account of what they saw rather than a lesson plan.

Have the student in the room for the whole of it, including the part where the tutor talks to you. A sixteen-year-old who hears the assessment of their own work second-hand will argue with it. One who hears it directly, from somebody who has just read five pages of their algebra, usually does not. This is also the session where it becomes clear whether the student can work with this particular person, which is the single best predictor of whether the arrangement survives to DP2.

Tell us honestly what the constraint is. If evening traffic on Ghodbunder Road means a weekday slot has to start after eight, say so before we shortlist rather than after. If the only quiet room in the flat is also where a younger sibling does homework, say that too: a tutor who knows will work around it, and a tutor who finds out in week three will quietly start arriving late. If you need one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai because of budget, say that as well, and we will tell you plainly which subjects that will and will not work for.

After the first session you decide whether to continue, with no obligation either way. If you do continue, we fix the standing weekly slot, confirm the gate and visitor arrangements with your building, and agree a review point. If you do not, tell us what did not fit and we will shortlist differently. An IB tutor Mumbai families keep for two years is almost always the second or third person they spoke to, not the first.
