sections.heading: How do we check that a tutor in Mumbai will coach and not co-write?
paragraphs: Every listed tutor passes four checks before a family sees them: identity against a government photo document, the qualification claimed, a reference from previous teaching or tutoring, and a subject conversation with somebody who knows the Diploma. For research essay work there is a fifth, and it is the one that fails most candidates. We describe a specific scenario, a DP2 student with a weak introduction ten days from submission, and ask what they would do. Acceptable answers involve questions, criteria, and the student rewriting. Unacceptable answers involve the tutor producing a model introduction, tightening the prose themselves, or drafting a structure for the student to populate. A surprising number of well-qualified people give the unacceptable answer and believe it is generous.

The line matters because the consequence is asymmetric. An authenticity finding on a research essay attaches to the student, not to the tutor who crossed the line, and it can affect the whole Diploma rather than one subject. Students also underestimate how visible co-writing is. A supervisor who has read a student's work all year, held recorded reflection sessions with them and heard them talk about the project notices when the register of the prose changes. The reflection record exists partly so that the person who knows the student best can see whether the document matches the person.

So the rules we hold tutors to are specific. Feedback is given on what the student wrote, by question and by pointing, never by replacement. Sources are found by the student; a tutor may teach search strategy and may say a source looks unreliable, but does not hand over a reading list that becomes the bibliography. Data is collected by the student. Translation and heavy language editing are not permitted in a subject where expression is assessed, and a tutor unsure where that boundary sits should ask the coordinator through the student rather than guess. A good home tutor states all of this to the student in the first session, because students are the ones who will push.

What you should verify yourself is simpler than it sounds. Ask to see dated drafts, so there is a visible trail from bad to better. Ask your child to explain, unaided, why one paragraph was changed. Read the reflection record and check it sounds like them. And be wary of anyone who offers a guaranteed grade or a finished sample essay to work from, both of which circulate in Mumbai and both of which put your child's Diploma at risk. An IB private tutor Mumbai families engage for this should be entirely comfortable with that scrutiny.

sections.heading: Supervisor meetings and the reflection record: the part students waste
paragraphs: The formal reflection sessions with the school supervisor are the spine of this project, and most students treat them as a box to tick. That is expensive in two ways. The obvious one is that the reflection record itself forms part of what is assessed, so a thin, retrospective, written-the-night-before account loses marks that cost nothing to earn. The less obvious one is that the supervisor is the only person with both subject authority and knowledge of the student, and a well-used meeting redirects a failing project in twenty minutes where a tutor would need weeks.

A useful meeting is prepared for. The student should arrive with a specific question rather than a progress report: whether this narrower version of the question is still answerable in the subject's terms, whether this body of evidence is adequate, whether this section is analysis or description, whether this limitation needs stating openly. They should leave having written down what was said, that day, in their own words, because reconstructing a conversation six weeks later produces exactly the thin reflection the criteria punish. Honest reflection is also allowed to record difficulty: a method that did not work and what was done instead is better material than a smooth account of untroubled progress.

A tutor's role sits entirely outside that relationship. They prepare the student to use the meeting, they help turn a vague worry into a precise question, and they work on what the supervisor asked for afterwards. They do not attend, do not write to the supervisor, do not advise the student to disregard a supervisor's direction, and do not supply the reflection text. Where supervisor and tutor appear to disagree, the supervisor is the one marking the work first and the student follows them, with the tutor's job reduced to making sure the student has understood the instruction rather than merely heard it. IB extended essay help in Mumbai that respects this boundary is far more useful than help that competes with the school.

Two failure patterns show up again and again. The first is the student who goes quiet between reflection sessions, does nothing, and then compresses six weeks of research into the fortnight before a meeting; the record shows it and the essay shows it. The second is the student whose supervisor gave a clear structural instruction early, who did not understand it, who was too embarrassed to ask twice, and who spent four months writing in the wrong genre. A tutor who sees the reflection notes catches the second pattern in one session, which is the single highest-value thing this kind of home tutoring does. Extended Essay (EE) IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai cover is how our own listing describes the service, and it undersells the part that matters: somebody reading the supervisor's comments with your child and checking they landed.

sections.heading: What a term of EE home tutoring changes, and what it cannot
paragraphs: At four weeks the deliverable is clarity, not pages. The student should have a question they can state in one sentence without hedging, a written list of the evidence they need and where it comes from, and a dated plan running to the next reflection session. That is a modest-looking output and it is the correct one; a student who has produced three thousand words in four weeks on an unapproved question has produced a problem rather than progress. If four weeks have passed with no narrowing and no evidence plan, the match is wrong and you should raise it then.

By the end of a term, look for genre. Early research essays by capable students read like extended school essays: confident, well-written, and organised around topics rather than around an argument that answers a question. The change you want to see is structural, where sections start existing because the argument needs them, where evidence is interrogated rather than presented, and where the conclusion says what the research could not establish. Supervisor comments shifting from structural objections to detailed quibbles is the clearest external signal available to a parent who cannot judge the subject content.

Across the full cycle, hold on to proportion. The essay is one component of a Diploma that is mostly decided by examined papers, and a strong essay does not rescue a weak subject profile. We do not guarantee grades, on this or anything else, and a service that offers a specific outcome on an externally moderated research essay is telling you something about its methods. What good coaching reliably produces is a submitted essay, on time, on an answerable question, built from evidence the student actually gathered, with a reflection record that matches the person who wrote it. Students also come out of it able to run a long project, which is the only part of the Diploma that transfers directly to a university degree.

The limits are specific and worth stating. Coaching cannot invent evidence that was never collected, and in DP2 that is the commonest dead end we meet. It cannot change a registration subject after the deadline. It cannot repair a reflection record that was never kept. It cannot substitute for the supervisor, whose judgement comes first. And it cannot make a student care about a question chosen to impress a university admissions page, which is a problem best solved before registration rather than after.

One term: structure driven by argument, evidence interrogated not listed

sections.heading: Starting IB extended essay home classes in Mumbai
paragraphs: Bring five things to the first session. The school's handbook or task brief. The registration subject and the current wording of the question. Any reflection session notes. The draft, however rough or however embarrassing. And the school's dates, which are the dates that will be enforced. Families who bring all five get a decision out of the first hour; families who bring a description of the problem spend that hour establishing what the problem is.

The first session should end with three things written down: whether the question survives as it stands, what evidence the student must obtain and by when, and what the next reflection session will be used for. Expect the tutor to be unwelcome about the question if it needs to be, especially in DP2, where the right advice is often to make a flawed question work rather than start again. Expect them to refuse to touch the prose. Expect a short plan naming the next three deliverables and their dates, so you can see progress without having to judge the content.

On cost, what you pay turns on the registration subject and its scarcity in Mumbai, the level of the student, how far a tutor travels and against which traffic, the session length, and whether written feedback on drafts between sessions is included. That last item is where the real work in research supervision sits, so parents comparing IB tuition fees in Mumbai across providers should compare what is included rather than the headline hourly rate. A cheaper hour with no draft feedback is the expensive option here. We will not print a figure, and a provider who prints one without knowing the subject and the stage is guessing.

If the match is wrong, tell us in week four. The outgoing tutor writes a handover covering the question, the evidence position and the weakest criterion, the incoming tutor reads it before the first session, and we keep your slot where we can. Chasing the best IB tutor in Mumbai is understandable and usually unhelpful; what moves an essay is somebody who knows the registration subject, respects the supervisor, and will tell your child in October that the question needs cutting. A home tutor for Extended Essay (EE) Mumbai parents actually recommend to each other is almost always that person rather than the most decorated one.
bullets: Bring the handbook, the question, the reflection notes, the draft and the dates
First session ends with a verdict on the question and an evidence deadline
Expect refusal to touch the prose, and a written three-deliverable plan

faqs.question: What is a tutor actually allowed to do on an Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Coach, question and give feedback on writing the student produced. A tutor can interrogate the research question, explain what each criterion rewards, teach search strategy, point at a section that reports where it should argue, and ask why a conclusion follows from the evidence. A tutor cannot write or rewrite sentences, supply sources that become the bibliography, collect data, draft a structure the student cannot explain, or produce a model essay to work from. The test is whether your child could defend every choice to their supervisor tomorrow without notes. If not, it does not belong in the document.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Borivali on a weekday evening during the drafting months?
faqs.answer: Yes, and Borivali is one of the easier matches in the city because the Western Line and Metro Lines 2A and 7 both serve it, so a tutor from Kandivali East, Malad or Dahisar reaches you predictably. What we avoid is sending somebody from the Central or Eastern Suburbs across at 7pm, because research sessions are often short and urgent, and a long commute for a forty-minute draft review stops happening by the second month. If the registration subject is scarce in the Western Suburbs, we will propose screen sessions for drafting and keep the travelled sessions for the question stage.

faqs.question: Do we need a parent at home while draft feedback is happening?
faqs.answer: Somebody should be in the house and the door should stay open, which is our standing expectation for every placement. You do not need to sit in, and with a DP2 student it is usually counterproductive, because useful draft feedback involves being told that a section does not argue anything and seventeen-year-olds absorb that badly in front of a parent. What is worth doing afterwards is asking your child to explain one change in their own words. If they can, the coaching is working within the rules. If they cannot, you have found a problem early.

faqs.question: My daughter has an approved question but the sources do not exist. What now?
faqs.answer: Change the question rather than the standard of evidence, and do it with the supervisor rather than around them. This is the most common crisis in DP1 and it is recoverable if caught early: the usual fix keeps her subject and her interest but swaps the evidence base for one she can reach, which often means something local, published or physically accessible in Mumbai. A tutor's job is to generate three viable alternatives and test each for reachability before she takes them to the supervisor. What does not work is continuing with a question that can only be answered from material nobody can get.

faqs.question: How do Extended Essay deadlines fall across a Mumbai school year?
faqs.answer: Registration and question approval land late in DP1, a substantial first draft is usually wanted around the end of DP1 or very early in DP2, and final submission falls early in DP2 while the examined run-up is already under way. The summer between the two years is the only long uninterrupted block the student gets and is the block most often wasted. October of DP2 is the collision month, with the essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and internal deadlines together. Ask your coordinator in writing for the registration, draft and submission dates and plan against those.

faqs.question: Is online supervision good enough for a science Extended Essay with laboratory work?
faqs.answer: For the design, the analysis and the writing, yes. For the bench work, no. An online tutor can help scope a measurable relationship, plan controls and repeats, check that the uncertainty treatment is honest, and read the evaluation that most students under-write. What a screen cannot do is watch your child handle apparatus, judge whether a reading is being taken correctly, or notice a safety issue. For a science essay, keep the practical work inside the school's laboratory with the supervisor's knowledge, and ask the school what it will permit a student to run unsupervised before planning anything.

faqs.question: We live in Thane. Will a tutor come out along Ghodbunder Road?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the schedule built around that road rather than against it. A tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in about twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak, so we match within Thane wherever the subject allows and put sessions at times that avoid the worst of it. Mulund-based tutors sometimes cross over for the right subject. For short draft reviews during the drafting months we would usually suggest a screen session rather than an hour of Ghodbunder traffic each way.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees depend on for research essay supervision?
faqs.answer: Five variables, and anyone quoting a figure without them is guessing. The registration subject and how scarce it is in Mumbai, since World Studies, Economics and Business Management specialists are thinner on the ground than science teachers. The student's stage, because question-setting and final drafting are different kinds of work. Travel distance and direction, as an evening crossing costs two hours to deliver one. Session length, where several short reviews can total more than one weekly hour. And whether written feedback on drafts between sessions is included, which on this work is the item most worth paying for.

faqs.question: Four weeks in and there are no pages. Should we be worried?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, because pages are the wrong four-week measure here. What should exist is a question stated in one sentence without hedging, a written list of the evidence needed and where it comes from, and a dated plan to the next reflection session. If those three exist, the project is in better shape than one with three thousand words on an unapproved question. If none of them exists after four weeks, tell us that week. The usual cause is sessions spent discussing the subject rather than making decisions, and the usual fix is a different tutor with a handover note.

faqs.question: Can the tutor talk to the school supervisor to agree an approach?
faqs.answer: No, and we would decline if asked. The supervisor's relationship is with your child, the reflection sessions form part of the assessed record, and a tutor in that channel confuses whose work is being judged. The tutor's contribution is to prepare your child to use the next meeting well: one precise question to ask, a draft to bring, a note written the same day. Where something genuinely needs raising with the school you raise it as the parent, and the tutor helps you ask a specific question rather than express a general worry about progress.

faqs.question: Can you promise a higher mark on the essay?
faqs.answer: We cannot, and we do not guarantee grades. The essay is marked externally against published criteria, which puts the outcome outside the reach of any tutor or school. What coaching reliably delivers is a submitted essay on an answerable question, built from evidence your child gathered, finished before the deadline rather than during it, with a reflection record that reads like them. Be wary of any Mumbai service offering a guaranteed grade on an externally assessed research essay, because the only way to approach a promise like that is by doing work the student should be doing.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to our school or its Diploma coordinator?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform, not affiliated with any school named on this page, and we do not contact schools, coordinators or individual teachers, nor request marking material a school has not published. Schools are named because Mumbai parents recognise their calendars and the pressure points those calendars create. The only documents a tutor works from are your school's published handbook, the current subject guide and your child's own drafts and reflection notes, which is exactly how this kind of supervision should work.

sections.heading: How IB Gram finds an IB French tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: A parent searching for an IB French tutor in Mumbai is usually in one of three situations. There is the Grade 9 or 10 student who picked French as a second language and has quietly stopped understanding the listening exercises. There is the DP1 student who chose French B and cannot keep pace with the reading comprehension now that the texts are authentic rather than textbook. And there is the DP2 student whose individual oral is weeks away, who writes well and freezes the moment a teacher stops reading from a slide. Those three need different tutors, and the match starts with working out which one you are describing rather than with a list of names.

The query form asks for the board, the route, the year group, the school and the two or three windows in your week that are genuinely free. Those last details decide more than parents expect. A French specialist who can take a Thursday 7pm slot in Khar West is a different person from one who can take Saturday mornings in Chembur, and the honest answer is that the second list is longer. Searches for "IB tutors near me Mumbai" make sense for exactly this reason: travel time is the real constraint, not willingness. Once the shortlist is ready you see teaching history, the routes each tutor has taught and the areas they cover, before anyone has your phone number.

The trial session is a diagnostic, not a sales call. A good French tutor spends it finding out what your child can do unprompted: read a short authentic text aloud, answer four or five questions about it with no preparation time, write a few sentences using the tenses they claim to know. Most students sound considerably stronger on paper than in speech, and the size of that gap is the thing the tutor is measuring. You get a short written read on where the child actually is, what the first month would target, and you decide after that whether to continue. Nobody asks you to commit to a term in advance.

sections.heading: Which French route is your child actually on?
paragraphs: French inside the International Baccalaureate (IB) runs on four different routes, and the route matters far more than the year group. In the Middle Years Programme (MYP) French sits inside language acquisition and is placed by phase rather than by grade. In the Diploma Programme (DP) it is usually French B at Standard Level (SL) or Higher Level (HL). French ab initio at SL exists for students genuinely starting the language in DP1. French A, taught as a literature subject, applies to the small number of students who read and write French at near-native level.

Working out which one applies to your child takes two minutes with the right document. Look at the report card first: a phase descriptor means MYP, while a mention of ab initio or of Language B at SL or HL means the DP. Look next at the header of the last mock paper for a syllabus code, which tells you whether the school entered Cambridge IGCSE French or an Edexcel International GCSE in Years 9 to 11. If both are ambiguous, the school's IB coordinator or examinations officer will confirm the route in one email, and that answer is worth having in writing before you book anybody. Tutors cost the same whichever route you guess wrong on; the wasted term does not.

This page covers French at IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 with a tutor Mumbai parents can keep as the route changes under the child. The MYP-specific detail, phase placement, the interim objectives and how eAssessment preparation is structured, belongs on our MYP French pages, and pointing you there is more useful than half-covering it here. What matters at this level is that the routes are not a simple ladder of difficulty. A student who scores well in MYP French can still find DP French B hard, because the DP asks for sustained argument and inference in the language rather than accurate sentences about familiar topics.

sections.heading: Listening, reading, writing and the speaking test
paragraphs: Four skills, assessed separately, and almost every student is uneven across them. Reading usually comes first, because it is the skill ordinary schoolwork rewards most often. Writing follows, because text types can be practised to a pattern. Listening and spontaneous speech lag behind, and they lag quietly: a child can hold a strong class-test record and still lose the thread thirty seconds into an unfamiliar recording. An IB French home tutor in Mumbai who opens with grammar worksheets is solving the easy half of the problem while the half that decides the grade sits untouched.

The listening work is the least glamorous and the most productive thing a tutor can do. The recordings use accents, speeds and registers a Mumbai classroom rarely produces, and the questions reward a student who can hold a number, a time and a reason in their head while the audio keeps moving. Tutors who teach this well use short, frequent listening rather than long sessions: one authentic clip, replayed two or three times, with the student writing down what they caught after each pass and comparing versions. The second pass is where the gain shows, and the student can see it, which is what keeps them doing it between sessions.

Writing is where text types decide marks that have nothing to do with vocabulary. A blog entry, a formal letter, an article and a set of instructions are not interchangeable, and a student who writes an elegant paragraph in the wrong register loses marks their French did not deserve to lose. For the speaking test the examiner-facing skill is unprepared response: looking at a stimulus, saying something true about it, then defending that when asked why. Ask your school for the current subject guide before planning anything around components, because the IB revises its guides on its own cycle and only the version for the year your child sits is worth working from.

sections.heading: French home tuition across Mumbai, zone by zone
paragraphs: An IB French tutor in Mumbai is matched on travel time before anything else, because French specialists are not spread evenly across Mumbai, Maharashtra. They cluster where the schools that teach French cluster, which puts the deepest pool around BKC, Juhu, Bandra, Powai and the island city, and the thinnest at the far ends of the Western and Central lines. South Mumbai covers Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Churchgate, Walkeshwar and Worli, and tutors here are matched inside the island: someone coming down from Andheri for a 6.30pm lesson on Peddar Road will quit by the third week. The Western Line, the Harbour Line, Metro Line 3 and the Coastal Road are the routes that matter for these matches.

In the Western Suburbs, which run from Bandra and Khar West through Santacruz, Juhu, Andheri, Goregaon, Malad and Kandivali to Borivali, matching along the Western Line works and matching across it does not. A tutor in Khar reaches Santacruz in ten minutes and Goregaon in forty at 6pm, and Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made the Dahisar to Andheri run far more predictable than the Western Express Highway ever was. The Central Suburbs bring Powai, Chandivali, Kurla, Ghatkopar and Mulund into play, where Powai is the standing exception: no station of its own, so tutors arrive by road off JVLR from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and the SCLR carries the Chembur side.

The Eastern Suburbs stretch from Chembur and Wadala through Vikhroli and Bhandup, and the Eastern Freeway makes a Chembur tutor genuinely available in South Mumbai on a Saturday morning in a way the map hides. Navi Mumbai works node to node across Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, linked by Palm Beach Road and the Sion–Panvel Highway, with the Atal Setu changing what a weekend lesson from the island city costs in time. In Thane, Ghodbunder Road sets the timetable: a tutor near the station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour at 7pm. French home classes across Mumbai are built around those facts rather than around a radius on a map.

sections.heading: What the Mumbai school year does to French deadlines
paragraphs: Most Mumbai IB schools sit the May examination session, which pushes the real pressure into January, February and March. Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, the American School of Bombay, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School at Goregaon East (JVLR), B.D. Somani International School at Cuffe Parade, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo and Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai all work to that rhythm, with internal deadlines set by each school rather than by the IB. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page.

The practical consequence for French is that the oral and the written coursework land in the same weeks as everything else. A DP2 student in Walkeshwar can have her French oral window, a Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay deadline and two Internal Assessment (IA) drafts inside a single fortnight. French is the one she will push back, because speaking feels like something you can simply do on the day rather than something you prepare, and the student has no evidence to the contrary until the recording is made. That single misjudgement is the most common reason a French grade sits below the rest of an otherwise consistent transcript.

Term planning therefore works backwards from your school's own calendar, not from a generic one. October and November are when a tutor can still build vocabulary range and listening stamina without a deadline in the room. December and January are mock season, which gives useful feedback and is a poor moment to start new material. February and March belong to oral preparation and timed writing. By April the work is maintenance and nerve management. Families who start French tuition in June or July, at the opening of the Mumbai academic year, get the version of this that actually works, and your school's examinations officer is the person who can confirm every date.

sections.heading: Home classes, online lessons or a mix of both?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default for French in Mumbai and it deserves to be. A tutor sitting across the table hears hesitation, catches a dropped verb ending and can hold a conversation the student cannot escape from, which is precisely what the speaking test asks for. An IB French home tutor in Mumbai also gets the quiet half of the room, your child's own books and desk, and a parent who can tell what is happening without asking for a report. The travel cost is real and it is the reason we match inside a zone rather than across the city.

Online works better for French than for most subjects, on two conditions: headphones, and a camera the student actually leaves on. Listening practice is cleaner online because the audio goes straight into the ear instead of across a room with a mixer running in the kitchen. Sharing a text on screen and annotating it live suits reading comprehension. Recording a two-minute spoken answer and playing it back immediately is trivial online and awkward in person. What a screen cannot replicate is the pressure of a person waiting for an answer, so a purely online plan tends to leave speaking weaker than everything else. An IB online tutor in Mumbai is the right answer when the alternative is no tutor at all.

Hybrid is where most families settle after a term: one home tuition slot a week for speaking and feedback, one shorter online session for listening drills and marked writing. It also survives the Mumbai monsoon, which is the practical argument rather than the pedagogical one. When Ghodbunder Road is standing still or the Andheri subway is under water, the online session happens and the week is not lost. Families in Panvel, Kasarvadavali and Dahisar East, where the specialist French pool is thin, often choose hybrid from the start: a home tutor for French Mumbai parents can schedule around a school week, plus an online specialist for the route itself.

sections.heading: How do you check a French tutor can actually teach the oral?
paragraphs: Ask the tutor to run five minutes of unprepared French with your child during the trial, then listen from the next room. You are not judging the accent. You are listening for whether the tutor keeps the student talking, repairs errors without stopping the flow, and asks a follow-up question the student did not see coming. A tutor who switches to English inside the first minute is teaching French grammar rather than French, and that distinction will show up in the oral long before it shows up in a report card.

On our side, every tutor's identity and qualification documents are checked, the routes they claim to have taught are confirmed against their teaching history, and references are called where a school or an examination board is named. What IB Gram does not do is tell you a tutor is excellent because a form says so, and we do not guarantee grades, because no honest platform can. IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation to any school or board named on this page, so verification here means documents, experience and the routes someone has genuinely taught rather than a promise about results.

Three things are worth checking yourself. Ask which route the tutor has taught most recently and which text types they teach for the written paper. Ask how they would handle a student who understands the grammar and still cannot follow a recording; the useful answer involves shorter clips more often, not more worksheets. And be wary of anyone offering a guaranteed grade or a fixed score improvement, because moderation does not work that way and the offer tells you something about the tutor. There is no single best IB tutor in Mumbai for French, only the right match for one route and one timetable. An IB private tutor Mumbai families have kept for two years is a stronger signal than a long list of certificates.

sections.heading: Why the speaking test decides how French tuition is planned
paragraphs: The speaking test is the component that reshapes a tuition plan, because it is the only one a student cannot cram. Vocabulary can be loaded in a fortnight. Reading comprehension improves with technique and past papers. Spontaneous speech needs repeated low-stakes practice spread over months, which is why a tutor booked in February for an oral in March is being asked to do something unreasonable. The honest conversation with a parent in that position is about damage limitation: which three topics the student can hold under pressure, and how to stop a blank from becoming a silence.

Mumbai adds a specific wrinkle worth naming. Many students here already run three languages before French arrives: English at school, Hindi or Marathi in the city, and Gujarati, Tamil, Konkani or another language at home. French becomes a fourth. That is an advantage for grammatical awareness and a disadvantage for fluency under pressure, because more systems compete for the same sentence at the same time. Tutors who have taught French in Mumbai schools recognise the pattern immediately: a child who code-switches mid-sentence is not careless, they are overloaded, and the remedy is rehearsal of whole chunks rather than another round of correction.

A workable plan looks like this. From the start of the year, speaking takes five to ten minutes of every single session, on topics the course sets rather than topics the student enjoys. By the second term the student records answers and listens back, which is uncomfortable and effective in roughly equal measure. In the month before the oral window, sessions become full simulations using a stimulus the student has not seen. What IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on is partly this: a tutor running recorded simulations is preparing and marking outside the session, and scarcity at the Higher Level end of French moves availability more than any other factor, along with travel distance, session length and the board itself.

sections.heading: What progress in French looks like at four weeks and one term
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see two things and not a third. The student should be able to say more in French before switching to English, and their written work should show the tutor's corrections being applied rather than repeated verbatim in the next piece. What you should not expect at four weeks is a grade change. School French grades move on assessment cycles, and a month of tuition usually falls between two reporting points, so the first honest evidence lives in the exercise book and the recordings, not on the report card.

By the end of a term, listening is the test. If a student who could not follow a recording in August is catching the main idea and two supporting details in November, the tuition is doing its job. If reading and writing have improved while listening has not moved at all, say so to the tutor directly and ask what changes next week. The right answer involves more frequent listening with shorter clips and a written record of what was caught. The wrong answer is another grammar pack, and you are entitled to push back on it.

Over one exam cycle the realistic claim is a student who walks into the oral able to speak for the required time about a stimulus they have not seen, and who does not lose written marks on register. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and will not publish a figure suggesting otherwise. If a tutor is not working out, and the signs are a student going quiet, sessions drifting into chat and marked work stopping, tell us inside the first fortnight. We shortlist a replacement and pass the handover notes on, so your child restates nothing and starts from where they actually are.

sections.heading: Starting IB French home tuition in Mumbai
paragraphs: Three documents make the first session twice as useful. Bring the last French assessment with the teacher's written comments, the school term calendar, and the mock paper header showing the route or syllabus code. If you have any recording of a previous oral, even one made on a phone in the back of a car, bring that too. A tutor learns more from ninety seconds of your child speaking than from a page of marks, because the marks tell you the score and the recording tells you why.

The first session runs as a diagnostic and ends with a plan you can read: what the tutor thinks the gap is, what the first month targets, and how speaking gets into every session rather than the last ten minutes of some of them. Ask for that in writing. Vague plans produce vague tuition, and a French plan that never mentions listening or the oral is not a French plan. An IB home tutor in Mumbai should also tell you what the student does between sessions, which for French means twenty minutes of listening rather than an hour of conjugation tables.

Scheduling is the last decision and the one that determines whether any of this lasts. Pick the slot you can protect for a full term, not the one that looks ideal in September. A Tuesday 7pm in Lower Parel that survives two work trips beats a Saturday 10am that collapses the first time there is a birthday party. If crossing the Bandra–Worli Sea Link or running up the Western Express Highway makes a weekday evening fragile, say so at the start and the shortlist changes shape. A tutor who lives twelve minutes away and arrives on time beats a stronger profile that arrives late by November.

faqs.question: What does an IB French tutor in Mumbai cost?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate, and anyone quoting one before seeing the case is guessing. IB home tuition in Mumbai is priced per session against five things: the board and route, the level, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels and how long each session runs. French at Higher Level is scarcer than French at MYP phase level, so it sits higher. A tutor crossing from Bandra to Cuffe Parade is pricing an hour of traffic into every visit. Ask for the rate per session and what marking outside the session is included, and compare those two numbers rather than headline figures.

faqs.question: Can a French tutor travel to Cuffe Parade for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor already lives or teaches in South Mumbai. A 6.30pm or 7pm start in Cuffe Parade works for a tutor based in Colaba, Churchgate, Walkeshwar or Worli, because the Coastal Road and the island's short distances make the return trip manageable. The same slot offered to a tutor in Andheri or Powai looks fine on a map and falls apart by the third week, when Peddar Road at 6pm has eaten forty minutes twice. We shortlist within the zone for weekday evenings and open the search wider only for weekend mornings, when the travel maths changes completely.

faqs.question: My child is in the MYP, not the DP. Is this page for us?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the honest answer is to read the MYP French pages instead for the detail you need. This page covers French across the IB and IGCSE routes together: how they differ, which tutor suits which, and how the Mumbai school calendar squeezes the subject. Phase placement, the interim objectives and how your school prepares eAssessment are genuinely different conversations, and we keep them on their own pages rather than compressing them into a paragraph here. The matching process, the verification checks, the zone coverage and the fee factors described on this page apply to an MYP request in exactly the same way.

faqs.question: Is French ab initio easier than French B?
faqs.answer: It is different rather than easier, and choosing it for the wrong reason costs a student a year. Ab initio at Standard Level assumes little or no prior French and builds from the ground, which suits a student who arrives in DP1 having never studied the language. French B assumes prior study and asks for inference, opinion and sustained argument in the language. A student with three years of school French who drops into ab initio is often bored and then careless. Ask your IB coordinator which route the school will actually enter your child for, because availability varies by school and the decision is not always the family's.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for the speaking test?
faqs.answer: It works for everything except the pressure, and the pressure is half the skill. Online is excellent for listening practice, because audio into headphones is cleaner than audio across a room, and for recording a spoken answer and playing it straight back. What a screen softens is the experience of a person sitting opposite waiting for you to finish a sentence, which is exactly the condition of the oral. Most families who care about the speaking component run one home session a week for conversation and a shorter online session for listening and marked writing, and that split holds up better than either mode alone.

faqs.question: How does a tutor get a gate pass for our building in Powai?
faqs.answer: The same way any regular visitor does, and it is worth setting up once rather than weekly. Most Powai and Hiranandani Gardens complexes will register a standing weekly visitor if the flat owner raises the request with the society office, after which the tutor's entry takes thirty seconds instead of a phone call to your flat. Give the tutor's name, mobile number and the fixed day and time at the start, and ask whether the society wants photo identification on file. Tutors who teach home tuition in gated complexes expect this and will send their details without being chased twice.

faqs.question: Can my child start French in Grade 11 after moving from a CBSE school?
faqs.answer: Often yes, through the ab initio route, but the decision belongs to the school rather than to you or to us. A student arriving from a CBSE background with no French usually enters French ab initio at Standard Level, which is designed for exactly that case. The workload in the first term is heavier than it looks, because the student is learning a language and the IB's assessment style at the same time. Speak to the DP coordinator about which language options the school is running that year, then book tuition for the first term rather than waiting to see how it goes.

faqs.question: Her listening score has not moved after a month. What now?
faqs.answer: Say it to the tutor in plain terms and ask what changes next week. One month is enough time to see movement in listening if listening is being practised properly, and a flat score usually means the sessions are still mostly grammar and translation. The fix is structural: short authentic clips several times a week, replayed with a written record of what was caught each pass, rather than one long comprehension exercise per session. If the plan does not change after that conversation, ask us for a different shortlist. A tutor who cannot adjust a method is the wrong tutor, not a sign the child cannot improve.

faqs.question: Should one tutor teach French and her other subjects too?
faqs.answer: For French, no. Language teaching is a separate craft, and a strong Maths or Economics tutor who also offers French is usually offering school-level French rather than route-level teaching. Where one tutor across subjects does make sense is MYP support in the lower grades, where the work is study skills as much as content. For DP French B or ab initio, book a French specialist and keep the subject separate even if it means a second weekly visit. If travel makes two home visits impractical, run the French session online and keep the in-person slot for the subject that needs it more.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Someone responsible should be in the flat, and that is our standing position for home tuition with a minor. It does not mean sitting in the room. A parent, grandparent or a trusted adult at home is enough, and most families use the time to be somewhere else in the house. Set the session up in a shared space rather than a bedroom, with a table, a plug point and the door open. For the first session it helps if a parent is around at the start and the end, because that is when the tutor explains what they found and what the first month will target.

faqs.question: Will tuition get my child a 7 in French?
faqs.answer: Nobody can promise that, and we do not guarantee grades. What tuition can do is close specific gaps: a student who cannot follow a recording learns to catch the main idea and the details, a student who writes in the wrong register learns the text types, a student who freezes in the oral gets enough rehearsal that the format stops being a shock. Those are the things a tutor controls. The grade also depends on the rest of the Diploma Programme load, the school's own assessment calendar and how much the student does between sessions, and any tutor pricing a specific number is selling you something else.

ib-french-tutor.closingCta: Send the route, the year group, the school and the two evening windows you can actually protect. We come back with a shortlist of verified French tutors who have taught that route, with teaching history and coverage area, before anyone calls you. You pick one, run a diagnostic trial session, and decide after it. If the match is wrong in the first fortnight, ask for a replacement and the handover notes travel with it.

ib-hindi-tutor.heroIntro: Parents who hire an IB Hindi home tutor in Mumbai are rarely solving a fluency problem. The child talks easily and writes badly, because the International Baccalaureate (IB) examines a formal written register in Devanagari that nobody uses at the dinner table. This page explains the routes, the paper, and how home tuition for Hindi is organised city-wide.
trustPoints: Matched on written Devanagari and route, not on who speaks Hindi fluently
Marked script returned every session, with handwriting speed tracked separately
Identity, qualification and school teaching history verified before you see a profile
Replacement arranged quickly when a match does not suit the student

sections.heading: How we match a Hindi tutor to a Mumbai family in practice
paragraphs: Requests for Hindi arrive with the least useful information of any subject we handle. Almost all of them say some version of "we need a Hindi teacher, three times a week". Hindi is the one subject where a parent can find twenty willing candidates in their own building and still hire the wrong one, so our first questions go in a different direction: what does your child's written work look like, how fast does she write in Devanagari, and does the report name Language B, Hindi A, or Hindi as a Second Language. One photograph of a marked answer tells us more than a twenty-minute phone call.

A shortlist is then built around the written paper rather than around conversation. We look for tutors who have taught the named route in a school, who have marked written work against the criteria the school actually uses, and who can produce an example of a corrected student script. Only after that do we filter on geography and on the two slots you can hold every week. A family in Vikhroli with a 7pm Tuesday and a 10am Sunday gets a very different list from a family in Colaba with weekday afternoons free.

You then speak to the tutors on the list before any booking. Ask each one how she corrects handwriting, what she does with a student who speaks well and writes in a mixture of Hindi, English and Marathi, and how much of the lesson will be spent writing rather than talking. An IB Hindi home tutor in Mumbai who never asks your child to write under time is going to be comfortable and useless. The tutor who produces squared paper and a stopwatch in the first session is the one worth keeping.
bullets: 1. Send the route named on the report plus a photo of one marked written answer
2. We shortlist on written-paper and script experience before anything else
3. Geography and your two weekly slots narrow the list to two or three names
4. You interview each name yourself, asking specifically about handwriting correction
5. A paid diagnostic session grades script, register, listening and speaking separately

sections.heading: Hindi A, Hindi B or Hindi as a Second Language: which one is on the report?
paragraphs: Three different Hindi courses run in Mumbai schools and families mix them up constantly. In the Diploma Programme (DP), a student who grew up with Hindi as a first language may take Hindi A, which is a literature or language-and-literature course and is examined as such. A student who learned Hindi mainly at school takes Language B at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL). On the Cambridge International Education side, Hindi as a Second Language is its own syllabus, separate from Hindi as a first language, and the two are not taught alike.

Below that, Hindi normally sits inside Middle Years Programme (MYP) Language Acquisition, where students are placed in phases according to prior experience rather than year group, and inside the Primary Years Programme (PYP) as an additional language. Our MYP Hindi pages handle the phase structure and the criteria in detail, so this page does not repeat them. What matters on a board-wide page is that a phase placement made in Year 6 often goes unreviewed, and a child who has moved ahead of her phase spends three years doing comfortable work before the Diploma exposes the gap.

Mumbai adds its own layer. Most schools here offer a choice of second language, usually among Hindi, Marathi, French and Spanish, and the choice is made at a particular year by school policy rather than by the board. Hindi is picked more often than any other, frequently on the assumption that a child who hears it daily will coast. The subject line on the statement of entry is where you check what was actually chosen, and the school's coordinator is the only reliable source for whether a switch is still possible. Ask in writing, and ask before the year starts.
bullets: Hindi A: a literature course for first-language students, examined on texts
Language B at Higher Level or Standard Level: school-learned Hindi, different reading load
Hindi as a Second Language: its own Cambridge syllabus, not a lighter Hindi A
MYP phases and PYP additional language: covered on our MYP Hindi pages
Second-language choice is set by school policy; confirm the route in writing

sections.heading: The reading and writing paper, listening, and the speaking component
paragraphs: Hindi as a Second Language is assessed through a reading and writing paper, a listening component and a speaking component, and the reading and writing paper is where Mumbai students lose most of their marks. Reading is not the difficulty; a child who watches Hindi content handles an unseen passage reasonably. Writing is the difficulty, and inside writing it is register and script accuracy, not vocabulary. A student who can discuss a film for ten minutes will still write an application letter in the voice she uses on a family group chat.

Script accuracy means matras, nukta and the small vowel marks that change a word entirely and that no spell-check has ever corrected for your child. Examiners mark what is on the page. A tutor who reads a line aloud, hears it as correct because she knows what was meant, and moves on is training your child to fail the paper politely. The correction has to be made on paper, in pen, with the student rewriting the line, and it has to happen every week until the errors stop appearing.

The listening component is harder than families expect because the recordings do not sound like the Hindi your child hears in Mumbai. Speakers from different regions, formal announcements, and vocabulary from registers she never meets socially all appear. The speaking component usually involves a prepared element followed by a conversation, and the prepared element is where structure can be taught. For the current paper structure, components and assessment conditions, use the syllabus document your school issues or ask the examinations officer, because the boards revise these on their own timetable and last year's description may not describe your child's session.

Matras and nukta errors are invisible to a fluent reader and obvious to an examiner

sections.heading: Where Hindi home tuition runs across Mumbai
paragraphs: Hindi is the opposite of a scarce subject, so geography stops being about availability and becomes entirely about schedule. An IB Hindi home tutor in Mumbai can be found near almost any address in Mumbai, Maharashtra; the work is finding one near you who has also taught the examined course. In the Eastern Suburbs, tutors move easily between Chembur, Govandi, Bhandup and Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines, with the Eastern Freeway and the Monorail from Chembur to Wadala making the southern end reachable. In the Central Suburbs, Ghatkopar, Vikhroli and Kurla are connected by the Central Line and Metro Line 1 towards Andheri, and Powai is reached by road because it has no station.

The Western Suburbs hold the largest number of candidates and the worst traffic. Matching along the Western Line or Metro Lines 2A and 7 works: Dahisar to Borivali, Kandivali to Malad, Goregaon East to Jogeshwari. Asking a tutor to cross from Juhu to Goregaon East across the Western Express Highway for a 6.30pm slot does not work in June and does not work in September. In South Mumbai, families in Walkeshwar, Tardeo, Peddar Road and Fort are matched within the island, where the Coastal Road and Metro Line 3 have changed evening timings more than any other recent project.

Navi Mumbai and Thane are straightforward for Hindi. Airoli, Vashi, Nerul, Belapur and Kharghar each have resident teachers, and Palm Beach Road plus the Navi Mumbai Metro from Belapur to Pendhar keep node-to-node travel short; the Atal Setu matters more for weekend lessons than weekday ones. In Thane, Pokhran Road, Majiwada and the long Ghodbunder Road corridor out to Kasarvadavali decide everything about timing, so we match a Kasarvadavali family with a Kasarvadavali tutor rather than someone near Thane station. Families in Mulund sometimes cross over, and once the Thane-Borivali tunnel corridor is in use that calculation changes again.

Central Suburbs: Ghatkopar, Vikhroli and Kurla along the Central Line and Metro Line 1

sections.heading: Second-language choices in Mumbai schools, and when the pressure lands
paragraphs: The academic year here runs from June to March or April, and Hindi gets squeezed at predictable moments. The first written assessments land in August and September, which is when most parents discover that daily conversation has not produced an examinable writer. Mock examinations in November and December put the written paper next to five other subjects. February is when speaking components and coursework deadlines cluster. A Year 11 student in Kandivali East revising for a Mathematics paper on Monday and a Hindi written paper on Wednesday will spend Sunday on Mathematics, because Hindi feels like the subject she already knows.

Families we work with attend a wide spread of schools: JBCN International School in Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Bombay Cambridge International School in Andheri East, Oberoi International School off JVLR in Goregaon East, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Gopi Birla Memorial School in Walkeshwar, and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul. Each sets its own internal deadlines and its own second-language policy. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named here, and we do not guarantee grades for any course.

The decision point worth marking in your own calendar is the year your school fixes the second language, usually in the middle school years. A child placed in a Hindi phase at ten and never reassessed arrives at the Diploma with three comfortable years behind her and no written stamina. If you are considering a switch, the question is not whether Hindi is easier; it is whether your child can write three pages of formal Hindi in exam conditions by the time she sits the paper. Ask the school for the assessment calendar in June and plan the year against it.
bullets: August and September: the first written assessments expose spoken-only fluency
November and December: mock papers sit alongside every other subject's revision

sections.heading: Does Hindi home tuition work better than online lessons in Mumbai?
paragraphs: For Hindi, yes, and the reason is handwriting. Script errors have to be caught as the pen moves, which means somebody sitting beside your child watching the stroke order, the matra placement and the speed. A tutor on a screen sees a finished paragraph; a tutor at the table sees why it went wrong. This is the clearest case for home tuition in any language subject we handle.

Online still has a place, and it is a specific one. Reading comprehension, listening practice, vocabulary building and the prepared part of the speaking component all transfer to a screen without loss, and an IB Hindi online tutor in Mumbai can run a short mid-week session that would never justify an hour of travel. The practical arrangement that works is that your child photographs each piece of written work and sends it before the lesson, so the tutor has already marked the script and spends the session on the corrections rather than on reading. Without that discipline, online Hindi becomes conversation practice for a child who did not need conversation practice.

Hybrid suits most families on this subject: one weekly home tutoring slot for writing and marked script, one short online session for listening and oral preparation. It also protects the arrangement from the two things that end weekly lessons in this city, which are monsoon traffic and a tutor whose travel time quietly doubled when a new timetable moved the slot from 5pm to 6.30pm. Agree the split after the diagnostic session, and agree what happens on a day when nobody can travel, because in July somebody will not be able to travel.
bullets: Home tuition leads for Hindi because script errors must be caught as they happen
Online covers reading, listening and prepared speaking without any real loss
Send photographs of written work before an online lesson so marking is already done
Hybrid protects the arrangement from monsoon travel and shifting school timetables
Decide in advance what happens on a day when travel is impossible

sections.heading: Fluent speaker or trained teacher: what do we verify before a Hindi tutor starts?
paragraphs: This distinction matters more in Hindi than in any other subject on the platform, because the supply of fluent speakers is effectively unlimited and the supply of people who have taught the examined course is not. Every tutor goes through the same baseline: government photo identity, the qualification claimed, the schools and boards taught in with dates, and references we telephone and question rather than file. For Hindi we additionally ask for a sample of marked student script, because that single document separates a teacher from a speaker faster than any interview.

Your own checks are simple and you should run all of them in the first fortnight. Ask to see your child's written work after each session and look for corrections in the margin, not a tick and a score. Ask the tutor what register she is teaching towards and have her show you the difference between two versions of the same sentence. Ask how she handles code-mixing, since a Mumbai child writing Hindi will reach for English and Marathi words without noticing. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade or who treats the written paper as something to worry about later in the year.

If the match is wrong, say so early. We arrange a different tutor without a debate and without asking you to justify it beyond a sentence, because the common failure in Hindi is not a bad person, it is a kind relative-of-a-friend who was never going to run a written-paper programme. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and makes no claims about outcomes; what we can promise is that a replacement takes days rather than weeks, and that the second match will be built from what you tell us went wrong in the first.
bullets: Baseline checks: photo identity, qualification claimed, teaching history and called references

sections.heading: Your child speaks Hindi every day and still loses marks. Here is why
paragraphs: Mumbai produces a particular kind of Hindi student, and every examiner has met her. She has heard Hindi since she could walk, from family, from drivers and shopkeepers, from television and from everybody in the building lift. She can argue in it. She cannot write it. The Hindi she owns is a spoken, code-mixed, highly practical register that borrows English nouns and Marathi verbs without hesitation, and the paper she sits asks for formal written Hindi in accurate Devanagari with the conventions of a letter, a report or an essay observed. Those two things overlap much less than the word Hindi suggests.

The gap hides for years because school tests often reward participation and reading comprehension, both of which she does well. It surfaces in two places: a timed written paper, where she writes slowly and makes matra errors under pressure; and the formal end of the speaking component, where she has to sustain a structured piece rather than a conversation. By then she is in Year 10 or the second Diploma year with five other subjects on her desk and a belief, reinforced by everybody around her, that Hindi is the subject she does not need to study. Correcting that belief is half the work of a Hindi as a Second Language tutor in Mumbai.

The practical programme is unglamorous. Timed writing every week, the same text types cycled until the structure is automatic, script corrections rewritten rather than noted, and a vocabulary list built from the registers she lacks rather than the ones she has. Fees reflect this: what IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on is the route and level, the tutor's experience with the examined paper, session length, travel and the time of day, and for Hindi the honest driver is how much marking the tutor is doing between sessions. A tutor marking three written pieces a week is doing more unpaid work than one running conversation hours, and the rate reflects it. That marking, rather than the hour in your living room, is what an IB Hindi home tutor in Mumbai is really being paid for.
bullets: Spoken Mumbai Hindi is code-mixed and practical; the paper wants formal written Hindi
The gap hides behind good comprehension and confident classroom participation

sections.heading: What four weeks, one term and one exam cycle realistically change
paragraphs: At four weeks the measurable change is mechanical, and it is the right thing to look for. Your child should be writing faster in Devanagari, making fewer matra errors in work done under time, and producing a piece of writing each week that comes back with margin corrections. Nothing about her grade has changed yet. Anybody promising otherwise after a month has not seen enough Hindi papers.

At one term the register starts to move. She writes a formal letter differently from a diary entry, she reaches for a Hindi word she would previously have replaced with English, and the structured part of her speaking is organised rather than improvised. Hindi as a Second Language home classes Mumbai families run for a full term should by then have produced a visible file of marked work, and you should be able to flick through it and see the same error disappearing across six pieces. If every piece shows the same correction in week twelve as in week two, the method is wrong and we should be having a different conversation.

Across an exam cycle, the limit is worth stating plainly. Tuition changes preparation, and preparation changes the odds; nothing changes the outcome, and we do not guarantee grades or publish success figures. A student who writes one extra timed piece a week on her own gains more than one who treats the tutor's hour as her entire Hindi week. And occasionally the right advice is to stop: if a child is failing in four subjects, adding Hindi lessons is not the intervention she needs, and we would rather say that than sell you a slot.
bullets: Four weeks: faster script, fewer matra errors under time, weekly marked writing
One term: register separates, vocabulary widens, prepared speaking becomes structured

sections.heading: Booking Hindi home classes: the first fortnight
paragraphs: Write to us with four things: the school and year group, the route as the report names it, a photograph of one marked piece of written Hindi, and the two weekday slots you can actually hold for a year. The photograph does most of the work. It tells us whether you need a script-and-register specialist, a reading and listening programme, or someone preparing a first-language student for a literature course, and those are three different tutors.

You will have a shortlist within a day or two, with the route each tutor has taught and the areas she covers. Speak to each one, then book a paid diagnostic session. In that session expect a timed piece of writing, a listening extract and a short speaking task, followed by a plain statement of where your child sits in each and what the first month will cover. Ask for that plan in writing before the second session, and ask what your child is expected to do between lessons.

From there it is weekly, and the only thing that goes wrong quietly is marking drifting away. Check the file every fortnight for the first two months. A home tutor for Hindi as a Second Language Mumbai parents keep for two years is almost always one who was given clear feedback in the first month, so tell us early if the sessions have turned into conversation. If your child is in the MYP, start instead from our MYP Hindi page, which is written around the phase structure.

faqs.question: Can a Hindi tutor travel to Thane for an evening slot on Ghodbunder Road?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Hindi we can almost always find one who already lives on that stretch. The Ghodbunder Road corridor from Majiwada out to Kasarvadavali is slow enough after six that we match a Kasarvadavali family with a Kasarvadavali tutor rather than sending somebody from near Thane station. Mulund tutors sometimes cross on the Eastern Express Highway for a weekend slot. For a standing weekday evening lesson, resident-of-the-same-corridor is the only arrangement that survives a monsoon and a school timetable change in the same term.

faqs.question: My child speaks Hindi at home. Does she still need a tutor?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the reason surprises most families. The course examines formal written Hindi in accurate Devanagari, with the conventions of letters, reports and essays, and spoken fluency at home does not produce that. A child who argues comfortably in Hindi can still write slowly, drop matras under time pressure, and reach for English nouns in a formal answer. Look at a timed piece of her written work rather than listening to her talk. If the marks are coming off writing rather than reading, a Hindi home tutor is solving a real problem rather than an imagined one.

faqs.question: Is Hindi genuinely an easier second language than French or Spanish?
faqs.answer: It is easier to start and no easier to finish. A Mumbai child begins with a large spoken vocabulary and comfortable listening, which makes the early years feel light compared with a language learned from zero. The written paper then asks for a register and a script she has never produced formally, while her classmate in French has been writing in a foreign script-free language under instruction the whole time. Pick the subject your child will study, not the one that looks cheapest in Year 8.

faqs.question: How do we fix slow Devanagari handwriting before the exam?
faqs.answer: With timed writing every week and nothing else. Speed in script comes from repetition under a clock, so the tutor should be setting a piece to a fixed time in every session, marking it on paper, and having your child rewrite the corrected lines rather than reading the corrections. Expect the first few timed pieces to be unfinished. Measurable improvement in speed usually shows inside a month, which is why we treat it as the first thing to look for rather than as something to address near the exam.

faqs.question: What do Hindi tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Route and level, the tutor's experience with the examined paper, session length, travel distance, the time of day, and for this subject the marking load between sessions. A tutor returning three marked written pieces a week is working well beyond the lesson hour and prices accordingly, which is reasonable and worth paying for. We will not quote a city-wide figure, because the same request costs differently in Cuffe Parade and in Airoli. Ask any tutor to explain her rate in terms of these factors before agreeing to it.

faqs.question: Will the tutor come to our building in Mulund, and what about parking?
faqs.answer: Yes, and settle the gate and parking question in week one rather than week five. Most Mulund and Bhandup societies prefer a tutor registered as a standing weekly visitor, with the name and slot left at the security desk once, instead of a fresh entry every time. Where visitor parking is limited, a tutor arriving by the Central Line to Mulund station and taking a short auto often keeps better time than one driving on the Eastern Express Highway. Ten minutes lost at a gate each week is a lesson lost every term.

faqs.question: Does online Hindi tuition work when the subject needs handwriting?
faqs.answer: Partly, and only with one discipline in place. Your child photographs each written piece and sends it before the lesson, so the tutor marks the script in advance and the session goes on corrections rather than on reading aloud. Reading comprehension, listening and prepared speaking all work well on a screen. What online cannot do is watch the pen move, which is where matra placement and speed are actually fixed. Most families here use one home tuition visit for writing and one short online slot mid-week.

faqs.question: We are switching from Marathi to Hindi. Can a tutor catch her up?
faqs.answer: Usually, but check with the school first whether the switch is still permitted for her year, and get the answer in writing. The academic catch-up is mostly script conventions and text types rather than vocabulary, since a child in Mumbai arrives with plenty of spoken Hindi. Expect a concentrated first term on formal writing. Ask for a tutor who has taken a student through exactly this switch, because the sequence she uses matters more than her fluency, and tell us at the outset so the shortlist reflects it.

sections.heading: What we need before we can shortlist a History tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: History is the subject where a bad match looks fine for two months. So the request we need is specific: the programme year, the level, the prescribed subject for the source paper if the school has told you, the two world history topics, the Higher Level (HL) regional option if applicable, and one marked essay or source answer.

Then the order of work is fixed. 1. We confirm the level, because the HL regional option is a separate body of content and a separate essay style. 2. We check the topics against who in our pool has actually taught them. 3. We read the marked work to locate the problem, which is usually argument structure rather than knowledge. 4. sections.heading: IGCSE History, DP Standard Level or Higher Level: which is it?
paragraphs: Three distinct courses, and the answer is on the school's subject registration rather than in the textbook. IGCSE History runs as an options-based course with source work and a depth study, varying by board and by school. Diploma Programme (DP) History runs at Standard Level (SL) and Higher Level (HL), sharing the source paper and the world history essays, with Higher Level adding a regional option and its own longer essay paper. Middle Years Programme (MYP) students meet the groundwork inside Individuals and Societies, without the formal assessment structure.

The level is the easy part. The harder and more useful question is which content your child is actually sitting, because the board publishes a menu and the department picks from it. One school in Bandra and one in Chembur can both teach DP History and share almost no material. Ask the Individuals and Societies head or the Diploma coordinator for the prescribed subject, the two world history topics and, for HL, the regional option, in writing. Then check the current subject guide for how the components are structured in your child's session, since guides are revised on the board's own cycle.

Tuition looks different at each stage. MYP work is about building the habit of using evidence and asking where a source came from. IGCSE work needs breadth, source technique and tight paragraph discipline. DP Standard Level work is argument-led: fewer topics, deeper evidence, stricter command-term reading. Higher Level adds the regional option, where essays are longer, examples must be more specific and some awareness of competing historical interpretations is expected. A tutor comfortable at IGCSE is not automatically comfortable with an HL regional essay, and we ask directly rather than assuming.

Our DP History pages carry the format-specific detail for DP1 and DP2, including the home and online variants, so this page stays board-wide on purpose. A home tutor for History Mumbai families book through us is matched to the course and the topics first. Everything else, the evening, the format, the length of the session, is arranged after that, because the wrong content expertise cannot be fixed by a convenient slot.

sections.heading: The source paper, the essay papers and the historical investigation
paragraphs: The source paper is the component students can be taught to pass quickly, and the one most schools rush. It presents a small set of sources on the prescribed subject and asks a predictable sequence: say what a source conveys, compare and contrast two of them, assess the value and limitations of one with reference to its origin, purpose and content, and then write a short essay using the sources alongside your own knowledge. The question types repeat session after session. A student who has drilled them arrives knowing the shape of every question before reading a word.

The world history essays are a different skill. Here the candidate answers on topics chosen by the department, drawing examples from more than one region, and the marks sit in the structure: a thesis that answers the question asked, paragraphs that each carry a dated and named example, a counter-argument taken seriously rather than dismissed in a clause, and a conclusion that commits. Chronological narration scores badly no matter how accurate it is. The examiner is not checking whether your child knows the story.

Higher Level candidates also sit the regional option paper, where essays run longer and examples need more precision. Awareness that historians disagree, and why, starts to earn credit at this level, which catches out students who learned one account and treat it as the account. This is also the paper most often reached last in the school's teaching order, so HL students regularly arrive at the final term with the least practice on the component that asks the most.

The historical investigation is the student's own research question, with a section evaluating the sources chosen, the investigation itself, and a reflection on what doing the work revealed about the discipline. It carries a meaningful share of the final mark, and you should get the current figure and word limits from the subject guide or the school's coordinator rather than from any revision site, because these details change between cycles. A good IB history tutor in Mumbai spends the early sessions narrowing the question, since a question that is too broad is the most common reason the whole piece underperforms.

That changes the geography, because a tutor can fit fewer long blocks into an evening than short ones, so the travel they will accept is shorter. Across Mumbai, Maharashtra, this is the constraint that decides who we can actually send you.

In South Mumbai we match inside the island: Colaba, Fort, Churchgate, Grant Road, Mumbai Central, Worli, Prabhadevi, Parel and Mahalaxmi. The distances are small and the evening signals at Peddar Road and Haji Ali are not, and Metro Line 3 and the Coastal Road have helped some routes without helping all of them. sections.heading: Who chooses the topics your child is examined on?
paragraphs: The department does, not the student and not the board. The board publishes a menu of prescribed subjects, world history topics and regional options, and each school picks a combination that suits its teachers. This is the most practically important fact on this page, because it means two DP History students in the same tuition group can need almost entirely different material, and it means a tutor must be matched to a combination rather than to a subject name.

Ask for three documents in June: the internal assessment schedule, the list of topics being taught this year, and the mock timetable. Hand all three to the tutor in the first session. The Mumbai school year runs from June to March or April, and History students feel the squeeze twice, once when the investigation draft lands alongside other internally assessed work in the autumn, and again when mocks arrive in December or January while the regional option is still being taught. Monsoon weeks in July and August cost evening visits in Chembur and along Ghodbunder Road, so build a weekend catch-up into the arrangement.

Timing also decides what tuition can be. Starting IB home tuition in Mumbai in June means the investigation question can be chosen carefully and the source paper drilled slowly across months.
