sections.heading: Starting IB home tuition in Mumbai in any month of the year
paragraphs: You can start in any month, and the month only changes what the first four sessions are for. Starting in June, the first sessions are diagnostic and unhurried. Starting in September, they run alongside the first IA topic decisions. Starting in January, the first session is a calendar exercise before it is a teaching one. Starting in April, the tutor's job is rehearsal and pacing. Tell us the month and we will tell you honestly what the realistic goal is, including when the realistic goal is smaller than you hoped.

To make the first session useful, have four things ready. The school's assessment calendar for the term. The last two pieces of marked work, with the teacher's comments still on them. The subject list with levels, written as the school writes them, including HL and SL or Core and Extended. And one sentence from the student, in their own words, about what they find hardest. That last one is the most useful document in the pile and takes two minutes to produce.

The first session itself is a baseline. The tutor works through the marked work, asks the student to attempt one task unaided, identifies the gap between what the class has covered and what the student can do, and leaves with a plan for the next three sessions tied to the dates on the school calendar. No new syllabus content is taught in the first hour, which occasionally disappoints parents and almost always pays for itself by week three.

Most of these enquiries start as IB tutors near me Mumbai and end up being a question about travel and timing. So tell us the zone, whether it is Powai or Kharghar or Walkeshwar, and the two evenings that actually work in your week. We will match inside your corridor, send profiles with board, programme, subject and level stated, and if the match is not right after a fortnight we will change it. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school or examination board, and we do not guarantee grades.
bullets: Have the school assessment calendar and two pieces of marked work ready
Write subjects exactly as the school does, with HL, SL, Core or Extended
Ask the student for one sentence on what they find hardest
The first session is a baseline, not a syllabus lesson
Name two evenings that genuinely work before you name a preferred tutor

faqs.question: When in the IB year is the best time to start home tuition?
faqs.answer: June or July, in the gap between academic years. Supply of experienced tutors is loosest then, there is no deadline pressing, and a tutor can spend the first three sessions diagnosing gaps rather than firefighting. A June start also means the tutor already has a gate pass and a travel routine before the monsoon and before the term rhythm sets in August. Every other month still has a sensible version of the same work: September is for IA topic selection, December for the Extended Essay draft, January for sequencing colliding deadlines, March for timed papers. The only month where expectations have to shrink sharply is April, because study leave is for rehearsal, not new content.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees depend on if you will not quote a price?
faqs.answer: IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on five things, and quoting a single figure would be misleading because any of them can double the rate. Board and level: Higher Level Diploma Programme subjects cost more than IGCSE Core. Subject scarcity: Higher Level Chemistry, Design Technology or a second language has a smaller pool than Maths. Travel distance and direction: an hour each way across the Western Express Highway is an hour the tutor is not teaching, and it is priced in. Session length and frequency, since a weekly ninety-minute slot and two short sessions cost differently. And the month, because February demand is not June demand. Ask each tutor to quote per session, including travel, in writing.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start in January of DP2?
faqs.answer: No, but the job changes from teaching to triage and you should expect a different conversation. In January the mocks, final Internal Assessment submissions and the Theory of Knowledge essay fall inside the same few weeks, so the first useful hour is usually spent building a realistic calendar: which deadline is immovable, which draft is good enough to submit, what gets consciously dropped. Content gaps that are still open get managed rather than closed. What a January start cannot do is recover a weak Internal Assessment topic chosen in October or produce Extended Essay research that never happened. Be clear with the tutor that the goal is protecting the grade, not transforming it.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our building on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if the building is inside the tutor's zone or on one corridor. The honest constraint is direction and hour. A tutor living near Thane station will take a seven o'clock slot in Majiwada without complaint and will quietly start rescheduling a Kasarvadavali slot once the Ghodbunder Road evening run adds forty minutes. The same is true of Peddar Road and Haji Ali in South Mumbai, and of the Bandra to Andheri stretch at six. Give us two workable evenings rather than one, and accept a tutor from your own corridor over a slightly stronger profile from across the city. The corridor match is what survives February.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, but be at home for the first two. You are not supervising the teaching; you are checking that the tutor asks questions rather than lecturing, that the student is writing, and that the arrangement feels right in your own home. After that, a parent in the next room is enough and often better, because teenagers perform differently with an audience. What does need a parent long-term is the practical layer: a reliable table with a light, no television in earshot, phones left in another room, and someone who notices when two sessions in a row end early.

faqs.question: Our society requires a visitor pass every week. How does that work?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once as a recurring visitor rather than getting a pass issued each week. Most managed complexes in Powai, Kharghar, Mulund West and Thane will add a named tutor to a standing weekly entry list if a resident requests it in writing, and some ask for an identity document copy. Do this in the first week, not the fourth. It matters most in February, when many societies tighten visitor entry during examination weeks and a tutor who started in August already has a record at the gate while a tutor who started in January does not. Ask your tutor for the identity document the profile references and hand that copy to the office.

faqs.question: What happens to a home session when the monsoon shuts the roads?
faqs.answer: It becomes an online session, which is why the online fallback should be agreed in June rather than improvised in July. A waterlogged Milan subway, a halted Harbour Line or a blocked stretch of the Eastern Express Highway cancels a session nobody wanted to cancel, and the sessions lost in late June and July are the foundation sessions that are hardest to make up later. Agree three things at the start: that the tutor will call by a fixed hour if travel is impossible, that the session runs online instead at the same time, and how a genuinely missed session is rescheduled. Put it in the first message, not the first crisis.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the evidence before you change the tutor, because at four weeks you should be looking for process rather than marks. Specifically: is there written work that has been marked against named criteria, can the student state what they are working on and why, and has the panic about one named topic reduced. If all three are missing, the problem is the match. If the written work exists and is marked but class test scores have not moved, that is normal at four weeks and often normal at eight. Grade movement follows process by a term, and we do not guarantee grades at any horizon.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out. How does a replacement happen?
faqs.answer: Tell us what specifically is wrong and we arrange a different profile; you are not locked in for a term. The useful detail is not that it is not working but which part: the subject depth, the level, the hour, the travel reliability, or the fact that two people simply do not get along. Each one points at a different replacement. We also ask the outgoing tutor for a short handover of what has been covered, so the new tutor does not spend two sessions re-diagnosing. Changing tutors costs roughly a fortnight of momentum, which is cheap in September and expensive in February.

faqs.question: Does online tuition genuinely work for IB subjects?
faqs.answer: It works well for some jobs and poorly for others, and the split is predictable. Online is strong for short doubt sessions before a test, past-paper walkthroughs, Theory of Knowledge and essay-subject discussion, and any scarce Higher Level subject where the alternative is no specialist at all. It is weaker for early diagnosis, for students who need somebody physically present to start work, and for Maths at the stage where the tutor must watch the hand move across the page. Two conditions make online work: a camera angled at the paper, and a parent who enforces that angle for the first fortnight. Without them it drifts into conversation.

faqs.question: What should a tutor be doing during study leave in April?
faqs.answer: Running timed papers, marking against the published mark scheme, and protecting sleep. April is rehearsal. A tutor should be setting full sections under the clock, reading command terms aloud until the student reacts to them automatically, drilling the two or three highest-yield topics per paper, and mapping the week against the actual examination timetable. A tutor should not be introducing a new topic, starting a new textbook, or stacking extra hours that displace rest. If somebody proposes covering untaught content in April, that is a sign the calendar went wrong in September, and the right response is to triage rather than accelerate.

faqs.question: We are sitting the November session. Does the same plan apply?
faqs.answer: Yes, shifted by about six months, and the sequence matters more than the dates. For a November candidate the diagnostic window is December and January, Internal Assessment work runs February to May, the collision of mocks, final submissions and the Theory of Knowledge essay lands in July and August, technique work belongs in September, and October is study leave. Retake candidates have a narrower version again, often one or two papers with a fixed weakness and a short runway, where the honest plan is concentrated technique work rather than re-teaching a full syllabus. Tell us the session month in the first message so the shortlist is built around the right calendar.

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches a second child in Mumbai when the first child's tutor does not fit
paragraphs: A request for a second child reads nothing like a first request. The parent already knows what Higher Level (HL) means, already knows that an Internal Assessment (IA) has a deadline the school sets rather than the International Baccalaureate (IB), and usually opens with a sentence like: we want the same person we had for our elder son. Sometimes that works. More often it does not, because whatever made that tutor effective was specific to one child, in one year, in one programme. So the first conversation about a second child is mostly a conversation about the first child. What did the elder one actually need. What did the tutor do that moved anything. What would you change if you were starting over. Parents answer those three questions quickly and precisely, and the answers change the shortlist more than the subject does.

The process from there is short and it does not vary by zone. 1. You tell us the child, the year group, the board and the two or three things going wrong, plus whatever the elder child's arrangement taught you. 2. We ask for the most recent school report or the current predicted grades, and the weekly timetable including sport, music and anything else already fixed. 3. We shortlist tutors who have taught that exact year and that exact component, filtered first by the corridor you live on rather than by the whole city. 4. You speak to the shortlist yourself and ask the questions your first experience taught you to ask. 5. The first paid session is a diagnostic, and the tutor sends you a short written plan after it, naming what they will start with and why.

The shortlist for a younger sibling is rarely the shortlist you saw the first time, and that surprises people. Pools differ sharply by subject and by year. An IB private tutor in Mumbai who teaches Diploma Programme (DP) Economics HL comes from a small group who have taught or marked that course, and most of them have their weekday evening slots filled by September. IGCSE Maths Extended in Year 10 has a far wider pool running from Bandra up to Dahisar East and across to Thane, so you get real choice of personality and timing. If both your children need the scarce end of the market in the same term, the honest answer is that one of them is getting a Saturday morning, and it is usually better to give the Saturday to the child who is not sitting exams that year.

One practical thing changes the second time: we ask your permission to read what the previous tutor wrote. If the elder child's tutor kept a running note of topics covered, past papers attempted and recurring errors, that note is worth more to the incoming tutor than any report card. Families who keep it save themselves roughly a fortnight of a new tutor working out what is already known. Families who do not keep it pay for that fortnight twice when the third child comes along.
bullets: We start by asking what the elder child's tutor did that actually worked

sections.heading: MYP, DP and IGCSE under one roof: what changes between your children
paragraphs: Two children in the same flat can be sitting in two different assessment systems, and a parent who learned one system thoroughly with the elder child often finds the younger one's school reports unreadable. The IB ladder runs Primary Years Programme (PYP) in the early years, then MYP from roughly Year 6 to Year 10, then the two-year Diploma Programme. MYP is criteria based: every subject reports against criteria A to D, each criterion carries its own eight-point scale, and the teacher applies task-specific clarifications that change from unit to unit. IGCSE, offered by Cambridge International Education and by Pearson Edexcel, works differently. It reports a single grade per subject against thresholds that shift slightly each session, and its feedback is terse by comparison. A parent fluent in criterion language reads an IGCSE mock report and sees almost nothing actionable in it.

That mismatch is the ordinary condition of a Mumbai household with children three or four years apart. A Year 9 child at an IGCSE school and a DP2 child at an IB school are living in different weeks. The Year 9 child has end-of-unit tests and a long runway. The DP2 child has IA deadlines, a Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay, an Extended Essay (EE) and the May session fixed in the calendar whether anyone is ready or not. Parents who run both at once learn to stop comparing. The question is not which child is doing better; the two scales do not convert. The question is whether each child is where their own programme expects them to be at that point in its cycle.

Board changes mid-school add a third layer. It is common in this city for a family to keep the elder child on an IGCSE pathway through Year 11 and then move them into DP, while the younger child stays on a straight PYP to MYP to DP route inside one school. Those two children need different things from a tutor. The one who crossed over needs translation work: what a markband expects compared with a mark scheme, how an IA differs from coursework, why an examiner rewards a stated limitation. The one who never left the IB system needs nothing of the sort and will be bored by it. Running all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai across one household therefore means running two curricula in parallel, not one curriculum twice.

There is one structural decision worth taking early with each child separately rather than copying from the elder. In IGCSE, the Core and Extended split in Maths and the tiered papers in some Sciences decide which grades are even reachable. In DP, the three HL and three SL choices decide how heavy the IA load sits in DP1. A family that put the elder child on Extended Maths because they could cope with it should still run the Core and Extended conversation again for the younger one, with that child's own Year 9 marks in front of them.
bullets: MYP reports criteria A to D; IGCSE reports one grade against shifting thresholds
Two children on two boards are living in two different assessment weeks
A child who crossed from IGCSE into DP needs explicit translation work
Core versus Extended should be decided per child, not copied from a sibling
HL and SL choices in DP1 set how heavy the IA load becomes

sections.heading: Subject choice across both boards, and the internal assessments each child carries
paragraphs: Subject choice is where families most often repeat a mistake, because the elder child's combination looks like a proven template. It is not. Each subject carries its own internal assessment with its own shape, and the load those pieces create depends entirely on the child holding them. DP Mathematics carries an exploration, a piece of independent mathematical writing that defeats confident calculators who have never had to pose their own question. The experimental sciences each carry a scientific investigation with its own data and error analysis. DP Economics carries commentaries built on real published articles. History carries an IA with its own source evaluation section. Language A carries written work and, at HL, an essay on a literary text. Business Management carries a research project. On top of all of that sit the EE and TOK, which belong to no single subject and therefore get postponed by nearly everyone.

On the IGCSE side the equivalent pressure is coursework and the practical components. Depending on the subject and the school's option, a child may face a Paper 1 multiple-choice component, a structured Paper 2, an extended-response Paper 4 and then either a practical exam or the alternative-to-practical paper that tests the same skills on paper. Those components reward quite different habits. A child who revises by rereading notes can survive a recall-heavy paper and then lose a grade on the extended-response component because nobody taught them how to answer a six-mark question. A tutor who has actually taught that paper knows this and starts with command words rather than content.

This is why there is no one all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Mumbai who can carry two children through two different years. The claim gets made, and it collapses the moment one child needs an IA sign-off conversation in the same fortnight that the other needs drilling on IGCSE Chemistry mole calculations. What a household can realistically run is one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai at the lower years, where a strong Maths and Science generalist genuinely covers MYP 2 and MYP 3 work, and then separate specialists once either child reaches Year 10 or DP1. The honest line between those two situations usually falls at the point where the child's own subject teachers start giving component-specific feedback.

A worked example makes the difference concrete. A DP1 child taking Physics HL has to choose an investigation topic, and the usual failure is choosing something with no controllable variable, which caps the methodology marks before any data is collected. A good tutor kills that idea in week one and pushes the child toward something measurable with school equipment. Meanwhile the younger sibling in Year 10 IGCSE Physics needs none of this. They need to stop losing marks on units and significant figures. Same subject name, two completely different pieces of work, and no reason to expect one person to be the right fit for both.
bullets: Every DP subject carries its own internal assessment with its own failure mode
The EE and TOK belong to no subject, so both get postponed
IGCSE papers reward command words as much as content knowledge
One generalist can cover MYP 2 and MYP 3 for both children
Specialists become necessary once a child reaches Year 10 or DP1
Do not copy the elder child's subject combination onto the younger one

sections.heading: Where home tuitions run across Mumbai, zone by zone
paragraphs: IB home tuitions in Mumbai are matched by corridor, not by postcode, and with two or three children the corridor logic gets strict. South Mumbai, in Mumbai, Maharashtra, is dense and short-distance but slow: Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Peddar Road, Walkeshwar, Tardeo, Babulnath and Worli are all within a few kilometres of each other, yet a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba in the evening peak loses time at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals. Tutors here are matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs, using the Western Line from Churchgate to Mumbai Central, the Harbour Line through Dockyard and Sewri, Metro Line 3 from Cuffe Parade towards BKC, and the Coastal Road. A family in Walkeshwar with one child in Fort and another in Parel is still one trip for one tutor, which is why island households get the easiest two-child scheduling in the city.

The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, so the only sane rule is to match along the line rather than across it: Khar West to Santacruz, Juhu to Andheri West, Malad to Kandivali East, Borivali to Dahisar East. Metro Line 1 across Versova, Andheri and Ghatkopar and Metro Lines 2A and 7 from Dahisar to Gundavali have made some of these hops predictable in a way the Link Road never was. In the Central Suburbs, Powai and Chandivali hang off the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road (JVLR) with no station of their own, so tutors reach them by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, while Kurla and Mulund sit directly on the Central Line and the Santacruz Chembur Link Road (SCLR) ties the two sides together.

The Eastern Suburbs stretch from Chembur and Govandi up through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund, served by the Central and Harbour lines, the Eastern Express Highway and the Eastern Freeway, which puts Wadala and Chembur closer to South Mumbai than the map suggests. Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, so Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel each sit a short drive from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway, with the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines, the Belapur to Pendhar metro and the Atal Setu linking them outward. Thane spreads west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road, and Ghodbunder sets the whole schedule: a tutor living near the station reaches Kasarvadavali quickly off-peak and slowly in the evening.

Searches like IB tutors near me in Mumbai make more sense once you have two children in two schools in two different directions. The common Mumbai pattern is one child in a Bandra or BKC school and the younger one still in a neighbourhood school closer to home, which means the family's own travel is already split. Adding a tutor who crosses the Bandra Worli Sea Link twice a week on top of that rarely survives the monsoon. The arrangements that last a full term are the ones where the tutor's own commute is short and dull. A Powai tutor for a Powai household, a Nerul tutor for a Nerul household, a Thane West tutor who does not have to cross Ghodbunder Road in the evening.
bullets: South Mumbai households get the easiest two-child scheduling in the city
Match along the Western Line, not across it, from Khar West to Dahisar East

The Eastern Freeway makes Chembur and Wadala quicker to reach than expected
Navi Mumbai works node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar, Panvel

sections.heading: Why the Mumbai school calendar hits two children in different years at different times
paragraphs: The academic year in most IB and IGCSE schools here starts in June, and the pressure points are fixed enough to plan around. The first real assessments land in October and November. December brings a break that families either use or waste. January and February are mock season for DP2 and for Year 11, and they are also when IA deadlines cluster, because schools want final drafts in hand before study leave. March and April take the DP2 and Year 11 cohorts into the May session and the IGCSE series. May and early June are quiet for the exam years and are the single best window to start anything with a younger child, because the tutors who were full all winter suddenly have weekday evenings free.

With two children the calendar collides rather than repeats. A family with a DP2 child at Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC and a Year 10 child at Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai will hit February with one child finishing a Physics IA and a TOK essay in the same fortnight and the other sitting pre-mock tests. The household cannot give both children the quiet table, the undisturbed evening and the parent attention in that fortnight. Deciding in December which child gets priority in February is a far better conversation than discovering the clash in the week it arrives. Usually the exam-year child gets the February evenings and the younger one gets a heavier June and July.

School calendars vary enough that the detail matters. Families across the city deal with assessment rhythms set by the American School of Bombay and Ascend International School in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School, Jamnabai Narsee International School and Utpal Shanghvi Global School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off JVLR in Goregaon East, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Activity High School on Peddar Road, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, NES International School in Mulund West, the JBCN International School campuses at Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul. Naming them is context about what a tutor must work around, nothing more.

To be explicit about that: IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, nor with the IB organisation, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. We do not hold school calendars, we do not negotiate deadlines, and we cannot get an extension for an IA. What a tutor can do is read the school's published assessment schedule with you in the first session and work backwards from it, which is more useful than it sounds when two children's schedules are competing for the same fortnight.
bullets: June start, October and November first assessments, December break
January and February are mock season and IA deadline season together
May and early June are the easiest months to start with a younger child
Decide in December which child gets priority in February
IB Gram is independent and not affiliated with any school named here

sections.heading: Should the second child have home tuition or online lessons in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Start the younger child at home and move them online only if the timetable forces it. IB home tuitions in Mumbai give a tutor things no screen provides: the child's actual handwriting under time pressure, the state of their folder, whether the younger sibling is working at the dining table with the television on, and whether the elder child's old notes are being used or ignored. For a child in MYP or early IGCSE, those physical signals are most of the diagnosis.

Online earns its place for narrow, specific reasons, and in a two-child household those reasons appear often. The scarce DP subjects are the clearest case. If the only person who has taught DP Economics HL properly is in Thane and you are in Cuffe Parade, an IB online tutor in Mumbai beats a mediocre tutor who can reach your door. Online also solves the slot collision that two children create: when both need Tuesday at six and only one tutor can be in the flat, the elder child takes the screen in the bedroom and the younger keeps the table. Online holds up better for DP work, where the material is abstract and screen sharing a marked draft is genuinely efficient, and worse for younger children, where attention leaks within twenty minutes and nobody notices the phone under the desk.

Hybrid is what most multi-child families settle into after a term, and it is worth planning rather than drifting into. The usual shape is one session at home each week for the work that needs watching, and one online session for drill, doubt clearing or a draft review. The monsoon makes this close to compulsory: in July and August the home slot is the one that gets cancelled, and having an agreed online fallback means the week is not simply lost. Families on Ghodbunder Road, along the Sion Panvel Highway and anywhere dependent on the Western Express Highway in the evening should assume at least a few weather cancellations each year and decide in advance what happens to those hours.

The trade-off nobody mentions is supervision load. Home sessions supervise themselves because an adult is in the next room. Online sessions transfer that job to you, and with two children on two screens in a two-bedroom flat the arrangement that looks cheaper in travel terms costs you more in attention. If you are going to run both children online on the same evening, put them in different rooms, keep the doors open and accept that the first fortnight needs you present rather than nearby.
bullets: Begin the younger child at home; move online only if the timetable demands it
Online wins when the right specialist lives on the wrong side of the city
DP material survives a screen better than MYP or early IGCSE work does
Hybrid: one home session for watching, one online for drill and drafts
Agree a monsoon fallback before July cancels your first home slot
Two children online on one evening need two rooms and your attention

sections.heading: What should a Mumbai family check again before hiring a second tutor?
paragraphs: Check everything again, including the things you checked last time, because the tutor is different even if the agency is not. Second and third rounds of IB home tuitions in Mumbai get the same checks as the first, and before a new IB home tutor in Mumbai starts in your flat, IB Gram verifies government photo identity, the degree or teaching qualification claimed, and a teaching history that names the specific board, programme level and components the tutor says they have taught. We ask for references from families whose children sat the same course, not just any families. Where a tutor has worked in a school we confirm the role rather than accepting a title. None of this certifies teaching quality, and we say so plainly: it rules out the easy failures.

The checks you run yourself are the ones that actually decide it, and the second time around you know what to ask. Give the tutor a past-paper question from your child's current unit and ask them to mark a real answer in front of you, out loud, saying where the marks went and why. A specialist does this immediately and talks about command words and markbands. A generalist talks about the topic. Ask what they would do in the first three weeks and listen for whether the answer is specific to your child's year and component or could apply to anyone. Ask directly how many DP2 or Year 11 students they are already carrying through this exam cycle, because an honest answer about capacity tells you whether your February will be covered.

Handover between tutors is the step families skip and then regret. When a tutor finishes with one child or is replaced, ask for a closing note: topics covered, past papers attempted with dates, recurring errors, what was deliberately left undone, and the current standing with the school's own teacher. Keep it in the same place you keep report cards. When the younger child reaches that year, or when a tutor changes mid-course, the incoming tutor reads it in ten minutes and starts from a real position instead of a guessed one. Families who have kept these notes across two children tell us the third arrangement was the easiest one they ever set up, and that is the whole argument for keeping them.

One more check belongs to the household rather than the tutor. If a tutor is going to come weekly for two children, sort out building access properly on day one: the society gate register, the visitor pass, whether security needs a standing entry for a recurring slot, and which lift the tutor is allowed to use. In larger complexes a tutor turned away at the gate once will quietly stop prioritising your slot, and nobody will tell you that is what happened.
bullets: Identity, qualification and component-specific teaching history are verified
References come from families whose children sat the same course
Ask the tutor to mark one real past-paper answer aloud in front of you
Ask how many exam-year students they already carry this cycle
Get a closing handover note: topics, papers, recurring errors, what was skipped
Fix society gate access and a standing visitor pass in the first week

sections.heading: What a family learns the second time around and should have known the first
paragraphs: What families get wrong about IB home tuitions in Mumbai the first time is almost always the same thing: they buy a subject when they needed a diagnosis. The elder child is weak in Maths, so a Maths tutor is hired, and six weeks later the marks have not moved because the problem was never Maths. It was that the child could not produce written work to a deadline, or had no reading stamina for a long source question, or had quietly stopped understanding something two years earlier. By the second child, parents start asking a different first question: what exactly is going wrong, in which component, with which kind of task. That question gets you a different tutor, and it gets you one sooner.

The second lesson is about money, and it is worth being precise because there is no price list that would be honest. IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on the board and level, since DP HL and a Year 11 exam-year course sit above MYP work; on subject scarcity, since the pool for DP Economics HL or Further Maths is thin and the pool for IGCSE Maths is wide; on travel distance and the time the tutor loses getting to you, which is why cross-city matches cost more and hold worse; on session length and weekly frequency; and on when you book, since a tutor with no winter slots left prices differently from one you approach in May. With two children the only reliable saving is a shared corridor and a shared evening, not a shared tutor.

The third lesson is the one nobody warns parents about. Running tuition for two or three children is a budget of time and attention, not of money. Each weekly session consumes a quiet room, an adult in the house, a child who is not being taken somewhere else, and one slot of your own evening attention for the five-minute debrief afterwards that actually makes the session worth paying for. Three children at two sessions a week each is six evenings of that, which no household has. Families who make this work do two things. They put siblings back to back in one evening wherever the subjects allow, so one tutor visit covers two children and one lift journey. And they accept that the child who is not in an exam year takes a thinner schedule for a term, by decision rather than by accident.

The fourth lesson is to stop treating the elder child's outcome as evidence. The elder child did well and so the approach must be right; the elder child struggled and so tuition does not work. Neither conclusion holds. Parents also ask who the best IB tutor in Mumbai is, and the honest answer is that the question has no single answer across two children, because the variable that matters is fit between one tutor's way of explaining and one child's way of getting stuck. The useful version of the question is narrower: who has taught this exact component, to this year group, close enough to reach us on a weekday, and can they still take a student this term.

The real constraint with two or three children is evenings, not rupees
Back-to-back sibling sessions save one tutor visit and one lift journey

sections.heading: When does keeping the same home tutor across several years stop helping?
paragraphs: Continuity is worth a great deal and then, at a specific point, it stops being worth anything. An IB home tutor in Mumbai who stays with a child from MYP 3 through MYP 5 builds something a new tutor cannot buy: they know which topics were faked, which habits were never fixed, and what this particular child does when they are embarrassed about not understanding. That knowledge compounds. It is why the second and third year of a good arrangement are usually better than the first, and why we encourage families to keep a tutor through the MYP years even when progress in a given term is flat.

The point where it changes is DP1. The Diploma Programme asks for something the MYP years did not: independent written work, an argument the student owns, a tolerance for being told a draft is not good enough yet. A tutor who has been kind and encouraging to a child since Year 7 sometimes cannot deliver that message, and the child cannot hear it from them. This is the most common reason a family that is happy with a tutor should still change, and it feels disloyal, which is why it gets postponed. The signal to watch for is a student who is comfortable in sessions and not improving between them. If your child's tutor has become a safe place rather than a demanding one, DP is when that costs a grade. What worked in Year 9 rarely works unchanged in Year 12.

The honest version of progress has three horizons. At four weeks you should see process, not marks: homework being started earlier, past papers being attempted in timed conditions, the child able to say what a question is asking before answering it. At one term you should see marks on school assessments in the specific components that were targeted, plus a change in the tutor's own account of what is still weak. At one exam cycle you should see whether the gap between predicted and actual narrowed. If nothing has moved by the end of the first term, something is wrong with the match or with the diagnosis, and continuing on hope is the expensive choice. We do not guarantee grades, and anyone in this city who does is selling you something they cannot deliver.

Changing a tutor for one child does not have to disturb the other. Tell us what is not working in specific terms: the child is not doing the work set, the explanations are not landing, the slot keeps moving, the tutor is strong on content and weak on exam technique. We ask the outgoing tutor for the closing note, shortlist again against what you have just learned, and leave the other child's arrangement exactly where it is. Families sometimes assume both children have to move together out of fairness. They do not, and doing so usually breaks the arrangement that was working.
bullets: Continuity compounds through the MYP years and is worth keeping
DP1 is where a comfortable long-standing tutor can become the wrong one
Watch for a child comfortable in sessions but not improving between them
Four weeks shows process, one term shows marks, one cycle shows the gap
We do not guarantee grades, and no honest platform in Mumbai does
Replacing one child's tutor leaves the other child's arrangement untouched

sections.heading: Starting IB home tuitions in Mumbai for more than one child
paragraphs: Send one enquiry for the household rather than one per child, and say plainly that there are two or three of them. It changes the shortlist immediately, because we then look for tutors whose travel and slots can serve the whole family rather than optimising for one child and discovering the clash later. Tell us each child's year group and board, the subjects and components in question, the evenings and weekend mornings that are genuinely free once sport and music are counted, your building and the nearest station or road, and what you learned from any previous arrangement including what you would not repeat.

What to have ready for the first session is short. For each child: the most recent school report or predicted grades, the school's published assessment schedule if you have it, the current unit or topic list, one recent piece of marked work with the teacher's comments still on it, and any closing note from a previous tutor. The marked work does more than the report card, because a diagnostic session is built on seeing how the child loses marks rather than being told that they do.

The first session itself is a diagnosis, not a lesson, and it will look slower than you expect. The tutor works through the marked piece with the child, sets one or two timed questions, and establishes where the actual break is. They should then tell you, in plain language, what they are starting with, what they are deliberately leaving for later, and what they need from the household: a table, a quiet hour, a parent in the house for the younger child, a standing gate pass. If a tutor finishes a first session without telling you those things, ask before the second one is booked.

After that, the rhythm is weekly sessions with a short debrief, a review at four weeks against the plan the tutor wrote, and a decision at the end of the term about whether to continue, change the focus or change the tutor. For a family running two or three children through IB and IGCSE years, that review is the single habit that matters most, because it is what stops a flat arrangement drifting for two more terms. Bring both children's reviews to the same conversation and you will usually find one obvious reallocation of evenings staring at you.
bullets: Send one enquiry for the household and name every child in it
List the evenings genuinely free after sport and music are counted
Bring one recent marked piece per child, comments still attached
The first session diagnoses; expect it to feel slower than a lesson

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both my children at home in the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the subjects and year groups are close enough that one person genuinely covers both. Back-to-back sibling sessions work well for MYP Maths and Science, or for two children both in early IGCSE, and they save a travel trip and an evening. They stop working once one child reaches DP1 or Year 11, because the component knowledge required diverges and you end up with a specialist for one child and a compromise for the other. Where the subjects do not allow it, the usual answer is one tutor at home for the younger child and an online specialist for the elder in a different room.

faqs.question: My elder child's tutor was excellent. Why would they not suit my younger one?
faqs.answer: Because fit is between one tutor's way of explaining and one child's way of getting stuck, and siblings get stuck differently. A tutor who was patient and structured can be exactly wrong for a quick child who needs pushing, and a demanding tutor who turned around a drifting DP2 student can flatten a nervous Year 9. The year group matters as much as the personality: someone outstanding on DP Maths HL may not have taught MYP in years. Try them if you want, but treat the first session as a real diagnostic rather than a formality, and be willing to change.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on when two children are studying?
faqs.answer: They depend on board and level, subject scarcity, travel distance, session length and frequency, and when in the year you book. We do not publish a price list, because an honest one would need all of those variables. With two children, the saving that actually exists comes from shared logistics rather than a bulk rate: one tutor travelling once for two back-to-back sessions, both children on the same evening, and a tutor whose own commute is short. Cross-city matches cost more and hold worse. Booking in May or June, when exam-year demand has cleared, usually gives you more choice than booking in November.

faqs.question: How do records get handed over when we change tutors between years?
faqs.answer: Ask the outgoing tutor for a closing note and keep it with your child's reports. It should list topics covered, past papers attempted with dates, the errors that kept recurring, what was deliberately left undone, and where the child stands with their own school teacher. We ask for this whenever a tutor finishes or is replaced, and we pass it to the incoming tutor with your permission. A new tutor who reads that note starts from a real position in the first session instead of spending two weeks rediscovering it, and the same note is useful again when a younger sibling reaches that year.

faqs.question: We live in Kasarvadavali on Ghodbunder Road. Will a tutor come on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor is based in Thane rather than travelling from Mumbai's western suburbs. Ghodbunder Road decides this: a tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali quickly off-peak and slowly in the evening peak, and a tutor coming from Borivali or Mulund will quietly start arriving late by the second month. We match Thane households to Thane tutors, with Mulund tutors as the occasional exception on the Eastern Express Highway side. For a scarce DP subject where no local specialist exists, online is the arrangement that survives the monsoon, and most families here end up hybrid.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: At four weeks you should be looking for process rather than marks, so check that first. Is homework being started earlier, are past papers being attempted under time, can the child say what a question is asking before answering it? If none of that has changed, raise it with the tutor directly and ask what they think the actual break is. If the answer is vague or still the same as the first session, change the tutor. Marks move on school assessments over a term, not a month, but the underlying habits should visibly shift inside four weeks.

faqs.question: Does online actually work for the younger child while the elder has home sessions?
faqs.answer: It works for the elder child far more reliably than for the younger one, so run it the other way round. Online suits abstract DP material, marked-draft review and doubt clearing, where screen sharing is genuinely efficient. A child in MYP or early IGCSE leaks attention inside twenty minutes online and nobody sees the phone under the desk. If your timetable forces the younger child onto a screen, keep them in the room with the open door, sit within earshot for the first fortnight, and treat the arrangement as temporary rather than the plan.

faqs.question: Should we keep the same tutor when our child moves from MYP 5 into DP1?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the test is whether that tutor can tell your child a draft is not good enough yet. DP asks for independent written work and a tolerance for hard feedback that the MYP years did not. A tutor who has been encouraging since Year 7 often cannot switch register, and the child cannot hear it from them. If sessions are comfortable and nothing is improving between them, that is the signal. Keeping continuity through MYP is usually right; carrying it into DP1 unexamined is the most common expensive mistake families make with a second or third child.

faqs.question: What if a tutor is not working out for one child but is fine for the other?
faqs.answer: Change the one and leave the other alone. Tell us specifically what is failing: work not being done, explanations not landing, the slot drifting, strong content but weak exam technique. We ask the outgoing tutor for a closing note, shortlist again against what you have just learned, and keep the second child's arrangement exactly as it is. Families often assume both children must move together out of fairness, which usually breaks the arrangement that was working. Two children are two separate matches that happen to share an address and an evening.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home for both children's sessions?
faqs.answer: For the younger child, yes, at least for the first few weeks; for an older student, not usually. Home sessions supervise themselves when an adult is somewhere in the flat, and that is most of their value over online. What actually needs a parent is the five-minute debrief afterwards, which is where you learn whether the hour did anything. Where both parents work late, the common arrangement is a session that ends before you get home and a short tutor message the same evening, with one session a week deliberately scheduled when someone is in.

faqs.question: My children are on different boards, one IGCSE and one IB DP. Do we need two tutors?
faqs.answer: Almost always yes once the elder child is in DP. Running IB home tuitions in Mumbai for two children on different boards means working two curricula in parallel, with different assessment language, different internal assessment shapes and different deadline calendars. One strong generalist genuinely covers both children at MYP 2 and MYP 3 level. Beyond Year 10 the components diverge too far: a tutor spending the fortnight on an IA sign-off cannot also drill IGCSE mole calculations. Keep the shared evening and the shared corridor if you can, and accept two people.

sections.heading: How a fees question becomes a shortlist of home tutors in Mumbai
paragraphs: A parent who writes in asking about IB home tutor fees in Mumbai usually expects a number to come back. What comes back instead is a short list of questions, because a quote offered before anyone knows the subject, the level, the address and the hour is a guess with a confident tone. Parents often ask for the best IB tutor in Mumbai and a fee in the same sentence, and both questions have the same answer: it depends entirely on the request. The request that produces a usable quote names the programme and the year, the exact subject and route, the assessment that is closest, the building and the suburb, and the two or three evening slots that would genuinely work in that household.

The shortlist comes out of those answers rather than a rate card. A Diploma Programme (DP) Year 2 student in Worli sitting the May session with a Physics Internal Assessment (IA) draft due needs someone who has marked that component against the current criteria, and the pool of people who have is thinner than the pool who can teach the syllabus well. A Middle Years Programme (MYP) Year 4 student in Kandivali East who needs her Maths confidence rebuilt draws on a far wider pool. Two requests, two shortlists, two sets of quotes, and none of them comparable with each other.

The sequence is deliberately unexciting, and it runs in the same order whether the request comes from Cuffe Parade or Kharghar. Nothing is quoted until the third step, because the first two steps are what make the third one mean anything. If a platform or an agency hands you a figure before it has asked where you live and what your child is being assessed on next month, that figure is a marketing number rather than a quote, and it will be revised the moment reality arrives.

At the introduction stage you speak to the tutor directly before any money moves. That conversation is where the scope gets written down: how long a session runs, what happens between sessions, whether marking and written feedback sit inside the quote, how travel is treated, and what notice either side gives. IB Gram keeps that summary on the record so that a disagreement in week six has something to refer back to instead of two different memories of one phone call.

sections.heading: Why does a DP Higher Level quote in Mumbai differ from an MYP one?
paragraphs: Because the work behind the session is different, not because the hour is longer. A Diploma Programme (DP) Higher Level (HL) tutor in Mumbai is marking Paper 3 style questions, reading Internal Assessment (IA) drafts against published criteria and tracking a predicted grade that universities will eventually see. A Middle Years Programme (MYP) tutor is teaching criteria A to D and building working habits. The second job is valuable; the first carries more unpaid hours stacked around it.

Within the International Baccalaureate (IB), each tier changes the preparation load in a way that shows up in what a tutor asks for. Primary Years Programme (PYP) support is mostly in-session: a tutor arrives, works through number sense or reading fluency, and leaves. The Middle Years Programme adds criterion-referenced tasks and the personal project in Year 5. The Diploma Programme adds six subjects, Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and an Internal Assessment in almost every subject, each with its own deadline. A DP2 tutor is effectively on call through January and February and quotes with that month in mind.

The Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel side splits differently. An International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) student choosing between Core and Extended Mathematics, or between the single-award and double-award science routes, needs a tutor who knows which paper combination that school enters students for, because teaching the wrong tier wastes a term nobody gets back. AS and A Level work sits closer to Diploma Programme HL in preparation load than to MYP. IB Gram matches across all IB and IGCSE subjects and the whole span of IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor requests in Mumbai.

None of this gives you a figure, and it is not meant to. It gives you a reason to ask a question when a DP Higher Level Chemistry quote and an MYP Year 3 Mathematics quote arrive at the same amount from the same person. Either the Higher Level work is being under-scoped or the MYP work is being over-scoped, and a tutor who cannot explain why the two are identical has not thought about either of them properly.

sections.heading: The thin-pool subjects in Mumbai, and what a small tutor pool does to a quote
paragraphs: Subject scarcity is the lever parents underestimate most. IB Gram lists all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai can be matched for, but the pools behind those subject names are uneven. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches (AA) at Higher Level, Physics HL, Chemistry HL and the less commonly taught Language B options sit in thin pools across the city. Business Management, Economics at Standard Level (SL), English A Language and Literature, and MYP Mathematics sit in deep ones. A thin pool means fewer people can take a 7pm weekday slot, and the people who can take it are aware of that.

Depth of experience matters as much as breadth of coverage. A Mathematics AA HL tutor has to be comfortable with Paper 3, the long investigative paper, and with an Exploration the student has usually scoped badly on the first attempt. A Chemistry HL tutor is marking an Internal Assessment built on an experiment the student ran once in a school laboratory and cannot repeat. An Economics tutor is reading commentaries against a rubric that rewards specific diagrammatic work and penalises vague evaluation. Each of those is marking time spent between sessions, and the honest quotes say so instead of pretending the work fits inside the hour.

Languages behave differently again. A Spanish Language B HL student in Juhu needs oral practice, which means a tutor whose spoken Spanish is strong enough to run a mock individual oral, and that narrows the Mumbai pool sharply. Hindi B and French B are easier to staff at every level. On the Cambridge side, First Language English and Mathematics are everywhere, while Additional Mathematics, Computer Science and Music are not. A parent looking for a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai households commonly need will get a same-week answer for some subjects and a wait for others.

The practical move is to ask what a tutor has actually marked rather than what they can teach. The question that separates two candidates is narrow: which components of this subject have you assessed against the current criteria, and in which examination session? A tutor who answers with specifics is quoting from experience and can tell you where the marks leak. A tutor who answers with a general statement about loving the subject is quoting from hope, and hope is the most expensive thing on this page.

sections.heading: Travel time and the contested evening slot across Mumbai's six zones
paragraphs: Geography enters a quote twice, once as distance and once as the hour. A tutor in Mumbai, Maharashtra gives up an evening rather than an hour, and the part of the evening they give up is invisible to the family at the table. IB home tutor fees in Mumbai therefore move by zone for reasons that have nothing to do with what a zone can afford. South Mumbai is short-distance and slow: Worli to Colaba is a modest hop that the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals can stretch past forty minutes in the evening peak. Tutors are matched inside the island, between Cuffe Parade, Fort, Walkeshwar and Napean Sea Road, served by the Western Line out of Churchgate, the Harbour Line and now the Coastal Road.

The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, so a tutor moving from Bandra West to Khar West or Santacruz West travels easily, and the same tutor sent from Juhu to Kandivali East at six in the evening does not. Matching along the line works; matching across it does not. Metro Line 1 lets an Andheri West tutor reach Ghatkopar, Metro Lines 2A and 7 have changed the Dahisar and Borivali picture, and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link makes a Malad West tutor workable in Worli on a Saturday morning and nowhere near workable on a Tuesday at seven.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR in between. Powai is the exception that shapes every quote there: it has no station of its own, so tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar East, and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road is what makes a Kurla match viable at all. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund West, and the Eastern Freeway makes a Chembur tutor reachable from Wadala and the island far faster than the map suggests.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, and tutors are matched node to node: Vashi to Sanpada, Nerul to Seawoods, CBD Belapur across to Kharghar and Panvel along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway. The Atal Setu and the Trans-Harbour Line have shortened the crossing, but pulling a tutor off the island for a weekday evening slot in Kharghar still rarely survives a full term. Thane spreads from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road, and Ghodbunder sets the schedule: Kasarvadavali is twenty minutes from the station off-peak and close to an hour at seven.

sections.heading: Which months push Mumbai families into a second weekly session?
paragraphs: January and February, and then April into the May session. That is when Mumbai families add a second weekly slot, and the second slot is the largest single change most households ever make to what they spend on tutoring. At Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School and Ecole Mondiale World School the Diploma Programme internal deadlines cluster inside that window, and a good tutor's diary fills accordingly by December.

The calendar itself is reasonably predictable. Mumbai schools run June starts, so Diploma Programme Year 1 begins in June and the first real assessment pressure arrives around November. Internal Assessment drafts in the sciences and Mathematics land in the DP2 winter, the Extended Essay final submission sits just before or just after the December break depending on the school, and the Theory of Knowledge essay deadline usually falls in the same fortnight as at least one Internal Assessment. Cambridge candidates at Cathedral and John Connon School or B.D. Somani International School face mocks in December and January and the main series after that.

Monsoon matters more than parents expect, and it belongs in a fee conversation rather than a weather conversation. From June to September an evening journey across Ghodbunder Road in Thane or along the Western Express Highway can double, and a tutor who committed to a 7pm slot in Kasarvadavali may simply not arrive. Families who plan a term ahead often write a monsoon rule into the arrangement: one online session permitted each month without renegotiating anything. That single line prevents most of the arguments that happen in July and most of the sessions quietly lost in August.

IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named on this page. Naming a school here means only that families in that neighbourhood attend it and that its calendar sets the local pressure points. A tutor who has worked with students from Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane or NES International School in Mulund West knows roughly when the mocks fall and plans the weeks before them; that is useful, and it is the only claim being made.

sections.heading: Does the quote change when an IB online tutor in Mumbai replaces home classes?
paragraphs: Usually yes, and the reason is travel rather than teaching. Home tuition is IB Gram's lead service in Mumbai because a tutor at the dining table sees the handwriting, the missing diagrams, the working skipped in the margin and the phone lying face down beside the notebook. That same tutor also spends an hour of their evening on the Western Express Highway or the Harbour Line, and that hour is real whether or not anybody bills it.

Home classes hold a schedule together in a way online rarely manages. A standing weekly slot in a Bandra West flat or a Hiranandani Gardens tower becomes part of the week, and a student cannot drift off to another tab while someone is sitting beside them. The trade-off is reach. The best-matched Mathematics AA HL tutor for a student in Panvel may live in Andheri West, and asking that person to cross the creek twice a week for a full term is exactly how arrangements collapse in month three. Online keeps the match and loses the table.

Hybrid is what most families in Mumbai settle on without ever naming it. One home session a week for the work that needs a shared page, and one online session for question practice, past paper walkthroughs and the sort of check-in that takes half an hour and could never justify a journey from Mulund West to Nerul. In exam term the online session is usually the one that gets added, because it can sit at an hour no travelling tutor could offer. All IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes Mumbai parents book can be run on this split.

The honest comparison is not home against online on an hourly basis. It is the total cost of an arrangement set against whether it survives a term. An online arrangement that runs for twelve straight weeks does more for a DP2 student than a home arrangement that lapses in week five because the tutor could not keep crossing Mumbai at 7pm. Ask any tutor which mode they can genuinely sustain through both the monsoon and the exam term, and take the answer seriously.
bullets: Home tuition shows a tutor the handwriting, the diagrams and the distractions
Online keeps the best-matched tutor when the journey is unreasonable
Hybrid usually means one home session plus one online practice slot

sections.heading: What IB Gram checks in Mumbai before you agree to a weekly slot
paragraphs: Verification is what makes a quote worth reading at all. Before a tutor reaches a shortlist, IB Gram confirms identity against a government photographic document, confirms the degree claimed, and asks for evidence of the board work asserted: which syllabus, which components, which examination sessions. A tutor who says they teach Diploma Programme Chemistry is asked which Internal Assessment criteria they have marked against and when. IB home tutor fees in Mumbai mean very little if the person quoting has not been checked at that level.

There is a second layer that matters more for home tuition than for online work. A tutor entering a residential building in Mumbai is entering a family's home on a weekday evening, so the match is made with gate protocol in mind: the society visitor register, the photo pass that towers in Powai and Thane West routinely require, and whether the building will allow a standing entry for a recurring slot. IB Gram does not control a society's rules and cannot change them; it makes sure the tutor knows them before the first visit instead of discovering them at the gate.

What you should check yourself is narrower and more useful than anything a profile contains. Ask for the tutor's own account of a student they took through the same component, including what went wrong in the middle. Ask them to mark one page of your child's existing work in front of you during the introduction, which takes ten minutes and tells you more than any credential. Ask whether the quote changes if a session runs over. And ask whether they currently teach the same subject at a school full time, because a school teacher's availability collapses in exactly the month you need it most.

IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and a verified tutor is not a promise of a particular result. Verification removes one category of risk, which is the risk of paying someone who is not who they said they were. The remaining risk is fit, and fit is tested in the first four weeks by watching the work rather than by rereading a profile. An IB private tutor Mumbai families hire with none of these checks done is a gamble with a term of school attached to it.

sections.heading: What moves IB home tutor fees in Mumbai, and how do you compare two quotes?
paragraphs: Six things move a quote, and they move it independently of each other. The programme and level, because Diploma Programme Higher Level work carries marking that Middle Years Programme work does not. Subject scarcity, because the pool for Mathematics AA HL or a less common Language B is small and small pools behave like small pools. Travel distance and journey time, because a tutor crossing from Chembur to Bandra West surrenders more of the evening than one walking across Hiranandani Gardens. Session length and frequency, because two shorter sessions cost a tutor two journeys. Whether it is one student or a pair sharing the table. And demand at the hour you want, because the 7pm weekday slot is contested right across the city.

That is why two quotes for the same subject are rarely the same product. One tutor may be quoting for contact time only: they arrive, they teach, they leave, and anything your child sends afterwards goes unread until the next visit. Another may be quoting for contact time plus marking of a past paper between sessions, written feedback specific enough to act on, a short monthly update to you, and printed practice material. Those two arrangements can look like the same hour quoted differently when they are not the same hour at all, and the difference is invisible unless somebody asks.

A quote becomes comparable the moment you ask a fixed set of questions and write the answers side by side. What exactly is included in a session. Is marking of work between sessions inside the quote or billed separately. Is travel time charged, and does that change if the slot moves later. What happens if we cancel. What happens if you cancel. How much notice does each side give, and is the notice the same in both directions. How and when is payment made, and covering what period. Ask all seven of every tutor on your shortlist and IB home tuition fees in Mumbai stop being a mystery: the thinner quote usually turns out to be the thinner service, and occasionally it turns out to be the better one.

Paying a full term in advance is the single place a fee conversation goes genuinely wrong. The money has gone, the leverage has gone, and if the match is wrong in week three you are arguing about a refund instead of arranging a replacement. Ask instead for a short cycle either side can walk away from: four sessions, reviewed, then renewed if it is working. And budget for the things nobody quotes, because they are what actually surprises families. Past paper packs, a revision guide and printing. The second weekly session that appears in exam term. The younger sibling who watches the arrangement working and wants one too, usually in a different subject with a different tutor.

sections.heading: When to review, what to expect, and what no tutor in Mumbai can promise
paragraphs: At four weeks you are not looking for a grade to move. You are looking for three things: your child can start a question without being told how to start it, the tutor can tell you specifically what is weak rather than generally how it is going, and the work coming back repeats fewer of the same errors. At one term you should see a shift in school assessments and a draft that needed fewer rounds of correction. At one exam cycle you find out whether the predicted grade moved. Anything faster than that is noise, and anyone selling you faster than that is selling.

The honest limit is worth stating plainly rather than burying. IB Gram cannot guarantee grades, and neither can a tutor who has marked Diploma Programme Physics for a decade. What a working arrangement changes is the quality and the quantity of deliberate practice between today and the examination, and that is the only variable anyone in this chain controls. A student who does not open the subject between sessions will not improve regardless of who sits at the table, how carefully the tutor was verified, or what the arrangement cost.

Which leads to the least intuitive sentence on this page. The cheapest arrangement is not the one with the lowest hourly rate. It is the one that ends soonest because it worked. A tutor who fixes a DP2 student's Mathematics AA HL Exploration approach in six sessions has cost that household less than one who provides pleasant and inconclusive company for three terms, whatever the two hourly rates happened to be. So ask every tutor at the introduction what the exit looks like: what has to be true before your child stops needing them, and how you will both recognise it.

When a match is not working, say so in week three instead of week ten. Tell IB Gram what specifically is wrong: the pace, the explanation style, a tutor arriving late off the Eastern Express Highway twice running, a personality mismatch nobody could have predicted from a profile. A replacement is arranged from the same verified pool, and the incoming tutor is briefed on what has already been covered so that the family is not paying twice for the same four weeks of diagnosis.
bullets: Four weeks: fewer repeated errors and a tutor who can name the weakness
One term: a shift in school assessments and fewer draft rounds
One exam cycle: whether the predicted grade actually moved

sections.heading: What to prepare before the first home tuition session in Mumbai
paragraphs: Three things on the table before the tutor arrives: the last two pieces of marked school work with the teacher's comments still on them, the subject guide or syllabus the school is following, and the assessment calendar for this term. A parent who hands those over in the first ten minutes saves an entire session of diagnosis, which is a session paid for either way. If your building in Powai or Thane West needs a visitor pass logged in advance, arrange it the day before rather than letting the tutor wait at the gate while the slot burns away.

The first session is diagnostic and should feel diagnostic. A good tutor spends part of it watching your child attempt a question unaided, because what a student does when stuck is the entire diagnosis and nothing else reveals it. By the end you should have a specific statement of what is weak, a plan for the next four sessions, and one clear sentence about what will happen between sessions and who is responsible for it. If the first session is a lecture delivered at your child, that is a signal worth acting on early.

Agree the administrative part before session two rather than after a disagreement. Session length, the standing slot and the fallback slot, who confirms a change and by when, how marking between sessions is handled, the notice each side gives, and the payment cycle. Keep it short and keep it written down somewhere both of you can find it. A search for IB tutors near me Mumbai will produce a long list of options; the arrangement that lasts a full term is the one where both sides wrote down the same understanding on day one and neither had to remember it.
bullets: Bring the last two marked school assignments with teacher comments
Have the subject guide and this term's assessment calendar ready
Arrange the society visitor pass the day before the first session
Expect a diagnosis and a four-session plan, not a lecture
