sections.heading: How is a tutor checked before they ring your doorbell in Mira Road?
paragraphs: Before a tutor reaches a shortlist, IB Gram checks identity, qualification documents and claimed teaching experience against something other than their own description of it. Subject claims are tested in conversation with somebody who knows the syllabus, so a tutor who says they teach Higher Level Physics is asked about the individual investigation rather than about their degree.

The checks that matter for a visit are duller and more important. Photo identity is verified, and the name on it is the name that reaches your building's gate register. Home area is recorded, because it is the single best predictor of whether a weekday slot in Mira Road will hold through October. Prior engagements are followed up where families agree to it. Tutors are told plainly that they may not solicit cash payments outside the platform, and that approaching a family directly after a match ends the relationship.

Then there is what you should check yourself, and no platform substitutes for it. Sit in on the first session, or at least be in the flat. Ask the tutor to show you the markscheme they are working from. Ask which of your child's actual pieces of work they have read. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, promises a particular score, or talks about results before they have seen a single page of your child's writing. The strong ones are noticeably more cautious in the first week than the weak ones.

One more practical point specific to this corridor. An IB home tutor in Mira Road who is new to your building will be stopped at the gate, asked for identity, and sometimes made to wait while somebody calls your flat. Tell the tutor which gate to use and leave their name with security the day before, and the first session starts on time instead of fifteen minutes late. After two or three visits most buildings here issue a standing visitor entry, which quietly removes the commonest cause of a lost first ten minutes.

sections.heading: Which rung of the ladder justifies paying for travel across Mumbai?
paragraphs: This is the question the rest of the page exists to answer, and the answer is uncomfortable: the younger the child, the more you should pay for proximity, and the older the child, the more you should pay for the specialist and stop caring where they live. That inverts what most families on this corridor actually do.

A PYP child needs the tutor in the room. The hour is spent reading aloud, counting on fingers that are then taken away, and being asked to say why. None of that transmits well through a laptop to a seven-year-old. So for PYP, pay for the nearest competent person: a patient graduate in Bhayandar who is good with small children beats a DP examiner in Juhu who will cancel twice a month. The travel premium is worth paying here and almost nowhere else.

An MYP child is the balanced case. In-person for the written criteria work, online for the drill. The deciding factor is usually the child's own self-management: a Year 8 who sits down without being asked can take two online sessions and one visit, while a Year 8 who needs supervision cannot. Watch what happens across the first four weeks rather than deciding in advance, and be ready to change the ratio rather than the tutor.

A DP student should hire the specialist. By then the work is Internal Assessment drafting, Extended Essay structure, Theory of Knowledge argument and past-paper technique, and all four transmit perfectly well through a shared screen. Paying a travel premium to get a generalist into your flat for DP Chemistry is the commonest misallocation of money on this corridor. The honest version of IB home tutoring in Mira Road for a DP2 student is one in-person session a fortnight for accountability and everything else online, with the subject expert drawn from the whole IB tutor pool in Mumbai rather than from the three kilometres around your building. Families who get this right usually do it in DP1; families who get it wrong discover it in January of DP2.

sections.heading: Progress by week four, by the end of a term, and by the exam series
paragraphs: Four weeks buys you diagnosis, not improvement. By the end of week four you should be able to name the specific gap: the child cannot set up a stoichiometry calculation, or writes a Theory of Knowledge paragraph without ever stating a claim, or loses marks in Mathematics purely on notation. If your tutor cannot name a gap that precisely after four sessions, that is the first thing to raise, and it is a legitimate reason to change tutor.

One term, roughly June to October or November to March, is the first point at which a mark can reasonably be expected to move, and even then it moves unevenly. Written work improves before timed work. A student will often produce a much better Internal Assessment draft in term one while their examination marks sit still, because examination performance depends on recall under pressure that takes longer to build. Parents who judge at week six usually dismiss a tutor who was working.

One full examination cycle is the honest horizon. Across that span you should see the internal components submitted on time and at a standard the school is satisfied with, and a visible narrowing of the gap between the student's best work and their average work. That last measure is the one worth watching closely: consistency improves before peak performance does, and consistency is what a written paper in May actually rewards.

What nobody can offer is a number. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor will tell you what your child will score, because the result depends on moderation, on a May session this tutor has no sight of, and on a teenager's choices in April. A tutor who promises a specific grade is telling you something about their sales process rather than their teaching. What a strong tutor will give you is a straight answer at four weeks about whether this is a tuition problem at all, because sometimes it is a sleep problem, a subject-choice problem or a school-fit problem, and paying for IB home tuition in Mira Road will not fix any of those three.

sections.heading: Starting IB home classes in Mira Road: what to have ready
paragraphs: Getting started is quicker than most families expect, and the delay is almost always on the parent's side rather than the tutor's. Have four things ready before you send the first message: the exact year group and programme, the subjects, the last report or marked assessment sheet, and two time windows you can genuinely protect for the next two months.

The marked work matters more than parents think. A tutor who has read one piece of it walks into the first session with a hypothesis instead of a questionnaire, which means you buy teaching rather than an hour of getting acquainted. If you have nothing recent, a photograph of two pages of your child's exercise book does the same job. Send it before the session rather than producing it during the session.

The first session itself is diagnostic. Expect the tutor to set a short piece of work, watch how your child attacks it, and then ask questions that sound basic. Expect them to leave with a plan for the next three sessions and to tell you one thing your child does well, because a tutor who only lists deficits loses the child by week three. Expect to be asked about the study space and about when the child actually gets home from Dahisar or Borivali.

On logistics, three things save everyone time. Leave the tutor's name with your building's security the day before. Agree the cancellation rule in the first week rather than the first crisis: this corridor floods, and a plan that assumes nobody ever misses a session collapses in July. And settle whether a parent will be in the flat, because a Year 4 session with nobody home runs differently from a DP session where the door stays shut. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai will have a clear opinion on all three; ask for it.

faqs.question: What does the first session with an IB home tutor in Mira Road actually cover?
faqs.answer: It diagnoses rather than teaches. The tutor sets a short task in your child's current topic, watches how it is attacked, and asks deliberately basic questions to find where the understanding breaks. They should leave with a three-session plan, one specific strength they noticed, and a request for any marked work you have not yet sent. If your child's school is in Dahisar or Borivali, expect questions about the school run and the realistic start time as well.

faqs.question: How does a tutor get past the gate and the visitor register at my building in Mira Road?
faqs.answer: Leave their full name and the session time with security the day before, and the first visit starts on time. Most buildings on this corridor run a visitor register and a phone call up to the flat for anybody unknown, which costs ten to fifteen minutes on a first visit. After two or three sessions, buildings here usually add a regular tutor to a standing visitor list and the problem disappears. Tutors carry photo identity, and the name on it matches the name you were given.

faqs.question: Can a tutor commuting down from Vasai or across from Bhayandar hold a 7pm weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Bhayandar yes, Vasai usually no. A tutor living in Bhayandar is close enough to reach Mira Road at seven through most of the year, including the monsoon. From Vasai the creek crossing and the train frequency make a weekday evening unreliable by October, and what looks workable in June starts cancelling. For a Vasai-based tutor a weekend morning slot holds far better. Ask any candidate where they live and what their worst-case trip looks like, not their best.

faqs.question: What makes IB tuition fees in Mira Road higher or lower?
faqs.answer: Five things, and none of them is a fixed rate. Board and level: Diploma Programme Higher Level work is priced above MYP. Subject scarcity: a Spanish or Visual Arts specialist is priced by rarity rather than distance. Travel: a tutor crossing from Kandivali in the evening prices that hour in, which is why the same tutor online is cheaper. Session length and frequency. And the tutor's own teaching or examining background. Ask for the travel component separately so you can see what proximity costs you.

faqs.question: My child is in PYP. Is a tutor in the flat better than an online class?
faqs.answer: Almost always yes. A seven- or eight-year-old does not hold attention on a screen for a full session, and the Primary Years Programme work that matters, reading aloud, number sense and explaining an answer, needs somebody physically present to notice when attention has gone. For this rung, choose the nearest patient teacher over the most decorated one. A tutor from Bhayandar or Mira Road itself who is genuinely good with young children will do more than a Diploma Programme examiner who cancels twice a month.

faqs.question: Does a Diploma Programme student need someone physically present for Internal Assessment work?
faqs.answer: No, and insisting on it narrows your choices badly. Internal Assessment drafting is document work: a shared screen, a marked-up draft and a conversation about the criteria do the job as well as a kitchen table does. What a physically present tutor adds at this stage is accountability, which is why a fortnightly visit alongside weekly online sessions suits most DP2 students. The specialist you need for Chemistry or Economics may well live in Andheri, Thane or anywhere else in Mumbai, and that is fine.

faqs.question: We have moved to Mira Road from a CBSE school. Where does my child actually start?
faqs.answer: With a written diagnostic in English and Mathematics, before you choose subjects. The gap between an Indian board and the IB is rarely content; it is that marks now come from explaining, structuring and referencing rather than from reproducing. A child who was strong at CBSE Mathematics can lose marks in MYP purely on communication criteria. Give it a term with a tutor who has made that transition with other children, and ask your school's coordinator which year group placement they recommend.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not the right fit after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Say so, and ask for a replacement rather than opening a refund argument. A mismatch after three sessions is usually about manner rather than competence: a child who needs warmth has been given a drill sergeant, or the other way round. Tell us what specifically did not work, because that detail makes the second match better. The replacement draws on the same shortlist, and the diagnostic work already done is handed over, so you are not starting the search from nothing.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected in any way to the schools families on this corridor attend?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to any school named on this page, including the ones Mira Road families travel across the Mumbai boundary to reach in Dahisar and Borivali. Schools are mentioned because their calendars and their internal assessment formats shape what a tutor needs to know. Any tutor claiming a formal relationship with a school, or offering to pass on that school's internal materials, is misrepresenting the arrangement and should be reported to us.

faqs.question: How much notice do you need before a tutor can start IB home tuition in Mira Road?
faqs.answer: For common subjects a few days is usually enough to produce a shortlist and get a first session booked inside the week. For scarce subjects, the languages, Visual Arts, Music and Film, or for an unusual slot such as a weekday morning, allow longer and expect the shortlist to be online-weighted. The tightest periods on this corridor are August, when the first reports land, and October, when mock examinations start, because every other family reaches the same conclusion at the same time.

faqs.question: Is a weekend morning slot easier to keep than a weekday evening one?
faqs.answer: Considerably, on this corridor. A Saturday or Sunday morning session avoids the Western Express Highway peak entirely, draws from a pool that stretches to Borivali, Kandivali and Malad rather than stopping at Dahisar, and runs with a child who has slept. The trade-off is that weekend slots are competitive and families book them a term ahead. The practical answer most Mira Road families reach is one weekend session in person as the anchor and midweek online sessions for maintenance.

sections.heading: How we match an IB home tutor in Nariman Point
paragraphs: A request for an IB home tutor in Nariman Point rarely comes from a flat in Nariman Point. The district is offices. The law firms, banks and consultancies on the back bay reclamation are where the parent sits at four in the afternoon, while the child who needs teaching is in Cuffe Parade, Colaba or a building facing Marine Drive. Our first question is therefore not the subject. It is the address the lesson happens at, and who is home when the doorbell rings.

The second question is the programme year, because an IB enquiry can mean a Year 4 child finishing a Primary Years Programme (PYP) unit or a DP2 student with a Chemistry Internal Assessment (IA) draft due. We ask for the school, the year group, the subjects taken at Higher Level (HL), the report card comment that worried you, and the two evening slots that genuinely work. Five minutes of that detail replaces a fortnight of trial lessons with the wrong person.

Then we shortlist from tutors who already teach inside the island city. Someone living in Worli, Prabhadevi or Byculla reaches a Cuffe Parade address far more reliably than a tutor from Andheri, and reliability across thirty weeks matters more than a marginally stronger CV. You see two or three profiles with board teaching history, the subjects each covers at HL and SL, and the slots each can hold. You pick. Nobody is assigned to you.

The first visit is a working session, not a sales call. The tutor reads the school assessment calendar, looks at the last two pieces of marked work, and sets a plan for the term. If the fit is wrong, you say so after session two and we start again from the brief we have already written. IB home classes in Nariman Point that nobody believes in by week three never recover, and dragging them out costs a term.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: which rung of the IB ladder is your child on?
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) is three programmes rather than one, and the help a child needs changes completely between them. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) ends in an exhibition where a child researches a question and presents it to the school. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) marks against published criteria instead of percentages and closes with a personal project. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the final two years, with subjects split between Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) alongside the core.

Parents in Cuffe Parade usually call us at one of two moments. The first is the MYP to DP transition, when criterion letters give way to the seven-point scale and a child who coasted on comprehension suddenly needs command terms. The second is January of DP1, when the Internal Assessment (IA) calendar arrives and the Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay, the Extended Essay (EE) and several subject IAs begin competing for the same handful of weekends.

Which rung you are on also decides what a home tutor can usefully do. In the PYP there is no syllabus to drill, so the work is reading stamina, number sense and the habit of explaining an answer out loud. In the MYP it is criterion literacy: a Year 9 student who writes beautifully can still score poorly against one criterion because nobody showed her what the descriptor asks for. In the DP it is paper technique against the current subject guide.

If your child sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel papers rather than IB ones, the tier and board questions are a different conversation and our IGCSE home tutor page for this locality covers them. Everything below assumes the IB. For the structure of any subject in the year your child actually sits it, read the current subject guide with the school Diploma Programme coordinator rather than trusting a figure found online, including anything on this page.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and the assessments sitting under each one
paragraphs: An IB enquiry that says every subject is rarely true in practice. Families here ask for Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Economics, Biology, English A, Hindi A or French B, and the two hardest to staff in South Mumbai are HL Mathematics and HL Physics for DP2. We cover all IB and IGCSE subjects our tutors in Nariman Point can genuinely teach, and we say plainly when a subject needs an online specialist instead of a local generalist who will improvise.

The Higher Level decision is the one worth slowing down on. HL is not the same course taught harder: it carries additional material and a volume of past-paper work that eats weekday evenings, and a student carrying three HL subjects plus the Extended Essay (EE) in DP1 has very little slack left. More South Mumbai students are rescued by moving one subject to Standard Level (SL) in time than by adding a second tutor in April.

Each subject also carries its own internal assessment, and that is where home tuition earns its place. A science Internal Assessment (IA) needs a research question narrow enough to be measurable, which is one conversation with someone experienced and six weeks of drift without it. A Mathematics exploration needs real mathematics, not a survey with a graph attached. Economics commentaries need current articles and a diagram that explains the news. History needs a question whose sources exist in Mumbai libraries.

For papers, components and criteria, work from this year's guide. Subject guides are revised on the board's own cycle, so a tutor quoting a structure from four years ago is teaching from memory, and your school coordinator holds the current version. What a good match gives you instead is a tutor who has taught the subject to this board, at this level, and can show you a marked piece of your child's work inside the first fortnight.

sections.heading: Cuffe Parade, Colaba and Marine Drive: where a Nariman Point lesson happens
paragraphs: Nariman Point sits at the southern tip of the back bay reclamation in Mumbai, Maharashtra, with Churchgate as its nearest station, and the parent searching for a tutor here is usually at an office desk on that reclamation. The lesson, though, happens at home: a Cuffe Parade tower behind the World Trade Centre, a Colaba flat off the Causeway, or a building on the Marine Drive curve. We therefore schedule against two journeys, the tutor's and yours.

South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers about eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. That single fact is why we match within the island rather than bringing someone down from the suburbs: a 6:30pm slot held by a tutor living in Lower Parel survives the monsoon, while the same slot held from Andheri does not survive October.

Rail and metro help in specific ways. A tutor living along the Western Line reaches Churchgate quickly and walks in from there, which is why Churchgate-adjacent slots fill first. Metro Line 3 has changed the Cuffe Parade to Bandra Kurla Complex run, so a tutor teaching in BKC during the afternoon can reach a Cuffe Parade address by early evening. The Coastal Road has made the Worli approach quicker outside peak hours, and the Harbour Line brings tutors in from Dockyard Road and Sewri.

Marine Drive has its own quirk: parking is street parking, so a tutor arriving by car in the evening may circle for ten minutes. Most tutors here come by train, metro, bus or auto, which makes the start time more predictable rather than less. Colaba sessions are easiest on weekday evenings and hardest on Sunday mornings, which is why an IB home tutor in Nariman Point is usually matched from Byculla or Mazgaon rather than from Andheri.

sections.heading: What the South Mumbai school calendar does to a Mumbai family's evenings
paragraphs: Children at these addresses mostly attend schools within a few kilometres. Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort and B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade are the two names that come up in almost every enquiry from this corridor, with Bombay International School at Babulnath and Aditya Birla World Academy at Tardeo close behind. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of them; we match tutors for families whose children happen to study there.

Their calendars matter more than their reputations. A DP2 student sitting the May session is in a different world from a Year 9 MYP student, and the pressure points are predictable: October and November for IA drafts and EE progress meetings, January for mock examinations, February and March for final submissions, April for the study-leave scramble. Home classes booked in June cost far less effort than home tuition begged for in the second week of February.

School-set work shapes the week too. Assessment tasks cluster, and a child with three criterion-marked pieces due in the same week needs a tutor willing to put the planned topic aside and triage. Parents working in the Nariman Point business district carry a second calendar on top of that: quarter-end, audit season and board weeks, when nobody is home before nine. Tell us which weeks those are and we build the term around them instead of rescheduling six times.

One more calendar reality: the school sets the deadline, not the tutor. If a coordinator moves an IA checkpoint forward, the plan changes that week and the tutor works to the new date. We also do not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor in Mumbai will. What a tutor can commit to is attendance, marked work in your hands, and a straight read on where your child stands before the school report says it out loud.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or a mix for an IB student in Nariman Point?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default here and it earns that position. A tutor at your dining table sees what a camera does not: the brother practising guitar in the next room, the exercise book with three untouched pages, the fact that your daughter writes her working in the margin and then rubs it out. An IB home tutor in Nariman Point who has sat in your flat for a term knows exactly how your child stalls, and stops it earlier each time.

The honest cost of visits is travel. A tutor who gives you a 7pm slot in Cuffe Parade has given up the slot before it, because crossing the island for one lesson is not worth it otherwise. That makes weekday evening home classes scarcer and dearer than a mid-morning booking, and it means a tutor with two students in the same building can hold a schedule that a tutor with one cannot. Standing weekly slots survive here; floating ones do not.

Online works better than many parents expect for specific jobs. Past-paper review, Mathematics exploration supervision, Economics commentary feedback and EE drafting all work well on a shared screen, and an IB online tutor in Nariman Point can be a specialist elsewhere in India for an HL subject nobody on the island teaches. It works badly for a Year 6 child who needs a person in the room, and badly in late monsoon when power or connectivity drops mid-session.

Most families here settle on a mix. One weekly session at home for teaching, one online for drafts and paper review, and a shift to fully online during examination weeks, when forty minutes of travel is better spent revising. We also run fully online matches for families who travel for work for half the month. Say which pattern you want in the enquiry and we will tell you honestly whether it suits the subject and the year group.

sections.heading: How is an IB home tutor in Mumbai actually checked?
paragraphs: Before a profile reaches you we check identity against a government photo document, the degree claimed, and the board teaching history: which school, which programme, which years, which subjects at HL and SL. A tutor who says they taught the Diploma Programme should be able to describe the assessment calendar they worked to and the IA deadlines they marked against. We ask. Vague answers end the conversation before you ever see a name or a rate.

References come from parents, not from employers alone, and we ask them one narrow question: did the tutor turn up, and did marked work come back? Reliability is what collapses first in Mumbai. A capable tutor who cancels twice in October has cost your child the IA window, and no amount of subject knowledge recovers that in February. We also sanity-check the travel claim: can this person truly reach a Cuffe Parade or Marine Drive address at 7pm, every week, in July?

There are checks only you can do, and they take one session. Ask to see a piece of your child's work marked by the tutor inside the first fortnight. Ask which year's subject guide they teach from. Ask what they will do in the week three tasks fall together. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, or who talks about results before they have read a single piece of your child's writing.

Keep the admin small and written down. Agree the slot, the rate, the cancellation rule and the replacement rule before session one, in a message you can scroll back to. For visits, leave the tutor's name and number at the building security desk so the visitor register is not a weekly argument. An IB home tuition arrangement in Nariman Point runs on those small agreements far more than on anybody's curriculum vitae.

sections.heading: What IB tuition fees in Nariman Point depend on
paragraphs: Nobody can quote you a rate without knowing five things, and any page that does is guessing. Fees move with the programme stage, because DP2 work at Higher Level takes more preparation than an MYP Year 7 session. They move with subject scarcity: an HL Mathematics or HL Physics specialist on the island has a short waiting list and prices accordingly. They move with session length, with how many sessions a week you want, and with travel.

Travel is the factor parents underestimate. A tutor giving up a Peddar Road to Cuffe Parade run at six in the evening is selling you ninety minutes of their day for a sixty-minute lesson, and that shows up in what a weekday home tutor charges against a Saturday morning booking. Two students in the same Cuffe Parade building, or two siblings in one flat, change that arithmetic far more than any negotiation over the hourly rate will.

There are also costs that are not the hourly rate. Past-paper packs and workbooks. A second tutor for one scarce subject in DP2. The examination-season surge from January, when the same tutor has three families asking for extra hours and the slot you did not book in June is gone. Ask what the rate includes: marking between sessions and message access, or only the hour spent in your flat with the door shut?

We will not publish a price list, because an honest one would need a column for every subject, level and address in South Mumbai. What we will do is tell you the range we are currently seeing for your exact request before you speak to anyone, and say when the cheaper option is the right one. A Year 8 MYP student usually does not need a DP examiner, and paying for one buys very little.

sections.heading: What does realistic progress look like in the first term?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not expect a grade change. You should expect three things: sessions that happened on time, a diagnosis you recognise, and at least one piece of marked work in your hands. If your child's Economics commentary came back with comments about the diagram rather than the spelling, the tutor is reading the criteria properly. If nothing has been marked by week four, that is a conversation to have now, not something to wait out until the next report.

At one term the measurable change is usually in process rather than score. Homework starts on the day it is set instead of the night before. The IA research question is agreed and narrow enough to finish. Command terms are used correctly in test answers. School assessment may move a little or not at all, because a single poor test can mask real progress, and teachers notice participation before they notice marks.

Across a full exam cycle the honest picture is mixed. Students who start in DP1 with a standing weekly slot generally reach the final year with IAs submitted on time and past papers already worked, which is where most of the difference comes from. Students who start in March of DP2 are doing damage control, and we say that at the enquiry rather than after you have paid for a term. We do not guarantee grades, and we will not pretend otherwise to win a booking.

When it is not working, say it early. The usual causes are dull: the slot is too late and the child is exhausted, the tutor teaches content when the gap is technique, or the chemistry is simply absent. We rematch from the brief we already hold, so you are not filling in a blank form again, and the incoming tutor reads the diagnostic notes from the outgoing one with your permission.

faqs.question: Does online IB tuition really work for a Diploma Programme student?
faqs.answer: For some jobs it works as well as a visit, and for others it does not. Past-paper walkthroughs, Internal Assessment supervision, Extended Essay drafting and Economics commentary feedback are all fine on a shared screen, and online access is often the only route to a genuine specialist in a rare Higher Level subject. Teaching a brand-new topic to a tired fifteen-year-old at 9pm is harder online, and late-monsoon power cuts in South Mumbai interrupt more sessions than traffic does. Most DP families end up running a hybrid week.

faqs.question: What if there is no progress after a month?
faqs.answer: Raise it at four weeks, not at three months. An IB tutor Mumbai parents keep for a full term is one who has already shown you marked work and named the specific gap, so if nothing has come back marked, that is the first problem to solve. Ask the tutor what they think the gap is and compare it against the school's last written comment. If the two do not line up, we rematch from the brief we already hold, and your child does not repeat the whole diagnostic.

faqs.question: How do we handle the building's visitor and gate pass rules each week?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once rather than negotiating weekly. Most buildings in Cuffe Parade, Colaba and along Marine Drive run a visitor register or an app-based gate pass, and a standing weekly entry in the tutor's name removes the five minutes of friction that otherwise eats the start of the lesson. Give the security desk the name, the number and the slot. If your building needs a resident to approve each entry, tell us, because it rules out tutors arriving straight from another lesson.

faqs.question: Should my child take a subject at Higher Level or Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Decide on workload and destination, not on ambition alone. Higher Level adds depth, extra material and a far larger volume of past-paper practice, so three Higher Level subjects plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge makes for a heavy DP1 year alongside school assessment. Talk to the Diploma Programme coordinator about this year's subject guide and about what the universities your child is considering actually ask for. A tutor can tell you whether the current work rate is sustainable at that level.

We keep the enquiry brief, the diagnostic notes and the slot requirements, so a replacement starts from what is already known instead of a blank form, and with your permission the incoming tutor reads the outgoing one's notes. Fit fails for ordinary reasons: the slot is too late in the evening, the tutor teaches content when the gap is examination technique, or the child simply does not talk to them. None of those is worth a wasted term.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all of my child's IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Up to the Middle Years Programme, often yes; in the Diploma Programme, rarely. One IB private tutor in Nariman Point can reasonably hold two or three related subjects at MYP level, and that continuity is worth a great deal for a younger child. At Higher Level the subject guides are deep enough that a Chemistry specialist is not a Mathematics specialist, and pretending otherwise shows up in the Internal Assessment. Most DP families here end with one main tutor and a second for the single hardest subject.

There are exceptions for rare Higher Level subjects, where we would rather give you a specialist arriving at eight, or working online, than a nearby generalist who cannot teach the paper.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP and DP inside one set of Oberoi Exquisite towers
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) is three programmes rather than one, and a single tower in Oberoi Exquisite usually holds children in all of them. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs through the early years and finishes with the exhibition, a long collaborative inquiry that asks a ten or eleven year old to research a question of their own, present it and defend it. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers the middle school years and is reported against published criteria in every subject, which is exactly why an MYP report card can look alarming to a parent who grew up on percentages and has no idea whether a 5 in criterion C is a problem.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is the final two years and this is where the structure hardens. A DP student carries six subjects drawn across the subject groups, some at Higher Level (HL) and some at Standard Level (SL), plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and the creativity, activity and service commitment. Each of the six subjects brings an Internal Assessment (IA) that the school marks and the IB moderates. Confirm the live structure for the session your child will actually sit with the school's Diploma coordinator and the current subject guide rather than with anything written online, including this page, because the IB revises its guides on its own cycle.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL: what an IB home tutor talks through first
paragraphs: Subject choice is the decision that quietly sets the next two years, and it is usually made in a fortnight of forms. The list of all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Oberoi Exquisite can be asked to cover runs long, but the IB side of it narrows quickly: one subject from most of the groups, a language decision, and the choice of which three to take at Higher Level. Plenty of families in these towers are weighing a Cambridge Core or Extended route for a younger child in the same month, and that decision belongs to a separate page; this one stays with the IB.

Higher Level adds content, but what it really adds is the expectation that a student can hold several ideas at once under time pressure. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches rewards a student who enjoys proof and algebraic structure. Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation suits one who thinks in models, data and context. Choosing three Higher Level sciences because a university admissions page mentioned two of them is the most common avoidable mistake we are asked to fix in October, and a tutor who has taught those courses to real students will tell you honestly which combination this particular child can carry alongside the Extended Essay.

Then there are the Internal Assessments, and they do not arrive politely spaced. A science investigation, a mathematics exploration, a history or business piece of independent research and an arts process portfolio all have school-set interim deadlines, and in a Mumbai IB school those deadlines cluster. The useful work a tutor does on an IA is rarely about content. It is about scoping a question small enough to answer properly, keeping the method honest, and reading the published criteria with the student so they can see what the words are actually asking for. Ask the subject teacher for the current criteria rather than trusting a summary.

Requests for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Oberoi Exquisite parents send through almost always name two subjects and one deadline. That is the right way to brief us. A named subject plus a dated piece of work tells us which tutor to approach; a request for general improvement does not.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online, or a mix for an IB student in Oberoi Exquisite?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default here and it should be. IB home classes in Oberoi Exquisite happen at your dining table or your child's desk, with the books the school actually set open in front of both of them, and that proximity does something a video call cannot: the tutor sees the half-finished diagram, the margin note the teacher wrote, the page the student skipped. For PYP and early MYP children it is not really a choice. A nine year old left alone with a screen and a worksheet will find the window.

Online tutoring earns its place for specific jobs. Essay feedback, Theory of Knowledge discussion, past-paper walkthroughs and a short pre-deadline check-in all work well on a shared screen, and an online slot survives a July evening on the Western Express Highway that a physical visit would not. An IB online tutor in Oberoi Exquisite also widens the pool enormously, which matters when the subject is scarce. If your child needs a specialist in a less common Language B or in Music, insisting on home visits may mean waiting weeks for nobody in particular.

The arrangement most families in these towers settle into is hybrid, and it is not a compromise. One home session a week for the real teaching, plus a half-hour online slot in the days before a deadline when the student has a draft and a specific question. The honest trade-off is discipline: hybrid only works if the online half is treated as a real appointment rather than something to be moved whenever the evening gets busy. Families who protect it get more out of a single home visit a week than families who book two and attend one and a half.

sections.heading: How an IB home tutor is checked before reaching your gate in Mumbai
paragraphs: Every IB home tutor in Oberoi Exquisite is checked on four things before a profile reaches you: government photo identity, the degree or teaching qualification they claim, documented experience of the specific programme stage they are offering, and references from families or schools they have taught for. Programme stage is the one parents most often forget to ask about. Years of experience with the CBSE or ICSE syllabus is real teaching experience, and it is not the same as having marked an MYP task against criteria or scoped a DP Internal Assessment with a student.

Then there is a subject conversation rather than a form. We ask a prospective tutor to talk through a piece of real student work in their subject and say what they would do next with it. That single exercise separates a strong graduate who knows the content from someone who can teach it, which is the distinction that matters once they are sitting at your table on a Wednesday.

There is a second half to this, and it belongs to you. Meet the tutor yourself in the first session rather than leaving the flat. Ask which school boards they have taught and for how long, and ask them to describe the last IA or personal project they supported. Ask what they will send you after each session. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, or who tells you the school is marking your child unfairly before they have read a single piece of marked work. An IB private tutor Oberoi Exquisite parents interview properly is worth three who arrived on a recommendation nobody checked.

We keep this deliberately unglamorous. No tutor is sent to a flat in these towers without a named profile going to the parent first, and nobody is asked to let an unknown person through the gate on trust.

sections.heading: What should progress look like after a month of IB home tuition?
paragraphs: At four weeks you are looking for process, not marks. The honest markers are that your child can say what the session covered without being prompted, that homework is being started earlier in the week, and that the tutor has sent you something concrete about what is weak. A grade is a lagging indicator in the IB and four weeks is not long enough to move one. If nothing has changed in how the work gets done by week four, that is the moment to raise it, not week twelve.

At one term you should see it in the school's own evidence. A criterion that was consistently low starting to move, a test paper where the student finished rather than ran out of time, an IA proposal that the teacher accepted without a rewrite. Progress in the IB is usually uneven across criteria, so expect a report that improves in two places and stands still in a third. That is normal and it is not a reason to change tutor.

Across a full examination cycle the realistic claim is narrower than the marketing on most tutoring sites. Good tutoring improves preparation, technique and the quality of internally assessed work, which are the parts that are actually in a student's control. It does not control the paper, the moderation or the day. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor offers a guaranteed grade; anyone who does is telling you something about themselves rather than about your child.

When it is not working, say so early. Most mismatches here are not about competence but about pace, language or temperament, and three or four sessions is usually enough to know. Tell us what specifically failed, because a student who needed more worked examples and less open discussion is a different brief from one who needed the opposite. The replacement picks up from where the work stopped rather than starting the diagnosis again.

sections.heading: Getting started with an IB home tutor in Oberoi Exquisite

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 and has not finalised Higher Level subjects. Is it too early for a tutor?
faqs.answer: No, this is one of the most useful months to have one. A tutor who has taught the course can tell you how a particular child copes with the Higher Level workload of that subject, which no prospectus can. The real question is not whether your child could manage Higher Level Chemistry in isolation. It is whether they can carry it alongside two other Higher Levels, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Use the first three or four sessions diagnostically, then confirm the final combination with the school's Diploma coordinator.

faqs.question: Does online IB tutoring work as well as home tuition for a DP student?
faqs.answer: For some tasks it works better and for others it clearly does not. Essay feedback, Theory of Knowledge discussion and past-paper walkthroughs transfer well to a shared screen, and an online slot survives a wet evening on the Western Express Highway that a physical visit would not. faqs.answer: Wherever there is a hard surface, decent light and no television in view. Some families use the clubhouse reading area for an older student who works better away from a younger sibling, which is worth confirming with your committee rather than assuming. An IB student is already carrying six subjects, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and a service commitment, and filling every evening with home tuition produces a tired child rather than a stronger one. Start with one or two sessions and change the number when the evidence actually changes.

A Mathematics tutor comfortable from MYP3 up to Standard Level Diploma can genuinely do both, and back-to-back sessions in one visit save travel for everybody and usually cost less. sections.heading: IB programmes families on Pokhran Road are working through
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) is three separate programmes with three separate kinds of pressure, and a parent on Pokhran Road usually needs help with exactly one of them. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs through the early years and is assessed by the teacher rather than by anything external. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) introduces published assessment criteria and the Personal Project. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year course with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices, Internal Assessment (IA) work in every subject, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK).

Most of the requests that reach us from this corridor sit in two bands, and they do not look much like the Mumbai city-wide pattern. The first is MYP 4 and MYP 5, where a child who coasted through the earlier years suddenly meets criteria that reward a kind of writing nobody taught them explicitly. The second is DP1, where the subject load arrives all at once and a student who was strong at fifteen finds that strong is no longer the unit of measurement. A good IB home tutor works on the thing the criteria are actually testing rather than on more questions of the same type.

That distinction is the whole argument for subject-specialist matching. A MYP Individuals and Societies teacher and a DP Economics teacher are not interchangeable, even where the content overlaps, because the MYP student is being marked against a criterion descriptor and the DP student is being marked against subject-specific assessment objectives. We match to the programme first and the subject second. If your child is mid-way through DP1 and still unsure about dropping an HL, that is a conversation to have with the Diploma Programme coordinator at school, not with a tutor, and any tutor worth booking will tell you the same.

Weightings, paper counts and component structures change on the IB's own revision cycle, so take those from the current subject guide or from your school's coordinator rather than from any tutoring website. What a tutor can tell you reliably is what the skill underneath a component is, how long it usually takes a student to build it, and whether your child is behind on content or behind on exam technique. Those two problems look identical on a report card and need completely different work.

sections.heading: Which IB subjects and levels do tutors here actually teach?
paragraphs: Across the Pokhran Road corridor the live demand is Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics, Business Management, English A and the second-language subjects, at both Higher Level and Standard Level. Tutors who cover all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Pokhran Road can reach within twenty minutes exist in reasonable numbers for those; for Higher Level Mathematics and for the less common languages the pool thins out and the honest answer is that you may be choosing between a weekday slot with the right specialist and a convenient slot with someone adequate.

Subject choice is where parents here lose the most time. Across both boards the decision has the same shape: pick for the thing your child can sustain for two years, not for the thing that sounds strongest on a transcript. In the Diploma Programme that means HL and SL selection, and the Core and Extended split belongs to the IGCSE years, which a sibling page covers properly. The Diploma question we get asked most often on this corridor is whether to take three Higher Levels in the sciences, and the answer usually depends on how the student handles simultaneous Internal Assessment deadlines rather than on raw ability. Parents often open by asking who the best IB tutor in Pokhran Road is, when the useful question is which single subject the hours should go to this term.

Every Diploma subject carries internal assessment of some kind, and this is the work that tutoring actually moves. A Physics investigation, a Business Management commentary, a Mathematics exploration and a Language A written assignment are all graded against published criteria by the school and then moderated externally. A tutor cannot write any of it and should not be editing it line by line. What they can do is read the criteria with the student, look at what the draft is currently evidencing, and name the specific criterion where the marks are being left on the table.

The practical shape of IB home tuition in Pokhran Road is usually one subject twice a week or two subjects once a week each. Two subjects with the same tutor works when the subjects share a skill, so Mathematics with Physics or Economics with Business Management, and works badly across a science and a language. For a DP2 student in the January to March window we often recommend dropping to one subject and giving the hours to whichever IA is furthest behind, which is a less profitable recommendation and a more useful one.

sections.heading: Which parts of Thane does a Pokhran Road tutor cover?
paragraphs: A tutor matched for Pokhran Road will normally also take students in Thane West, Majiwada and Vasant Vihar Thane, because all four sit inside the same short driving radius off the Pokhran Road No. 1 and No. 2 spine. Thane station is the anchor at the western end, and the Central Line and the Trans-Harbour Line both run from it, which matters because a meaningful number of tutors here commute by train rather than by car.

Thane spreads west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Ghodbunder Road and Majiwada, and the Ghodbunder stretch is what sets the schedule for everyone. A tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in about twenty minutes when the road is clear and close to an hour in the evening peak. That single fact is why we match Thane tutors to Thane families as a rule. Mulund tutors do cross over, usually via the Eastern Express Highway, and for a Saturday morning slot that works; for a 7pm Tuesday it does not hold for a full term.

Within the corridor itself the distances are small enough to be irrelevant. Lodha Splendora and Kalpataru Aura are both reachable from the station end without touching Ghodbunder Road at all, and a tutor can hold a 4:45pm slot in one and a 6:15pm slot in the other on the same evening. That is unusual for Mumbai, Maharashtra, where most tutors can realistically serve one student per evening. Families booking all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Pokhran Road tutors cover therefore get a choice of hours the rest of Mumbai does not have. It is the reason a standing weekly slot on this corridor tends to survive longer than the same arrangement in the Western Suburbs.

If you are further east towards Owale or past Kasarvadavali, be straightforward with us about it at the shortlist stage. We would rather tell you that a 7pm weekday slot is not realistic and offer you 8pm or a Saturday than place a tutor who will be late twice a month until the arrangement quietly dies. Parents who type IB tutors near me Pokhran Road into Google and get city-wide listings are usually trying to solve exactly this problem, and the listing cannot solve it because it does not know which end of the corridor you live on.

sections.heading: The school year along Pokhran Road No. 2
paragraphs: Families on this corridor send their children to Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School, to NES International School, and to the schools clustered in and around Hiranandani Estate a little further along. Billabong High International School has a Thane campus too. Those schools set the calendar every tutoring arrangement here has to fit, and they do not all set it the same way, so the first thing we ask is which school rather than which board.

The rhythm looks roughly like this, and it runs a few weeks ahead of the Mumbai state-board calendar. The year opens in June and the first six weeks are genuinely quiet, which is the cheapest and most useful time to start home tuition and the time almost nobody does. Late September and October bring the first serious internal assessments and the first report that a parent takes seriously. December and January are the heaviest stretch: mock examinations, Internal Assessment drafts and the Extended Essay all land in the same few weeks, and for a DP2 student sitting the May session this is the point at which a term's drift becomes visible and expensive to fix.

February and March are about finishing rather than learning. By then the useful work is past-paper technique, reading examiner comments properly and deciding which topics to stop revising. A tutor who is still teaching new content to a DP2 student in March has misread the situation. April is study leave, the May session follows, and results in early July are the point at which families start asking about retakes and re-marks, which are a school conversation first.

Naming these schools is local context and nothing more. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School, NES International School or any other school on this corridor, has no arrangement with any of them, and cannot guarantee grades or admissions outcomes for any student. If a tutor ever implies they have inside knowledge of a particular school's marking, treat that as a reason to be wary of them rather than a selling point.

sections.heading: Home tuition in Pokhran Road, online classes, or both?
paragraphs: Start with home tutoring, because for most families on this corridor it is simply the better option and the local geography makes it affordable in time terms. An IB home tutor in Pokhran Road who lives at the station end loses fifteen minutes to travel, not fifty, so they will take a 5pm slot that a tutor crossing Mumbai would refuse. A tutor in the room also sees the things a camera does not: the phone face-down on the table, the handwriting that collapses in the last ten minutes, the question your child will not ask out loud.

Online tuition earns its place in three specific situations. The first is a scarce specialist, usually Higher Level Mathematics or a language, where the right teacher is somewhere else in Mumbai, in Powai or Bandra, and the alternative is nobody. The second is the examination run-in, when a thirty-minute question review three times a week is worth more than one long weekly visit. The third is the monsoon, when Ghodbunder Road and the Eastern Express Highway can turn a reliable arrangement into a weekly negotiation. Screen-sharing a past paper is genuinely good for marking practice and genuinely poor for a student who needs someone to notice they have stopped working.

Hybrid is what most families here settle into by the second term, and it works best when it is deliberate rather than accidental. One home visit a week for new teaching and relationship, one short online session for drafts and doubts. The rule we give parents is that the mode should follow the task: anything involving a long explanation, a diagram drawn together or a difficult conversation happens in person, and anything involving checking a draft or clearing two questions happens on a screen. Deciding mode session by session is how arrangements drift into being online-only by March.

The trade-offs are real in both directions. Home classes cost more because travel is priced in, and they are harder to reschedule at short notice. Online sessions are cheaper and almost infinitely flexible, which is precisely the problem, because a flexible slot is the first one to be moved when something else comes up. If you want the arrangement to survive a full academic year, a fixed weekday evening home visit with a standing gate pass is the version that holds.
bullets: Home visits suit new teaching, long explanations and difficult conversations
Online suits scarce specialists, draft checking and the monsoon weeks
Hybrid works when the mode follows the task, not the mood
Home classes price travel in; online sessions get moved more easily
A fixed weekday slot with a standing gate pass survives the year

sections.heading: How is an IB home tutor in Pokhran Road checked before the first visit?
paragraphs: Before a tutor appears on a shortlist we confirm their identity against a government photo document, their claimed degree against the awarding institution, and their board experience against something specific rather than a general claim. 'I have taught the Diploma Programme' is not evidence; naming the year groups taught, the subjects at Higher Level and Standard Level, and the kind of Internal Assessment work supervised is. A tutor who cannot describe a criterion in their own subject in plain language has not taught it recently.

Then there is the part that only matters because this is home tutoring. Someone is entering your flat, usually when one parent is still at work. We confirm the tutor's current address because travel claims that are not true are the single most common cause of an arrangement collapsing, we take references from families they have worked with, and we ask the tutor to carry photo identification to the first visit so your security desk at Lodha Splendora or Kalpataru Aura has something to log.

There are checks only you can do, and they take one session. Watch who is talking. A tutor who talks for fifty of sixty minutes is lecturing, not teaching, and a child who is nodding is not necessarily following. Ask your child one question after the first session: what did you get wrong today and why. If they can answer, the tutor made the error visible, which is the entire job. Ask to see what the tutor wrote on the page, because a session that leaves no trace is hard to build on next week.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, quotes a success rate or claims a special relationship with a school on this corridor. None of those are things an honest tutor can offer. IB Gram does not guarantee grades either, and we will not pretend that a verified tutor plus a fixed slot is the same thing as a result. What verification buys you is a smaller chance of wasting a term on someone who was never going to be able to do the work.
bullets: Identity, degree and board experience confirmed before a tutor is shortlisted
Current address confirmed, because false travel claims break weekly slots
Tutors carry photo identification for your society security desk
Watch the talk ratio in session one and ask what your child got wrong
Promises about specific grades or school marking are a warning sign

sections.heading: Why a 4:45pm slot works here and almost nowhere else in Mumbai
paragraphs: This is the thing that makes Pokhran Road different from every other locality we write about. The schools and the homes are on the same road. Pokhran Road No. 2 is Thane's school corridor, with Singhania and the Hiranandani Estate schools strung along it, so the distance between the gate a child walks out of at 3:30pm and the lift they take up to their flat is minutes rather than an hour. Everywhere else in Mumbai, the school run is the reason tuition starts at eight.

Work through what that does to a week. A DP1 student at a school on this corridor is home by four. A tutor living near Thane station arrives at 4:45pm, teaches until six, and is at a second student in Majiwada by 6:30pm. The student does homework at eight and sleeps at eleven instead of starting tuition at nine and finishing at half past ten. Over a term that is not a small comfort; it is the difference between a child who can absorb a difficult explanation and a child who is being taught Mathematics while exhausted.

It also changes what a tutor can charge their time to. Because two or three students on the same corridor are reachable in one evening, a tutor is not pricing a sixty-minute lesson at ninety minutes of travel. That is why IB home classes in Pokhran Road are usually easier to arrange at a sensible hour than the same request in Powai or Khar, and why a tutor here is more willing to add a second short session in the pre-examination weeks. The corridor is doing the work, not any cleverness on our part.

The catch is that the good slots go early and they go to whoever asks first. Between 4:30pm and 6:30pm on Monday to Thursday there are only four or five usable slots per tutor per week, and by late July they are gone for the year. Parents who come to us in September asking for a 5pm slot are usually offered 8pm, accept it, and then discover in November why it was available. If you want the after-school hour, ask in June.

One more consequence worth knowing. Because the corridor's tutors cluster near the schools, a tutor who teaches your child may also teach a classmate. That is normal and nothing to worry about, but it is worth saying out loud at the start if your child would be uncomfortable with it, because it is far easier to match around at the shortlist stage than to unpick in October.
bullets: Schools and homes share one road, so children are home before four
A tutor can teach two corridor students in a single evening
Shorter travel means a second short session before examinations is realistic
Only four or five after-school slots exist per tutor each week
Ask in June for the 4:30pm to 6:30pm window, not September

sections.heading: What progress should look like at four weeks and at one term
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at marks. You should be looking at whether your child can say what they are bad at. A student who moves from 'I just don't get Chemistry' to 'I can't do the mole calculations when the question gives me volume' has made the most valuable progress available in a month, because the problem is now small enough to work on. If after four weeks of home tuition the description is still as vague as it was in week one, something is wrong with the match and not with the child.

At one term, expect movement on the specific things that were named in week one and nothing more. One criterion up on an Internal Assessment draft. Working consistently through a paper instead of running out of time. Homework that gets started on the day it is set. Marks sometimes move in a term and sometimes do not, particularly in the Diploma Programme where a school's internal grading can tighten as the course goes on, so a flat grade with visibly better work is a normal and acceptable outcome at this stage.

At one examination cycle you will know whether the arrangement worked, and you will know it from the paper rather than from the tutor's account of it. This is also where the honest limits sit. A tutor working with a DP2 student from January, in Thane or anywhere else in Mumbai, cannot undo eighteen months of missed foundations before May, and anyone who says otherwise is selling. We do not guarantee grades, we will not quote a success rate, and we would rather tell you in week two that the subject load is the real problem than take fees for a term of pleasant sessions.

The failure mode to watch for is the comfortable arrangement. Everyone is polite, the tutor arrives on time, the child does not complain, and nothing changes. It is harder to spot than a bad fit and it wastes more money. The test is simple: ask for one concrete thing your child can now do that they could not do last month. If neither your child nor the tutor can name one, ask for a replacement, and do it in November rather than in February.
bullets: Week four: your child can name the specific thing they cannot do
One term: one criterion up, or a paper finished within the time

sections.heading: Getting started with home classes in Pokhran Road
paragraphs: Three things make the first session worth paying for. The last marked piece of work, with the teacher's comments still on it. The current timetable, including whatever sport or music already owns two of your evenings. And one sentence from your child about what they want to be different, which is usually more precise than the version a parent gives us.

The first visit itself is diagnostic and should feel like it. A tutor who spends session one teaching has skipped the part that makes sessions two to twenty useful. Expect them to work through the marked paper with your child, find where the understanding actually stops, and leave with a short plan for the next three or four weeks. Expect to be told something you did not want to hear. A tutor who finds nothing wrong in the first hour either was not looking or is managing you.

On the logistics, settle them before the tutor arrives rather than at your gate. Tell your society office that a tutor is coming weekly and ask what they need: most complexes along this corridor will issue a standing visitor pass once a resident requests it, which turns a ten-minute argument at the gate into a signature. Decide where the lesson happens and keep it there. The dining table with the television off beats a bedroom, and a child sitting beside a tutor rather than across a sofa will actually write things down.

An IB private tutor Pokhran Road families book for a weekly visit is priced differently from an IB tutor Mumbai parents reach only online, because travel and scarcity both sit inside the number. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents enquire about is not always available in the slot you want, and we will say so rather than putting a weaker match in a convenient hour. If the right tutor for your child only has Thursday at 5:15pm, take Thursday. The fit is the part that is hard to replace; the time is the part you can negotiate with your own week.
bullets: Bring the last marked work, the timetable and your child's own sentence

faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor in Pokhran Road cost?
faqs.answer: IB tuition fees in Pokhran Road depend on five things, and any site quoting you a figure before asking about them is guessing. Those five are the board and programme, the level, how scarce the subject specialist is, how far the tutor travels to reach you, and the session length and frequency. Higher Level Diploma Programme subjects cost more than Middle Years Programme work, Higher Level Mathematics costs more than Business Management because the pool is smaller, and a tutor crossing from the Ghodbunder end prices the travel in. We will give you a range for your specific request once we know the year group and subject, and we will tell you which of those five factors is driving it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Pokhran Road for a 7pm weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more easily than in most of Mumbai, provided the tutor already lives in Thane. A tutor near Thane station reaches the corridor in fifteen to twenty minutes outside peak traffic. The slot that goes wrong is the one where the tutor is coming from past Kasarvadavali, because the Ghodbunder Road stretch can take close to an hour in the evening and a tutor who is fifteen minutes late twice a month will eventually be late every week. We check where a tutor actually lives before shortlisting them for an evening slot, and if the geography does not work we will offer you 8pm or a weekend morning instead of pretending.

faqs.question: How does gate access work at Lodha Splendora or Kalpataru Aura?
faqs.answer: You request it, not the tutor. Most larger complexes on this corridor will issue a standing visitor entry for a weekly tutor once a resident puts the request to the society office, usually with the tutor's name, phone number and identity document details. Do that before the first session. Without it, every visit begins with a phone call to your flat from the security desk and a tutor standing at the gate, which costs five to ten minutes of a sixty-minute lesson. We ask tutors to carry photo identification to every visit regardless. If your complex insists on per-visit approval, set a recurring reminder rather than relying on the tutor to chase it.

faqs.question: Where in the building should the lesson actually happen?
faqs.answer: At a table, in a shared part of the flat, with the television off. The dining table is the right answer in most Pokhran Road flats. A bedroom desk works if the door stays open and the phone is out of the room. Avoid the sofa entirely, because nobody writes anything on a sofa and Diploma Programme work is written work. Some complexes along this corridor have a study room or a library in the clubhouse, which is useful if your flat is noisy in the evening, but check whether an external tutor is permitted there before booking it. Consistency matters more than the room itself: the same table every week builds a habit.

faqs.question: Does online IB tuition really work for a DP2 student?
faqs.answer: For some tasks it works very well and for others it does not. An IB online tutor in Pokhran Road is genuinely good for marking past-paper answers together, clearing two or three doubts in half an hour, and reviewing an Internal Assessment draft on a shared screen. It is weak for first teaching of difficult content, for a student whose attention drifts the moment nobody can see their hands, and for the conversations where a tutor needs to read a face. For DP2 specifically, we often suggest one home visit a week plus two short online reviews in the January to March window, which is more contact for less travel.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three weeks?
faqs.answer: You tell us and we replace them, without needing a justification you would be comfortable saying to the tutor's face. Three weeks is the right moment to raise it rather than the awkward one. We ask two questions when it happens, because they make the next match better: was the problem the teaching or the person, and did your child talk during sessions. A content mismatch means we look for a different subject specialist. A rapport problem usually means we change the tutor's age, style or gender rather than their qualifications. The replacement tutor starts with your original notes plus what the first three weeks taught us.

faqs.question: My son is in MYP 4 and has not chosen Diploma subjects yet. Can a tutor help?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help with the evidence, not with the decision. What they can do is tell you honestly whether your son's current Middle Years Programme work in a subject suggests he would cope with it at Higher Level, which is a far more useful input than his enthusiasm in April. The decision itself belongs with your school's Diploma Programme coordinator, who knows which subject combinations the school can actually timetable and what the university pathways look like for its leavers. Bring the tutor in for the question 'is he ready for this' and the school in for the question 'can he take this'.

faqs.question: Is there any progress to see after a month of home tuition?
faqs.answer: Yes, but not in marks. After four weeks the thing to look for is precision: can your child name the specific skill or topic that is failing them, instead of naming the whole subject. That shift is the real first milestone and it usually arrives between weeks two and four. You should also see homework started earlier and fewer blank starts on past-paper questions. What you will probably not see is a changed grade, because most schools on this corridor do not assess often enough for a month to show up. If the description is still vague at week four, raise it with us.

faqs.question: Do I need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole hour, but someone should be in the flat. For a younger Primary Years Programme or Middle Years Programme child we would say yes, be around, though not in the room, because a parent watching changes how a child behaves. For a Diploma Programme student, an adult in the flat is enough. What we do ask is that you are present for the first session and the last five minutes of it, because that is when the tutor tells you what they found. Being there for that five minutes is worth more than sitting through the other fifty-five.

faqs.question: Which Thane schools do your IB families here come from?
faqs.answer: Mostly Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School, NES International School and the schools around Hiranandani Estate, with some families at the Thane campus of Billabong High International School. We name them as local context only. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any of these schools, and has no arrangement with any of them. The reason we ask which school is practical rather than promotional: the internal assessment calendar and the mock examination dates differ between them, and a tutor planning a term needs to know whether your December is clear or completely full.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two children in Majiwada at the same slot?
faqs.answer: Only if they are in the same year group and the same subject, and even then we are cautious. Two Diploma Programme students taking the same Higher Level subject at the same school can share a session productively, because the content and the deadlines line up. Two siblings two years apart cannot, and what actually happens is that the older one gets taught and the younger one listens. If the budget is the reason for asking, a better answer is usually one shorter session each per week than one long shared session. We will tell you which of those your two children are.

faqs.question: Does the Ghodbunder Road commute affect evening session timings here?
faqs.answer: It affects everything about scheduling in Thane, which is why we ask where a tutor lives before we ask what they teach. Thane spreads west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Ghodbunder Road and Majiwada, and the Ghodbunder stretch is the slow part: twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening. A tutor based at the station end can hold a 5pm and a 6:30pm slot on the same corridor. A tutor coming the other way cannot reliably hold either. Monsoon weeks make it worse, and that is when a hybrid arrangement earns its place.

You speak to them before committing to anything. Ask your society for a standing visitor pass in the same week, and the first home classes can usually run within seven to ten days.

sections.heading: How IB Gram finds an IB home tutor in Powai
paragraphs: Most enquiries from this corner of Mumbai open the same way: a year group, two subjects that have gone wobbly, and the evenings that are free. For Powai we ask for one extra thing immediately, which is the address down to the society and the tower. Hiranandani Gardens is not a single address but a grid of towers off Central Avenue, and a tutor who accepts a 7pm slot without knowing whether she is walking across a podium or driving round to the far end of the layout will be late inside her first fortnight. Residents of Lodha Bellissimo get asked for the same detail for a different reason: clearance there runs through one visitor desk, and a tutor who has not been listed in advance stands at the barrier while the lesson clock runs.

The shortlist is then built on road distance rather than map distance. We would rather put forward a tutor from Kanjurmarg who holds the same slot for two terms than a better-credentialled one from the Western Suburbs who starts cancelling in week five. This is the single biggest difference between matching in Powai and matching in a suburb that has its own platform.

Two or three profiles come back with the things a parent can check: the degree, the board experience, which year groups they have taught, and how many evenings a week they already hold inside this corridor. You speak to them before anything is confirmed. That call is where the useful question is not whether the tutor is good, but what else she is teaching on Wednesday and where that lesson is, because the honest answer tells you whether your slot is the first of her evening or the third.

The first paid session is diagnostic. The tutor reads the last school report, the most recently marked piece of work and whatever internal assessment is currently open, then writes back what she believes the actual problem is. Often enough the subject knowledge is fine and the written communication is not, which changes what the next six weeks look like.
