sections.heading: Which IB programme is your child actually in?
paragraphs: Three answers are possible and they need different tutors. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs the Primary Years Programme (PYP) in the early school years, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) through middle school, and the Diploma Programme (DP) across the last two years. Your school coordinator will confirm which year group sits in which stage, because Mumbai schools label the transition years differently and the IB revises its own documentation on its own cycle.

A PYP parent in Powai is usually not worried about examinations at all. The worry is that the child reads less than the cousin in a CBSE school, or that nobody has mentioned times tables since last year. PYP is inquiry-led and reported against learning outcomes rather than marks, so a tutor's job here is quieter: build fluency in reading and number work without turning the week into a second school day. One hour twice a week at the dining table, with the tutor leaving a short note for the parent, does more at this stage than a long Saturday session.

MYP changes the question, because the reporting is criterion-based and a child can be strong at a subject and weak at the criterion the teacher is marking. Parents here often arrive confused about why a bright child scores in the middle band. A tutor reads the criterion descriptors with the student and makes her mark her own draft against them, which is a dull hour that pays for itself. Deeper MYP subject-group work belongs on our MYP page, so we keep this to the structural point: the MYP to DP step is where Powai families suddenly start calling.

DP is where the volume arrives. The student carries subjects at Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), an Internal Assessment (IA) in most of them, the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the creativity, activity and service strand alongside. Nothing in that list is hard on its own. The difficulty is that they land in the same months, and a DP1 student at Hiranandani Foundation School who is three weeks behind in Biology has no slack to absorb an EE deadline. An IB home tutor in Powai working with a DP student spends as much time on sequencing as on content.
bullets: PYP work stays short, frequent and built around reading and number fluency
MYP help usually means reading the assessment criteria, not adding more content

sections.heading: Subject choice, Higher Level and Standard Level, and the assessments attached to each
paragraphs: One enquiry covers all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Powai can be matched for, but the IB side of that list is what this page is about, and the first real decision is the subject combination. The Diploma Programme asks for a spread across subject groups with some taken at Higher Level (HL) and some at Standard Level (SL). The current combination rules, and the number of each your school allows, come from your Diploma Programme coordinator, not from a tutoring site. What a tutor can tell you is what each choice costs in evening hours.

Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra chapters bolted on. It asks for a different kind of answer: more unfamiliar application, more willingness to carry an argument through a long response, and in the sciences more comfort with being asked to design rather than describe. A student who is coping at SL Economics because she has memorised the diagrams will stall at HL, where the examiner wants her to say which diagram is the wrong tool for the question. That difference is the honest reason to take HL help early in DP1 rather than in the term before examinations.

The internal assessments are the part families underestimate. Most subjects carry one piece of coursework that the school marks and the IB samples, and it is written during the normal teaching year, not in a convenient gap. A Powai student doing Biology, Geography and Business Management will write three unrelated pieces of extended work with three different sets of expectations, and the Extended Essay sits on top of all of them. A tutor is most useful at the question-setting stage, because an investigation with a vague research question cannot be rescued by good writing later.

Theory of Knowledge gets its own mention because it is the subject nobody has a textbook for. Parents cannot help with it and most students treat it as an obstacle. A tutor who has read a few dozen TOK essays can do something specific: make the student choose a real-world example she actually knows something about, from her own school, her own reading or her own Mumbai, instead of a borrowed one from the internet. For current structures, word limits and submission expectations, read the subject guide your school issues and ask the examinations officer, because these are revised and a figure quoted online will eventually be wrong.

sections.heading: Powai, Hiranandani Gardens, Chandivali and the roads a tutor uses
paragraphs: Powai sits in the Central Suburbs of Mumbai, Maharashtra, hanging off JVLR between the Western and Eastern halves of the city, and it behaves like neither. The Central Suburbs otherwise run along the Central Line from Kurla to Mulund and along the Eastern Express Highway. Powai is attached to that system only by road, which is why IB home tuition in Powai is planned differently from tuition in Ghatkopar or Vikhroli, where a tutor steps off a train and walks.

Hiranandani Gardens is the part of Powai most families mean when they say Powai: a dense cluster of residential towers with schools, shops and clinics inside walking distance, which means a tutor who lives there can hold four lessons in an evening without touching a main road. That makes resident tutors the scarcest and most useful people on our Powai list. Chandivali, immediately next door, is the overflow: a tutor living in Chandivali reaches most of Powai in the time it takes a Hiranandani Gardens resident to find parking, and the Chandivali to Powai leg avoids the JVLR signals entirely in one direction.

Andheri East is the third source, and the most common. It carries both the Western Line and Metro Line 1 towards Ghatkopar, so a tutor who teaches in Andheri East during the day can come across to Powai afterwards. The cost is the stretch between the two, which is slow in the evening peak in a way that no map app predicts reliably in the monsoon. Kanjurmarg is the quiet fourth option and often the best one: it is on the Central Line, it is close, and the drive in is short enough that a 7pm start genuinely means 7pm.

What this means in practice is that your realistic tutor pool is drawn from Hiranandani Gardens, Chandivali, Andheri East and Kanjurmarg, with Ghatkopar adding depth for subjects where the specialist count is low. We do not pretend a tutor from Bandra or Thane will hold a weekday evening slot in Powai for a full term. Some will offer. Most stop by the second month, and a replacement mid-term costs your child more than waiting two weeks for the right local match would have. An IB private tutor Powai parents keep for a full term is nearly always someone who already lives inside this corridor.

sections.heading: The Powai school calendar and its pressure points
paragraphs: Families in Powai mostly sit across three school ecosystems, and their calendars are what set the tutoring year. Hiranandani Foundation School is inside the neighbourhood and runs both Cambridge and IB pathways. Podar International School has a Powai campus. Oberoi International School sits along JVLR at the Goregaon East end of the corridor, so a Powai family driving there each morning is already making the same journey a tutor makes in the evening, in reverse. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Hiranandani Foundation School, Podar International School, Oberoi International School or any other school named here; we mention them because their timetables decide when your child is under pressure.

The Mumbai school year starts in June and the first weeks are deceptively calm, which is exactly when a tutor is most worth booking. By late July and August the first unit tests land and the DP1 students discover what Higher Level feels like. September and October bring the first real internal assessment drafts and the mid-term break, which is the best working window of the year: a tutor can run longer sessions during the day and clear a backlog that would take a month of evening hours.

November to January is the heavy stretch. School mock examinations for DP2, internal assessment submission deadlines set by the school rather than the IB, and the Extended Essay final draft tend to collide. A DP2 student at an IB school in this corridor can have a mock week, an IA deadline and a TOK essay inside the same fortnight, and the Diwali break in the middle of it rarely survives as a holiday. Parents who call in January asking for intensive help are usually two months late, and the honest answer is that we can still help, but less than we could have in September.

February to April is examination preparation proper, and from mid-April the May session takes over. Tutors in Powai get asked for daily slots in this window and there simply are not enough evenings in the week to give every family one. Book the standing slot you want for March in November. The other thing worth knowing is that different schools in the same corridor run their internal deadlines weeks apart, so your neighbour's timetable is not your timetable. Ask your own school for its published assessment calendar and give it to the tutor at the first session.

The October mid-term break is the best backlog-clearing window of the year

sections.heading: Should an IB home tutor in Powai come to you or teach online?
paragraphs: For most Powai families the answer is home first. An IB home tutor in Powai gets a child who is physically at the table with her books out, no second screen, and a parent within earshot who can tell within a fortnight whether the hour is working. Younger students in the Primary Years Programme and the Middle Years Programme learn materially better with someone in the room, and a DP student who has been drifting usually needs the accountability of a person arriving at the door more than she needs a better explanation. Home tuition also means the tutor sees the actual study space, which is often the real problem.

The honest cost of home tutoring is travel, and in Powai travel is not symmetrical. A tutor coming in from Andheri East in the evening peak is giving up time she could have spent teaching, and that shows up in what she charges and in how many slots she can offer. It also means a late lesson is sometimes a short lesson. A tutor who lives in Hiranandani Gardens or Chandivali has none of that friction, which is why we push hard for a local match even when it means a slightly longer wait.

Online earns its place in specific cases rather than as a cheaper default. An IB online tutor in Powai makes sense when the subject specialist you need is not in the corridor at all, when a DP2 student wants a short targeted session the night before a mock rather than a full hour, when the monsoon has shut a road, or when the family travels during breaks and wants continuity. A shared screen and a graphics tablet handle worked problems and essay drafting well. They handle a distracted fourteen-year-old badly.

Hybrid is what most of our longer Powai engagements settle into: one home session a week as the anchor, one shorter online session for review, and the online slot used as the fallback when JVLR is standing still. Set that pattern deliberately at the start, agree with the tutor what triggers the switch, and the arrangement survives both the monsoon and the examination season. Decide it in week eight and you will lose two lessons to confusion first. One enquiry covers all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Powai parents ask about, so you do not need to send a separate request per subject or per mode.

sections.heading: How tutors are checked before they reach your gate in Mumbai
paragraphs: Every IB tutor Mumbai families reach through IB Gram is checked before a profile is shown to you: identity against a government photo document, the highest qualification claimed against the certificate, and the board experience against something verifiable such as a school appointment or named student work. We ask which boards and which year groups, separately, because a tutor who has taught the Cambridge pathway for a decade is not automatically ready for a Diploma Programme internal assessment. An IB home tutor in Powai who says she handles everything across every programme is describing an ambition rather than a timetable, and we ask for specifics.

There are checks a platform cannot do for you, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. We cannot sit in the room. So there is a short list a Mumbai parent should run personally, and it takes one call. Ask the tutor which board and which syllabus year she is teaching to. Ask her to describe the assessment criteria for one of your child's subjects without looking them up. Ask what she does in a session where the student has not done the agreed work. The answers separate someone who teaches the IB from someone who teaches the subject.

Then do the things that are about your flat rather than the syllabus. Ask the tutor to send an identity document photograph for your society records before the first visit, so the gate has her listed. Keep lessons in a room with a door open to the rest of the home. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, discourages you from speaking to the school, or wants several months paid up front. None of those three is normal practice, and all three are easier to spot in the first week than the fifth.

Fees are the other thing to settle before the first session rather than after it. IB tuition fees in Powai depend on the programme stage, whether the subject is taken at Higher Level or Standard Level, how scarce the specialist is, the length of the session and how far the tutor travels to reach you. A Hiranandani Gardens resident teaching MYP Mathematics and a Diploma Programme specialist coming in from Andheri East for an HL subject are not the same cost, and they should not be. We do not publish a price list, because any figure would be wrong for half the families reading it. Ask for the rate, the session length, the cancellation rule and how the monthly count is handled, in writing, in the introductory call.
bullets: Identity, qualification and board experience checked before a profile reaches you
Ask the tutor to describe one assessment criterion without looking it up
Send the tutor's identity details to your society office before the first visit
Be wary of up-front multi-month payment or pressure to bypass the school
Agree rate, session length and cancellation terms in writing at the start

sections.heading: Why Powai has no station of its own, and why that sets your lesson time
paragraphs: Powai has no railway station inside it. The nearest usable rail access is Kanjurmarg on the Central Line, or Andheri East on the Western Line with Metro Line 1 running from there towards Ghatkopar, and both of those are a road journey away at the end. This is the single most important scheduling fact about IB home classes in Powai, and almost every tutoring problem families here report traces back to it. A suburb with a station has a tutor pool shaped like a line along the tracks. Powai's pool is shaped like a circle of roads, and circles jam.

Work through what that does to a Tuesday. A tutor finishing a lesson in Andheri East at six has to cross to Powai in the worst half hour of the day. She arrives between twenty and forty minutes after she intended, not because she is unreliable but because the road does what the road does. Your child, who finished school at three and has been waiting since five, is now starting at half past seven and finishing at nine. The lesson is technically delivered. Educationally it is half a lesson, and by the third week somebody quietly cancels.

Now run the same Tuesday with a tutor from Hiranandani Gardens or Chandivali. She walks or drives for a few minutes, starts on time, and because her travel cost is near zero she can take an earlier slot at five thirty for a younger child and a seven o'clock slot for a DP student in the same building cluster. That is why we weight proximity so heavily in the shortlist, and why we would rather tell you to wait a fortnight for a local Economics specialist than send someone from the Western Suburbs this week. The right question to ask any tutor offering you a Powai slot is simply where she is coming from and what she is teaching immediately before.

There are two workarounds worth knowing. The first is the direction of travel: the Chandivali and Kanjurmarg approaches are far less affected than the Andheri East one, so a tutor from either side can hold a genuine seven o'clock start. The second is the weekend morning. Saturday and Sunday mornings in Powai are the best-value slots in the week because nobody is fighting JVLR, and a ninety-minute weekend session for internal assessment drafting is worth more than two rushed weekday hours. Families who book one weekday evening plus one weekend morning get the most stable arrangement we see in this corridor, and in the monsoon they lose the least.

An Andheri East tutor in the evening peak routinely loses the first half hour

sections.heading: What should change in the first month, and what should not?
paragraphs: In four weeks you should see three things and no more: the student knows what she is being assessed on, she brings the agreed work to the session, and she can explain one topic she previously avoided. You should not see a transformed report card. Four weeks is roughly four to eight contact hours, which is not enough time to rebuild a year of shaky foundations, and any tutor suggesting otherwise is selling. If none of those three things has happened by week four, say so plainly rather than waiting politely for the term to end.

By one term you are looking for a changed working pattern. The student starts drafts before the deadline week instead of during it. Her internal assessment has a research question that her school teacher has approved rather than tolerated. Marks in school tests usually move at this point, though not evenly, and a student who was failing to finish papers often shows improvement in completion before she shows it in accuracy. That is normal and is a better early signal than the total.

Parents often ask us to send the best IB tutor in Powai, and the honest reply is that no such single person exists. There is a best match for a Diploma Programme Economics student in Hiranandani Gardens who is free on Thursday at seven, which is a narrower and far more answerable question. Over a full examination cycle the honest statement is that tutoring improves preparation, and preparation improves the odds. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and neither should any tutor you speak to. What we will do is tell you when we think the hours are not being used well, which sometimes means recommending fewer sessions in a subject that is fine and more in the one nobody wanted to discuss. A tutor who tells you in month two that your child needs a different kind of help is doing the job properly.

If it is not working, the replacement process is deliberately boring. Tell us, with one specific example rather than a general feeling. Common causes are a mismatch of pace, a tutor teaching the wrong board's approach to the same content, or simply a personality that a quiet fifteen-year-old will not talk to. We arrange a different match, hand over what the previous tutor recorded so the new one does not restart from zero, and keep the slot time if the new tutor's travel allows it. Nobody has to have an uncomfortable conversation with the outgoing tutor; that part is ours.

sections.heading: Starting with an IB home tutor in Powai this week
paragraphs: To get a useful shortlist back on the first attempt, send five things: the school and year group, the exact programme stage, the subjects in question, the society and tower, and two evening windows that genuinely work. The society name matters more here than anywhere else in Mumbai, because it decides which tutors can realistically reach you. Parents who send Powai and nothing else get a slower and worse match than parents who send Hiranandani Gardens, tower name, Thursday or Friday after half past six.

Have three documents ready for the first session: the most recent school report, the last two marked pieces of work, and your school's assessment calendar if it has been published. The report tells the tutor what the school thinks. The marked work tells her what is actually going wrong, which is usually narrower and more fixable. The calendar tells her how much runway there is. With those three on the table, a competent tutor can tell you at the end of the first hour what she thinks the problem is and what she would do about it over six weeks.

Internally we tag this kind of request as all IB and IGCSE subjects IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai, which is a clumsy label for a simple thing: a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families might ask about, one enquiry, any year group, and a shortlist of people who can get to your door. If your child is at the Middle Years Programme to Diploma Programme step, say so, because that is the transition where the right tutor matters most and the wrong one wastes a term.

One last practical note for this corridor. Ask for a start date, not a start week. A tutor who says she can begin Tuesday at seven and sends her identity details for the gate on Monday is a tutor who has thought about the journey. A tutor who says she will confirm closer to the time has not, and in Powai that difference shows up by the third lesson rather than the tenth.
bullets: Send school, year group, programme stage, subjects, society and two evening windows
Have the last report and two marked pieces of work ready for session one
Ask for a start date and the tutor's gate details, not a start week

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually travel to Powai for a 7pm weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, but which tutor depends entirely on where she starts from. Because Powai has no station, a 7pm start is reliable from Hiranandani Gardens, Chandivali or Kanjurmarg, workable from Ghatkopar, and genuinely difficult from Andheri East in the evening peak. We therefore shortlist by road distance rather than by credentials alone. If your preferred time is 7pm sharp on a weekday, ask us for a tutor inside the corridor and expect to wait a little longer for the match. If you can offer 8pm or a weekend morning, the pool widens considerably.

faqs.question: How does a tutor get through the gate at Hiranandani Gardens or Lodha Bellissimo?
faqs.answer: The same way any regular visitor does, and it is worth setting up once rather than weekly. Send your society office or gate desk the tutor's name, phone number and identity document before the first visit, and ask for her to be recorded as a standing weekly visitor rather than a one-off. In tower clusters such as Hiranandani Gardens, also tell her the tower name and the entrance, because the layout is large enough that the wrong gate costs fifteen minutes. Where clearance runs through a single visitor desk, a pre-listed tutor walks in and an unlisted one waits.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Powai depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and none of them is a published rate. Fees depend on the programme stage, whether the subject is taken at Higher Level or Standard Level, how scarce that specialist is in this corridor, the session length, and how far the tutor travels to reach you. A tutor living inside Powai who walks to your tower has no travel cost to recover; a Diploma Programme specialist coming across from Andheri East in the evening peak does. We do not publish figures because any number would be wrong for half the families asking. Settle the rate, the session length and the cancellation rule in writing before the first lesson.

faqs.question: Where in the home should the lesson actually happen?
faqs.answer: At a table in a shared room with the door open, not in a bedroom and not on a sofa. The dining table is the standard answer in most Powai flats and it works: hard surface, room for two sets of books, and enough household traffic that nobody is isolated. Keep the television off, keep phones out of reach rather than face down, and make sure there is a plug point for a laptop if the subject needs past papers on screen. If your flat is genuinely short of space, a society study room or library is a reasonable alternative, provided it is bookable at the same time each week.

faqs.question: Do I need to be at home while the session runs?
faqs.answer: Someone adult should be in the flat, particularly for the first few weeks and for younger students. You do not need to sit in the room, and hovering usually makes a teenager worse rather than better. What helps is being present enough to hear the tone of the hour and to catch the tutor for two minutes at the end. That two-minute handover is where you learn whether the agreed work was done, and it is far more useful than a monthly written report. For Primary Years Programme students, a parent nearby is not optional.

faqs.question: Does my child need Higher Level or Standard Level help first?
faqs.answer: Start with the subject where she is closest to losing the thread, which is not always the Higher Level one. Higher Level subjects demand unfamiliar application and sustained argument, so they consume more tutoring hours per improvement, but a Standard Level subject that has quietly collapsed will cost her more in the final total. The practical approach is to spend the first session diagnosing across both, then commit hours where the gap is widest rather than where the label looks most serious. Your Diploma Programme coordinator can confirm the current combination rules if changing a level is still an option.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one IB subject?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and you should be sceptical when the answer is an easy yes. Within a group, a strong tutor often handles two related subjects well. Across groups, a single tutor covering a science, a language and an essay subject at Higher Level is unusual and worth probing. For younger Primary Years Programme and Middle Years Programme students a single generalist is often the better arrangement, because consistency matters more than depth. For Diploma Programme students we would rather give you two specialists on different evenings than one person stretched across subjects she teaches at different standards.

faqs.question: Is online a real substitute when the Chandivali road is blocked?
faqs.answer: For a single session, yes, and that is exactly what it is best at. Agree at the start that a blocked road or a monsoon evening converts the lesson to an online one rather than cancelling it, and the term stops losing hours to weather. An IB online tutor in Powai can run worked problems and essay drafting on a shared screen effectively. What online does not replace is the accountability of someone arriving at the door, so use it as the fallback and the review slot rather than the main arrangement, especially for a student who has been drifting.

faqs.question: What happens if we miss a session during the Diploma Programme examination run?
faqs.answer: Tell the tutor as early as you can and agree in advance how missed lessons are handled, because in March and April there is very little spare capacity in Powai. Most tutors will reschedule a session cancelled with a day's notice and charge for one cancelled an hour before, which is reasonable given the travel involved. During school mock weeks, families often switch to shorter, more frequent online slots instead of the usual home hour, and that is a sensible adjustment rather than a downgrade. Put the rule in writing in the first week and neither side has to negotiate it under pressure.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Say so, with one specific example. Three sessions is enough to know whether a student will talk to this person, and not enough to know whether the teaching is working, so the useful complaint at that point is about fit rather than results. We arrange a replacement, pass on what the first tutor recorded about where your child actually is, and hold the same slot where the new tutor's travel allows it. You do not have to tell the outgoing tutor anything; that conversation is ours to have. Waiting a full term out of politeness is the expensive option.

faqs.question: How soon can an IB home tutor in Powai start?
faqs.answer: Usually within a week for common subjects, and two to three weeks for a scarce Higher Level specialist who also has to be reachable in this corridor. The limiting factor is almost never qualification; it is whether someone with the right subject already holds free evenings within reach of Powai. Sending your society name and two workable evening windows in the first message is what shortens this most. If your need is urgent, ask us for an online start while the home match is arranged, then move the lesson to your table once the right local tutor is confirmed.

faqs.question: Our neighbour's deadlines are different from ours. Why?
faqs.answer: Because internal deadlines are set by each school, not by the International Baccalaureate. Two Powai children in the same tower attending different schools can have internal assessment submission dates weeks apart, and school mock examinations rarely align either. This is why we ask for your school's own published assessment calendar at the first session instead of working from a general IB timetable. It is also why advice swapped at the gate is unreliable: the parent telling you there is no rush may be looking at a genuinely later deadline than yours.

sections.heading: How do you get an IB home tutor in Seven Bungalows into the house by next week?
paragraphs: Send one message with the child's year group, the IB programme they are in and the two or three subjects that are actually slipping. IB Gram comes back with a shortlist of tutors who already work this side of Andheri West, usually within a day. For most Seven Bungalows families the first session happens inside a week, and nothing is paid before you have met the person. The request we see most often is for all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Seven Bungalows can hold under one roof, which is sometimes one person and sometimes two.

What we ask for is deliberately short, because a long form filters out exactly the parents who are in a hurry. The year group and the programme tell us which assessment the child is sitting. The subject list tells us whether one tutor can hold the whole brief or whether two specialists should split the week. The slot you can realistically keep tells us more than anything else. A 5pm start works for a Middle Years Programme student who is home by half past four, while a Diploma Programme student who reaches Seven Bungalows at six needs 7pm, which is the hardest hour on this corridor and the reason some matches never settle into a routine.

Matching along the line, the way Khar pairs with Santacruz and Malad with Kandivali, is what survives a full term of home tuition.

sections.heading: Which IB years does a Seven Bungalows home tutor cover, PYP, MYP or DP?
paragraphs: All of them, from the Primary Years Programme (PYP) through the Middle Years Programme (MYP) to the Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1 to 12. What changes between them is what the tutor is actually for. In PYP the work is reading and number fluency. In MYP it is command terms and assessment criteria. In DP it is the architecture of the whole subject load plus the core, all with deadlines that collide. Our own listing line reads all IB and IGCSE subjects IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai, which is a clumsy way of saying one platform, both boards and every year group.

A PYP tutor in a Seven Bungalows flat is not there to drill worksheets. The vocabulary of a unit of inquiry is what trips a child who reads slowly, because a Year 4 student who cannot decode the question will never show what she knows about the answer. So the hour goes on reading aloud, on explaining a word before using it, on number sense rather than speed, and on getting a sentence out of the child before it goes on paper. Parents who expect a textbook and a red pen sometimes find this unfamiliar, and the tutor should be able to explain that choice in the first session.

MYP is when most Seven Bungalows parents first get in touch. Each subject group is assessed against published criteria grids, and a child who writes a clean paragraph can still score low because the paragraph answered a different command term from the one printed on the task sheet. Analyse, evaluate, justify and describe are not interchangeable, and a tutor's first job is often to read the task sheet with the student until the verb becomes visible. The Personal Project in the final MYP year is the first genuinely independent piece of work, with a process journal attached, and organisation rather than ability tends to decide how it lands.

DP is the heaviest brief in the house. A split of subjects between Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), an Internal Assessment (IA) attached to nearly every one, plus the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) running alongside. Do not take component weightings, paper counts or durations from any blog, this one included. The International Baccalaureate (IB) revises subject guides on its own cycle, so the current guide and the school's internal deadline calendar should come from the DP coordinator. Core and Extended tier choices sit on the IGCSE page in this set rather than here.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL decisions, and the internal assessments that follow
paragraphs: The decision that shapes two years is made in a few weeks at the end of Year 10 or the start of DP1: which subjects go to Higher Level and which stay at Standard Level. Each of them carries its own internal assessment, so the choice is not only about interest and university plans. It is about how many long independent pieces of writing a particular child can run at once.

The shape of the work differs sharply by subject group. A Group 4 science IA is an individual investigation: a research question narrow enough to be answerable, a method the student can actually run, and uncertainty treated honestly rather than hidden. A Mathematics exploration lives or dies on the question, and a well-presented piece built on a trivial question cannot be rescued late. Language A asks for close reading of specific texts rather than general literary opinion. Individuals and Societies IAs reward a tight source base over a wide one. Group 6 and the performing subjects run on process portfolios where the documentation is the assessment, not an afterthought.

Here is the collision a DP1 at a school like JBCN International School, Oshiwara actually meets. The Group 4 IA proposal is due in one fortnight. The TOK exhibition draft is due in the same fortnight. A Mathematics exploration topic is supposed to be chosen before the term ends, and there is a Language A assessment in between. Nothing in that list is unmanageable alone, and all four together is where a capable student stalls. A tutor who comes to the house twice a week in that period is doing triage as much as teaching, and the honest sequencing conversation matters more than another hour of content.

Subject scarcity is the other real constraint. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics, Business Management and English are well covered across the Western Suburbs, so a tutor for those can usually be in Seven Bungalows for a weekday evening. A less common HL subject, a second language at a high level or a specialist arts option may have very few tutors in Mumbai at all, and for those the honest answer is online with a specialist rather than a nearby generalist who will be learning the syllabus a week ahead of your child. We list tutors for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Seven Bungalows families ask about each term, and we will say plainly when the right answer is a screen rather than a doorbell.

sections.heading: Versova, Four Bungalows and Andheri West: the pool a Seven Bungalows family draws from
paragraphs: Almost every tutor who takes a standing weekday slot for IB home tuition in Seven Bungalows lives within about fifteen minutes of it, in Versova, Four Bungalows or Andheri West. That is the working radius. Beyond it, the match depends on the hour of the day rather than on the tutor, which is a bad foundation for a two-year programme. Parents who type IB tutors near me Seven Bungalows into a search box at 9pm usually mean something precise by it: somebody close enough to still be arriving on time in week nine.

Seven Bungalows sits at the far western edge of Andheri in Mumbai, Maharashtra, with the sea at one end of it and Link Road inland. The geography is simple once you stop reading the map as distance. Versova is the terminus of Metro Line 1 (Versova–Andheri–Ghatkopar), so a tutor coming from Andheri or even the Ghatkopar end has a rail option that ignores road traffic entirely, and that matters for weekend slots more than weekday ones. Link Road and the Western Express Highway carry everything north and south, and Metro Lines 2A and 7 (Dahisar–Andheri–Gundavali) have made the Dahisar and Borivali end reachable in a way it was not a few years ago. The Western Line (Bandra–Dahisar) remains the spine for anyone travelling up from Bandra, Khar or Santacruz.

What this means in practice is a rule we apply to every Seven Bungalows request. Match along the line, not across it. A tutor from Santacruz or Khar can hold a 7pm slot here for a whole term. A tutor who has to come from the eastern side of the city through the Andheri bottleneck will manage it brilliantly for three weeks and then start asking to shift the day. A tutor from Four Bungalows, a few minutes away, is the one who still turns up on the evening it rains, and across Mumbai that reliability is worth more to a DP2 student than a marginally more decorated CV.

Then there is the thing that is genuinely true of Seven Bungalows and not of its neighbours. It stays low-rise and residential right down to the Versova beach end, so parking is easy, and tutors who drive openly prefer it to Lokhandwala, where a 7pm arrival can mean ten minutes of circling before the hour even starts. A tutor who knows she can park on the lane will take a Seven Bungalows evening slot she would decline two kilometres away. Parents here get a wider pool for the same fee because of a parking fact, which is not an obvious advantage until you have lost a tutor over it.

sections.heading: What the school calendar in Seven Bungalows does to your evenings
paragraphs: Children here mostly travel a short way inland to school, and the two names that come up most in Seven Bungalows enquiries are JBCN International School, Oshiwara and Billabong High International School. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with either of them, or with any other school on this page. We name them because their calendars set the pressure points your evenings have to absorb.

The daily shape is predictable. A child in the MYP years is usually home between four and half past, tired but still able to work, which makes a 5pm or half past five start the easiest hour of the week to protect. DP students come home later, often closer to six, and then need to eat before anything useful happens. That is why 7pm is the most requested home tuition slot in Seven Bungalows and the one that fills first every term. If your child's realistic hour is 7pm on a Tuesday, say so in the first message rather than after two tutors have already been matched.

The annual shape matters more. October and November are when internal assessment drafts and school examinations stack up against each other. February and March are mock season, and the mock result is the one that produces the panicked search for a tutor. April and May belong to the May examination series, by which point adding a new subject tutor is damage control rather than teaching. The quietest and most productive months are June through September, which is precisely when almost nobody calls. A family that starts home classes in July pays the same as a family that starts in February and gets three times the room to work in.

Ask the school for the internal deadline calendar and put it where everyone can see it. A tutor who plans against the school's own dates stops guessing. What a tutor should not be doing is repeating the school lesson with a different voice. The useful version takes the teacher's feedback sheet, identifies the two criteria that keep losing marks, and works on those until the next piece of work comes back different.

sections.heading: Home classes, online or hybrid for an IB student in Seven Bungalows?
paragraphs: Start with home. In this locality the case for an IB home tutor in Seven Bungalows is unusually strong, because the travel that makes home tuition expensive elsewhere in Mumbai is cheap here. Easy parking and a short ride from Versova or Four Bungalows mean the tutor spends the hour teaching rather than recovering from the journey, and a tired tutor teaches a worse lesson than a fresh one.

Home classes also solve things a screen cannot. A tutor in the room sees the page the student is actually writing on, spots the handwriting that slows down when confidence drops, and can take a worked example away to mark. For a child who quietly stops paying attention after twenty minutes, physical presence is the intervention. The honest cost is rigidity: a home slot is a fixed hour on a fixed day in a fixed flat, and when the child has a school trip or the tutor has a family emergency, that hour is simply lost.

Online is better in specific situations, and pretending otherwise wastes everybody's time. An IB online tutor in Seven Bungalows can be the right call for a scarce Higher Level subject, for intensive exam-season sessions where you want three short meetings rather than one long one, for the monsoon weeks when nobody should be on the road at 7pm, and for a student who is travelling. Screen sharing a worked solution is genuinely good now. What online loses is the unprompted glance at the page and the informal five minutes after the hour, which is often where the real question appears.

The pattern that holds best over a term is hybrid: one longer home session a week for the teaching, plus a shorter online checkpoint before a deadline. That keeps the fixed hour that gives the week its shape and adds flexibility where it is needed. Whichever mode you choose, agree it in writing before the first session, along with what happens to a missed hour, because that one unanswered question causes more ended matches than teaching quality ever does.

Home classes catch the slowing handwriting and the quiet drift at minute twenty

sections.heading: How does IB Gram check a home tutor in Mumbai before you meet them?
paragraphs: Every tutor is checked on four things before being listed: identity with a government photo document, the degree or qualification claimed, demonstrated experience with the specific board and programme, and references from families or schools they have worked with. A profile that cannot clear all four does not go up. Before an IB home tutor in Seven Bungalows is sent to you, somebody has read that profile against your actual request.

Board experience is the check that matters most and the one parents under-weight. A brilliant university graduate who has never seen an MYP criterion grid or an IA moderation comment will teach excellent content and still leave your child losing the same marks. We ask tutors which syllabus versions they have taught, which internal assessments they have supervised, and what they do when a student's draft is strong on content and weak against the criteria. Vague answers are the signal.

Then there is the part only you can do, in the first forty minutes, in your own living room. Ask the tutor to explain the difference between analyse and evaluate as the mark scheme uses them. Ask which criterion your child is losing marks against and how they know. Ask to see the current subject guide on their phone or laptop, and watch whether they reach for it comfortably. Ask what they will do in the first three sessions. A tutor who answers those four clearly is almost always worth keeping, whatever else the profile says. Parents often ask who the best IB tutor in Seven Bungalows is, and the only useful version of that answer is the person whose replies to those four questions are specific rather than reassuring.

One warning sign is worth stating plainly. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because no honest tutor can offer one. IB Gram does not guarantee grades either, and anybody selling an outcome is selling something they do not control. A good tutor will tell you what they think is achievable and what would have to change for it, and they will say it before you have paid for a month. The same goes for anyone claiming an inside relationship with a school: IB Gram is independent and not affiliated with the schools named here, and you should treat such claims from anybody as a reason to ask more questions.

Ask which syllabus versions and which internal assessments they have supervised

sections.heading: Why the same 7pm slot every week decides whether IB home tuition in Seven Bungalows works
paragraphs: The single best predictor of whether home tuition helps is not the tutor's qualification. It is whether the slot survives. A fixed Tuesday and Thursday at 7pm that holds for eleven weeks beats a better tutor whose slot moves three times, because IB work is cumulative and a moved session breaks the chain between the draft and the feedback on it.

Slots break for boring reasons, nearly all of them geographic. The tutor took a second family on the far side of Andheri West and now arrives at a quarter past. The 6pm crossing got worse after the monsoon dug up a stretch of road. The tutor's own commute changed and the Western Express Highway leg now takes twenty minutes longer than it did in June. This is why we match inside the Versova pocket wherever possible and why the easy parking in Seven Bungalows matters so much: a tutor who can stop on the lane and walk up has removed the most common ten minutes of slippage before it happens. An IB home tutor in Seven Bungalows who lives in Four Bungalows is simply more likely to still be arriving on time in week nine.

Look at an evening from the tutor's side and the economics become obvious. An hour of teaching in Seven Bungalows costs a nearby tutor perhaps twenty-five minutes of travel in total. The same hour in a locality where she has to circle for parking can cost her an hour of road. A tutor with a finite week sells that hour to whoever wastes least of her evening, which is why families here get access to tutors who have stopped taking work in harder-to-reach pockets. It also explains why two tutors with identical qualifications quote differently for the same subject. An IB private tutor Seven Bungalows families book for a fixed 7pm Tuesday is pricing the whole evening, not the hour you see.

Which brings us to money. IB tuition fees in Seven Bungalows depend on a short list of things: the board and the level, because HL and IA supervision demand more preparation than SL revision; the scarcity of the subject, since a rare Higher Level option has fewer tutors in Mumbai bidding for the work; travel distance and the hour, because a 7pm weekday slot across the suburb is the most expensive hour in anyone's week; session length and frequency, where two shorter sessions usually cost more than one long one; and the time of year, as February and April demand is simply higher than July demand. Ask for the rate per session in writing, ask whether travel is inside it, and ask what a cancellation costs. A tutor who will not answer those three questions before the first session is telling you something useful.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at grades, and a tutor who points at a grade after four weeks is either lucky or managing you. What should have changed is behaviour. The child starts homework without a negotiation. She can say out loud what a task is asking for before writing. The blank-page stall at the start of a question is shorter. A draft exists where previously there was an intention to draft. If none of that has moved in four weeks of home classes, something is wrong with the match and not with the child.

By the end of a term there should be a piece of marked work to argue about. The useful signal is the type of comment on it: feedback about depth, evidence and criteria rather than feedback saying the student has missed the point. A mock result may move or may not, because mocks are deliberately hard and sometimes land mid-repair. What should be visible is a student who knows which two criteria she loses marks on and can explain what she is doing about them.

Across a full exam cycle the honest picture depends heavily on when you started. A DP1 student who begins home tuition in August has two years of room. A DP2 student who starts in January has one mock and a handful of weeks, and the realistic aim is consolidation of what is nearly there rather than repair of a two-year gap. We will say so at the point of matching. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, we do not publish outcome claims, and no honest tutor will promise a specific point score for your child. Every IB tutor Mumbai families meet through this platform is told that rule before being listed.

If it is not working, say it early. The two-week question exists so that you do not spend a term being polite. Tell us what is wrong in concrete terms, because the fix differs: a pace mismatch is often solved by the same tutor changing approach, while a personality mismatch almost never is. A replacement is arranged from the existing Seven Bungalows shortlist, your subject brief and school context carry over, and you do not pay twice for the same first session.

sections.heading: Getting started in Seven Bungalows: what to have ready for home classes
paragraphs: Send four things and you will get a usable shortlist the same day: the year group and programme, the subjects that are slipping, the two or three evening slots you can actually protect, and one sentence about what triggered the search. That last sentence does more work than the rest. A mock result, a teacher's comment, a missed IA deadline and a child who has gone quiet all need different tutors. A single home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents hope exists rarely does at Higher Level, so tell us which two subjects matter most.

Before the first session, put three documents in one place. The last two pieces of marked work, with the teacher's comments still on them. The school's internal deadline list for the term. The current subject guide if the school has shared it. A tutor who can read those in the first ten minutes skips a fortnight of diagnosis. Also sort the room: a table, a chair at the right height and a lamp beat a sofa, and the dining table with the television off beats a bedroom where a sibling is practising piano.

The first home tuition session is diagnostic and should feel like it. Expect the tutor to work through a piece of recent marked work, ask the student to attempt something unseen, find the exact point where understanding stops, and leave with a plan for the next three sessions rather than a package. You should hear what the plan is before the tutor leaves the building, and so should your child.

Your job in the first month is light but not optional. Be at home for the first session or two, then step back. Protect the slot against everything except illness. Read the tutor's session notes rather than asking the child how it went, because an eleven-year-old will say fine about anything. And answer the two-week question honestly, which is the one thing that lets us fix a mediocre match before it costs a term.

faqs.answer: For a strong, self-managing student, yes, and for a scarce subject it is often better than the local alternative. Screen sharing a worked solution, annotating a draft live and recording a session for revision all work well now. Where online struggles is with a student who drifts without a person in the room, or who needs the informal five minutes after the hour when the real question finally surfaces. faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Tell us immediately, and be specific about what has not moved. Four weeks is enough to see behaviour change even when marks have not: homework started without an argument, shorter stalls, a draft that exists. sections.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: which rung is your child actually on?
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) is three programmes bolted into one ladder, and families in Sewri routinely ask for help on the wrong rung. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs through the early years and sets no external examinations. What it does carry is a transdisciplinary structure and a reporting style that reads strangely to a parent who grew up with marks out of a hundred. Support at this stage is about reading comprehension, number sense and written explanation, not revision.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers the middle school years and is assessed against published criteria for each subject rather than a single percentage. A child can be strong on one criterion and weak on another inside the same subject, which is why a good home tutor in Sewri asks to see the criterion-level feedback before deciding what to teach. The personal project lands near the end of the programme and needs planning and scheduling help far more than it needs subject coaching.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two years that shape university applications. Each subject is taken at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL), and the difference is not simply more chapters: HL adds depth and a different style of question. Your school's DP coordinator holds the current subject combinations and the internal deadlines, and the official subject guide for each course is where the assessment structure actually lives. Those guides are revised on the IB's cycle, not ours, so read this year's.

Families get hurt at the transition. A child moving from MYP into DP1 at JBCN International School, Parel, or at any of Mumbai's island-city schools, meets a step change in writing expectation inside the first term, and the report that reflects it arrives in October or November. IB home tuition in Sewri booked in that window is remedial work on a deadline. Booked in the term before, the same tutor is doing preparation, and it costs the family fewer weeks of panic.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and the assessment each subject carries
paragraphs: Subject choice is where island-city families spend the least time and lose the most ground. A child who picks a Higher Level subject because a friend did, or drops one because of a single bad test, is making a two-year decision in an afternoon. Our listing covers all IB and IGCSE subjects and a tutor in Sewri is matched per subject, not per child, so a DP2 student can run Chemistry with one tutor and Mathematics with another without either pretending to cover both.

Every DP subject carries an internally assessed component, and each one fails differently. A science IA is an individual investigation the student designs, so the risk is a research question too broad to answer in the pages available. A Mathematics exploration is a written piece on a chosen topic, where the risk is picking something with no mathematics in it. Language A courses carry written tasks and an oral; Economics and Business carry commentaries or a research project. Ask the teacher for this year's criteria sheet.

Then there is the core. The Extended Essay (EE) is an independent research piece supervised inside the school, and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) carries an exhibition and an essay. Neither is a timetabled subject, so neither competes for attention the way Chemistry does, and both go wrong quietly. A DP1 student in Sewri who has not settled an EE topic by the end of the monsoon term has failed nothing yet, but she has spent the easiest planning window she will get.

Scarcity is real and it is subject-shaped. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English have a deep pool across South Mumbai. A second language at Higher Level, Computer Science, Psychology or Visual Arts narrows that pool sharply, and that is the case where IB home classes in Sewri sensibly become hybrid: a local tutor for the weekly table session and a specialist online for the assessed work. Pretending a generalist covers Visual Arts produces a pleasant match and a poor portfolio.

Sewri station matters more to the tutor than to the student. Someone living near Dockyard Road or Wadala can be at your gate in a quarter of an hour without touching a main road, which is why we weight rail access heavily when we shortlist. Parel has filled with office towers over the past decade, which cuts both ways: more qualified people live within ten minutes of you than did in 2010, and the 6pm to 8pm road load through Parel is heavier than the distance suggests.

What is new is the eastern edge. Sewri is now the island-city end of the Atal Setu, so Navi Mumbai sits a bridge away instead of a creek away, and a tutor in Vashi or Nerul can reach Sewri for a Saturday morning session in a way that was not practical before. Weekday evenings we still match inside the island. For a scarce subject the bridge has genuinely widened the pool, and the section further down explains how to use it.

sections.heading: The school calendar Sewri families actually live by
paragraphs: Children on this corridor are bussed, driven or taken by train to international schools across the island city. JBCN International School, Parel is the nearest IB and IGCSE campus for much of Sewri, and Bombay International School draws families from the western half of South Mumbai. Both run a calendar that has nothing to do with the state board year, and that calendar sets your tuition timetable whether or not anyone planned for it.

The year opens in June with the monsoon term and the first assessments that count land in August. October and November are the hardest fortnight in a DP student's year: school internal examinations, IA drafts and the TOK essay converge, and a Mumbai school layers its own mock timetable on top of all three. January and February belong to final IA submissions and mocks. By May, when external examinations run, tuition is triage and not teaching, and good tutors say so in October.

School-set deadlines sit earlier than the official ones, deliberately, because a coordinator needs time to check and upload work. A parent working backwards from a published date is already a fortnight late. Ask the examinations officer or the DP coordinator for the internal deadline sheet in June, and hand a copy to your home tutor in the first session. A tutor holding that sheet plans a term; a tutor without it reacts week to week and charges you for the difference.

The second calendar nobody mentions is travel. School buses on this corridor return later as the term wears on, through Parel and Wadala evening traffic, so a 6pm start that looked comfortable in June is a 6.40pm scramble by August. Build the slot at 7pm and keep it there. sections.heading: Home tuition, online or a mix: what works in Sewri at 7pm?
paragraphs: Home tuition wins on a weekday evening here, and online wins for a scarce subject or an exam-season intensive. An IB home tutor in Sewri gets a child already at the table, a phone that can be left in another room, and a parent close enough to hear whether anything is happening. At 7pm on a Tuesday that is worth a great deal, because the alternative is a tired fifteen-year-old negotiating with a screen.

Building access is the part that actually breaks schedules. This corridor mixes older low-rise blocks with newer redevelopment towers, and the two behave differently at the gate: the older buildings need a word with the watchman and nothing more, while the newer towers want the tutor's name left at the building office so a standing weekly entry is pre-approved instead of argued each week. Do that once in week one. A tutor held eleven minutes at the gate loses a quarter of the session.

Where the lesson happens matters more than parents expect. A dining table with the television off beats a bedroom desk behind a closed door, especially for MYP work where the tutor needs to see rough working as it happens. A DP Physics or Chemistry session wants a flat surface, a plug point and nobody walking through. If the flat genuinely has no quiet corner at that hour, say so on the call and we will match an online specialist rather than send someone into a room where work cannot happen.

Hybrid is what most DP families on this corridor settle into by the second term: one home visit a week for teaching, one short online session for draft feedback, where sharing a screen beats reading over a shoulder. An IB online tutor in Sewri also answers the monsoon problem, because the week the roads flood is the week a standing slot is lost. Online is weaker for a child who drifts without an adult in the room, and for anything with hand-drawn working.

sections.heading: How are IB tutors in Mumbai checked before they reach your door?
paragraphs: Every tutor submits identity proof, degree documents and a teaching history we check by reference before any profile reaches a parent in Mumbai, Maharashtra. Before an IB home tutor in Sewri is put in front of you we also confirm the narrow thing you are hiring for: not that the person teaches science, but that they have taught this subject at this level recently and have seen IA work that a school has already marked and commented on.

Three separate things are verified and they are often confused. Identity, so you know who is entering your flat. Qualification, so the degree is real and in the subject claimed. Recent teaching, because a syllabus revision leaves a tutor who last taught the course four years ago subtly out of date in ways a parent cannot spot. We also record which boards each tutor works across, since many Mumbai tutors teach both IB and IGCSE, and we note where they are strongest.

Your own checks matter more than ours and they take one phone call. Ask which year groups the tutor taught last term. Ask to see a piece of written feedback they gave on a student's draft with the name removed. Ask how they would handle a criterion-level comment the family does not understand. Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade, or who answers a syllabus question confidently without once referring to the current subject guide.

What verification cannot do is predict whether a tutor and a fifteen-year-old will work together. We do not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor does either. What we can do is keep the first two sessions low-risk and the swap fast. An IB private tutor Sewri parents hire through this platform is replaceable without an argument or a penalty, and that matters more than any rating, because the usual failure is not incompetence but mismatch.

sections.heading: The Atal Setu changed who counts as a local tutor in Sewri
paragraphs: Sewri is now the island-city end of the Atal Setu, and that one piece of concrete has quietly changed the matching maths for families here. For two decades the Sewri tutor pool was the island and nothing else: Wadala, Mazgaon, Parel, Dadar, Worli. Navi Mumbai was a creek and an hour away and never entered the conversation. The bridge lands on your side of the water, so a tutor in Vashi, Nerul or Belapur is now a bridge run rather than an expedition.

It does not change your Tuesday. A weekday 7pm slot still needs someone who can be at the building by 6.55pm after their own working day, and no bridge makes a 6pm departure from Belapur reliable in the evening peak. What it changes is the weekend and the scarce subject. A Saturday morning double session with a specialist who lives in Navi Mumbai is now a sane arrangement, and so is a fortnightly in-person review of an IA with a tutor who is otherwise online.

Take a DP1 student in Sewri sitting Economics at Higher Level, with an IA commentary due in the same fortnight as her school internal examinations. The deep Economics HL pool in South Mumbai is small and fully booked by October. Before the bridge, her realistic options were an online specialist she had never met or a nearby generalist. Now the shortlist can hold a Navi Mumbai tutor for two consecutive Saturdays while the Wednesday slot stays with a tutor from Parel. Two tutors by design, not a failed match.

Use the bridge deliberately and it buys specialists. Use it carelessly and it buys cancellations, because a tutor who agreed to cross for a weekday evening starts arriving late in week three and apologetic in week five. When we shortlist across the Atal Setu we say so on the profile, we put that slot on a weekend, and we name which tutor is the local anchor. Families who treat the bridge as a weekend widening of the pool keep their tutors for a full year.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks, do not look at marks. Look at whether your child can explain what the tutor did last week without being prompted, whether homework is attempted before the session instead of during it, and whether the tutor has told you something about your child's work you did not already know. If all three are missing after four sessions, the match is wrong and waiting another month will not repair it.

One term in, the evidence sits in the written work. A science IA draft with a defensible method. A Mathematics exploration with a question narrow enough to answer properly. An essay that answers the question asked rather than the one the child wanted. School report comments are a lagging indicator: an October report describes work done in August. Ask the tutor in week eight what they expect that report to say, because a tutor who guesses wrong is not reading the work closely enough.

Across a full cycle the honest picture is that tutoring changes the rate of improvement and the quality of what gets submitted, while results depend on a dozen things no tutor controls: sleep, the school's own teaching, which question comes up, moderation. We do not guarantee grades and we will not publish a success rate. Anyone offering either is telling you about their marketing rather than their teaching, and in Mumbai that pitch is common enough to be worth recognising.

IB tuition fees in Sewri depend on a short list of things, none of which is a published price. Board and level, because Higher Level DP work is scarcer to supply than MYP support. Subject scarcity, because a second language or Computer Science specialist has fewer alternatives. Travel distance and time of day, since a 7pm island slot costs a tutor more of their evening than a 4pm one. And session length and frequency, which is the one lever entirely in your hands.

sections.heading: Starting IB home tuition in Sewri this month
paragraphs: Three things make the first session useful and all three take ten minutes to find. The last school report, including the comments nobody reads. One recent piece of marked work, ideally with the teacher's annotations still on it. And the school's internal deadline sheet for the term, which the examinations officer or the DP coordinator holds. A tutor who walks in with those three has a plan by the end of the first hour instead of the end of the first month.

Decide the slot before you decide the tutor. Pick the two evenings you can genuinely protect for a whole term, including the fortnight when a school production or a football season eats one of them. A standing 7pm Tuesday that survives October is worth more than a flexible arrangement that quietly dies in August. Tell us both evenings and we shortlist against them, rather than asking a family in Sewri to bend around a tutor's existing calendar.

The first session is a diagnostic. The tutor reads the report, looks at the marked work, sets one short piece to see how your child writes with no pressure on it, and then tells you in front of you what the gap is and what the first month will cover. You should hear something specific: a criterion, a paper-style question, a method half-learned and never corrected. If you hear general reassurance instead, ask the question again.

After that, ask for a line a week. Not a report, a line: what we did, what is set, what I am watching. Parents who get that line stay on top of a DP year without hovering over it. If the line stops arriving, the engagement has gone quiet, and that is your early warning rather than the next report. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families find through us is expected to send it.

faqs.answer: There is no single rate, and anyone quoting one before hearing the subject is guessing. The number depends on board and level, since Higher Level DP teaching is scarcer than MYP support, on subject scarcity, on how far the tutor travels and at what hour, and on session length and frequency. faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor already lives inside the island city. Home tuition at 7pm works when a tutor comes from Wadala, Mazgaon, Parel or Dadar, because those are short runs that do not depend on a clear main road. faqs.question: How does a tutor get past my building security for a weekly session?
faqs.answer: Leave the tutor's name and phone number at the building office in the first week and ask for a standing weekly entry rather than a fresh visitor pass each time. Older blocks along this corridor need only a word with the watchman. Newer redevelopment towers log every visitor and will keep a tutor waiting at the gate if nothing is on file, which costs a quarter of a session in lift queues and phone calls. Settle it once, tell the tutor which entrance to use, and the slot stops being an argument at the gate.

faqs.question: Which schools do the children you work with in Sewri attend?
faqs.answer: Families on this corridor are spread across the island city's international schools, with JBCN International School, Parel the closest IB and IGCSE campus for much of Sewri and Bombay International School drawing from the western half of South Mumbai. Others travel further for a specific programme. We name schools only as local context: IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of them. What matters practically is the internal deadline sheet, because each school sets its own dates and those dates drive your tuition plan.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP, not DP. Is a tutor premature?
faqs.answer: No, but the work is different and you should expect different output. MYP support is about criterion-level weakness: a child who can do the science but cannot write the evaluation, or who reads well and plans badly. A tutor should be reading your child's criterion feedback and teaching to the weak strand, not running ahead into DP content. Starting in MYP also means the transition into DP1 arrives with the writing habits already in place, which is where island-city families most often find the gap too wide to close in one term.

faqs.question: How soon can IB home tuition in Sewri start after I enquire?
faqs.answer: Usually within a week, sometimes within two or three days outside the October and January crunch. The shortlist takes a day or so to build, you need an evening to make the calls, and the tutor needs one clear slot in their week that matches one of your protected evenings. The slow cases are scarce subjects and peak season: a Higher Level Economics or second-language specialist in October may genuinely have nothing free until a weekend, and we would rather tell you that than fill the slot with the wrong person.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after a month?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we re-match, usually inside a week. You do not owe anyone an explanation, though a sentence about what went wrong makes the next match better: wrong level, wrong pace, too much talking, no written feedback. A month is actually late for this call. By session two you already know whether your child answers questions or waits them out, and the swap is cheapest then. There are no packages to unwind and nothing to argue about, because a mismatch is a normal outcome rather than a failure.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for an IB student?
faqs.answer: It works well for some things and badly for others. Online is strong for IA and essay drafts, where a shared screen beats reading over a shoulder, and for scarce subjects where the right specialist does not live in South Mumbai. It is weak for a child who drifts the moment nobody is in the room, and for subjects with heavy hand-drawn working, where the tutor needs to watch the pen move. Most DP families on this corridor end up hybrid: one session at home each week and one online for feedback.

faqs.question: Can a Navi Mumbai tutor really come across the Atal Setu for us?
faqs.answer: For a weekend session, yes, and that is new. Sewri sits at the island-city end of the Atal Setu, so Vashi, Nerul and Belapur are now a bridge run rather than an hour around the creek. For a Saturday morning double session with a scarce-subject specialist it holds up well. For a weekday 7pm slot we still match inside the island, because a tutor leaving Navi Mumbai at 6pm in the evening peak will be late often enough to cost you the slot by the third week.

faqs.question: Who should help with the Extended Essay and TOK, the school or a tutor?
faqs.answer: The school owns both, and it should stay that way. Your child has an EE supervisor inside the school and a TOK teacher, and their guidance is the one that counts at submission. A tutor's useful role is scheduling and structure: holding the student to a topic decision early, reading a draft for argument rather than content, and asking the awkward question about whether the research question can be answered in the length allowed. A tutor who starts rewriting an EE is creating an academic honesty problem, not solving a writing one.

faqs.question: Do you cover Wadala, Mazgaon and Parel as well as Sewri?
faqs.answer: Yes. Those four places are matched as one pool, because the short links between them and the Harbour Line make the evening run practical in either direction. A tutor living in Wadala may teach two students in Sewri and one in Parel on the same evening. Searches like IB tutors near me in Sewri surface the same people as a Parel search for that reason. What changes between them is parking and gate protocol rather than travel time, and the tutor adapts to whichever building you are in.

sections.heading: Which IB programme is your child in, and what does that change?
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) is three different jobs wearing one name, and the answer changes completely depending on which one your child is in. In the Primary Years Programme (PYP), roughly Years 1 to 5, useful tutoring looks like reading fluency, number sense and the confidence to explain an answer out loud, not worksheet drilling. In the Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 6 to 10, each subject is marked against published criteria rather than a single percentage, so a child can write pages and still lose marks for never answering the command term. In the Diploma Programme (DP), Years 11 and 12, the structure hardens into Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices, the Internal Assessment (IA) in every subject, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK).

That matters for staffing on this belt. A PYP request can often be filled by a tutor living in Virar or Nallasopara who teaches primary across several boards. A DP Chemistry HL request cannot, because the pool of people who have actually marked that coursework is small and most of them live south of Dahisar. Parents of MYP children get the widest choice and the least urgency, which is exactly the window in which to start, rather than waiting for the DP year when every competent subject specialist in the Western Suburbs is already booked at 7pm.

Do not take programme structure from a page like this one, including ours. The IB revises subject guides on its own cycle, so component names, submission routes and the balance between coursework and examinations change between cohorts. Ask your school's IB coordinator for the guide that applies to your child's session year and for the school's own internal deadline calendar, which is almost always earlier than the official one. A good tutor will ask for both documents in the first week and plan backwards from the school's dates, not from a generic revision timetable.
