sections.heading: Choosing subjects and levels with a tutor who knows the Mumbai schools
paragraphs: IB Gram lists tutors across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Vasai can realistically cover, and the register is organised the way a parent searches: all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Vasai families ask for, grouped by programme stage rather than by board. The part parents underestimate is the level decision rather than the subject itself. A DP student taking Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level because an engineering application might need it, when the rest of their week is languages and humanities, will spend two years defending that choice. The honest version of subject advice names the trade-off: what the course demands weekly, what the Internal Assessment in it asks a student to produce alone, and whether your child has the self-starting habit that coursework rewards. An IB home tutor in Vasai who has supervised that coursework will tell you in the first month whether the level is right, which is the single most valuable thing they do.

Subject by subject, the work looks different. In the sciences the IA is an individual investigation, so the bottleneck is usually picking a question narrow enough to measure at home or in a school lab, not the write-up. In Economics and Business Management the commentary work rewards a student who reads one business story properly rather than skimming ten. In Visual Arts the comparative study is a research document, which surprises families who thought the subject was studio time. In a Language B course the individual oral is a conversation under conditions, and no amount of vocabulary lists substitutes for speaking practice with an adult who will not switch to English when the student stalls.

Across every subject, the fixable problem is almost never knowledge. It is that the student has not been shown what the marker is looking for in the specific thing they are writing. A tutor who has read the current assessment criteria can take a Year 11 lab report and show, line by line, where a sentence described a result instead of evaluating it. That is a two-session fix. Rebuilding three years of missing algebra is not, and a tutor who says otherwise in the first phone call is selling you something. We publish the subject list rather than a promise about any of it.

sections.heading: The school calendar Vasai families plan around
paragraphs: Most IB families on this belt are already commuting for school before anyone mentions tutoring. Children from Vasai travel south to campuses like Singapore International School in Dahisar East or JBCN International School, Borivali, which means a long train or bus leg each way and a child who walks in at five o'clock with a bag and no appetite for anything. That is the real reason evening slots here start later than they do in Powai or Bandra. A tutor who proposes six o'clock has not met the commute; one who proposes seven and keeps the session to a focused stretch rather than a marathon has.

The school year in Mumbai runs from June or July to March or April, and the pressure points are predictable even though the exact dates are not. The first stretch after the monsoon break is when MYP criteria assessments stack up. The weeks after the winter break are mock season, and for DP2 students that is also when Internal Assessment drafts and the Extended Essay meet in the same fortnight. By February the useful work is past papers and timing rather than new content. Ask your school's examinations officer or IB coordinator for the internal deadline sheet, since schools set their own dates well ahead of the official ones and those are the dates that actually govern your term.

Naming schools here is local context and nothing more. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Singapore International School, with JBCN International School, Borivali, or with any other school named on this page, and no tutor on the register speaks for a school. What a tutor can do is read that school's assessment calendar, work out which fortnight is going to hurt, and move the heavy sessions earlier. Families who book in June for a February problem get the tutor they want. Families who call in February take whoever is left on the belt.

sections.heading: Should you start with online lessons or hold out for IB home tuition in Vasai?
paragraphs: Start online, add home sessions before the exam stretch. That is not a sales line, it is what works on this belt. IB home tutoring in Vasai is the service most parents here ask for and it is the one we lead with, but a weekday evening slot in Vasai is genuinely hard to staff, because a tutor living south of the creek spends longer travelling than teaching. Families who insist on home-only from day one often wait weeks for a match, then lose it when the tutor's own schedule shifts. Families who begin with two online lessons a week secure a specialist immediately and convert to in-person sessions as the assessment calendar tightens.

In-person work earns its place in specific situations. A younger child who needs someone to sit beside them and watch the pencil. A student who will not open a laptop without opening six other tabs. Practical subjects where a tutor needs to see the apparatus or the sketchbook. A DP2 student in the last term before exams, working through papers under timed conditions with an adult in the room. For those, home classes are worth the scheduling fight and worth paying the travel premium that any honest tutor will include.

Online has real advantages here that nobody admits. An IB online tutor in Vasai is drawn from the whole of Mumbai rather than from a radius around Vasai Road, so a DP Economics HL specialist in Chembur is suddenly available, and an IB tutor Mumbai parents would otherwise never reach this far north becomes bookable on a Tuesday. Sessions survive the monsoon. A recorded screen of worked solutions can be rewatched the night before a test. The honest trade-offs are also real: a tired child hides more easily behind a screen, handwriting under timed conditions goes unchecked, and younger students drift without a parent nearby for the first ten minutes. The hybrid pattern most families here settle into is online midweek and one longer in-person block at the weekend.

sections.heading: How are tutors checked before they ring your doorbell in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Every tutor on the register has given photo identification, proof of the degree they claim, and a specific account of which IB programme stages and subjects they have taught, with the years. Where a tutor has worked with a school, that is recorded as their own employment history and nothing more. Where they claim coursework supervision, we ask which criteria they worked from. An IB home tutor in Vasai who cannot name the assessment criteria for the subject they are applying to teach does not reach a shortlist, because that is the part a parent cannot verify later from a conversation at the door.

There is a second layer of checking that only you can do, and it takes one phone call. Parents searching for the best IB tutor in Vasai are really asking two questions at once, competence and reliable availability, and ten minutes on the phone answers both. Ask which syllabus year they last taught the subject in, and listen for a specific answer. Ask them to talk you through one past paper question in the subject your child is struggling with, out loud, on the call. Ask what they would do in the first session, and be sceptical of anyone who says they will begin with a test and nothing else. Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade, because no honest tutor offers a guaranteed grade and the ones who do are usually the ones who vanish in February.

An IB private tutor Vasai families hire through a neighbour may well be excellent, but nobody has seen the certificate and there is no record when a session is cut short. On the practical side, keep the arrangement inside the platform. Pay through IB Gram so a missed or cut-short session is traceable rather than a disagreement over a cash figure. Keep the first few sessions in a room where an adult passes through. Expect the tutor to carry identification and to be willing to show it at your society gate, and expect them to register in the visitors book like anybody else. If something is off, say so the same week. Changing tutors in week two costs nothing; changing in month four costs your child a term.

sections.heading: What really happens when an IB home tutor in Vasai arrives at 7pm?
paragraphs: A tutor booked for seven o'clock in Vasai leaves earlier than you think. If they live on the belt, they are walking or taking a short autorickshaw ride and the risk is small. If they are coming up from Dahisar or Borivali, they are on a slow local around six, standing, with a bag of past papers, and a single signal failure between Mira Road and Naigaon turns a lesson into a phone call. This is the real reason IB home classes in Vasai are scarce rather than expensive: the time cost falls on the tutor, who is giving up the two sessions they could have taught closer to home. Anyone who understands that will schedule you a tutor from the belt, or schedule a weekend.

Then there is the building. A tutor reaching your gate for the first time will be stopped, asked who they are visiting, and asked to write a flat number in a register, and in many Vasai buildings the watchman will call up before letting them in. That takes a few minutes the first week and almost none after, as long as somebody at home knows a tutor is expected. A standing weekly slot works better when you tell the gate once that the same person comes every Tuesday. Add the lift, which in a seven-storey building at seven in the evening is carrying groceries and school bags, and the session that starts at seven sharp really starts at ten past unless the tutor budgets for it.

Inside the flat, the study space decides half the outcome. The dining table with the television off beats a bedroom desk facing a window onto the road, and both beat the sofa. A plug point within reach matters more than parents expect, since a tutor will want a tablet or laptop for past papers. On the creek side of Vasai the mosquitoes arrive at the same time as the tutor, so a coil or a closed window buys a better second half of the session. In July and August, when the Vasai Road subway floods and trains slow to a crawl, the sensible plan is agreed in advance: the slot moves online that week rather than being cancelled, and the in-person block is made up on a Saturday.

The last constraint is the journey home, and it is the one no other part of Mumbai teaches you to think about. A tutor finishing at half past eight in Vasai still has to get back, and a tutor who lives south of the creek will be home close to ten. That is why the realistic shapes for this belt are a tutor who already lives between Bhayandar and Virar, a weekend block of two longer sessions, or an online midweek pattern with in-person work concentrated in the weeks before mocks and exams. Pick the shape first, then the tutor. Picking the tutor first and hoping the logistics bend is the mistake that costs families a month.

sections.heading: What four weeks, one term and one exam cycle should look like
paragraphs: At four weeks you should have evidence, not a feeling. The tutor should be able to name the specific gaps they found, show you something your child produced that they could not have produced in week one, and describe a change in how homework is being done. If all you have after four weeks is a cheerful report that sessions are going well, that is a warning rather than progress. Ask for one piece of marked work and one sentence about what comes next. A tutor who has been paying attention answers in under a minute.

At one term the measure moves to school marks and to behaviour around deadlines. For an MYP student, the honest signal is criteria scores that stop swinging and command terms that are finally being answered. For a DP student it is an Internal Assessment draft that exists before the school's internal deadline instead of the night before, and past paper attempts that are timed rather than open-book. Marks often move later than habits do, and a term where the habits changed but the grade did not is a term that worked. Over a full exam cycle you should see timing under pressure improve, which is usually where the marks finally follow.

The limits are worth stating plainly. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor can. Three years of missed foundations do not close in six weeks, however good the match. A student who does not do the work between sessions will not improve, and a tutor who pretends otherwise is managing you rather than teaching your child. Attendance on both sides is the quiet variable: a slot that is cancelled twice a month is not a tutoring arrangement. What we can do is match a verified subject specialist to the belt you live on, tell you honestly whether the shape you want is staffable in this corner of Mumbai, and replace a tutor quickly when the fit is wrong.

sections.heading: Starting home classes in Vasai this month
paragraphs: Three documents make the first week faster. The most recent report card or criteria sheet, so the tutor starts from evidence instead of your summary. The school's assessment calendar for the term, including internal deadlines. And a short note of the two or three topics your child names as the worst, because children are usually right about where the floor gave way, even when they are wrong about why. Send those with your enquiry and the shortlist you get back will be noticeably better targeted than one built from a subject name and a year group.

The first session is diagnostic and should feel like it. Expect the tutor to spend most of it watching your child attempt work rather than explaining, because the useful information is in how a question is approached and where the pen stops. Expect them to ask what the school has already covered and to check it against the current guide rather than assuming. Expect ten minutes at the end with you in the room, with a plain summary of what they found and what the next three sessions will target. If none of that happens, say so before the second session.

Practical points for a first visit in Vasai. Give the tutor your building name, the nearest landmark and which side of Vasai Road you are on, not only a pin location, because the last three hundred metres are where time is lost here. Tell the gate the day before. Have the study space clear and the television off. Keep a younger sibling occupied elsewhere for the first session at least. And decide in advance what happens on a flooded evening in July, so that the first disrupted week is a rescheduling rather than a negotiation.

faqs.question: Can a tutor actually travel to Vasai for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends almost entirely on where the tutor lives. A tutor based in Vasai, Nallasopara, Virar, Naigaon or Bhayandar can hold a 7pm weekday slot for a full term without much drama. A tutor coming up from Borivali, Dahisar or Andheri is adding a long train leg in both directions, and those arrangements tend to fail in the second month rather than the first week. We tell you which case you are in before you commit, and if the belt has nobody free for your subject we will say that instead of sending a tutor who will quietly give up.

faqs.question: What do IB home tuition fees in Vasai depend on, and why will you not quote a figure?
faqs.answer: IB tuition fees in Vasai depend on five things, and quoting an average would mislead you on all of them. The programme stage, since DP work with Internal Assessment supervision costs more than PYP support. The level, because Higher Level specialists are scarcer. Subject scarcity, which is why a DP Physics HL tutor prices differently from a primary generalist. Travel, which is a real cost on this belt and the honest reason in-person rates here sit above online ones. And session length and frequency. Ask any tutor to break the figure into those parts, and be suspicious of a flat rate quoted before anyone has asked your child's year group.

faqs.question: Which nearby areas does a Vasai tutor also cover?
faqs.answer: Most tutors matched to a Vasai family also cover Virar, Bhayandar and Mira Road, along with Nallasopara and Naigaon in between, because that is one continuous stretch of the Western Line rather than three separate journeys. A few will go as far south as Dahisar East or Borivali for a weekend block. Very few will cross into Andheri or Goregaon on the same day as a Vasai session, and you should not want them to, since a tutor doing that is either exhausted or late. If you have family in Virar and want sessions split between two homes, say so early so the slot can be built that way.

faqs.question: My child gets home from school in Borivali at five and is exhausted. When should sessions start?
faqs.answer: Seven o'clock, with a shorter and tighter session than you think you want. Children commuting south to campuses like JBCN International School, Borivali or Singapore International School in Dahisar East lose a large part of the day to the journey, and a lesson stacked straight onto that is wasted money. A gap for food and a shower, then a focused stretch on one or two things, beats a long session where the last half is silent staring. For younger children, an earlier start on a Saturday is almost always more productive than any weekday slot.

faqs.question: How does a tutor get past our building gate and the watchman?
faqs.answer: The same way any expected visitor does, and it is smoother if you prepare it once. On the first visit the tutor will be asked who they are visiting, will write your flat number in the register, and may wait while the watchman calls up, so allow a few extra minutes. After that, tell the gate that the same person comes on the same day each week and the delay disappears. Tutors on the register carry photo identification and expect to show it. If your building insists on a pre-approved visitor entry in an app, send the tutor's name once and the problem is solved for the term.

faqs.question: Is an online lesson really as useful as a tutor at our dining table?
faqs.answer: For most secondary subjects it is close, and for some it is better. Online gives you access to specialists who would never make the trip to Vasai on a Wednesday, lets a student rewatch a worked solution, and survives a flooded evening in July. In-person is clearly better for younger children who need someone beside them, for practical and portfolio subjects, and for timed handwritten practice in the last term before exams. The pattern that holds best on this belt is online midweek with a longer in-person block at the weekend, and most families here arrive at it within a month anyway.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us in that week and we replace them, with no argument about whether you gave it long enough. The useful signal early on is not whether your child likes the tutor but whether the tutor can describe the problem precisely. If after three sessions they are still talking in general terms about confidence and effort, the match is wrong and waiting another month will not fix it. Say what specifically did not work, because that is what makes the second match better: a pace problem, a language problem, a tutor who lectured instead of watching your child work, or a slot that kept moving.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the evidence before you change anything. A month should have produced named gaps, at least one piece of marked work, and a changed pattern in how homework gets done. If those exist and the school marks have not moved, that is normal and often means the arrangement is working, since habits shift before grades. If those do not exist, the tutor has not been diagnosing, and a new match is the right call. Either way, put the question to the tutor directly and in writing, because a specialist who has been paying attention will answer it with specifics in a few minutes.

faqs.question: Do you cover the Primary Years Programme and MYP, or only the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: All three, though the pools differ in size. PYP and MYP requests on the Vasai–Virar belt are usually the easiest to fill, because strong primary and middle-school teachers live locally and are not competing with DP demand. DP requests, especially at Higher Level in the sciences and in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, draw on a smaller group of people, most of whom live further south and prefer online midweek. If your child is in MYP now and heading for DP, starting a year early is the cheapest way to secure a specialist you will want later.

faqs.question: What happens to a tutor's commute in the monsoon?
faqs.answer: It slows down badly, and the sensible response is to plan for it in June rather than argue about it in July. Heavy rain on this stretch of the Western Line means delayed trains, a flooded subway at Vasai Road and autorickshaws that will not go the last stretch. The arrangement that survives is one agreed in advance: during a washout week the session moves online at the same time, and the in-person block is made up at the weekend. Tutors who live on the belt are affected far less, which is one more reason the search starts with Virar, Nallasopara and Bhayandar.

faqs.question: Can we book weekend home classes instead of a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and on this belt it is often the better arrangement. Two longer weekend sessions remove the peak-hour train problem entirely, which means a wider choice of tutors and a lower chance of the slot collapsing mid-term. The trade-off is that a weekend block sits further from the school week, so homework support and test preparation need to be planned rather than reactive. Many families here run one weekend in-person block plus a short midweek online check-in, which covers both. Say at the enquiry stage that weekends work for you, because it changes the shortlist immediately.

sections.heading: How IB Gram finds an IB home tutor in Vile Parle East
paragraphs: A request from Vile Parle East usually arrives with three facts attached: the child's year group, the subject that has stopped making sense, and the only half-hour of the evening that is genuinely free. The third fact does more work here than in most of Mumbai. Because the airport approach roads and the Western Express Highway absorb the morning, nobody schedules a weekday lesson before 10am, and in practice the teaching day on this corridor runs from 5pm to about 9pm.

So the shortlist is built backwards from the clock. We take the free window first, then filter for tutors already teaching within reach of Vile Parle station, then filter again for the exact subject and level. A Diploma Programme Chemistry teacher who lives in Borivali looks excellent on paper and will quietly cancel by week five, because the 6pm run down the highway is not survivable twice a week. An IB home tutor in Vile Parle East has to be a short hop away, and any experienced IB home tutor in Mumbai will say the same about that run.

Two or three profiles come back, not twenty. Each one names the courses and levels that tutor actually teaches, the years of board teaching behind them, and the slots they can hold for a full term rather than a fortnight. You speak to them before anyone visits. Parents here almost always ask the same two questions on that call: how the first lesson diagnoses the gap, and what happens in April when the school's own revision timetable eats the evening.

Nothing is matched by subject label alone. Maths means one thing for a Middle Years Programme student working on criterion-based tasks and another for a Diploma Programme student with an Internal Assessment exploration to design. The request we take from a family in Vile Parle East, Mumbai, Maharashtra records the course title, the level, and the piece of work that is due next, because those three together decide which name on the list is the right one to call first.

sections.heading: The PYP, MYP and Diploma ladder a Vile Parle East family climbs
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) is three programmes, not one, and a family here can spend eleven years inside it without sitting a public examination until the very end. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs the early years as transdisciplinary inquiry: no papers, no marks out of a hundred, and report comments written against learner outcomes. Parents who move in from a state or national board often read those reports as vague, and the first job of a tutor is translation rather than teaching.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) is where the structure becomes visible. Work is judged against assessment criteria with their own descriptors, and a child can write a fluent essay and still lose ground on the criterion that asked for evaluation rather than description. The final MYP year adds the personal project, supervised at school and run largely by the student. A tutor here works on command terms and criterion language, not content recall, and families in Vile Parle East feel the shift from PYP comments to criterion grades hardest around Year 7.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year finish: six subject groups, some taken at Higher Level (HL) and some at Standard Level (SL), plus the core of Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the creativity, activity and service strand. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment (IA) marked in school and moderated by the board. Your coordinator confirms what the current subject guide asks for in your child's session, and we quote no weightings or deadlines at parents, because the boards revise both on their own cycle.

The rung that catches families is the jump into DP1. A student who coasted through MYP on classroom work meets HL content and an IA brief in the same term. We treat Years 1 to 12 as one ladder when matching, because the person who can teach DP1 content is not always the person who can rebuild Year 9 algebra underneath it. The coverage label on this page reads all IB and IGCSE subjects IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai, which only means both boards and every year group are matchable; if your child is in the Cambridge years, the IGCSE home tuition page for this locality owns tiering and coursework.

sections.heading: Which IB subjects actually need a specialist in Vile Parle East?
paragraphs: Not every subject needs a specialist, and pretending otherwise wastes your evenings. The two that generate most requests on this corridor are Mathematics and the sciences at Higher Level. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic fluency and proof, while Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation leans on modelling, data and the graphic display calculator. A student in the wrong one of those two can work hard all term and still feel slow, and that is a course-choice problem a tutor should name in week one instead of drilling around it.

In Physics, Chemistry and Biology the content is only half the work. The other half is the Internal Assessment: choosing a question narrow enough to measure, controlling one variable honestly, and writing an evaluation that does more than list sources of error. English A: Language and Literature asks for analysis of non-literary texts under time pressure, and the oral components reward rehearsal with someone willing to interrupt. Economics and Business Management both punish vague definitions far more heavily than weak opinions.

Language courses are the quiet problem in the Western Suburbs. Spanish, French and German teachers who know the IB oral criteria are scarce, and the scarce ones are booked by October. Hindi A and Marathi first-language students need someone comfortable with literary commentary in the language, not a conversation partner. All IB and IGCSE subjects a home tutor in Vile Parle East covers are listed by course and level, so you can see whether the person in front of you teaches your child's syllabus or only the subject's name.

Many families here ask for one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai international schools teach, and that request is usually worth splitting. One person can reasonably hold two related subjects at MYP level. At Higher Level, a Physics teacher marking an IA and an Economics teacher drilling definitions are two different professionals, and the second subject bolted onto a single tutor's brief is where quality drops first. Two specialists on alternate evenings beat one generalist four nights a week.

sections.heading: Santacruz East, Andheri East and BKC: where your tutor travels from
paragraphs: Vile Parle East sits on the Vile Parle East–Hanuman Road stretch, with Vile Parle station and the Western Line to its west and the Western Express Highway to its east, and the tutor pool follows that geometry. Most people who teach here live in Santacruz East, in Andheri East, or along the line between Bandra and Andheri. BKC counts in both directions at once: it is where many of these children go to school, and where some of their tutors sit during the working day.

The Western Suburbs run north–south along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, so matching along the line works and matching across it does not. A tutor in Khar reaching Santacruz, or Malad reaching Kandivali, is a ten-minute problem. The same person asked to cross from the eastern suburbs at 6pm is an hour-long problem, every week, until they stop coming. Metro Line 1 (Versova–Andheri–Ghatkopar) and Metro Lines 2A & 7 carry the north–south run, and the Aqua Line has made the BKC and airport side easier to reach from the south.

Parents searching for IB tutors near me in Vile Parle East are really asking about reliability, not distance. A tutor fifteen minutes away keeps a 7pm slot in July and still keeps it in January. A tutor forty minutes away keeps it until the first monsoon week or the first evening the highway backs up past the airport junction. We would rather introduce an IB private tutor in Vile Parle East who lives three stations away than a more decorated one who has to cross the city to get here.

Santacruz East brings tutors who also teach around Kalina and the university side. Andheri East brings the Chakala and MIDC professionals, including working engineers who take one or two Higher Level Physics students in the evening. BKC brings people whose day job sits inside the corporate blocks and who can reach a flat on this corridor by 7.30pm. All three pools are reachable without crossing the highway more than once, which is the most useful single fact about hiring an IB home tutor in Vile Parle East rather than two suburbs further north.

sections.heading: What does the Mumbai school calendar do to your evenings?
paragraphs: The Mumbai international school year starts in June, and the pressure is not spread evenly across it. Families around Vile Parle East send children to Bombay Cambridge International School in Andheri East and to Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, among others, and both run calendars that load internal deadlines into October and November and then again into February and March. June and July are the months when a tutor is easiest to find and most useful to start with.

October is when Diploma Programme students discover that an Internal Assessment draft, a Theory of Knowledge task and a school unit test can land in the same fortnight. February and March belong to mock examinations and predicted grades, which are what universities see first. April is the strangest month on this corridor: schools cut timetabled teaching for revision, every family wants extra sessions, and the good tutors across the Western Suburbs are already full. Booking in April means taking whoever is left.

The school run shapes the lesson slot as directly as the deadline calendar does. Children bussed to BKC or across to Andheri East leave early and reach home tired, and a lesson starting the moment the bus arrives is money spent on a sleepy child. sections.heading: Home tuition, online classes or a mix in Vile Parle East?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default here, for a plain reason: the work is on paper. A tutor sitting beside a Middle Years Programme student sees the arithmetic slip in the third line, flips back three pages of the exercise book, and watches what the child does when nobody prompts. For Years 1 to 8 we recommend home classes almost without exception, and most Diploma Programme families keep at least one weekly home lesson for exactly the same reason.

Online earns its place in two situations. The first is a scarce course: a Higher Level subject or a language with few qualified teachers in the Western Suburbs, where an IB online tutor in Vile Parle East with the right course experience beats a nearby generalist holding a textbook. The second is the late slot. A 9pm online lesson works on a Tuesday in February when nobody is driving anywhere, and it survives the monsoon evenings when the highway stops moving entirely.

The hybrid pattern is where most Diploma Programme families on this corridor end up: one home lesson a week for the paper work, plus a short online clinic before a draft is due or after a test comes back. It wastes no travel and it fits the compression of the 5pm to 9pm window. The honest trade-off is attention. Online sessions need a parent to confirm that the camera stays on the page and the phone stays out of the room.

Where online genuinely loses is the diagnostic. A tutor cannot spot a bluffed method over a video call as fast as across a table, and younger children drift inside ten minutes. Where home tuition loses is the calendar: a tutor with flu, a flooded stretch near Santacruz East or an airport-bound jam can cost you a week, while an online session is simply moved. Choosing an IB home tutor in Vile Parle East who also teaches online gets you both.

sections.heading: How do you check an IB home tutor before the first lesson?
paragraphs: Start with what IB Gram checks, then do the part only you can do. We verify identity, the degree claimed, and the board teaching record behind the subjects a tutor says they teach, and we ask for courses and levels specifically, because IB Maths is not a qualification. Tutors who teach at Higher Level are asked what they have marked, not only what they have taught, and references from previous families are requested for the ones we introduce.

Your own checks take about fifteen minutes. Ask which syllabus version your child is on and listen for whether the tutor asks the school or guesses. Hand over the last marked test and ask what the examiner wanted. Ask how an Internal Assessment is supervised, and whether the tutor will write any part of it, because the correct answer is a flat no. Be wary of anyone who promises a specific grade by a specific month.

The visit itself has a protocol, and in Vile Parle East it is the building's protocol, not ours. Most societies here want the visitor's name at the gate in advance, a photo identity card at the desk and an entry in the register, and many will approve a standing weekly visitor if the flat owner asks the society office in writing. Settle that before the first lesson rather than during it, so nobody is arguing downstairs at 7pm while your child waits upstairs.

Keep the lesson in a shared space. A dining table with the Wi-Fi password, a jug of water and no television beats a bedroom with the door shut, and a parent somewhere within earshot is normal practice rather than an insult. On a first visit, walk the tutor from the lift to the table yourself and stay for the opening minutes. An IB home tutor in Vile Parle East who objects to any of this is telling you something useful very early.

sections.heading: The 5pm to 9pm window that decides who teaches in Vile Parle East
paragraphs: Here is the fact that is true in Vile Parle East and almost nowhere else in Mumbai. The locality is pinned between the airport on one side and the Western Express Highway on the other, so the morning is unusable: tutors do not offer the 8am to 10am window at all, and families here stopped asking for it years ago. Almost every lesson on this corridor happens after 5pm, which makes the practical teaching day four hours long.

Four hours, two or three lessons. That arithmetic decides who is available to you. One tutor can hold a 5.30pm, a 7pm and occasionally an 8.30pm, and the middle slot is the one every family wants, because it sits after the school bus and before dinner. If your household can take 5.30pm or 8.30pm instead, the list of people who will teach your child gets visibly longer and visibly better. Parents who insist on 7pm in February are choosing a slot over a specialist.

Take a Diploma Programme student at a BKC school with Higher Level Physics and Standard Level Economics. She reaches home at 5.15pm, needs an hour to be human again, and has a Physics Internal Assessment draft due the same week as a Theory of Knowledge deadline. Two 7pm lessons a week do not exist for her in a month when every tutor's 7pm is gone. What works is Physics at 8pm on Tuesday, Economics online at 9pm on Thursday, and a long Saturday morning block while the roads are still empty.

The window also explains the rate. What IB tuition fees in Vile Parle East depend on is the level, how scarce the subject teacher is, how far that person travels, how long each session runs, and whether the slot is one of the contested ones. A Higher Level science teacher giving up an hour they could sell twice over prices it accordingly, and an off-peak 5.30pm or a Saturday block is where families on this corridor get the most teaching for their money. sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks and one exam cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks you are not looking for marks. You are looking for a changed method: homework started without a fight, working shown in full, the child able to say what the question was asking for. If a Diploma Programme student can explain why she lost marks on the last test without first reading the teacher's comment, the tutoring is working, whatever the next score happens to say. Four weeks is also long enough to know whether the two of them actually talk to each other.

At one term, school evidence should move. Internal grades, the quality of an Internal Assessment draft handed in on time instead of at midnight, a mock paper where the lost marks sit in new places rather than the same place. Progress in Mumbai schools shows up in the teacher's comments before it shows up in the number, and a tutor who cannot tell you which specific criterion is still weak at the end of a term has not been paying attention.

Across one full examination cycle the realistic claim is narrower than the advertising in this city suggests. A tutor changes preparation, accuracy and pacing. The paper is still written by your child in May, under time, on a day nobody controls. Parents ask us who the best IB tutor in Vile Parle East is, and the truthful answer is that the strongest available teacher for Higher Level Chemistry and the strongest for Standard Level Economics are two different people with two different diaries.

When it is not working, say so in week three rather than month three. Ask for a replacement and give one line of reason: wrong level, wrong pace, wrong personality, missed sessions. A request made on a Monday is usually re-matched inside the same week, and the new tutor is briefed on what the last four weeks covered so your child is not diagnosed from scratch again. We do not guarantee grades, and we do not keep a family with a tutor who has stopped earning the slot.

sections.heading: Which programme and level does your enquiry actually need to name?
paragraphs: Name the programme, the year inside that programme, and the level. That is the complete answer, and leaving any part of it out is why so many enquiries stall. In Mumbai school conversation, Year 11 means Middle Years Programme (MYP) Year 5 at one school and IGCSE Year 11 at the school across the road, and a tutor who teaches one competently may not teach the other at all.

The structure underneath those names is worth knowing before you write. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs to roughly Year 6 and is assessed by the school rather than an external board, so tutoring there is about reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining method out loud. MYP runs Years 7 to 11 with criterion marking in every subject. IGCSE runs the two years to Year 11 with terminal papers. DP and Cambridge AS and A Level both occupy the final two school years, with intake years differing by school.

Level is the second half of the sentence and the part most often missing. In DP you take three subjects at HL and three at Standard Level (SL), and the HL version of a subject is not the SL version with extra lessons; in Mathematics the HL courses carry whole topics the SL courses never meet. In IGCSE Mathematics the split is Core and Extended, and Extended is where the harder algebra, the transformations and the full trigonometry live. Cambridge International Education also tiers several sciences. Writing Maths, Year 11 tells a tutor nothing. Writing IGCSE Mathematics Extended, Year 11, Cambridge tells them in one glance whether they can help.

Say which specification year you are on if you know it. Both boards revise their syllabuses, and a tutor who last taught a subject two specifications ago is reading a different set of assessment objectives from the one your child's teacher is marking against.

sections.heading: Subject choice across both boards, and the internal assessments each one carries in Mumbai
paragraphs: Every subject on both boards carries coursework with its own deadline, and naming that piece of coursework in your first message is the fastest way to get a serious reply. A tutor reading DP2 Physics, Internal Assessment (IA) draft due in three weeks, lost on uncertainty analysis knows exactly what the first two sessions are. A tutor reading needs help with Physics does not.

In DP the Internal Assessment is subject specific and weighted differently in each one. The sciences ask for an individual investigation with a research question the student designs, and the mark is dominated by analysis and evaluation rather than by a clean result. Mathematics asks for an exploration, where the usual failure is an interesting topic with almost no mathematics in it. History asks for an investigation with a source evaluation section students routinely underwrite. Business Management, Economics and Psychology each have their own shape. Above all of them sit the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK), which belong to no subject and are therefore the two things nobody timetables until they are late.

IGCSE coursework is lighter but not absent. Several Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel subjects carry a coursework component or an alternative-to-practical paper, and the languages carry speaking and listening components with their own recording windows. The decision that matters more at IGCSE is subject choice itself: which sciences to take separately rather than as Coordinated Sciences, whether to carry a second language, and whether Extended Mathematics is realistic for a student currently uncomfortable with fractions and indices.

A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai does not exist as one person, and anybody claiming to be one should worry you. What exists is a roster covering all IB and IGCSE subjects a home tutor in Mumbai can reasonably specialise in, matched one subject at a time. Enquiries asking for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai in a single booking get split into separate subject requests before anybody is contacted, because a DP Chemistry HL tutor and a DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL tutor are two bookings.

The six zones families in Mumbai, Maharashtra actually use are South Mumbai, the Western Suburbs, the Central Suburbs, the Eastern Suburbs, Navi Mumbai and Thane.

The Central Suburbs run on society groups. Powai, Chandivali, Kurla, Ghatkopar and Kanjurmarg include complexes with enough flats to hold their own tutor market, reached along JVLR, the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR) and Metro Line 1 rather than by train, and a message in a Hiranandani Gardens group gets answers within the hour. The Eastern Suburbs, from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund West and Wadala, still run partly on noticeboards and the neighbour two floors up, and the Eastern Freeway, the Monorail and the Central Line make the island city closer than the map implies.

sections.heading: The Mumbai school calendar decides how long your search takes
paragraphs: Most Mumbai IB and IGCSE schools open the academic year somewhere between early June and mid-August, which means most families in the city start looking for a tutor inside the same few weeks. The May examination session then empties the senior school and frees tutors, which is why a mid-year start is easier to staff than an August one. sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: which one to ask for in the first message
paragraphs: Ask for home tuition first. An IB home tutor near me in Mumbai is what most families reading this want, and asking for it plainly gets a yes or a no in one message instead of three. IB home tuition in Mumbai also carries the highest reply rate when the slot is sensible, which in this city means a weekday start after 5:30pm or a weekend morning.

The honest trade-off is pool size. Asking for home classes narrows the roster to tutors who can reach your area at your time and keep doing it for a full term. An IB online tutor in Mumbai, by contrast, draws on the whole city and on specialists outside it, which matters for the thin subjects: Latin, Philosophy, Music, Film, Design Technology, Computer Science HL and the less common Language A and Language B options. For those, insisting on home tuition can mean waiting a month for somebody who was never going to exist in your postcode.

Hybrid is where most families settle, and it is worth naming in the enquiry rather than negotiating in month two. The usual shape is one home session a week for the work that needs paper, a shared desk and somebody watching the student's hand move, plus one shorter online session for a draft review, a past paper walkthrough or a question that came up on a Wednesday. It also absorbs the Mumbai evening that goes wrong without losing the week.

Whichever you want, state it as a preference with a fallback. Home tuition preferred, open to hybrid gets replies from both pools. Home only and non-negotiable gets replies from one, and in August that one may be empty. An IB private tutor in Mumbai offering all three formats is common; one offering only the format you refused is a wasted week.
bullets: Home tuition: best for paper-based work, narrowest pool, needs a fixed slot
Online: widest pool, and often the only option for thin subjects
Hybrid: one home session plus one online review, survives a bad traffic evening
State a preference with a fallback or you halve your replies
Weekday starts after 5:30pm and weekend mornings get answered fastest

sections.heading: What should you check yourself before a tutor reaches your Mumbai flat?
paragraphs: Check three things no platform can check for you: whether they have taught your exact syllabus recently, whether they can describe a student they failed to help, and whether a reference will take your call. Before an IB home teacher near me in Mumbai begins a standing weekly slot, IB Gram verifies identity, qualifications and teaching history, and lists the subjects, programmes and areas each tutor covers.

What verification establishes is that the person is who they say they are and has taught what they claim. It does not establish that they suit your child, and no checking process can. That judgement comes from two or three narrow questions in the first conversation. Which specification are you teaching this subject from? What are the four criteria in this MYP subject? What does an examiner actually reward in the evaluation section of a science IA? An IB tutor in Mumbai who answers those in specifics is reading the same documents as your child's teacher. One who answers in enthusiasm is not.

Ask the awkward question too. Tell me about a student this did not work for separates experienced tutors from confident ones. Anybody who has taught for a few years has a student who did not improve, and the honest answer names a reason: the student would not work between sessions, the gap was two years wide with an exam in March, or the subject choice was wrong from the start. An answer of that has never happened is the answer to walk away from.

The small checks take two minutes each. Confirm your society's visitor process with your own building office rather than assuming, agree the cancellation notice and who absorbs a missed session, and get written confirmation of the weekly slot before the first full week. These are the things that quietly end arrangements in month two.
bullets: IB Gram checks identity, qualifications and teaching history before a profile goes live
Ask which specification they teach from and listen for a version
Ask them to describe a student they could not help
Agree cancellation notice and who absorbs a missed session in writing
Confirm your building's visitor process with your own society office

sections.heading: Running the week: three shortlisted, two trials and the reference call nobody makes
paragraphs: An IB home tutor near me in Mumbai is found in a week, not in an afternoon, and the week has a shape. Days one and two are for sending the enquiry to every channel at once rather than in sequence: the school parent group, your society group, one neighbour whose child takes the same subject, the building noticeboard if your society still keeps one, and a platform. Running them in parallel is the whole trick. Families who try the society group, wait three days, then try a platform spend three weeks on a one-week job.

Days three and four are for reading replies, and most are not worth pursuing. A reply worth your time names the board, says which level and year group the tutor teaches, and asks you a question back, usually about what the student has already been marked down for. A reply saying yes I can teach all subjects, when can we start is a scheduling answer to a teaching question. So is one that quotes a rate before asking anything about the student. Parents search for the best IB tutor in Mumbai and no such person exists in the abstract; there is only the person who fits this board, this level and this slot. Cut to three and tell the others no immediately, because October comes around.

Days five to seven are the trials. Run two, not three and not one, and give both the same task: look at this marked paper or this IA draft and tell us what the first two sessions would do. Afterwards ask your child one question, which is whether they understood more at the end than at the start. That signal beats whether they liked the person. Then make the reference call almost no family makes. Five minutes with a parent the tutor has taught for a term tells you about punctuality, cancellations and whether the work actually changed, and tutors who are good hand over a number without hesitating.

Sometimes all three say no. In August that is normal and it is not a verdict on your enquiry. Loosen exactly one constraint and resend the same message: move the slot by an hour, accept hybrid instead of home only, or split a two-subject request into two bookings so each fits somebody's timetable. Resending an identical message to the same people a week later is the one approach that reliably produces nothing.
bullets: Day one: send the same enquiry to every channel on the same day
Day three: keep only replies that ask a question about the student
Day five: trial two tutors on the same marked paper
Day six: make the reference call about punctuality and cancellations
Day seven: confirm one tutor and one protected weekly slot

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks you are not looking for a grade. You are looking for three things: the student starts work without a forty-minute delay, homework reaches the teacher on the day it is due, and the student can tell you which criterion or assessment objective a piece of work is being marked against. If none of those has moved in four weeks, the problem is the match or the format, and it is worth saying so then rather than in January.

At one term the honest expectation is movement in one paper type rather than across a whole subject. A DP Mathematics student who was losing marks on structured long answers starts finishing them while the multiple choice stays where it was. An IGCSE Chemistry student stops dropping units and significant figures. A History student's source evaluation paragraph turns into something an examiner can award. That pattern, narrow and visible, is what real improvement looks like at twelve weeks, and it is more trustworthy than a jump across everything at once.

At one exam cycle the thing that has actually changed is usually behavioural. The student plans backwards from a deadline, writes a draft early enough to get feedback on it, and reads the mark scheme before writing rather than after being marked. Grades follow that more reliably than they follow lesson hours. We do not guarantee grades, and anybody in Mumbai offering you a guaranteed band is selling something they cannot deliver. Outcomes depend on the work done between sessions, how wide the starting gap is and how much time is left.

The limits are worth stating plainly. Two sessions a week cannot close a two-year gap in six weeks. A student who will not open a book between sessions will not improve regardless of who sits opposite them. And a subject chosen badly at the start of DP1 sometimes needs a subject change rather than a tutor, which is a conversation with the school rather than with us.
bullets: Four weeks: faster starts, homework on time, the student names the criterion
One term: one paper type improves, not the whole subject at once
One exam cycle: planning backwards from deadlines becomes a habit
We do not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor in Mumbai will
A badly chosen subject needs a school conversation, not more hours

sections.heading: Starting your search for IB home tuition in Mumbai this week
paragraphs: Put five things in one place before writing to anybody: the last report card, one recently marked paper with the comments still on it, the brief for whatever coursework comes next with its due date, your child's school timetable, and two evening slots genuinely free for the next three months. That is a fifteen-minute job and it is the difference between a reply in a day and a reply in a week.

Then write six lines. Board and year group. Subject with level. What has already gone wrong, quoted from the marked paper rather than summarised. The next deadline and its date. Two possible slots. Your area at suburb level, plus whether you want home tuition, online or hybrid. Nothing else. An enquiry listing all IB and IGCSE subjects IB and IGCSE Years 1 to 12 and then asking for a tutor in Mumbai gets filed, because nobody can tell what it wants.

The first paid session should not be a lesson. It should be a diagnostic: the tutor works through the marked paper with your child, identifies whether the issue is content, method or exam technique, and ends with a written plan naming the next three sessions and what each covers. Ask for that plan in writing. If it never arrives, the tutor is improvising, which is fine for one session and expensive across a term.

After that, review at four weeks in a short conversation involving all three of you, and again after the next graded piece of work. IB tutors near me in Mumbai are not a one-time decision. Most arrangements that fail do so because nobody scheduled that conversation.
bullets: Report card, one marked paper, and the next coursework brief with its date
Six lines: board, year, subject with level, problem, deadline, two slots
Say your suburb and your format preference in the same message
Ask for a written plan naming the next three sessions
Review at four weeks and again after the first graded piece

faqs.question: What should my first message to a tutor actually say?
faqs.answer: Six lines: board, exact year group, subject with its level, what has already gone wrong, the next deadline with its date, and two slots you can protect. Add your suburb and whether you want home tuition, online or hybrid. Quote the marked paper instead of summarising it, because lost marks on the evaluation section of the Biology IA tells a tutor what the first session is and struggling with Biology does not. Leave everything else out. Good tutors read dozens of enquiries a week and answer the ones they can already plan for.

faqs.question: How long does the search usually take?
faqs.answer: About a week if you run the channels in parallel, three weeks if you run them one after another. Days one and two are for sending the same enquiry to the school parent group, your society group, a neighbour, the noticeboard and a platform simultaneously. Days three and four are for cutting replies to three. Days five to seven are for two trials and one reference call. In August, when the whole city is looking at once, add a week and expect more declines. Starting the hunt for an IB home tutor in Mumbai in the previous term is the cheapest improvement available to you.

faqs.question: Why is nobody replying to my enquiry in August?
faqs.answer: Because August is when the whole city starts at once, not because your enquiry is bad. Most Mumbai IB and IGCSE schools open the academic year between early June and mid-August, so demand for evening slots peaks in the same few weeks and tutors fill their timetables quickly. Loosen one constraint and resend: shift the slot by an hour, accept hybrid instead of home only, or split a two-subject request into two bookings. Resending the identical message to the same people a week later produces nothing. Where you have the option, start in the previous term.

faqs.question: Is my society WhatsApp group a good place to find a tutor?
faqs.answer: It is the fastest channel and the narrowest one. A message in a large complex group in Powai or in Hiranandani Gardens often gets replies within the hour, because somebody already teaches in the building and the logistics are solved. The blind spot is that it returns whoever is already there rather than whoever fits your subject and level, and a DP Physics HL request answered by a general Maths tutor is a worse outcome than waiting two days. Use it alongside the school parent group and a platform, not instead of them.

faqs.question: Should I shortlist one tutor or three?
faqs.answer: Three, then trial two. One name leaves you with accept or restart, and restarting mid-term is how families lose six weeks. Three lets you ask the same question about the same marked paper and compare the answers, which tells you more than any profile does. It also leaves a briefed fallback if your first choice takes a school posting. Say no to the people you are not pursuing immediately and politely, because the October and January crunches come around and you may want to write to them again.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and level first, then subject scarcity, travel and session length. A DP Higher Level science or a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL booking sits above an MYP Year 7 one because fewer people can teach it. A thin subject with few Mumbai specialists sits higher again. Home sessions carry the tutor's travel time, so somebody crossing a zone in evening traffic prices that in, while online removes it. Longer sessions and multi-subject bookings usually shift the per-hour figure. We publish no price list, because any number printed here would be wrong for most requests.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to my building on Ghodbunder Road on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if the tutor already lives or teaches in Thane. The Ghodbunder Road stretch from Majiwada out to Kasarvadavali takes close to an hour in the evening peak from the station end, so a Thane-based tutor will hold that slot for a term while one commuting from the Western Suburbs often will not, whatever they say in week one. Ask where the tutor travels from before you agree a time, and prefer a start after 5:30pm or a weekend morning. A nearby tutor who stays is worth more than a slightly stronger one who quietly stops coming.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a gate pass, and who arranges it?
faqs.answer: You do, and it takes one message to your society office. Most Mumbai complexes will issue a standing visitor entry for a named person at a fixed weekly time once a resident requests it, which is far better than the tutor being logged as a fresh visitor every week and waiting at the gate. Do it before the first full session rather than after the first argument at the gate. Tell the tutor which gate to use and whether parking exists, because somebody circling for fifteen minutes is somebody late every week.

faqs.question: Does online tuition really work for IB subjects?
faqs.answer: For some subjects it works as well as home tuition, and for others it does not. Essay subjects, Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay support and draft review work well online because the document is on a screen either way. Mathematics and the sciences need a shared surface and somebody watching the student's working, which is harder though manageable with a tablet and a stylus. Thin subjects with few Mumbai specialists are often only available online. Most families end up using online for review and home classes for the paper-based work.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out after three weeks. What happens?
faqs.answer: Tell us in week three rather than week ten, and we move you to the next person on your original shortlist. That is the practical reason for shortlisting three: the replacement is already briefed on the subject, the level and the deadline, so you lose days rather than weeks. Before switching, check whether the problem is the tutor or the format, because a student who cannot concentrate at 8pm may do better at 6pm or online. We do not guarantee grades and we do not pretend every match works first time.

faqs.question: Do I need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, but be there at the start and end of the first two. The start is where you hand over the marked paper and the deadline. The end is where you get the three-line summary of what was covered and what is due. After that an adult in the flat is sensible rather than necessary. What matters every week is the space: a table, a chair, a plug and the television off. A quiet dining table does more for a session than a stronger tutor in a room with a match on.

faqs.question: I messaged six tutors in Powai and got one reply. What do I change?
faqs.answer: The message, almost certainly. Enquiries saying need IB tuition in Powai, please share details get ignored because the tutor cannot tell whether it is PYP reading or Diploma Programme Physics HL, and finding out costs them three messages. Rewrite it with the board, the year group, the subject and its level, the specific thing going wrong, the next deadline and two slots. Then send it to the school parent group and a platform as well as the society group. Six messages into one channel is one channel, not six attempts.

You will get three matched profiles listing subjects taught and areas covered, not a directory to sift. Trial two, make one reference call, and confirm a weekly slot. If the first tutor is wrong, tell us in week three and the next name on your shortlist is already briefed.

sections.heading: How we arrange home tuition in Mumbai, step by step
paragraphs: A request for home tuition in Mumbai is really a request for a stranger to be let into a flat every week at a fixed hour. That is the part most enquiry forms ignore, so it is the part this page starts with. Before anyone talks about syllabus codes or Internal Assessment (IA) drafts, the arrangement has to survive a guard who has never heard of the tutor, a lift that stops running at a certain hour, and a Tuesday evening that was always going to be difficult.

The sequence below is deliberately boring. It exists because the arrangements that collapse in week three almost never collapse over teaching. They collapse because nobody agreed who opens the door, because the tutor was logged at the gate as a delivery visitor and turned away, or because the slot was never genuinely free. Settling the household details first means the first hour goes on the subject rather than on logistics. Parents who have run tuition before recognise this immediately; parents arranging it for the first time usually find it the most useful part of the page.

Where a family sits in the city changes the order slightly. In South Mumbai the building is often old, the lift is small and the watchman keeps a paper register, so the tutor's name has to be left downstairs in advance. In a Thane township or a Navi Mumbai node the gate runs on a visitor app and a resident has to approve each entry from a phone. In a Bandra bungalow there is no gate protocol at all, only a doorbell and a dog. We ask which of these you have before the first visit is scheduled, not after it goes wrong.

None of this involves a school. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, and no tutor is presented as a representative of one. What we arrange is a weekly appointment in your house with an adult whose identity and board experience we have checked. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor who has not yet met your child can tell you what four weeks will produce.
bullets: 1. You send year, board, subjects, address and the evenings that are genuinely free

4. First session is a full working lesson in a shared room, with a parent at home
5. After two sessions you confirm, adjust the slot, or ask for a different tutor

sections.heading: Which programme is in the room: PYP, MYP, DP or IGCSE?
paragraphs: Four different programmes can be sitting at your dining table, and each one changes what the session physically needs. International Baccalaureate (IB) Primary Years Programme (PYP) work needs floor space and materials. Middle Years Programme (MYP) work needs a laptop and the school portal. Diploma Programme (DP) work needs printed past papers and a quiet two hours. Cambridge International Education's IGCSE work needs the syllabus document open beside the exercise book. Knowing which one it is tells you which room to clear.

A PYP child in Class 3 or 4 is doing unit-of-inquiry work that spreads: chart paper, cut-outs, a tablet, a reading book. That lesson belongs on a large flat surface where a parent can glance over without hovering, and the useful block of attention is shorter than most parents expect. The tutor is often working on reading fluency or number sense rather than a syllabus. In a one-bedroom flat in Girgaon that means the dining table, cleared, with the television off. In a Powai tower it usually means the dining table anyway, because the study room is where an older sibling is doing DP Chemistry.

MYP Years 4 and 5 bring criterion-referenced tasks, which means the tutor needs the task sheet and the criteria strands open side by side, normally on a screen. IGCSE students in Class 9 and 10 are working to a published syllabus and a mark scheme, so a printer, or at least a tablet large enough to read a past paper on, matters more than floor space. Core versus Extended in IGCSE Mathematics, and the choice between separate sciences and Coordinated Science, are decisions taken at home as much as at school, and a home tutor who has seen the actual class notes advises better than one working from a description over the phone.

DP1 and DP2 are the longest sessions and the ones that most want a door that can be shut, which creates the only real tension with the safety practice described further down this page. The answer most families settle on is a room with the door left open, or a dining area that is out of the main walking line. Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices, Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and six subject internal assessments mean a DP2 student needs a working surface they can leave covered in paper between sessions.
bullets: PYP: large flat surface, materials out, television off, short focused blocks
MYP: laptop and school portal open, criteria strands visible beside the task
IGCSE: a printed past paper or a large tablet, syllabus document to hand
DP: two uninterrupted hours and a surface that can stay covered in paper
Any programme: the room stays shared, never a closed bedroom

sections.heading: What the tutor brings and what your household provides
paragraphs: A household rarely needs all IB and IGCSE subjects covered by one tutor in Mumbai. What it usually needs is one or two subjects taught well and a clear division of equipment. The tutor brings the syllabus, past papers, a mark scheme, worked examples, their own pens and a plan for the hour. The house provides light, a hard surface, a chair that is not a bed, a charging point and, for a science, a table steady enough to draw a graph on. Everything else is negotiable, and arguing about it during session one wastes the session.

Subject choice across both boards is the decision parents most often want a second opinion on, and it goes better at a kitchen table than on a call. In DP the question is which three subjects go to HL, and whether Mathematics goes Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation. In IGCSE it is Core or Extended in Mathematics, and how many sciences to carry. A home tutor who has seen the student's own exercise book, in their own handwriting, with the teacher's comments still in the margin, gives a more honest answer than anybody reading a report card from across the city.

Every subject carries an internal assessment, and each one lands as a problem inside the house. The Physics IA needs data collected at school but written up at home. The Mathematics exploration needs a topic chosen at home, usually badly at first, then narrowed. English Language and Literature needs an individual oral the student has to rehearse out loud, which in a shared flat means picking an hour when nobody else is on a call. Business Management and Economics need a real article. A tutor sitting in the room can hear that oral rehearsal and correct the pacing; a tutor on a video call hears it through a laptop microphone and misses half of it.

The practical rule we give families is to provide the space and the electricity and let the tutor bring the paper. Do not buy a shelf of reference books before the first month is out. Do not print a hundred past papers. Plenty of students already own more material than they can use and not enough structure to use it, and a guidebook bought in a hurry ends up unopened under the bed. The tutor will tell you after two sessions what is genuinely missing, and often it is nothing more than a better lamp and a plug socket within reach.
