sections.heading: How to check a tutor can teach above the specification
paragraphs: Before any tutor is listed we verify identity documents, the qualification claimed and the teaching history against the current specification. For enrichment requests we ask two further things: what is the hardest thing you have taught in this subject, and when did you last learn something new in it. The second question matters more than it sounds. A tutor whose subject knowledge stopped at the syllabus will run out of road with a strong student inside a term, and both the tutor and the student will know it before the parent does. We do not rate tutors with stars and we publish no results claims, so these conversations are the check.

Parents should run three tests on the first call, and they take ten minutes. Ask the tutor to set a question in this subject that they would not expect the student to finish, and listen to whether they can produce one on the spot. Ask what they would recommend the student read, and whether the answer is a book or a revision guide. Ask what they would do if the student asked something they did not know, because the only acceptable answer is that they would say so and find out, and a surprising number of tutors cannot say that out loud. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Mumbai families hire for depth work has to be comfortable being the second cleverest person in the room sometimes.

Parents often search for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai, and for this request the phrase is particularly unhelpful, because the right person is defined entirely by the subject and the student. The best tutor for a Year 10 who wants to understand why calculus works is a mathematician who enjoys explaining it, and that person may be mediocre at examination technique. Decide which of the two things you are buying before you start, because the tutor who maximises a predicted grade and the tutor who makes a subject interesting are usually different people, and asking one to be the other produces a disappointing version of both.
bullets: Ask the tutor to set a question they would not expect the student to finish
Ask what the student should read, and judge whether the answer is a revision guide
A tutor who cannot say they do not know is the wrong tutor here
Ask when the tutor last learned something new in this subject
Decide whether you want examination technique or genuine depth, not both at once

sections.heading: Is my child bored in class, or quietly struggling in Mumbai?
paragraphs: They look identical from the outside, which is why so many Mumbai families hire the wrong kind of help. Both the bored student and the quietly struggling student say the subject is easy, do the minimum homework, resist showing their working, lose interest in class and describe the teacher as dull. Both produce a slow drift downwards in marks that nobody can fully explain. Hiring an enrichment tutor for a struggling student is demoralising and expensive, and hiring a revision tutor for a bored student guarantees the student stops cooperating within a month.

Four tests separate them reliably. First, set one genuinely hard question inside a topic the student calls easy and watch the opening minutes: a bored student leans in almost immediately, while a struggling student goes quiet, changes the subject or asks whether this will be in the exam. Second, ask them to teach you the topic. A bored student explains it fluently and starts adding things that were not asked for; a struggling student recites a definition and stops. Third, look at where the marks were actually lost. Boredom shows up as careless arithmetic and long structured questions abandoned halfway; difficulty shows up as the same conceptual step failing in four different questions. Fourth, compare speed with accuracy, because both students finish early, and only one of them finishes early and right.

Then there is the question of racing ahead, which is the most common and least useful response to boredom. Teaching Diploma content to a Year 10 feels like progress and rarely is. The student meets the material without the mathematical or analytical maturity to hold it, builds a shallow memory of it, and is then bored a second time when the class arrives there eighteen months later with the memory faded. Worse, a student who believes they have already covered a topic stops listening in the lesson where the department explains the conventions, the expected working and the framing their examinations will actually use. There is no reward anywhere in either system for having covered content early. There is a real penalty for disengaging from the classroom.

Which brings up the answer nobody selling tuition wants to give. Sometimes a capable, bored student does not need a tutor. They need a thing of their own: a competition, a project with an actual output, a coding problem nobody has set them, a research group, a debating circuit, an instrument, a sport, a job, a book list and the hours to read it. A tutor adds one more adult directed hour to a week that is already entirely adult directed, and for a self motivated student that can be exactly the wrong move. Where a tutor genuinely earns the slot is narrower and clearer: a subject the school does not offer, early mentoring on an Extended Essay or an Internal Assessment question, preparation for an external subject examination, or a student who wants to go deep and has nobody at home or at school to argue with about it. If your situation is not one of those, we will tell you, and we would rather lose the booking than take it.
bullets: Both boredom and quiet struggle produce the same complaints and the same drift
One hard question in an easy topic separates them within two minutes
A bored student teaches you the topic and adds to it; a struggling one recites
Boredom loses careless marks; difficulty loses the same step repeatedly
Covering Diploma content early earns nothing and costs classroom attention
A competition, a project or a book list often beats another weekly hour

sections.heading: What does progress look like when the grade is already high?
paragraphs: The usual markers are useless here, because the mark cannot go up much and may well dip while the student is doing something harder than usual. At four weeks, progress looks like the student bringing their own questions to the session instead of waiting to be set work, and saying out loud that something was difficult. At one term it looks like a piece of work that was not required by anyone: a longer answer than the task asked for, a piece of reading they finished, an Extended Essay question they have actually narrowed. At one examination cycle the grade is whatever it was always going to be, and the honest measure is whether the student still finds the subject worth their time.

That is also the limit of what anyone can promise. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and for an already strong student the claim would be particularly empty, because the grade was largely secured before any tutor arrived. What enrichment can reasonably do is keep a capable student engaged with a subject through two years that would otherwise bore them, give them practice at being stuck, and produce one or two pieces of work that are genuinely their own. Those are real outcomes and they are worth paying for. A higher number on a report card is not what you are buying.

Review it honestly at the end of each term, and be willing to stop. The most common failure in enrichment arrangements is not a bad tutor but a good one who has run out of road, which happens quietly and which the student will notice first. Ask the student directly whether the hour is still worth it and take the answer seriously, including when the answer is no. If the fit is wrong rather than finished, tell us and we will reshortlist from the same brief. If the honest conclusion is that the hour would be better spent on a project the student chose themselves, that is a successful ending, not a failed arrangement.
bullets: Four weeks: the student brings their own questions instead of waiting for work
One term: a piece of work nobody required them to produce
The mark may dip while the work gets harder, and that is acceptable
No tutor can guarantee a grade, least of all for a student already near the top
Ask the student each term whether the hour is still worth it, and believe them

sections.heading: Getting started: the first home tuition session for a capable student
paragraphs: Send three things. A piece of work the student is proud of rather than a report card, because the strongest work shows the ceiling better than an average does. A sentence from the student, in their own words, about what is missing from the subject at school. And the one or two subjects this is actually about, since looking for one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is the wrong shape for this request. If the student will write that sentence themselves, the match is usually right within one try.

The first session should not be an assessment and should not be a revision hour. The tutor sets something hard in a topic the student claims is comfortable, lets them struggle with it properly, and spends the rest of the hour on why the hard version is hard. By the end, a parent should have heard the tutor say something about the subject that they themselves did not know, and the student should want to finish the question. If neither of those happened, this is not the right tutor, and there is no harm in saying so after one session.

Then set the terms the same way you would for any arrangement: the slot, the notice on both sides, how feedback reaches you, and the firm line that the tutor does not write any part of an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or coursework no matter how capable the student is. Book a review for the end of the term, and go into it genuinely willing to conclude that the hour has done its job and the student should spend next term on something of their own choosing.
bullets: Send the student's best work, not their report card
Ask the student to write one sentence on what is missing at school
Expect one or two subjects, not a timetable covering everything
Judge session one on whether the student wanted to finish the question
Book a term end review and be willing to end it there

faqs.question: My child gets high marks but says class is boring. Is a tutor the answer?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and often not. Start by separating boredom from quiet struggling, because they look the same and need opposite responses. If it is genuine boredom, the next question is whether the student needs an adult or needs room. A self motivated fifteen year old with a competition, a project or a reading list frequently gets more from those than from another scheduled hour led by someone else. A tutor earns the slot when the subject is not offered at school, when an Extended Essay or Internal Assessment needs early mentoring, or when the student wants to go deeper and has nobody to argue with about it.

faqs.question: Should we start Diploma content while our son is still in Year 10?
faqs.answer: Generally no, and it is the most common mistake made with strong students. Meeting Diploma material without the maturity to hold it builds a shallow memory that has faded by the time the class gets there, and it creates a student who believes they already know the topic and therefore stops listening in the lesson where their teacher explains the expected working and conventions. Nothing in either system rewards having covered content early. If Year 10 is genuinely too easy, add difficulty inside the current topics, take a subject separately rather than combined, or enter an additional subject. Depth earns something. Speed does not.

faqs.question: How do I tell boredom from quiet struggling when they look the same?
faqs.answer: Set one hard question in a topic your child says is easy and watch the first two minutes. A bored student leans in and starts trying things; a struggling student goes quiet, deflects, or asks whether it will be in the exam. Then ask them to teach you the topic: boredom explains fluently and adds detail nobody asked for, difficulty recites a definition and stops. Finally look at the lost marks. Boredom loses careless arithmetic and abandons long structured questions halfway. Difficulty fails at the same conceptual step across four different questions. Those three checks take an evening and will usually settle it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor take a subject further than our school offers?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the clearest cases for hiring one. If the school does not run Further Mathematics, a particular language, Music or Computer Science at the level your child wants, a tutor can teach it properly and, where it makes sense, prepare the student for an external entry that the school can advise you about. Be realistic about the workload before committing, because an additional subject taken outside the timetable sits on top of a full programme. Agree a review point after one term, and treat it as a genuine decision point rather than a formality.

faqs.question: Is it too early to start the Extended Essay in the first year of the Diploma?
faqs.answer: No, and for a capable student it is the single most valuable early work there is. The point is not to start writing but to choose well, which is where most Extended Essays are won or lost. A tutor can help test whether a research question is narrow enough, whether the sources genuinely exist and are accessible, and whether the subject fits the student's actual strengths. That work is conversation and reading, not drafting. The tutor must not write any part of the essay, supply sentences, or work inside the document, and your school's own supervisor remains the person who guides and signs off the process.

faqs.question: Will enrichment work help with university applications?
faqs.answer: It can, but not in the way families often assume, and nobody can promise an outcome. Admissions interest tends to sit with what a student has done and can discuss, rather than with the fact of having had a tutor. A student who read widely in a subject, built something, entered a competition or wrote a serious Extended Essay has material for an application and for an interview. An extra weekly hour that produced nothing visible does not. If applications are the motivation, bias the plan towards work with an output the student can point at and talk about unprompted.

faqs.question: Is an enrichment tutor priced differently from an exam tutor?
faqs.answer: Often yes, because the scarcity is different. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on board, level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length, and the ability to teach above the specification is itself scarce, particularly in Further Mathematics, Computer Science at Higher Level, a less common language or any subject needing a researcher rather than a teacher. Travel still prices in for home sessions. We do not publish a price list because an honest one does not exist, but we will tell you plainly which factor is driving a particular quote so you can decide whether online widens the pool enough to change it.

faqs.question: Our daughter is in Juhu and wants Latin, which her school does not teach. Can an online tutor do it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and online is almost certainly the right route for a subject that scarce. There is no reliable pool of Latin teachers within travelling distance of Juhu, Versova or Vile Parle for a weekday evening slot, and insisting on someone local usually means accepting someone who will be a chapter ahead of the student. Online removes the geography entirely and lets you choose on subject depth alone. Keep the sessions shorter and more frequent than you would for examination work, and ask the school what external entry route, if any, they would support before the second term.

faqs.question: Does a home tuition session for an older student still need a parent at home in Bandra West?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the flat, even for a seventeen year old, and most Bandra West and Khar West societies will separately want a resident to approve a visitor at the gate. Arrange standing entry so the home tutor is not negotiating with security each week. Beyond the safeguarding point, there is a practical reason to be nearby for enrichment specifically: overhearing ten minutes of a depth session tells you more about whether it is working than any monthly report will. Use the dining table rather than a bedroom and leave the door open, as you would at any age.

faqs.question: We are in Thane. Is a weekly home tuition slot worth it when there is no exam pressure?
faqs.answer: A fortnightly slot is usually the better commitment. Depth work needs time between sessions for the student to read, get stuck and come back with something, and a weekly home tuition visit across Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali or Hiranandani Estate is a heavy logistical load for an arrangement with no deadline forcing it. A fortnightly home session with short online contact in between holds far better through the year. Protect the slot by putting it on a weekend morning rather than a weekday evening, because Ghodbunder Road at seven will eventually end any arrangement that depends on it.

faqs.question: What if my child resists the extra sessions?
faqs.answer: Take the resistance seriously rather than negotiating around it. A capable student who does not want an extra hour is often right, and forcing it reliably turns a subject they liked into one they associate with being managed. Ask what they would rather do with the time and listen to the answer, because a project, a competition or simply unstructured reading may genuinely be the better use. If they do want depth but not this tutor, that is a different problem with an easy fix. If they want neither, stopping is a legitimate outcome and not a failure on anyone's part.

faqs.question: Do you have IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai who teach above the syllabus?
faqs.answer: In most subjects yes, though the pool is thinner than for examination coaching and varies sharply by area. Science, mathematics and computing specialists are easiest to find around Powai, Chandivali and the Central Suburbs, while the island city has more researchers and writers suited to humanities depth work. For a genuinely rare subject we will usually recommend online rather than pretend there is someone twenty minutes away. Tell us the subject and the level of stretch you want and we will say honestly whether a nearby match exists or whether widening to online gets you a better person.

ib-igcse-classes.closingCta: Send us the subject, the year group, a piece of work the student is proud of, and one sentence from the student about what is missing at school. You will get a short shortlist of tutors who can teach above the specification, with their open slots. If we think an activity or a reading list would serve your child better than a weekly hour, we will say so before you book anything.

ib-igcse-coaching.heroIntro: Parents looking for IB IGCSE coaching in Mumbai rarely plan for the day the tutor and the school contradict each other, yet it happens in most arrangements. This page is about that: whose view wins on assessed work, how to raise a real concern with a subject teacher, and how to keep a student in home tuition from being caught between two adults.
trustPoints: Tutors teach the method the school department is currently teaching
No tutor contacts your school, requests marks or disputes them for you
Predictions about what will not be examined are treated as a red flag
Feedback on a draft is advisory; the teacher's mark stands

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches IB IGCSE coaching in Mumbai to what the school teaches
paragraphs: Most tutor and school conflicts are built in at the matching stage, which is why the first questions we ask are about the school rather than the student. Which school, which campus, which subject teacher's sequence the class is following, which textbook or digital resource the department has set, and whether the student is in Year 10 or already into the second year of the Diploma Programme (DP). A tutor who knows that a Mulund department teaches enthalpy before kinetics, or that a Powai Maths teacher introduces the quadratic formula before completing the square, will not accidentally teach a method the class has not met and leave the student using it in a school test the following week.

The shortlist then goes out with that context attached, not just the subject name. Tutors are asked directly whether they currently teach that specification and how they handle the situation where a school does something differently from how they would. The answer to that second question is more revealing than any qualification. A tutor who says they would teach their own way because it is better is a tutor who will cost the family a term of confusion. A tutor who says they would teach the school's way first, then show the alternative once the student is secure, has done this before.

The last step is a short alignment conversation before the arrangement starts. The parent sends the tutor the school's task sheets, the teacher's written feedback on the last piece of work, and the term plan if the school publishes one. Those three documents tell a tutor more than an hour of conversation. They also establish, from day one, that the school is the reference point. Everything from that point on is coaching that supports what the school is doing, rather than a second parallel course running against it.
bullets: 1. Tell us the school, the campus, the subject and the year group
2. We shortlist tutors currently teaching that specification in your zone
3. Ask each tutor what they do when the school teaches something differently
4. Send the task sheet, the teacher's feedback and the term plan before session one
5. Agree aloud that the school's method is the one used in assessed work

sections.heading: Where the school and the tutor diverge in the MYP, IGCSE and the Diploma
paragraphs: Each programme produces its own kind of disagreement. In the Middle Years Programme (MYP) the clash is almost always about criteria. MYP tasks are marked against criteria A to D with level descriptors that schools interpret within their own standardisation, and a tutor trained on International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) grade boundaries will mark an MYP investigation as though it were a Physics paper. The student is then told their work is weak when the school has judged it appropriate for the level descriptor. Neither adult is lying. They are using different instruments.

At IGCSE the common dispute is tiering. Core and Extended entry is the school's decision, taken on the evidence of the student's work across Years 10 and 11, and a tutor who tells a family their child should be entered for Extended has formed an opinion from one hour a week with a student doing their best work under supervision. The teacher has formed one from classwork, tests and mocks. The tutor's view is worth hearing and worth raising with the school as a question. It is not worth treating as a verdict, and it should never be delivered to the student as one.

In the Diploma Programme the disagreements get sharper because the stakes are higher. Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices, the Internal Assessment (IA) in nearly every subject, the Extended Essay (EE) and the Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay all have published criteria that a good tutor knows well. Knowing the criteria is not the same as holding authority over them. The school applies them, standardises internally across its own teachers, submits the marks, and sees them moderated by the International Baccalaureate afterwards. A family that wants all IB and IGCSE subjects covered by home classes in Mumbai will quickly have several tutors with several views, and the simplest protection is one written rule: on anything assessed, the school's interpretation is the one the student follows.
bullets: MYP criteria are interpreted within each school's own standardisation process
Core and Extended entry is the school's judgement, not the tutor's recommendation
A tutor sees one supervised hour a week; a teacher sees everything else
Published criteria are public knowledge, but applying them is the school's job
With several tutors, write down that the school's reading wins on assessed work

sections.heading: Subject by subject: the method clashes that start most home classes badly
paragraphs: In Maths the clash is sequence. A tutor who introduces integration by parts to a DP student whose class has only covered reverse chain rule has given that student a tool they cannot yet justify, and in a school test they will use it, skip the working the teacher expects, and lose method marks for an answer that is correct. The same happens at IGCSE when a tutor solves every quadratic by completing the square because it is more elegant, while the department teaches the formula first and marks the working accordingly. Both approaches are mathematically sound. Only one of them matches what the marker in front of your child is reading.

In Chemistry and Physics it is usually notation and convention. Significant figures, units carried through working, state symbols in equations, whether an uncertainty is quoted as absolute or percentage in an IA, whether a Hess cycle or an energy level diagram is the expected presentation. Departments make consistent choices about these and mark against them. In English the clash is structure: a tutor who insists on a five paragraph essay shape for a Language A Literature commentary when the department has taught a thesis driven argument is not teaching badly, but the student now has two templates and will blend them under exam pressure into something that satisfies neither. In Economics it is diagram conventions and which evaluation framework the department has drilled.

The fix is the same in every subject and it is not complicated. The tutor teaches the school's method until the student is genuinely secure in it, and only then shows the alternative, labelled clearly as an alternative. Say that in the first session, with the student listening, so there is no ambiguity later. No one teaches all IB and IGCSE subjects and no tutor in Mumbai has sat in every department in the city, so expect the tutor to ask which convention the school uses rather than assume. A tutor who asks that question in week one is usually the one still working with the family in March.
bullets: Teach the school's method first; introduce alternatives only once the student is secure
Significant figures, units and uncertainty conventions are departmental choices, not universals
An essay structure taught twice becomes a hybrid that satisfies neither marker
Ask which convention the department uses before correcting a student's working
Label any alternative method out loud as an alternative, never as the correct way

sections.heading: Mumbai zone by zone, and why your tutor should know the local school sequence
paragraphs: IB Gram matches across Mumbai, Maharashtra, and the Central and Eastern Suburbs are where school and tutor alignment matters most, simply because so many international school families here are matched with tutors who teach several different schools in the same week. Powai and Chandivali hang off the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road with no station of their own, so tutors reach them by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar on the Central Line and Metro Line 1. A tutor covering Powai, Ghatkopar and Vikhroli in three evenings is working to three departmental sequences, and the one thing that keeps that straight is the task sheet the parent sends before each term.

Further east, Chembur, Govandi, Wadala, Bhandup and Mulund sit on the Central and Harbour lines with the Eastern Express Highway, the Monorail and the Santacruz Chembur Link Road threading between them, and the Eastern Freeway brings South Mumbai much closer to Chembur and Wadala than the map suggests. In Navi Mumbai the nodes govern everything: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short run from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway, served by the Harbour and Trans Harbour lines and Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1. The Atal Setu has shortened the crossing from the island city, but a tutor doing it twice a week in term time will not hold the slot to May.

Thane runs east from the station along Pokhran Road and Majiwada to Hiranandani Estate and Kasarvadavali, with Ghodbunder Road setting every schedule in the zone, and Mulund tutors occasionally cross over on the Eastern Express Highway. In the Western Suburbs, which stretch from Bandra East and Santacruz through Andheri West, Oshiwara, Goregaon, Malad and Kandivali to Borivali and Dahisar East, the Western Line, the Western Express Highway, the Link Road and Metro Lines 2A and 7 make north to south matching straightforward and east to west matching a daily negotiation.

South Mumbai is its own system. Fort, Babulnath, Tardeo, Peddar Road, Parel and Cuffe Parade are a short distance apart and a long time apart at six in the evening, with the Western Line into Churchgate and Grant Road, the Harbour Line to Dockyard, the Coastal Road and Metro Line 3 between Cuffe Parade and the Bandra Kurla Complex doing the work. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai based on the island almost never also teaches in the suburbs, which is good news for consistency: a South Mumbai tutor typically knows two or three local departments properly rather than eight of them loosely.
bullets: Send the term's task sheets to a tutor who teaches several schools a week
Powai has no station, so a road based grace window belongs in the schedule
Navi Mumbai nodes match to each other; island city crossings fade by October
Western Suburbs match north to south along the line, not east to west
A tutor who knows two departments well beats one who knows eight loosely

sections.heading: Who wins when a Mumbai school and your tutor disagree?
paragraphs: The school wins on anything assessed, and this is not a matter of politeness. The school registers the student as a candidate, teaches the prescribed course, administers and marks the internal assessment, standardises those marks across its own teachers, submits them to the International Baccalaureate for moderation or to Cambridge International Education for moderation, and signs the authenticity declaration that says the work is the student's own. A private tutor does none of those things and carries none of that responsibility. On a question of teaching, the tutor may well be right. On a question of what the student submits and how it is marked, the tutor has no standing at all.

That calendar also decides when a disagreement is survivable. The Mumbai international school year starts in June, with first assessments by August and term tests and mocks through October. January and February carry IA deadlines across most Diploma subjects, the Extended Essay submission and the TOK essay, and March and April go to prelims before the May examinations and the IGCSE May and June series. A method dispute raised in August is a ten minute conversation. The same dispute raised in February, with a draft due on Friday, becomes a crisis. Families at NES International School in Mulund West, JBCN International School in Chembur, Oberoi International School on JVLR, Thakur International School in Kandivali East and Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo are all working to some version of that shape.

Raising a genuine concern with a subject teacher works best when it is a question rather than an assertion, and when it comes from the parent rather than from the tutor through the parent. Email the subject teacher, not the head of school. Attach the student's own work, not the tutor's annotated copy. Ask what the student should do differently next time, rather than asking why the mark was what it was. Do not say that your tutor disagrees, because the moment a tutor is invoked the conversation stops being about the student. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, with the International Baccalaureate organisation, with Cambridge International Education or with Pearson Edexcel, and no tutor listed with us speaks to a school on a family's behalf.
bullets: The school enters the candidate, marks internal work and signs the authenticity declaration
Email the subject teacher, not the head, and attach the student's own work
Ask what to do differently next time instead of why the mark was given
Never mention the tutor's disagreement in a message to the school
A dispute raised in August is a conversation; in February it is a crisis

sections.heading: Does home tuition or online coaching catch a method clash sooner in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition catches it sooner, which is one of the better arguments for it. A parent in the next room hears the student say that this is not how the teacher does it, and the conversation happens that evening rather than after a disappointing test. Online sessions are more private, which suits an older student but means a clash can run unnoticed for a month. Both modes work, and most families running IB and IGCSE coaching in Mumbai across a full year use a mix.

The trade-offs are concrete. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai can hold the school's printed task sheet next to the student's exercise book and work through both, which is genuinely harder on a screen. A home session also makes it normal for a parent to ask, once a month, whether anything the school is doing is causing difficulty. Against that, home sessions depend on travel, and a tutor crossing the Western Express Highway at six will eventually ask to move the slot. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai can screen share the exact page of the department's resource, annotate it live and send the annotated file afterwards, which is the single best tool for keeping a tutor aligned with a school they have never visited.

Hybrid tends to resolve it. Keep the main weekly session at home, where the clash surfaces, and use online for extra sessions in the January and February crush when nobody can travel. Whichever mix you choose, agree one thing in advance: when the student reports that the school does something differently, the tutor pauses and checks rather than correcting the school in front of the child. That rule costs nothing and prevents almost all of the damage described further down this page.
bullets: Home sessions surface a method clash because someone else overhears it
Online screen sharing of the department's own resource keeps a tutor aligned
Older Diploma students often prefer online, which hides clashes for longer
Keep the weekly session at home and add online hours in the February crush
Agree the tutor pauses and checks rather than correcting the school aloud

sections.heading: What should a tutor do when they think the school is wrong?
paragraphs: A professional tutor who believes the school has got something wrong does three things and stops. They teach the school's approach so the student is not disadvantaged in the next assessment. They explain the difference to the parent privately, in writing, without drama and without telling the parent what to do about it. And they say nothing critical about the teacher in front of the student. That is the whole protocol. Anything beyond it, such as emailing the department, coaching the parent on what to write, or telling the student the teacher is mistaken, moves the tutor outside their role and almost always makes the student's position worse.

This is also what we check for before a tutor is listed. We verify identity documents, the qualification claimed and the teaching history against the current specification rather than the board in general. Then we ask the scenario questions: what do you do if a draft comes back marked lower than you would have marked it, what do you do if a student says the teacher has not taught something you think is examinable, what do you do if a parent asks you to email the school. The answers sort tutors quickly. We do not rate tutors with stars and we do not publish results claims, so these conversations are the check that matters.

Parents should run their own version of the same test on the first call, and it takes four questions. Which specification are you teaching right now. What do you do when the department's method differs from yours. Have you ever been asked to contact a school, and what did you say. What would you do if you thought an internal mark was too low. Families often search for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai and there is no such person, but there is a clear difference between a tutor who answers those four questions calmly and one who treats them as an insult. The second kind is the one who will put your child in the middle.
bullets: Teach the school's approach first so the next assessment is not affected
Raise the difference with the parent privately and in writing, without recommending action
Never criticise a named teacher where the student can hear it
Ask any new tutor what they would do about a mark they think is too low
A tutor offended by that question is the wrong tutor for this arrangement

sections.heading: Can a tutor challenge a disputed internal mark in a Mumbai school?
paragraphs: No. A private tutor has no standing whatsoever in a disputed internal mark, and understanding why saves families a great deal of wasted anger. Internal assessment marks are produced by the student's own teacher, standardised across the department so that two teachers of the same subject award comparably, and then submitted by the school. The awarding body moderates a sample afterwards and may adjust the school's marks as a whole. At no point in that process is there a slot for an outside opinion, and no school anywhere is obliged to read, acknowledge or respond to an annotated copy produced by a tutor.

What does exist is narrower and more useful. A parent may ask the subject teacher to explain the mark against the criteria, and a good department will do that willingly. A student may ask what specifically would have moved a strand from one band to the next, which is a far better question because it produces something actionable for the next piece. Many schools have an internal review route for a mark a family believes was misapplied, and the school office will say what it is. After results are published there is a formal enquiry process with the awarding body, but it is initiated by the school, not by a parent and certainly not by a tutor. If your tutor offers to take any of this on, decline, politely and firmly.

There is one more thing worth understanding about a disputed draft mark, because it is the most common version of this argument. A tutor marking a draft is marking it cold, against the published criteria, with no knowledge of what the rest of the cohort produced or where the department set its internal standard. A teacher marking the same draft is marking it inside that context. The tutor's mark is therefore often harsher and occasionally kinder, and in both cases it is less informative than it looks. Treat tutor feedback on a draft as a list of things to improve, which is what it is genuinely good for, and treat the teacher's mark as the mark, because that is what it is.

The reason to be strict about all this is not procedural tidiness. It is the student. A fifteen year old who is told by one trusted adult that their work is a six and by another that it is a four stops being able to judge their own work at all, which is the single skill the whole Diploma is trying to build. Decide, out loud and early, that the teacher's mark is the mark and the tutor's feedback is advice on the next piece. Say it to the student in those words. Never ask a student to carry a message, a question or a complaint from a tutor to a teacher, or from a teacher to a tutor. The damage from being the courier between two disagreeing adults lasts longer than any single grade.
bullets: Internal marks are standardised within the department and moderated by the awarding body
A parent can ask the teacher to explain a mark against the criteria
Ask what would move a strand up a band, not why the mark was given
Formal post results enquiries are initiated by the school, never by a tutor
Tell the student plainly: the teacher's mark is the mark, the tutor's note is advice
Never make the student the messenger between a tutor and a teacher

sections.heading: What progress looks like, and the damage nobody measures in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks, progress in an arrangement like this looks like alignment rather than marks. The student stops saying that the tutor and the teacher want different things. Work handed in at school uses one method consistently. At one term, a school report or a mock should move, and the teacher's written comments should start to echo what the tutor has been working on, which is the clearest evidence that the coaching is pointed in the right direction. At one full examination cycle you can judge the whole thing. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and neither does any tutor listed with us.

There is a second measure that nobody tracks and that matters more over two years. Does the student still trust their own judgement about their work? A student who has been caught between a tutor and a teacher for a term stops predicting their own marks, stops defending choices in their own essays, and starts asking which adult to believe instead of deciding what they think. That is the real cost of an unmanaged disagreement, and it does not appear in any report. If you notice it starting, fix the structure immediately: one authority on assessed work, feedback that is clearly labelled as advice, and no messages carried by the child.

When an arrangement is not working, say so to the tutor directly first, because a surprising proportion of these cases are solved by one conversation about whose method gets taught. If the tutor cannot work inside the school's approach, that is a genuine mismatch and not a failing on anyone's part, and we will reshortlist from the same brief with it recorded. Give the notice you agreed, settle sessions already taught, and move on. What should not happen is a family tolerating a running conflict for a term because changing tutors in February feels harder than living with it. It is not harder. It is just less visible.
bullets: Four weeks: the student stops reporting that two adults want different things
One term: teacher comments start echoing what the tutor has been working on
One examination cycle: the only honest verdict on the arrangement
Watch whether the student can still predict their own marks
A tutor who cannot work inside the school's approach is a mismatch, not a villain

sections.heading: Getting started: what to bring to the first home tuition session
paragraphs: Bring four documents and the first session will be worth three. The school's task sheet or assignment brief for the current piece of work, which tells the tutor exactly what is being asked. The teacher's last written feedback, which tells the tutor what the department values. One recent piece of the student's own work, unedited. And the subject list marked with Higher Level and Standard Level, or Core and Extended. A single home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is rarely realistic, so if two subjects are in difficulty, expect two people and sequence the scarcer subject first.

The session itself should begin with the tutor reading the teacher's feedback before they read the student's work, which is the opposite of what most tutors do. It tells them where the department's bar sits. Then they should teach something substantial, set one piece of work, and tell the parent in plain language what they think the actual problem is. Very often it is not the subject named in the enquiry. A student struggling with Diploma Economics evaluation is sometimes a student who writes well but has never been shown what evaluation means in that department's marking.

Before anything else is agreed, settle the alignment rule out loud with the student present: the school's method is used in assessed work, the tutor's alternatives are labelled as alternatives, the teacher's mark is the mark, and nobody sends messages through the child. It takes two minutes and it is the difference between coaching that supports the school and coaching that quietly competes with it. Then book the slot, agree how feedback reaches you, and diarise a review for the end of the term.
bullets: Bring the task sheet, the teacher's feedback and one unedited piece of work
Ask the tutor to read the teacher's feedback before reading the student's work
State the alignment rule aloud in session one, with the student listening
Expect two tutors if two subjects are in trouble, starting with the scarcer one
Diarise an end of term review on the day you agree the slot

faqs.question: Our tutor teaches a different method from the school. Whose method should my child use?
faqs.answer: The school's, in anything that is marked by the school or sent to an awarding body. The teacher is the person reading the work, applying the department's expectations about working, layout and notation, and awarding the marks that count. A tutor's method may be faster or more elegant and still cost marks because the expected steps are missing. The useful compromise is sequence: the tutor teaches the school's method until the student is genuinely fluent in it, then shows the alternative and labels it clearly as an alternative for later. A student who knows two methods is strong. A student who cannot tell which one is expected is not.

faqs.question: Our tutor says a topic will not be examined. Should we skip it?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who says this should be queried rather than followed. Specifications are published in full and schools teach them in full because any part of them can appear. A tutor predicting what will not come up is guessing from recent papers, and the cost of being wrong lands entirely on your child. There is a legitimate version of this advice, which is a tutor saying that a topic has historically carried fewer marks and so should be revised later rather than first. That is a prioritising judgement and it is useful. Skipping content on a prediction is not, and no school will support it.

faqs.question: Our tutor marked an Internal Assessment draft far lower than the teacher did. Who is right?
faqs.answer: Probably neither, and the comparison is less useful than it looks. The tutor marked the draft cold against the published criteria with no knowledge of what the rest of the cohort produced or where the department set its internal standard. The teacher marked it inside that context, which is the context the final mark lives in. Use the tutor's version for what it is genuinely good for, which is a specific list of what to improve in the next draft, and treat the teacher's mark as the mark. Asking the two adults to reconcile their numbers wastes a fortnight and teaches the student nothing.

faqs.question: How do I raise a concern with a subject teacher without it becoming a complaint?
faqs.answer: Write to the subject teacher directly, not to the head of school, and open with a question rather than a position. Attach your child's own work, never a tutor's annotated copy. Ask what specifically would move the next piece up a band, which is a question teachers answer willingly because it is about teaching rather than about them. Do not mention that a tutor disagrees; the moment a tutor is invoked, the conversation becomes a defence of a mark instead of a plan for the next one. Keep it short, keep it about the student, and send it when there is not a deadline that week.

faqs.question: Can our tutor appeal a mark the school has given?
faqs.answer: No. A private tutor has no standing in any part of the marking process and no school is obliged to read anything a tutor produces. Internal marks are set by the teacher, standardised across the department and submitted by the school, with the awarding body moderating a sample afterwards. What exists instead is narrower: a parent can ask the teacher to explain the mark against the criteria, many schools have an internal review route the office can describe, and a formal enquiry after results is initiated by the school. If a tutor offers to handle any of this for you, decline.

faqs.question: My child is confused by two different explanations. What do we do this week?
faqs.answer: Stop the second explanation immediately and name one authority out loud. Tell your child, in those words, that the teacher's method is the one used in anything that is marked and the tutor's version is something to look at later. Then tell the tutor the same thing in writing, so it is not ambiguous. Confusion between two explanations is not a sign that either adult is incompetent; it is a sign that nobody has said which one applies. In our experience this is fixed in a single session, and left alone for a term it quietly destroys a student's confidence in judging their own work.

faqs.question: Should the tutor and the subject teacher speak to each other directly?
faqs.answer: No, and tutors who offer to should be declined. A school's relationship is with the family, not with a privately hired third party, and a teacher contacted by someone's tutor is being put in an awkward position with no good way out. If information needs to move, the parent moves it: you can tell the tutor what the teacher said, and you can ask the teacher a question that the tutor's observation prompted. What you should not do is let the two professionals negotiate about your child over your head, because you then lose the ability to decide what your child is actually told.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who already knows our school charge more?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is usually worth it. Rates depend on board, level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length, and familiarity with a specific department sits inside the scarcity factor: fewer tutors know a given school's sequence and conventions well. A Higher Level Diploma subject carries a heavier marking load than a Year 9 IGCSE subject and is priced accordingly, and a tutor crossing the city twice a week is pricing that travel in. We do not publish a price list because an honest one does not exist, but we will tell you which factors are pushing a particular quote up.

faqs.question: We live in Mulund and the school is in Powai. Should the home tutor be near us or near the school?
faqs.answer: Near you, every time. The home tuition session happens at your dining table, not at the school gate, so the tutor's commute is from their home to yours on a weekday evening. A Mulund based tutor reaches you on the Eastern Express Highway in a predictable window; a Powai based tutor is fighting the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road at exactly the wrong hour. Knowledge of the Powai department matters, but it travels by document rather than by proximity: send the task sheets and the teacher's feedback, and a nearby tutor will align within a fortnight.

faqs.question: Can home tuition continue while a disagreement with the school is unresolved?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it usually should, provided the home classes switch to the school's method in the meantime. Pausing a home tutor while a question sits in a teacher's inbox costs the student two or three weeks they cannot spare, particularly in January. Tell the tutor to teach the school's approach for now and to park their alternative until the question is answered. Keep the weekly slot, keep the work going, and keep the disagreement entirely between the adults. The one thing that must pause is any commentary about the teacher inside the session itself.

faqs.question: What if the school tells us not to use a tutor at all?
faqs.answer: Listen to the reason before reacting, because it is often a good one. Some departments have seen students arrive with tutor written drafts and are protecting the authenticity declaration they have to sign. Others have found that a second set of explanations was confusing a particular student. Neither is a rule against outside help, and no school can forbid it. What you can do is tell the teacher how the arrangement works: the tutor teaches skills and the school's method, gives written feedback on drafts the student wrote, and does not touch assessed work. That usually ends the concern.

faqs.question: We live in Vashi. How close does the tutor actually need to be?
faqs.answer: Inside Navi Mumbai, and ideally inside two nodes. Parents searching for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai often assume the city is one labour market, but Vashi is matched from Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel along Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway, where a weekday evening run is predictable. A tutor coming from the island city across the Atal Setu will take the booking in June and start asking to move the slot by September. Ask every candidate where they personally live before you agree a time, not which areas they list as covered.

ib-igcse-coaching.closingCta: Tell us the school, the campus, the subject and the year group, and send the task sheet and the teacher's last written feedback with it. You will get a short shortlist of tutors who already teach that specification nearby, with their open slots. You speak to them, ask what they do when a school teaches something differently, and set the alignment rule in session one. If the fit is wrong, tell us and we reshortlist.

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai to your programme stage
paragraphs: Most requests for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai arrive carrying two facts: a subject and an address. Those two facts are not enough to build a shortlist, because the same subject behaves completely differently at the two ends of the pathway. Chemistry for a Year 10 student in Chembur means weekly topic tests, regular homework and a steady march through a wide syllabus. Chemistry for a second-year Diploma Programme (DP) student in Bandra West means one Internal Assessment (IA) report that has quietly eaten her weekends since the monsoon ended. Both students need help. They do not need the same tutor, the same session length or the same number of sessions a week.

So the first question we ask is where in the cycle the student sits and what the next four weeks hold. A Year 9 student picking International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) options wants someone who can hold three or four subjects loosely at once, keep homework honest and spot which subject is quietly slipping. A DP student eight weeks from an Extended Essay (EE) submission wants a specialist who can argue about a research question, read a messy draft properly and then get out of the way. Matching on nearest-available rather than on programme shape is the shortcut that makes an arrangement collapse in week six.

Shortlists go out with the tutor's board experience, the specific components and papers they have taught, the slots they can genuinely hold for a whole term, and their honest travel time to your building at the hour you want it. We say plainly when a request is hard. A Higher Level (HL) subject at an awkward hour in a part of the city with a thin pool takes longer to fill, and we would rather tell you that than send a weak profile quickly so the enquiry looks answered.

Parents comparing an IB and IGCSE private tutor Mumbai agencies supply against a platform match usually care about one thing: who is accountable when it stops working. Here the answer is the platform. You tell us the sessions are not landing, we ask what specifically is not landing, and we either rewrite the brief or change the tutor. Neither of those requires you to start the search again from nothing.
bullets: 1. Tell us the board, the year group and the next assessment date
2. We translate that into a session length and a weekly frequency
3. You receive profiles listing components taught and realistic travel windows
4. You meet one tutor before any standing weekly slot is agreed
5. We review the brief after four weeks and adjust the rhythm

sections.heading: Why IGCSE and Diploma work pull a tutor's week in opposite directions
paragraphs: IGCSE work is broad, frequent and short-cycle. A Year 10 student is carrying eight or nine subjects, each with its own homework, each with a class test every few weeks, and a final assessment that rewards coverage above almost anything else. The failure mode is not a single catastrophic gap. It is six small gaps across six subjects that nobody noticed because each one on its own looked survivable. A tutor working that shape needs to move quickly, cover ground, check retention from a fortnight ago and accept that depth in any single topic is rarely the point.

Diploma Programme work is the mirror image. A student carries six subjects instead of nine, three of them at Higher Level, and the volume of weekly homework is often lower than it was at IGCSE. What replaces it is long-cycle work: an Internal Assessment in every subject, a Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay and exhibition, and an Extended Essay of four thousand words that no teacher will chase weekly until it is nearly too late. These do not generate pressure evenly. They generate nothing for months and then everything at once.

That difference changes what a tutor is for. At IGCSE the tutor is a regular presence who keeps a wide front from sagging. In the Diploma the tutor is closer to a supervisor with subject expertise: someone who reads a methodology section, says the sample size will not support that claim, and sends the student back to redo two weeks of work. One role rewards consistency. The other rewards being available in concentrated bursts at exactly the right fortnight.

A household that runs both at once feels this as a scheduling conflict rather than an academic one. The Year 10 child needs three steady short sessions a week, every week, through the year. The DP child needs almost nothing in August and four long sessions a week in late January. Treating all tuition as one undifferentiated weekly expense, with identical slots for both children, means one of them is always being served badly.
bullets: IGCSE: many subjects, frequent homework, papers that reward syllabus coverage
Diploma: fewer subjects, deeper components, deadlines that arrive in clusters
IGCSE tutoring rewards regularity; Diploma tutoring rewards being there at the right fortnight
Core and Extended tiers decide how much IGCSE ground a tutor has to cover
Higher Level and Standard Level choices decide how long a Diploma session needs to be

sections.heading: Subject choice across both boards, and the internal assessment each one carries
paragraphs: At IGCSE the decision that shapes the next two years is tier. Mathematics, the sciences and several language syllabuses split into Core and Extended, and the tier caps the grade available. Families often make that choice in Year 9 on the basis of one difficult term, then spend Year 11 trying to reverse it. A home tutor is useful here before the choice rather than after it: a few weeks of Extended-level questions tells you more about whether a student can hold that tier than a school report does. Coursework exists in some subjects and not others, which is why one child's IGCSE year is almost entirely exam preparation and another's is punctuated by portfolio deadlines.

In the Diploma the equivalent decision is Higher Level against Standard Level, and it is harder to undo. Higher Level in Physics or Chemistry adds whole option topics and a markedly longer Paper 2. Higher Level in English or History adds a third paper or an extended comparative component. The mistake we see most often is a student taking three Higher Levels that all demand long written work, so the same fortnight in January carries a History internal assessment, an English written task and the Extended Essay final draft.

Every Diploma subject carries its own internal assessment, and they are not equivalent pieces of work. The Sciences want a genuine investigation with a defensible method and real error analysis. Mathematics wants an exploration with a personal angle that still does actual mathematics. Economics wants commentaries built on recent published articles. Language A wants an oral built around two extracts. A tutor who has marked or taught the particular one your child is facing saves more time than a generally strong subject teacher who has not.

This is why the shortlist for all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai covers is built component by component rather than subject by subject. A tutor can be genuinely strong at Diploma Biology and still be the wrong person for a Year 10 Biology student revising for an end-of-topic test on transport in plants, and the reverse is just as true. Families booking all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Mumbai agencies advertise as a single package should still ask, subject by subject, which papers and which criteria that tutor has actually worked with.

Higher Level adds option topics, longer papers and more written components

sections.heading: Where IB and IGCSE home tutoring in Mumbai reaches across the six zones
paragraphs: IB Gram matches home tutors across the whole of Mumbai, Maharashtra, and across Navi Mumbai and Thane, but matching works on corridors rather than on distance. In South Mumbai, families in Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar, Peddar Road and Worli are served by tutors who already live on the island, because a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers eight kilometres and still loses forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at seven in the evening. The Coastal Road has changed the northbound run more than the southbound one, and Metro Line 3 between Cuffe Parade and the Bandra Kurla Complex has made a BKC-based tutor viable in Nariman Point in a way that was not true before.

In the Western Suburbs the geography is a line, not a grid. Bandra West, Khar West, Santacruz, Juhu, Andheri West, Goregaon, Malad, Kandivali and Borivali sit along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway, and matching along that line works far better than matching across it. A Khar to Santacruz slot holds for a year. A Malad to Bandra slot at six in the evening does not. Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made the Dahisar to Andheri stretch workable for tutors who previously would not have taken it.

The Central Suburbs run on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road in between. Powai is the exception worth knowing about: it is physically central and has no station of its own, so tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar and their travel time swings widely. The Eastern Suburbs stretch from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund, and the Eastern Freeway makes Chembur and Wadala far closer to South Mumbai than the map suggests.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short drive from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway, and matching is done node to node. Pulling a tutor across the creek from the island city for a weekday evening rarely survives a full term even with the Atal Setu open. Thane spreads from the station east along Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road, and Ghodbunder sets the schedule: twenty minutes to Kasarvadavali off-peak, close to an hour at eight in the evening. Thane tutors cover Thane; Mulund tutors sometimes cross over.

sections.heading: Which months are the real pressure points in the Mumbai school year?
paragraphs: The pressure lands in different months for the two programmes, and a family running both should mark both sets of dates on the same calendar. For IGCSE students the heavy months are January and February, when mock examinations arrive and coursework in subjects that carry it has to be finalised, and then April and May for the examination series itself. For second-year Diploma students the heavy stretch starts earlier and lasts longer: Extended Essay final drafts and most Internal Assessment deadlines cluster between November and early February, mock examinations follow almost immediately, and the May session leaves very little recovery room between them.

Schools across the city run broadly the same rhythm even though their calendars differ in detail. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul all deal with the same two-part squeeze: a long autumn of coursework followed by a short, brutal examination run-up.

What matters practically is that the two squeezes overlap. The fortnight in late January when a Diploma student is finishing an Extended Essay is the same fortnight the Year 10 sibling has mocks. If both children are on the same two-hour evening slot with the same tutor, one of them loses. Families who plan for this in October rather than discovering it in January end up paying for roughly the same number of hours, just distributed differently.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school, examination board or organisation named here. Schools are named only because their calendars are what sets the timing of the pressure, and a tutor who has worked with students from a particular school already knows when that school issues its mock timetable.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a household running both programmes?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default for a reason, and the reason is sharper at IGCSE than in the Diploma. A Year 10 student with eight subjects benefits enormously from someone physically present who can see which exercise book has not been opened, notice that the Geography folder is empty, and insist on the next twenty minutes being spent on it. That kind of correction is much weaker through a screen. This is why IB IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai remains the lead service on this page rather than a fallback, and why most IGCSE briefs we fill end up as in-person weekly slots.

For Diploma work the balance shifts. An Internal Assessment review is a conversation about a document that both people are reading, and that works as well remotely as it does across a dining table. Many families run the sensible hybrid: the Year 10 child keeps a standing in-person slot three evenings a week, and the Diploma child sees a specialist remotely for longer, less frequent sessions, which also widens the pool when the subject is an uncommon one. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai can also be the honest answer when the only strong specialist for a Higher Level option lives in Thane and you live in Colaba.

The trade-offs are real in both directions. Home tuition costs travel time, which the household pays for in schedule rigidity: a tutor who crosses Ghodbunder Road to reach you cannot also take a seven o'clock slot elsewhere, so your slot is fixed and moving it is genuinely difficult. Remote sessions are easier to move and easier to keep running through a disrupted week, but they make it harder for a tutor to notice the things a student does not say.

A family running both programmes usually ends up with a mixed arrangement rather than a single answer, and that is the right outcome. What matters is that each child's mode is chosen on the shape of their work, not on whichever was arranged first for the older one.
bullets: Home sessions suit broad IGCSE work and students who need visible accountability
Remote sessions suit document-centred Diploma work such as drafts and commentaries

sections.heading: How a tutor is checked, and what you should check yourself in Mumbai
paragraphs: Before a profile reaches you, IB Gram confirms identity, academic qualifications and teaching or tutoring history, and asks for references that can actually be contacted. We also ask something more specific than most checks cover: which syllabus version a tutor has taught, which papers and components, and whether they have supervised internal assessment work or only taught content. Those are different skills. A tutor who has taught Diploma Economics content well may never have read an Economics commentary against the published criteria, and for a DP2 family in January that gap is the whole job.

There is a second check that only you can do, and it takes one session. Ask the tutor to look at the most recent marked piece of work and explain, out loud, where the marks were lost and what the student should have written instead. A tutor who knows the assessment criteria will do this in specifics and name the criterion. A tutor who does not will talk about effort, concentration and practice. That single exchange tells you more than any certificate.

For home sessions, do the practical checks in the first week rather than the second month. Confirm the tutor's identity at your society gate and agree how they will be cleared each week so nobody is standing outside arguing with security at seven in the evening. Agree where the session happens and that the door stays open. Agree what happens if the tutor is running late, and what counts as a cancellation.

An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai who is genuinely right for your household will not resist any of this, and will usually have asked several of the same questions already. Treat visible reluctance to be specific about components, criteria or timing as the signal it is.

sections.heading: How often and how long should sessions run for a Year 10 and a DP2 student?
paragraphs: For a Year 10 IGCSE student, three shorter sessions a week beat one long one, and sixty to seventy-five minutes is usually the right length. The work is broad and short-cycle, so the value comes from frequency: catching a misunderstanding four days after it happened rather than three weeks later, keeping homework from accumulating, and rotating across two or three subjects so none of them goes quiet. A two and a half hour Sunday block covering four subjects looks efficient on a timetable and produces very little, because the student stops absorbing roughly ninety minutes in and the rest of the week has no checkpoint in it.

For a second-year Diploma student the opposite holds. Ninety minutes to two hours, once or twice a week, is the useful shape, because the work is long-cycle and document-based. You cannot meaningfully review a draft methodology, interrogate the data and agree a rewrite in forty-five minutes. What you can do is agree, at the end of a long session, exactly what will exist by the next one. A Diploma student with three Higher Levels often needs no tuition at all in a quiet stretch and then four sessions a week for the three weeks around an Internal Assessment deadline.

This is why a weekly rhythm that suits a Year 10 student is wrong for a DP2 student in February. The Year 10 pattern is steady all year and barely changes between October and March. The Diploma pattern should look like a flat line with two or three sharp peaks on it: light from July to October, rising through November, heavy from early January to the mock results, then tapering into revision. A family paying for an identical fixed two hours a week for both children all year is overbuying for one child in September and underbuying for the other in January.

The practical adjustment is to book the IGCSE child's slots as a standing commitment for the term and the Diploma child's as a block agreed six to eight weeks ahead against known deadlines. Ask the tutor at the start of each month what the next four weeks need rather than assuming last month's answer still holds. Families arranging IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai for two children at different stages find that this one change, more than any change of tutor, is what makes the arrangement feel worth the money.

sections.heading: What progress should look like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at grades at all. What you should see is a tutor who can tell you, without notes, exactly which three things the student cannot currently do and what the plan is for each. You should see homework being completed before the session rather than during it, and the student able to say what last week's session was about. If none of that is true after four weeks, the problem is the match or the brief, and it is worth raising then rather than waiting for a report card to confirm it.

At one term the signal is different. For an IGCSE student you should see test scores stabilising and the number of topics the student actively avoids going down. For a Diploma student you should see a draft that exists, has been read against the criteria and been revised once. A first draft that has never been marked is not progress, however long it is. Grades at this point move unevenly and sometimes move the wrong way, particularly when a student stops guessing and starts attempting harder questions properly.

Over a full examination cycle, the fair thing to judge is whether the student walked into the examination hall knowing what the papers were going to ask and having practised under time. That is what tuition can reliably produce. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and anyone who offers you a guaranteed grade improvement is selling something that no tutor controls. Outcomes depend on the student's own work, the school's teaching, the papers in that session and a good deal that nobody can predict.

IB Gram is an independent platform. We are not affiliated with any school named on this page, with the International Baccalaureate organisation, with Cambridge International Education or with Pearson Edexcel. We match tutors and we stay accountable for the match. The teaching happens between your child and a person in your living room, and the honest version of what we sell is a well-chosen person and a schedule that fits the year.

sections.heading: Starting IB IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Have three things ready before you write to us and the first shortlist will be much better. First, the most recent marked work in the subject, including the marks and any comments, because that is what tells a tutor where the gap actually is. Second, the next three assessment dates the school has published, whether that is a Year 10 unit test or a Diploma Internal Assessment deadline. Third, an honest statement of the slots your household can hold every week for a term, including the evenings nobody is home.

The first session is diagnostic and should feel like one. A good tutor spends the opening half of it finding out what the student can do unaided, usually by working through a past question and watching where it breaks down. The second half is a plan: what will be covered in the next four sessions, what homework comes between them, and what the student should bring. You should receive that plan in writing, and it should be specific enough that you could check it against the next month.

If the household is running both programmes, say so in the first message. We will treat it as two briefs, not one, because the two children need different session lengths, different frequencies and different peaks in the year. Often the answer is two tutors; sometimes it is one tutor with two differently shaped arrangements. Parents searching for IB and IGCSE tutors near me Mumbai usually expect a single standard package, and the single standard package is precisely what fails a household at two different stages. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai households carry at once is rarely one person anyway; it is usually two people with two different schedules.

Tell us the board, the year group, the subjects, the area and the slots. We will come back with profiles that match the shape of the work rather than the nearest available diary, and we will say plainly if something cannot be filled at the time you want it.
bullets: Send recent marked work with the marks and the teacher comments attached
Send the next three published assessment dates from the school
