sections.heading: How do you judge a specialist in a subject you cannot assess yourself?
paragraphs: This is the real difficulty with a scarce subject, and no amount of credential checking solves it on its own. You can read a certificate in a language you do not speak and learn nothing. IB Gram confirms identity, qualifications and teaching history before any profile is shared, and records which syllabus, which papers and which components a tutor has worked with, but the question of whether this person is genuinely good at this particular course needs a different kind of test.

The most reliable test does not require you to know the subject. Ask the tutor to take one piece of your child's marked work and explain where the marks were lost, naming the criterion and saying what should have been written instead. Then ask what the most common reason is that students lose marks on that specific component. A specialist answers both in concrete detail and often disagrees with the school's marking in a specific, defensible way. A generalist answers in terms of effort, practice and confidence. You do not need the subject to tell those two answers apart.

Three further checks cost nothing. Ask which edition or syllabus year they last taught, because an out-of-date specialist is a real risk in options that have been revised. Ask them to describe the assessment structure of the course from memory, including the weighting, since anyone who has taught it knows this cold. And ask your child's supervising teacher at school to join or review the first session if they are willing, because even a teacher who does not read the language can tell whether the conversation is about assessment criteria or about vocabulary.

Finally, use the first four weeks as evidence. A specialist produces a plan tied to the published assessment structure within the first two sessions. If after a month you still have no written plan naming components and dates, the match is wrong regardless of how impressive the credentials were. This applies equally to an IB and IGCSE private tutor Mumbai families find independently and to one we match.

sections.heading: Is the subject genuinely scarce in Mumbai, or have you just searched badly?
paragraphs: Establish this before you widen the search, because most families who believe a subject is unavailable have searched for the wrong thing. Parents in this position usually begin by asking who the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai is, when the question that finds anybody is which tutor has taught this specific option. Three mistakes account for nearly all of it. The first is searching on the subject name rather than the course: searching for a French tutor when you need someone who has taught French Language A literature returns hundreds of people, none of them right, and the volume of results makes the subject look well covered. The second is searching only on the board: a tutor who teaches your language at A Level or at a university may well be the strongest option available and will never appear in a search for IB and IGCSE tutors near me Mumbai. The third is stopping at the first two names, which with a small pool is statistically meaningless.

A genuine scarcity test takes about a week. Ask your school's head of that department who they would call if their own teacher were away for a month. Ask the examinations officer whether any other student in the school is sitting the same option. Ask parents in the year group with the same option, since a shared tutor is common in these subjects. Ask us to run a component-level search rather than a subject search. If all four return nothing, the subject is genuinely scarce in this city and widening is the right next step rather than a failure of effort.

Widening to the whole country changes the odds substantially for Diploma options, because an option taught by two teachers in Mumbai may have thirty teachers across India's international schools. It changes nothing about the fee logic, except that you are no longer paying for travel, which usually offsets the premium a specialist commands. Going beyond the country is worth doing for genuinely rare courses, and the real cost there is the time zone: a tutor several hours behind means an early morning or a late evening slot, every week, for a year. That is a household decision, not an academic one.

The honest fallback matters as much as the search. Where no tutor exists, the best available structure is the school's own department plus the published materials: the subject guide with its assessment criteria, past papers and examiner reports, and the school's supervising teacher holding deadlines even if they cannot teach the content. Examiner reports in particular are underused and tell you precisely what cost marks last session. Add a general academic home tutor for structure and writing discipline, and you have something that works. It is not as good as a specialist. It is considerably better than a year of a generalist pretending, and we would rather tell you that than place an IB IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai who cannot actually teach the course.

sections.heading: What progress looks like when nobody local teaches the subject
paragraphs: Judge the first four weeks on structure rather than on results. In a scarce subject, the early win is that somebody has finally mapped the course: what the components are, what each is worth, what has to exist by which date, and which prescribed texts or topics are still untouched. If the student can tell you the shape of their own course after a month and could not before, the match is working. Scores at this stage mean very little, particularly where the student has had no real teaching in the subject and is starting from a lower base than their other subjects.

At one term the test is whether an assessed piece exists and has been marked against the criteria, not whether it is good. A first draft that nobody has judged against the published descriptors is not progress. A weak draft with criterion-referenced feedback and an agreed rewrite is. For an IGCSE private candidate the equivalent milestone is a complete past paper attempted under timed conditions with the mark scheme applied honestly, which is often the first moment anyone discovers which parts of the syllabus were never covered.

Across a full examination cycle, the fair question is whether the student walked in knowing what the papers would ask and having practised under time. That is what tuition can reliably deliver. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and in a scarce subject that honesty matters more than usual, because a student who is self-taught or privately entered carries more of the outcome themselves than a student inside a well-staffed class does.

IB Gram is an independent platform. We are not affiliated with any school named on this page, nor with the International Baccalaureate organisation, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. We match tutors, we record what each tutor has actually taught, and we tell you when the honest answer is that no specialist exists. Anyone promising you a guaranteed outcome in a subject with two qualified teachers in the country is not describing something they can control.

sections.heading: Looking for an IB IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai for a rare subject: what to send us
paragraphs: Send four things and the search starts properly on the first day. The exact course title as the school registered it, including the level and, critically, the option where the subject has options. The syllabus year or first-teaching year, since this decides whether an experienced tutor is current. The assessment pieces already due and their dates. And the slots your household can hold weekly, with a note on whether an early morning or a late evening would be possible if the specialist turns out to be in a different time zone.

We will tell you which search stage we are at and when. If a local match exists you will hear about it first, because home tuition is the better arrangement when it is available at the right quality. Parents who began by searching for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai and were told the subject does not exist locally often find that a corridor-level search run on the component rather than the subject turns up someone after all.

The first session should be diagnostic and should end with a document. For a scarce subject that document is a course map: components, weightings, deadlines, what exists already and what has to be produced next. If you do not have that after the first two sessions, tell us. A household that is also arranging an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai for the mainstream subjects should keep the two briefs separate, because they are different searches with different timelines. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai households carry week to week is a separate hire from a specialist in one rare course.

If no specialist exists anywhere we look, we will say that in those words and help you build the fallback structure instead. That is a worse outcome than finding the right person and a far better one than paying for a year of plausible-sounding teaching in a course nobody in the room has read.
bullets: Send the exact registered course title including level and option
Send the syllabus year so we can check the tutor is current
List assessment pieces already due and their dates
Say whether an early or late slot is possible across time zones
Keep the scarce-subject brief separate from your mainstream subject brief

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child's subject is genuinely unavailable in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Run four checks before you conclude it. Ask your school's head of department who they would call if their own teacher were away for a month. Ask the examinations officer whether any other student is sitting the same option. Ask parents in the year group with the same subject, since shared tutors are common in small-cohort courses. Then ask us to search on the component and option rather than the subject name. Most families who believe a subject is unavailable have searched on the subject name alone, which returns hundreds of irrelevant results and makes a thin pool look deep.

faqs.question: Why does a search for the subject return plenty of tutors who turn out to be wrong?
faqs.answer: Because the subject and the course are different things. A search for a Spanish tutor finds many capable teachers of the language, and almost none of them has taught a Language A literature course assessed against published criteria with prescribed works and a formal oral. The same gap exists in Music, in the arts subjects and in any Diploma subject where the school has chosen a specific option. The fix is to search on the course title, the level and the option exactly as the school registered it, which cuts the list down to a handful and makes the real scarcity visible.

faqs.question: What does widening the search beyond Mumbai actually get me?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma options, a considerably larger pool. An option taught by a small number of teachers in this city is usually taught across many international schools nationally, so a national search changes the odds in a way that searching harder locally does not. Going beyond India is worth doing for genuinely rare courses and introduces one real cost, which is the time zone. A tutor several hours behind means a fixed early morning or late evening slot every week for a year, and that is a household decision rather than an academic one. We will tell you which stage we are searching at.

faqs.question: Is a remote specialist really better than a good local tutor who does not know the course?
faqs.answer: For a scarce subject, yes, and it is not a close call. A tutor who has taught the exact option and marked that component works to the assessment structure from the first session, knows the usual failure points and can argue with a mark. A capable generalist teaches the content and leaves the student to work out how it is assessed, which is the part that actually costs marks. Where a genuine local specialist exists we will always offer home tuition first. Where one does not, swapping expertise for proximity is the wrong trade.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for an unusual subject?
faqs.answer: Scarcity is the biggest single factor, more than board or level. A subject with very few qualified teachers commands a higher rate because the alternative is nobody, and that is true whether the tutor is in Bandra or in another country. Level matters, since Higher Level and internal assessment supervision are specialist work. Session length and frequency matter. Travel drops out of the calculation for a remote match, which usually offsets part of the premium. We do not publish a price list because for a rare course the honest range is wide and depends on who is actually available.

faqs.question: Will you travel to our home in Kharghar or Panvel for a rare subject?
faqs.answer: For a mainstream subject, yes, and we match within the Navi Mumbai nodes wherever we can, since a tutor moving between Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel along Palm Beach Road can hold a weekday evening slot for a full term. For a rare subject it is usually not possible, because the specialist is rarely in Navi Mumbai and a cross-creek journey twice a week does not survive the year even with the Atal Setu open. The practical answer most families here take is a remote specialist for that one subject and home tuition for the rest.

faqs.question: My child is entering an IGCSE subject privately. Does that change the tutoring?
faqs.answer: Substantially, because the tutor is now the whole teaching provision rather than a supplement to it. You need someone who has taught that specific syllabus, not just the content, since a private candidate has to cover the full specification including any coursework or practical requirement that the exam centre expects. You also need a longer run-up: start a full year out rather than a term out. And you need to confirm with the entering centre exactly which components are assessed and which papers are being sat, because private entry rules vary and the school will not be tracking it for you.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor and a remote specialist work together for the same student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a household with one unusual subject this hybrid is often the best structure available. The remote specialist takes the scarce subject on a longer weekly session and owns the assessment plan. A home tutor handles the mainstream subjects, study discipline and timetabling in person, which is where physical presence genuinely earns its keep with a teenager. The two do not need to coordinate much, but it helps if both know the deadline calendar. Families running all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Mumbai providers sell as one package should split the scarce subject out of it.

faqs.question: What if the specialist we hire turns out to be out of date on the syllabus?
faqs.answer: It is a real risk in revised options and it is avoidable with one question asked early: which syllabus year or first-teaching year did you last teach this under, and what changed in the most recent revision. Anyone current answers immediately. If it emerges later, tell us and we will replace rather than patch, because an out-of-date specialist teaches confidently in the wrong direction, which is worse than an honest generalist. Checking the published subject guide yourself against what the tutor describes takes twenty minutes and is worth doing in the first fortnight.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out. How does a replacement happen in a small pool?
faqs.answer: Tell us what specifically is wrong and we restart the search from the stage that produced the match, not from the beginning. The honest difference with a scarce subject is timing: replacing a Mathematics tutor takes days, and replacing a specialist in a minority language can take weeks, so raise problems early rather than waiting to be sure. Keep the existing sessions running while we search unless they are actively harmful. We will also tell you if the realistic choice is between this tutor and nobody, because in a very small pool that is sometimes the true position.

faqs.question: What happens if there is genuinely no tutor for the subject anywhere?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and then we help you build the alternative rather than selling you a substitute. That structure is the school's own department plus the published materials: the subject guide with its assessment criteria, past papers, mark schemes and examiner reports, with the supervising teacher holding the deadlines even if they cannot teach the content. Examiner reports are the most underused document here and state plainly what cost marks last session. Add a general academic home tutor for writing discipline and timetabling. This happens rarely, mostly with minority languages at literature level, but it does happen.

ib-igcse-online-tutor.closingCta: Send the exact registered course title, the level, the option, the syllabus year and the deadlines already set. We search your corridor first, then the city, then the country, and we tell you which stage we are at. If a local specialist exists you will hear about home tuition first. If none exists anywhere, we will say so and help you build the fallback instead.

sections.heading: How IB Gram shortlists an IB IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: A request for an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai almost always arrives with too little detail, and that is normal. A parent writes that their daughter is in Year 10 at a school in Juhu, that Chemistry is the problem, and that nobody in the house is free before seven in the evening. The first job is to turn that into something a tutor can answer honestly: which board the school actually enters her for, whether she is heading for Core or Extended papers, how many subjects genuinely need help and how many are fine, and which two evenings can be held every single week for the rest of the term rather than whichever evening happens to be free this week.

The shortlist that comes back is deliberately short. Three names a parent will actually ring beats twelve profiles nobody opens. Each name arrives with the syllabus that tutor currently teaches, the zone they travel inside, and the slots they still have free. Parents then speak to them directly, and the questions worth asking at that point are not about qualifications, which have already been checked, but about how the arrangement will run week to week: how far ahead the slot is protected, what happens when the tutor is unwell or stuck on the Western Express Highway, whether work set between sessions comes back marked, and how a parent hears about progress without having to ask for an update every fortnight.

Then comes the step that private arrangements skip almost every time. Before the first session, both sides put the terms into one message: the day and time, the notice each side gives, what a cancelled session counts as, whether marking is included, how often feedback reaches the parent, what the tutor will not do, and how payment and records work. It takes ten minutes in June and it is close to impossible to raise calmly in February, when a Diploma Programme (DP) student has three Internal Assessment (IA) deadlines inside a fortnight and the tutor has four other families asking for extra hours. Writing it down early is not suspicion. It is the cheapest way to avoid a bad ending to something that started well.
bullets: 1. Send board, year group, subjects and the two evenings you can hold
2. We shortlist tutors already teaching that syllabus inside your travel zone
3. You speak to two or three tutors directly before anything is booked
4. Both sides put slot, notice, marking, feedback and payment in one message
5. The first session runs and you tell us whether to continue or reshortlist

sections.heading: IGCSE Years 9 to 11, the MYP and the Diploma change what you should agree
paragraphs: The programme your child is in decides how much of a written understanding you actually need. In Years 9 to 11 the International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) runs as a two year examined course with Year 9 used as preparation, and the school decides whether a student is entered for Core or Extended papers in Maths and the sciences. That decision can move as late as final entries, which matters for an agreement: if the tier changes in January, the work changes, the session length may need to change, and both sides should already know who raises that and when. Write in a line saying the subject list and tier can be reviewed once a term without either side treating it as a renegotiation.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) sits differently. MYP 4 and 5 are marked against criteria rather than grade boundaries, there is a personal project to steer, and a tutor used only to Cambridge International Education mark schemes will mark an MYP task wrongly without realising it. The Diploma Programme (DP) adds another layer again: six subjects split across Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and the Internal Assessment in nearly every subject. An HL subject usually needs a longer session than an SL one, and from the first week of DP1 the boundary around what a tutor may touch on the EE and the IA should already be written down rather than discovered later.

One practical consequence. A family that wants all IB and IGCSE subjects covered by home classes in Mumbai will end up with two or three tutors, not one, because nobody teaches DP Chemistry HL and DP English Literature HL to the same standard. When there is more than one tutor, the agreement should name which tutor owns which subject and who the parent speaks to about the overall picture. Arrangements fall apart far more often because two tutors each assumed the other was covering a subject than because either of them taught badly.
bullets: Year 9 is preparation; the examined IGCSE course runs across Years 10 and 11
Core and Extended entry is the school's call and can move before final entries
Diploma Higher Level subjects usually need a longer session than Standard Level ones
MYP criteria marking is not IGCSE grade boundaries and needs a different habit
Name one tutor per subject in writing so no subject is silently uncovered

sections.heading: Subjects, papers and what marking between home classes should include
paragraphs: Subject choice across both boards is where most of the difficulty hides. At IGCSE a family picks between separate sciences, Coordinated Sciences and Combined Science, and those are genuinely different entries with different paper counts, not three names for one course. Maths splits into Core and Extended. At Diploma level Maths splits again into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, and a tutor strong in one is not automatically strong in the other. Languages run from Language A Literature through Language B to ab initio. Every one of these carries internal work: coursework in several IGCSE subjects, an Internal Assessment in almost every Diploma subject, plus the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay sitting across the whole Diploma.

That internal work is why the marking clause matters more than parents expect. Marking is real labour and it is not automatically bundled into the hour you booked. An IGCSE Maths problem set takes fifteen minutes to mark and can come back the next morning. A Diploma History essay or an English Literature commentary takes considerably longer and should come back before the next session rather than being read aloud during it, which wastes the slot. An Internal Assessment draft is a third category: the tutor reads it against the published criteria and writes comments against each strand, and does not rewrite sentences, retype paragraphs or work inside the student's own document. Put a number and a turnaround in the message. Two marked pieces a month returned inside three days is a clear line that both sides can hold.

No one teaches all IB and IGCSE subjects and any tutor in Mumbai who says otherwise is telling you something useful about themselves. Some subjects are simply scarcer than others here. Economics, Business Management and Psychology are reasonably well covered across the city. Design Technology, Visual Arts, Computer Science at Higher Level, and second languages such as French, Spanish or Hindi B take longer to match and may need an online tutor rather than one who can reach Kandivali on a Tuesday. Expect the scarce subject to set the schedule for the whole week, and agree its slot first.
bullets: Agree how many marked pieces a month are included, and the turnaround
Separate sciences, Coordinated Sciences and Combined Science are different IGCSE entries
Diploma Maths splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation
An IA draft gets written criteria comments, never rewritten sentences from the tutor
Scarce subjects such as Design Technology or Hindi B take longer to match

sections.heading: Mumbai coverage zone by zone, and how far ahead a slot is held
paragraphs: IB Gram matches across Mumbai, Maharashtra, from Colaba to Kasarvadavali, and the single most useful thing to write into an arrangement is how far in advance the weekly slot is protected. In South Mumbai the distances are short and the clock is not. A tutor leaving Worli for Colaba covers around eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals. Families in Cuffe Parade, Napean Sea Road, Breach Candy and Walkeshwar are therefore matched inside the island rather than pulled down from the suburbs, working off the Western Line into Churchgate and Grant Road, the Harbour Line to Dockyard, and now the Coastal Road and Metro Line 3 between Cuffe Parade and the Bandra Kurla Complex. For this zone, hold the slot for the term and keep it off the evening peak.

The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Express Highway, the Link Road and the Western Line, which means a tutor going Bandra to Andheri is quick at four in the afternoon and defeated at six. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai works best when the tutor lives within two stations of you, so Khar West to Santacruz holds for a year and Malad to Kandivali holds for a year, while Borivali to Bandra does not. Metro Line 1 across Versova, Andheri and Ghatkopar, and Lines 2A and 7 from Dahisar down to Gundavali, have made some cross-suburb matches workable that were not before, and Juhu, Goregaon and Dahisar families should ask a tutor which line they would use before agreeing a start time.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road in between. Powai has no station of its own, so tutors reach it by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and a Powai slot should always carry a written grace window. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund, on the Central and Harbour lines, the Eastern Express Highway and the Monorail, and the Eastern Freeway makes South Mumbai reachable from Chembur and Wadala faster than the map suggests.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, so Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are matched node to node along Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway, with the Trans Harbour Line and Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 filling the gaps. The Atal Setu has shortened the run from the island city, but a tutor making that crossing twice a week on a school night rarely lasts a full term, and the agreement should say so honestly rather than pretend. Thane spreads from the station east across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road to Hiranandani Estate and Kasarvadavali, and the Ghodbunder stretch sets the whole schedule: twenty minutes off peak, close to an hour at seven in the evening.
bullets: Agree the slot for a full term rather than confirming it week by week
Match inside your zone: Khar West to Santacruz holds, Thane to Colaba does not
Write a monsoon fallback into the message: same slot, online, same week
Evening slots after seven fill first in Bandra, Powai and Kharghar
Arrange a standing gate pass instead of a fresh visitor entry every week

sections.heading: The Mumbai school calendar decides when this conversation is easy
paragraphs: The Mumbai international school year starts in June, and June and July are the two months when a tutoring arrangement can be set up slowly and sensibly. First assessments land by August. October brings term tests and Diploma mock cycles, which give the first honest reading on whether a new subject tutor is working. November and December are busy but navigable. Then January and February arrive, and almost every internal deadline in the Diploma Programme lands in the same few weeks: Internal Assessments across most subjects, the Extended Essay final submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay. March and April go to revision and school prelims, May carries the Diploma examinations, and the IGCSE May and June series follows straight behind.

Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School in the Bandra Kurla Complex, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul all work to broadly this shape, with their own internal deadlines layered on top. This is why February is the worst month to start a private arrangement and an even worse month to change the terms of one. Tutor availability is at its annual low, the student is under genuine pressure, and the parent has almost no leverage because changing tutors in February costs more than putting up with a tutor who is not quite right. A June conversation costs nothing. The same conversation in February costs the term.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, with the International Baccalaureate organisation, with Cambridge International Education or with Pearson Edexcel. Schools are named here as local context only, because their calendars set the pressure points a Mumbai family is actually planning around. No tutor listed with us speaks for a school, and no school has endorsed us. If a tutor implies otherwise during a first call, that is worth noticing.
bullets: June and July are the calmest months to agree terms properly
October term tests give the first honest read on a new subject tutor
January and February carry IA, EE and TOK deadlines in the same weeks
May examinations end the arrangement unless you agree otherwise in writing
School holidays are not automatic breaks; say which weeks pause in the message

sections.heading: Is home tuition or online better for private tutoring in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the better default and online is the better backup. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai who comes to your flat gets a student who cannot quietly open another tab, a desk the family controls, and a parent close enough to know whether the hour happened. Online holds the slot on the evening the Western Express Highway does not. Most arrangements that survive a full year use both, with one of them written in as the default.

The honest trade-offs run in both directions. Home sessions cost the tutor travel time they are not teaching in, which is why a tutor who takes a six o'clock slot across the city will eventually ask to move it, and why that request should not come as a surprise. A home session also depends on the household being quiet, which a flat with a younger sibling and a television is not. Online removes the travel entirely, which makes an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai the realistic answer for a scarce Higher Level subject or for a family in Panvel who would otherwise be matched with nobody. Online is good for screen shared worked solutions in Maths and Physics, and for a student who wants to rewatch an explanation. It is weaker for a Year 9 student who needs someone sitting beside them, and it is genuinely poor for coaching handwritten examination technique under time pressure.

Hybrid is where most families land, and it is the part of an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai arrangement that causes the most friction when it is not written down. Settle four things in the message. Which mode is the default. Who may switch a session to online, the tutor or the family or both. How much notice a switch needs, which is usually the same notice as a cancellation. And whether a switched session is treated identically for payment and marking, which it should be. Without those four lines, the monsoon turns every Tuesday into a negotiation.
bullets: Home tuition is the default; write it into the message as the default
Agree who may switch a session online, and how much notice that takes
Online keeps scarce subjects and monsoon weeks from losing the slot entirely
Handwritten examination technique is harder to coach through a screen
A hybrid month should change nothing about payment, marking or feedback

sections.heading: What IB Gram checks, and the records you should keep yourself
paragraphs: Before a tutor is listed we check identity documents, the qualification they claim, and their teaching history with the specific syllabus rather than the board in general. Someone who taught Cambridge International Education Physics five years ago is not the same as someone teaching the current specification this year. We talk to every tutor about the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay boundary before they take a Diploma student, because a tutor who is vague about it in a conversation will be vague about it in March. We do not rate tutors with stars, we do not publish result claims, and we do not ask tutors for testimonials.

There is a second layer of checking that only the parent can do, and it takes one phone call. Ask the tutor which syllabus version they are teaching right now and in which school or with which students. Ask them to explain one assessment criterion in their own words, without reading it out. Ask which component students most often lose marks on and why. A tutor who answers those three questions concretely is a different proposition from one who answers warmly. Parents search for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai and there is no such person. There is a tutor who fits this subject, this student, this slot and this travel distance, and the fit is what you are testing on that call.

Then keep records, because the written agreement is only useful if there is something to check it against. One message thread per month, listing the dates taught, the topic covered, the work set, the work returned marked, and an acknowledgement of each payment, takes about thirty seconds a week to maintain. It protects the tutor as much as the family. When a disagreement does arrive, usually about whether a session was cancelled in time or whether a draft was ever handed over, the thread settles it in a minute instead of turning into a conversation nobody wants to have with someone who is in their house every Tuesday.
bullets: Ask the tutor to explain one assessment criterion in their own words
Keep one monthly thread listing dates, topics, work set and work returned
Acknowledge every payment in writing in that same thread
Ask which syllabus version they teach now, not which board they know
Check the tutor's actual travel plan before agreeing a weekday evening slot

sections.heading: What should be in a written agreement with a private tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: A written understanding with an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai should cover nine things: the slot and how far ahead it is held, the notice each side gives for a cancellation, what a missed session counts as, whether marking between sessions is included, how and how often feedback reaches the parent, what the tutor will not do, how either side ends the arrangement, and how payment and records are handled. None of it is adversarial. Every item is something both people are already assuming, written down so that the two assumptions turn out to be the same assumption.

Start with the slot and the notice, because that is where almost every dispute begins. Say whether the slot is held for the term or confirmed week by week, and say it plainly, because a tutor quietly holding Tuesday at seven for you is turning down other work to do it. Then set one notice period and apply it in both directions. Twenty four hours is a common and fair line. Inside that window a session the family cancels is treated as taught; outside it the slot moves. The half families forget is the reverse case: if the tutor cancels inside the same window, the session is made up within the same week where the timetable allows, rather than quietly disappearing. An arrangement where only one side carries the cancellation risk does not survive a term of Mumbai traffic, school trips and family weddings.

Next, marking and feedback, which are separate things. Marking is what happens to the student's work. Feedback is what reaches the parent, and the most useful form is a short written note once a month rather than a verbal update at the door, because the doorway conversation happens with the student standing three feet away and so is never fully honest. Agree who the note goes to, roughly how long it is, and that it names one thing improving and one thing not. Then the boundaries, which should be written as plainly as possible: the tutor will not write any part of an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or coursework, will not supply sentences to be pasted in, will not edit inside the student's file, will not contact the school on the family's behalf, and will not share this student's work with other students.

Finally, ending it and paying for it. Both sides give the same notice, a part finished month is settled for sessions already taught rather than argued over, and anything the tutor holds that belongs to the student goes back. Agree when payment happens, by what method, and that each one is acknowledged in the thread. All of this belongs in a message, not a contract. A contract nobody reads protects nobody, and producing one before the first session changes a working relationship into a transaction. A message both people have read and replied to in words is a real record, it lives in the thread you already use for scheduling, and it is findable in February, which is the only month anyone ever needs to find it.
bullets: The slot, and whether it is held for the term or week by week
Equal notice both ways, and what a missed session counts as
Whether marking is included, how many pieces, and how fast it returns
How feedback reaches the parent, in writing, and how often
What the tutor will not do: no IA, EE or coursework writing, no school contact
How either side ends it, and how payment and records are kept

sections.heading: What should progress look like, and when can a Mumbai parent call it?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see the student working differently, not scoring differently. At one term you should see a school report or a mock that moves. At one full examination cycle you can judge the arrangement properly. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, no tutor can, and a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade is telling you something important about how they work. Write two review dates into the message, one in October and one in February, so that judging the arrangement is a diary entry rather than an argument.

Four weeks is about behaviour. Homework starts earlier in the evening. The questions the student asks get more specific, moving from saying a topic is confusing to naming the step they lose. They start bringing their own past paper questions to the session instead of waiting to be given work. None of that shows in a mark yet, and expecting a mark to move inside a month is the most common reason a perfectly good arrangement is ended too early. One term is where the number should start to move, in a school report, a term test or a mock, and if nothing at all has shifted by then it is a fair conversation to have, with the tutor first and with us second.

One examination cycle is the only honest test, and even then the result is shaped by things no tutor controls: how many subjects were weak at the start, whether the student did the work between sessions, and what else was happening that year. We do not guarantee grades and we would rather say so here than imply otherwise and have a family discover it in July. When an arrangement is not working, say it plainly to the tutor first, because a surprising number of mismatches are about pace or explanation style and are fixable in one conversation. If it is not fixable, give the notice you agreed, settle what is owed, and tell us. We reshortlist from the same brief with the mismatch recorded, and nobody has to justify themselves.
bullets: Four weeks: homework starts earlier and the questions get more specific
One term: a school report, term test or mock that moves
One examination cycle: the only honest test of the whole arrangement
Write two review dates into the message, in October and in February
No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a promise of one is a warning

sections.heading: Getting started: the message to send before the first home tuition session
paragraphs: Have four things ready before the first call. The most recent school report, so the tutor is working from evidence rather than a parent's summary. The subject list with Higher Level and Standard Level, or Core and Extended, marked against each one. The school's assessment calendar if you have been sent it, because the deadlines on it will shape the whole term. And the two evenings you can genuinely hold every week. One home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is rarely the right structure, so expect to be told that two subjects need two people and plan the week around the scarcer one.

The first session is not a test and should not be run like one. A good tutor reads one piece of recent work, asks the student what they think is going wrong, teaches something properly so the hour is worth having, and sets one piece of work with a clear deadline. By the end of it the parent should know what the tutor thinks the actual problem is, which is often not the subject named in the enquiry. A student failing IGCSE Physics is sometimes a student who cannot rearrange an equation, and that is a different term of work from the one the family was expecting to book.

Then send the message. Nine lines, written before session one rather than after session four, and sent to the tutor with a request that they reply in words rather than with a thumbs up. If they will not put the terms in writing, that is information. Diarise the October review the same day you agree the slot. The whole thing takes ten minutes, and it is the difference between an arrangement that ends cleanly whenever it needs to and one that ends badly in the middle of an examination term.

faqs.question: What should a written agreement with a private tutor actually cover?
faqs.answer: Nine things, and they fit comfortably in one message. The slot and how far ahead it is held; the notice each side gives for a cancellation; what a missed session counts as; whether marking between sessions is included and how quickly work comes back; how feedback reaches the parent and how often; what the tutor will not do; how either side ends the arrangement; and how payment is made and recorded. Nothing on that list is adversarial or unusual. Every item is something both people are already quietly assuming, written down so that the two sets of assumptions turn out to be the same one.

faqs.question: Is a message enough, or do we need a proper contract?
faqs.answer: A message is enough, and in practice it works better than a contract. A contract nobody reads protects nobody, and asking a tutor to sign one before the first session changes a working relationship into a transaction. What matters is that both people have read the same sentences and replied in words rather than with an emoji. Keep it in the thread you already use for scheduling, so it is findable later. If the arrangement runs through a company or covers several children across a year, a short written scope makes sense. For a weekly private arrangement between one family and one teacher, the message is the record.

faqs.question: What happens if we cancel a session at short notice?
faqs.answer: Whatever you agreed, applied identically in both directions. A common and fair line is twenty four hours: inside that window the session is treated as taught, outside it the slot simply moves. The part families forget is the reverse case. If the tutor cancels inside the same window, the session should be made up in the same week wherever the timetable allows, not quietly dropped. Write both halves into the message at the start. An arrangement where only the family carries the cancellation risk will not survive a term of Mumbai traffic, school trips, illness and the two or three weddings that always land on a Tuesday.

faqs.question: Will the tutor mark work between sessions?
faqs.answer: Only if you agreed it, which is exactly why it belongs in the message. Marking is real work and it is not automatically included in the hour you booked. Agree a number and a turnaround. Two marked pieces a month returned within three days is a clear line both sides can hold, and a Diploma Programme essay takes considerably longer to mark than an IGCSE Maths problem set, so the mix matters as much as the count. Also agree what marking means. For an Internal Assessment draft it means written comments against the published criteria, never corrections typed into the student's own document.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write my child's Internal Assessment or Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: No, and this should be written down before the first session rather than discovered in March. A tutor can teach the underlying skill, explain the criteria, discuss whether a research question is workable, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote themselves. A tutor cannot write any part of an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or coursework, cannot supply sentences to be pasted in, and cannot work inside the student's file. The school signs authenticity declarations on this work and the student signs them too. Putting the boundary in the agreement protects the student, the tutor and the family at the same time.

faqs.question: Should the tutor contact my child's school?
faqs.answer: No. A private tutor has no standing with the school and should not email a subject teacher, ask for a mark to be explained, or attend a parent meeting on your behalf. If something needs raising with the school, the parent raises it. Put this in the agreement, because it comes up more often than families expect, usually when a tutor disagrees with how a draft has been marked. The tutor's view can absolutely inform what you decide to say to the school, and often should. It simply cannot be delivered to the school in the tutor's name or from the tutor's email.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board, level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length, and we do not publish a price list because an honest one does not exist. A Higher Level Diploma subject carries a heavier marking load than a Year 9 IGCSE subject and is priced accordingly. A scarce subject costs more than a common one because fewer people can teach it. A tutor crossing from Andheri to Colaba twice a week is pricing that travel in, openly or otherwise. Agree the rate, the session length and exactly what marking is included in the same message, so that nobody is recalculating anything in month three.

faqs.question: Our home tutor has to cross Ghodbunder Road to reach us in Thane. How do we protect the slot?
faqs.answer: Move the slot rather than the tutor. A weekday home tuition session starting at six in Kasarvadavali means a home tutor leaving Thane station at around five, which is the worst possible hour on Ghodbunder Road and the single most common reason a Thane arrangement collapses by October. A half past seven start, or a weekend morning, usually holds for a full term where a six o'clock start does not. Write the start time into the agreement with a ten minute grace window in both directions, and agree in advance that a heavy monsoon week runs as an online class at the same time rather than being lost.

faqs.question: Does someone need to be at home during a home tuition session in Bandra?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the flat, though not in the room. For a Year 9 or Year 10 student that is a basic safeguarding expectation, and most Bandra West and Khar West societies separately want a resident to confirm a visitor at the gate anyway. Arrange standing entry for the tutor so they are not negotiating with security every week, set the session up at a dining table rather than in a bedroom, and leave the door open. None of this is distrust of a particular person. It is what a sensible home tuition arrangement looks like, and a professional tutor will expect it.

faqs.question: How do we end it if the tutor is not working out?
faqs.answer: You give the notice you agreed, in writing, and you do not have to justify the decision. Two weeks is a reasonable default and it should apply to the tutor as well as to you. Settle what is outstanding for sessions already taught rather than arguing over a half month. Then tell us, and we reshortlist from the same brief with the mismatch recorded, which is usually about pace, explanation style or the specific component the student is stuck on rather than subject knowledge. Most replacements happen because the fit was wrong from the start, not because anyone behaved badly.

faqs.question: We only realised we needed help in February. Is it too late?
faqs.answer: It is not too late, but February is the hardest month to start and the worst month to negotiate terms. Diploma Internal Assessment deadlines land together, Year 11 students are weeks away from the May and June series, and almost every experienced tutor's evening slots are already taken. Expect a shorter shortlist, fewer slot options and less flexibility on notice than you would have had in June. Agree the terms anyway, in the same single message, even though it feels rushed. A February arrangement with nothing written down is the one most likely to end badly in April, when nobody has the time to sort it out.

faqs.question: Do you have IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai if we live in Kharghar?
faqs.answer: Yes, and Navi Mumbai is matched node to node rather than across the creek. For Kharghar we shortlist tutors living in Kharghar, Belapur, Nerul or Panvel, because Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway make those a reliable twenty to thirty minute run, while a tutor travelling from the island city over the Atal Setu will quietly stop being available around week six. The same logic applies in Vashi and in Panvel. Ask any tutor where they actually live, not which areas they say they cover, before you agree a weekday evening slot.

sections.heading: How tuition gets arranged inside one Mumbai complex
paragraphs: Most requests for IB IGCSE tuition near me in Mumbai that reach us from a large complex arrive already half-formed. A neighbour has a tutor, the tutor has one evening slot left, and the parent wants to know whether this is a good idea before saying yes in the building group. That is a reasonable question and the answer is not automatically yes. The tutor your neighbour is happy with was chosen for a Year 10 child doing Cambridge IGCSE Core Maths, and you have a Diploma Programme Higher Level Chemistry candidate four months from mocks. Same tower, same evening, entirely different job.

So the process starts by separating the convenience from the match. 1. You tell us the board, the exact year group, the subjects and the tower, and whether a tutor already visits your complex. 2. We check whether that existing tutor actually covers your child's syllabus at your child's level, and say plainly if they do not. 3. You get a shortlist that includes the in-building option where it fits, and outside names where it does not. 4. You speak to the tutor yourself, including about the slot, because in a shared building the slot is the negotiation. 5. The first session is a diagnostic and you decide afterwards.

The step families skip is the third one. A tutor already cleared at your gate, already parked, already upstairs, is enormously convenient, and convenience quietly becomes the criterion. Ask yourself whether you would have chosen this person if they lived in Mulund and you lived in Kandivali East. If the answer is no, you are buying travel logistics rather than teaching, and that bill arrives in February.

Where the in-building tutor is the right person, say so early, because slots in a shared evening are allocated by seniority rather than by need. The family who started in June holds six o'clock. A family joining in October takes what is left, which is usually the last slot of the evening, with a tired tutor and a tired child. This is the single most under-discussed cost of joining a shared arrangement late, and it is worth a direct conversation rather than a surprise.

sections.heading: Two children in one tower, two different programmes
paragraphs: Buildings create an illusion of similarity. The children ride the same lift, wear two or three different uniforms between them, and are assumed by their parents to be doing roughly the same thing. They are not. The International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP), the IB Diploma Programme (DP) and Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel IGCSE at Years 9 to 11 assess so differently that a tutor strong in one can be mediocre in another, and a shared arrangement hides that difference behind a shared lift lobby.

The MYP child is being marked against criteria A to D with task-specific clarifications, and needs a tutor who can read a rubric and translate it into what to actually write. The IGCSE child is being prepared for terminal papers with a defined syllabus, mark schemes and predictable question structures, and needs drilling plus technique. The Diploma Programme child carries six subjects at Higher Level and Standard Level, an Internal Assessment (IA) in most of them, Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE), and needs a tutor who can triage. Those are three different professionals wearing the same label.

This matters inside a building because the tutor who is excellent for the Year 9 MYP child on the eighth floor gets recommended upward to the DP2 family on the twelfth, and the recommendation carries real social weight. The neighbour is not wrong about the tutor. They are wrong about the transferability. A good IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai parents trust for one programme will usually tell you themselves when a stage is outside their range, and the willingness to say so is one of the better signals you will get.

The question to ask is narrow and it works. Ask the tutor to describe, without looking anything up, how your child's course is assessed: how many papers, what weighting, what the internal component is worth, what the deadlines are. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Mumbai families have used for years in your building will answer instantly for the programme they know and vaguely for the one they do not. That five-minute conversation is worth more than the whole referral.

sections.heading: Which subjects a shared home tutor can carry, and which they cannot
paragraphs: In a shared building arrangement, one tutor usually ends up teaching more than one subject, because the evening is already theirs and adding a subject is easier than adding a person. That works for some combinations and quietly fails for others. Mathematics and Physics sit together honestly. Chemistry and Biology sit together at IGCSE and separate sharply at Diploma Programme Higher Level. Economics and Business Management look adjacent and are assessed nothing alike. Nobody genuinely covers all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai gets asked for, and the moment a tutor agrees to a fourth subject to keep a building client, teaching quality starts leaking.

The internal assessments are where the limits show first. A Diploma Programme Physics IA needs somebody who can argue about uncertainty and control of variables, not somebody who can check the graph. A Mathematics Analysis and Approaches exploration needs a supervisor who will say in October that the chosen topic contains no real mathematics. A Business Management IA needs a reader who knows the difference between describing a company and applying a tool to it. A History IA lives or dies on the evaluation of sources section, which is the part students write last and worst.

At IGCSE the equivalents are component-shaped rather than coursework-shaped. The Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper rewards a specific kind of experimental reasoning that is never taught directly. The Edexcel Maths calculator and non-calculator split changes how a student should revise. English Language coursework folders and the structured long-answer questions in Biology both lose marks for format rather than knowledge. Looking for a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai schools teach is a reasonable wish and an unreasonable expectation.

Subject and level choice is the conversation worth having before any of this. Higher Level versus Standard Level, Core versus Extended at IGCSE, and the combination a child carries into Year 11 shape the next two years more than a term of tuition can. A tutor who tells you your son should move Chemistry to Standard Level rather than adding a second weekly session is giving you better advice than the one who takes the extra hour, and in a shared building the second kind is more common, because the extra hour is right there.

sections.heading: Mumbai complexes where a shared tutor is already normal
paragraphs: Searches for IB IGCSE tuition near me in Mumbai cluster around home tuition in big complexes, because the arrangement is commonest where buildings are large enough to hold several IB and IGCSE families at once. In the Central Suburbs that means Hiranandani Gardens in Powai and the Chandivali complexes behind it, where a tutor can teach three consecutive hours without touching JVLR, plus the older societies of Ghatkopar and Kurla on the Central Line and Metro Line 1. In the Eastern Suburbs the pattern runs through Chembur, Wadala, Vikhroli and Mulund West, where the Eastern Freeway and the Chembur to Wadala Monorail decide whether a tutor can reasonably add a fourth family after leaving the island.

In the Western Suburbs the shared evening is a fixture in Lokhandwala and Oshiwara in Andheri West, in Thakur Village in Kandivali East, across Malad West, Goregaon East, Borivali and Dahisar East, and in the Khar West, Santacruz West and Juhu buildings closer to the schools. Here the Western Express Highway, the Link Road and Metro Lines 2A and 7 shape the direction of travel, so a tutor builds a tower evening precisely to avoid moving along that highway between six and nine.

South Mumbai works differently. Buildings in Worli, Prabhadevi, Tardeo, Napean Sea Road, Walkeshwar, Cuffe Parade and Colaba are vertical rather than sprawling, so the shared arrangement happens between floors of a single tower rather than between towers of a complex, and it is more discreet. A tutor working the island keeps to it, because the Coastal Road and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link help at some hours and the Peddar Road signals undo the gain at others. In Mumbai, Maharashtra the social rules around a shared tutor are tightest here, where neighbours know each other and say less.

Navi Mumbai and Thane are where shared tuition is most economically necessary rather than merely convenient. In Nerul, Seawoods, Vashi, Belapur, Kharghar, Airoli and Panvel, connected by Palm Beach Road, the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines, Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 and now the Atal Setu, a specialist will cross the creek for an evening of four families and not for one. The same is true along Ghodbunder Road in Thane, through Majiwada, Pokhran Road, Hiranandani Estate and Kasarvadavali, where a single family cannot justify the trip that a tower full of families can.

sections.heading: When one Mumbai school calendar empties a whole tower's week
paragraphs: In a mixed building the calendar is noise. In a building where most children attend one or two campuses, the calendar is a single switch. When Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Ecole Mondiale World School, Jamnabai Narsee International School, Hiranandani Foundation School, JBCN International School in Chembur or Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane runs an examination week, a production, a sports week or parent conferences, the tutor who built an evening around that school loses the evening rather than a lesson, and four families discover simultaneously that they all want to reschedule into the same Saturday.

The annual rhythm is predictable enough to plan around. Term opens in early June and the good shared evenings are fully allocated within about three weeks, which is why October joiners inherit the last slot. October brings Diploma Programme IA drafts and Extended Essay submissions. November and December bring mocks at most IB and IGCSE campuses in the city, and this is when a shared evening is under most strain, because every family in the tower wants extra hours in the same fortnight and there are only so many hours in it.

January and February bring the TOK essay and the final IA deadlines, then the Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel series and the Diploma Programme May session begin in March. By then, a shared arrangement that has run since June is worth more than its individual sessions, because the tutor knows which of the four children panics, which one overprepares the wrong paper, and which one has not opened a past paper since December. That accumulated knowledge is the real asset in a building home tuition arrangement.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, with the International Baccalaureate organisation, with Cambridge International Education or with Pearson Edexcel. Campuses are named only because their calendars drive the scheduling inside Mumbai buildings, which is the practical thing a parent joining a shared evening needs to understand.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online, or a shared group inside the building?
paragraphs: Home tuition one-to-one in your own flat is the default and remains the right answer for most children, because the tutor sees your child's desk, your child's notes and your child's distractions rather than a tidied version of them. In a shared building arrangement this is what usually happens anyway: the tutor teaches one child per hour in each family's own home, and the sharing is of the evening rather than of the lesson. That is the version to prefer. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai does not stop being one-to-one simply because the tutor stays in the building afterwards.

The genuine group version, two or three children from different flats taught together in one living room or the clubhouse study room, is a different product and should be chosen deliberately rather than drifted into. It works when the children are at the same board, the same level and roughly the same standard, and when the work is paper practice rather than diagnosis. It fails when one child is two topics behind, because that child becomes the audience, and in a building the audience role is visible to everyone's parents, which makes it worse than it would be in a classroom.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai earns a place in a building week for exactly the reasons a shared evening exists: scarce subjects. Your complex may hold four families needing Maths and one needing Diploma Programme Higher Level Economics, and the Economics specialist is never going to build an evening out of one child. That subject goes online and loses almost nothing, while the Maths stays at home where presence matters. Most well-run building weeks look like this rather than like a single arrangement.

The honest trade-off across all three answers to IB IGCSE tuition near me in Mumbai is control. One-to-one home tuition gives you full control of the slot and the content and costs the most travel. A shared evening gives you reliability, because the tutor will not drop a tower, and costs you flexibility, because moving your hour moves three other families. Online gives you the specialist and costs you the room. Pick the combination per subject rather than per child, and revisit it in November when the mock timetable lands.

sections.heading: What the gate checks, and what you still have to check yourself
paragraphs: Your society gate checks identity and nothing else. A standing visitor entry for a regular tutor, which most large Mumbai complexes will issue once a resident registers them, confirms that a named adult is expected at your tower on Tuesdays. It confirms nothing about whether that adult has taught Cambridge IGCSE Physics. Families routinely treat gate clearance plus a neighbour's recommendation as a complete check, and those two things together verify punctuality and likeability.

What gets verified before we introduce anyone is narrower and more useful: a government photo identity document, the boards and syllabuses the tutor claims to have taught, checked against the current assessment structure rather than against a resume line, and the teaching history they describe. What cannot be verified is anything that happened privately in another family's living room, and in a building that is exactly the evidence a referral is built on. A neighbour's account is genuinely valuable and it is not verification.

There is one check specific to shared arrangements that nobody asks for and everybody should: confidentiality. Agree, out loud and at the start, that the tutor will not discuss your child's marks, drafts, diagnosis or attitude with any other family in the building, and will not answer the lobby question about how the other children are doing. A professional tutor will agree immediately and will be glad somebody said it. A tutor who treats building gossip as rapport-building is telling you what they will say about your child upstairs.

Then do the parent checks that no platform can do for you. Ask the tutor to outline their first three sessions. Ask how they mark a draft and whether they write on it. Sit within earshot, not in the room, for the first two sessions and listen for whether your child is talking. And know the limit of all of it: we do not guarantee grades, because the practice between sessions belongs to the student, and a verified, well-matched tutor working with a child who does not do the work will still produce a disappointing result.

sections.heading: How does a shared tutor arrangement actually start, and how does it end?
paragraphs: It starts in a lift, a lobby or a building group, almost never through a typed IB IGCSE tuition near me in Mumbai query. One family finds somebody who works, mentions it, and within a fortnight the tutor has three hours in the tower instead of one. For the tutor this is the best offer in the city: a whole evening in one building, no travel between students, no forty minutes lost on the Western Express Highway or the Eastern Express Highway between the second child and the third, and a cancellation that costs one hour instead of a whole trip. That economics is why a tower tutor stays through February when a single-family tutor sometimes does not, and it is the strongest argument for joining one.

What families give up is the calendar. Your slot was decided by whoever joined first and by the tutor's route home, not by when your child works best. A Diploma Programme student who is sharp at six and useless at nine does not get to choose. Rescheduling for a school trip means asking three other families to move. Holidays stagger badly, so the tutor sits idle for an hour in the middle of an evening and eventually asks somebody to shift permanently. None of this is anybody behaving badly, and all of it is friction you should see coming rather than discover in October.

The awkward parts are specific and they repeat. One family decides to stop, which punches a hole in the middle of the tutor's evening and makes the next lift journey uncomfortable for everyone. Two children in the same building get compared, sometimes by the parents and sometimes by the children, because everyone knows who the tutor sees before and after. And a tutor's standing in a complex comes to rest on one visible result: a good Year 12 outcome on the ninth floor fills their week for a year, and a poor one, which may have nothing to do with the teaching, can cost them four families at once. Tutors know this, and a tutor who is managing their building reputation is not always making the best call for your child.

Which gives you the etiquette, in both directions. Recommending: describe what the tutor did, not what grade followed. Say the drafts came back written on, say the hour had a plan, say your daughter started explaining her method out loud. Do not promise an outcome you cannot attribute. Declining: the honest exit is difference, not deficiency. Different subject, different level, different need, a child who works better in the morning. You owe your neighbour a straight answer and you do not owe them a critique of their choice. And do not ask the neighbour what the tutor charges them, because the answer will be different from yours for legitimate reasons and the comparison poisons both arrangements.

The thing to guard against is quieter than all of it: the unspoken competition inside the building. Marks travel through a tower faster than anywhere else, children know exactly which neighbour the tutor sees next, and parents begin measuring their own child against the family upstairs rather than against last term. The defences are simple and they hold. Keep marks out of the building group. Do not ask the tutor about other children, and tell them you will not. Do not arrange the comparison conversation in the lobby. Judge the arrangement on whether your child is doing more unaided work than in August, which is the only comparison that has ever been worth making.

sections.heading: What should progress look like when the neighbours are watching?
paragraphs: At four weeks, the measures are the same as anywhere and the pressure to compare is not. Your child should be able to name what they are weak at in specific terms rather than saying the subject is hard. Arguments about homework should have reduced. The tutor should have told you something about your child you did not know. What should not be happening at four weeks is you asking whether the boy on the fourteenth floor is further ahead, and if that question has already formed, the building is affecting your judgment more than the teaching is.

At one term, look at behaviour under exam conditions rather than at marks. A Diploma Programme student should be finishing papers inside the time, not leaving the last question blank. An IGCSE Years 9-11 student should be shaping long answers to the mark allocation instead of writing everything they know. IA drafts should exist on paper with the tutor's comments written on them, and you should be able to read those comments and see what changed between the first draft and the second. These are all visible without reference to any other child in the tower.

At one examination cycle, the outcome carries far more than the tuition. A subject taken at the wrong level in Year 11, a teacher change mid-course, illness in March, or a student who attended every session and practised nothing, all move a result more than a good tutor can. We do not guarantee grades and nor can anyone else honestly, and in a building the pressure to imply otherwise is heavier because the next four referrals depend on the answer. Treat a confident promise made in a lift as the warning it is.

If the match is wrong, say so in week three rather than week ten, and say it to us rather than to the building group. A replacement is arranged without you having to justify the decision, and the tutor does not need to lose the rest of the tower over it. Most shared-building failures are fit failures rather than competence failures: the tutor who suits a methodical Year 10 child is not always right for an anxious DP2 candidate three months from finals, and nobody has to be at fault for the second arrangement to work better.

sections.heading: Arranging IB and IGCSE home tuition in your Mumbai building
paragraphs: Send five things and the first reply will be useful. The board and exact year group as the school writes it. The subjects with Higher Level, Standard Level, Core or Extended stated. Your complex and tower, because the building decides both the gate protocol and whether a shared evening already exists there. The evening windows that genuinely work after the school bus. And whether a tutor already visits your building, with the subject they teach if you know it.

Two more things sharpen it. The latest report card including the teacher comments that parents usually skim, since a line about not attempting extended-response questions tells a tutor more than the grade printed above it. And one sentence on what you actually want this term, which is often narrower than it first sounds: get an Extended Essay unstuck, survive December mocks, repair a term of missed Chemistry, or stop the arguments about Sunday evening.

The first session is a diagnostic rather than a lesson. The tutor works through recent school material and recent errors, finds out what your child can do unaided, and sends a short written note setting out what they found and what the next six sessions will cover. You are not committed to a term by sitting that session, and this matters more in a shared building, where saying no after one session is socially easier than saying no after a month.

If the in-building tutor is not the right fit for your child's programme, that is a normal outcome and not a verdict on your neighbour. You can decline the shared evening and still use the arrangement for one subject while taking another elsewhere or online. Families searching for IB and IGCSE tutors near me Mumbai from inside a large complex usually end up with a mixed week, and a mixed week built on purpose beats a single arrangement joined because it was already upstairs.
