sections.heading: Why short frequent sessions beat one long weekly session in Mumbai traffic
paragraphs: Two sixty-minute sessions in a week do more for a Cambridge IGCSE grade than one long session of the same total length, and in Andheri East the travel reality pushes a family the same way. The skills that move IGCSE marks are small and repeatable: place points on a grid, read the command word, show the working, write the causal step. They respond to frequent short repetition, and they decay across a six-day gap in a way that content knowledge does not.

Consider what actually happens inside a single long weekly session. The tutor spends the first part reviewing the week's school content, the middle part on a past paper, and the last part marking it while the student watches. The correction therefore arrives at the end of a tiring block, and the next chance to apply it is six days later, by which time the student has sat four school lessons and two homeworks with the same error baked in. Split the same hours and the correction lands inside twenty-four hours of the mistake, which is the whole mechanism. For Paper 6 skills, three ten-minute grid drills across a week beat thirty minutes in one sitting.

The travel reality then decides which half goes where. Andheri East in the evening peak is slow on every approach: the Western Express Highway, the JVLR side towards Powai and Chandivali, and the Jogeshwari crossing. A tutor who commits to two car journeys a week into that will reschedule one of them, and the one they reschedule is always the mid-week slot. So the long session goes to the weekend or to an early slot straight after school, when a tutor can arrive without fighting the peak at all, and the short mid-week session goes online, where a 45-minute slot starts on time and costs nobody an hour in each direction.

There is a third option worth knowing about, which is matching for the train rather than the road. Tutors who reach Andheri station on the Western Line or Marol on Metro Line 1 and walk the last stretch arrive inside a predictable ten-minute window whatever the highway is doing, because the train does not queue. When a family asks for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai across two or three subjects, this is how a standing weekday slot survives a full term: match the tutor who can come by train for the weekday session, and put the car-dependent specialist on the weekend.
bullets: Two shorter sessions beat one long one at the same total hours
Correction inside twenty-four hours stops an error becoming a habit
Paper 6 grid work suits ten-minute drills, not thirty-minute blocks
Long session at the weekend or straight after school, not at 7pm
Short mid-week session online, where the start time is reliable

sections.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks, one term and one exam cycle?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see a change in how your child works, not in the grade. At one term you should see a measurable shift on one specific paper type. At one exam cycle you should see a grade consistent with the tier your child was entered for. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and any tutor who offers you one is telling you something they cannot possibly know.

Four weeks is diagnosis plus habit. Concretely: working is shown on calculation questions, the command word is marked before the answer is written, a past-paper question is attempted before the notes are opened, and the student can tell you which papers they sit and at which tier. None of that shows up as a better test score yet, and it is the only thing that reliably produces one later. If none of it has changed after four weeks, something is wrong with the match and you should say so rather than waiting politely for the term to end.

One term is where a number should move, but only in one place. A student who was losing marks on Physics 0625 Paper 6 should be scoring on the plotting and precaution questions even if the theory grade is still flat. A Mathematics 0580 Extended candidate who was abandoning Paper 4 structured questions halfway should be finishing them. Broad improvement across everything in a single term is usually a sign of an easier paper rather than a better student. Ask your tutor which one paper type they are targeting this term, write it down, and hold them to it at the end.

The honest limits matter more than the promises. A tutor cannot replace attendance, cannot compress two missing years of foundation algebra into six weeks before a May series, and cannot raise a Core candidate above the Core ceiling, which is grade C whatever anybody tells you. If a child arrives in February of Year 11 with half the syllabus unlearned, the useful conversation is about which grade is reachable and which papers to protect, not about an A*. We would much rather have that conversation in the first week than in April.
bullets: Four weeks: shown working, marked command words, past papers before notes
One term: one named paper type measurably better, not everything at once
One exam cycle: a grade consistent with the tier entered
A Core entry cannot exceed grade C, whatever a tutor promises
Say something at week four if the habits have not changed

sections.heading: Booking an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai: what to prepare
paragraphs: Send four things and the first shortlist is usually accurate: the year group and tier, the subject list with syllabus codes if you have them, two or three slot windows that are genuinely free, and a photograph of one marked script. The marked script is the thing that does the work. Everything else can be corrected in a phone call, but a real piece of your child's marked writing cannot be described second-hand and cannot be faked.

The first session is diagnostic and should feel like it. Expect the tutor to put a past-paper question in front of your child inside the first fifteen minutes rather than teaching, to ask the student to talk through a wrong answer in their own words, and to leave with one specific target for the following week. A first session spent on introductions and a syllabus overview is a wasted session and you are entitled to say so. By the end of it you should have a written plan naming the papers being targeted and the order they will be worked on.

What IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on, since we publish no price list: the board and level, because DP Higher Level work carries a heavier marking load than IGCSE Core; subject scarcity, because an Economics 0455 or Computer Science 0478 specialist is rarer than a Maths tutor and priced accordingly; travel distance and whether the slot falls in the evening peak, because a tutor crossing from Chembur to Andheri East in the peak is selling you two hours of their day for one hour of teaching; session length and frequency, since two shorter sessions carry two travel costs; and whether the format is home, online or hybrid. Ask for the per-session figure and the number of sessions a month in the same sentence, so you are comparing the same thing between tutors.

If a tutor is not working out, tell us in writing and the replacement is handled rather than negotiated. We ask for one reason, because it improves the next match: slot reliability, subject depth, or the student simply not talking in sessions are three different problems with three different solutions. There is no notice period and no obligation to continue a block you have already paid for beyond the sessions actually taught.
bullets: Send year group, tier, subject list and two free slot windows
Photograph one marked script; it beats any written description
First session is diagnostic: a past paper inside fifteen minutes
Ask for the per-session fee and monthly session count together

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to Bombay Cambridge International School in any way?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Bombay Cambridge International School. We name the school because parents search for it, and because a tutor's plan has to fit the school's calendar. We have no access to its mark schemes, its internal assessment materials, its staff or its report data, and no tutor on our platform has or claims such access. If a tutor ever implies otherwise, tell us and we will drop them from your shortlist. An IB and IGCSE tutor for Bombay Cambridge International School students in Mumbai works from the published Cambridge syllabus and your child's own marked scripts, and nothing else.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and level first, then subject scarcity, travel and format. IB Diploma Higher Level work is priced above IGCSE Core because the subject depth and the marking load are genuinely different. A scarce subject specialist costs more than a Maths tutor, simply because fewer of them exist. Travel weighs more heavily in Mumbai than almost anywhere else: a tutor crossing two suburbs in the evening peak gives up two hours for one hour of teaching, and that sits inside the rate. Session length, frequency and whether the slot is home, online or hybrid finish the calculation. We publish no price list because any single figure would be wrong for most of these combinations.

faqs.question: Should my child take Core or Extended Mathematics 0580?
faqs.answer: Extended if a grade above C matters or if IB Maths is the plan; Core if the grade only needs to be secure. Cambridge Core papers in Mathematics 0580 award grades C to G, so a Core entry cannot produce a B however well the papers go on the day. Extended means Papers 2 and 4 and a larger syllabus, including functions, set notation and harder trigonometry. The entry decision belongs to the school rather than to us, but the preparation window is Year 10, not the February before the series. A tutor's first job in Year 9 is keeping the Extended route genuinely available.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 9. Is it too early for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Year 9 is the cheapest year in which to fix things, so no. The IGCSE content load in Years 10 and 11 assumes Year 9 algebra, graph skills and scientific vocabulary are already secure, and a child who reaches Year 10 shaky in those has no spare time to go back for them. In Year 9 a tutor is usually working one session a week on foundations and exam habits rather than grinding past papers, which costs less and achieves more than the same spend in Year 11. It is also the year in which the Extended tier is still freely available in every subject.

faqs.question: Can a tutor actually reach Andheri East for a weekday evening session?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor is matched for the commute and not only for the subject. For home tuition in Andheri East, Chandivali, Jogeshwari or Santacruz East we prefer tutors who can reach you by train or on Metro Line 1 and walk the last stretch, because Andheri station and Marol give a predictable arrival window that the Western Express Highway does not. Where the only suitable subject specialist is car-dependent, we put that tutor on a weekend or straight-after-school slot and run the mid-week session online instead. A 7pm weekday car slot across two suburbs tends to fail by week three.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: No, but somebody should be, and the study space matters more than the supervision does. Home classes work best at a table in a shared room with the door open rather than in a bedroom, with the phone out of the room and the television off. Most of our Mumbai families have a grandparent or house help present, which is entirely enough. What we do ask is that the same space is available at the same time every week, because a tutor who is moved from the dining table to a bedroom to a balcony across three weeks loses several minutes of every session simply settling in.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is late or misses a session?
faqs.answer: A missed session is made up or credited, and persistent lateness is a reason to change tutors rather than something to tolerate. Mumbai traffic means a genuine fifteen-minute delay happens to everybody, and we ask tutors to message the moment they know. What is not acceptable is a pattern: three late arrivals in a month usually means the slot was never realistic for where that tutor lives. Tell us and we will either move the slot, move that session online, or shortlist someone who lives closer. Society gate passes are worth arranging once, in advance, so that the gate is never the reason for the delay.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for practical papers like Paper 6?
faqs.answer: For Paper 6, the alternative to practical, online works well; for Paper 5, the timetabled practical test, it does not. Paper 6 is a paper-based skills test covering plotting, best-fit lines, precautions, anomalous readings, parallax and repeat readings. All of that can be drilled on a shared screen, and in some ways better, because a tutor can put a fresh grid up every ninety seconds. Paper 5 needs hands on real apparatus, which the school provides and we do not. If your child is entered for Paper 5, the useful tutoring is on recording and processing results, and that is still mostly paper work.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Say so immediately, in writing, and ask the tutor for the specific target they set in week one. At four weeks the honest expectation is changed habits rather than changed grades: working shown, command words read properly, past papers attempted before the notes come out. If even those have not moved, the usual causes are a mismatched tutor, a slot too late in the evening for the child to concentrate, or a diagnosis that was simply wrong about where the marks were going. All three are fixable, and all three get worse with another month of politeness. We will arrange a replacement without an argument.

faqs.question: How do I replace a tutor who is not working out?
faqs.answer: Message us with one reason and the replacement is arranged; you owe nothing beyond the sessions already taught. The reason matters only because it improves the next match. Slot reliability means we shortlist by location next time. Subject depth means we go for a specialist in that syllabus code rather than a capable generalist. "My child does not talk in sessions" usually points to a different teaching style rather than a weaker tutor. There is no notice period, no exit conversation and no pressure to continue a paid block. For common subjects a replacement is usually in place within a few days.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all my child's IB and IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and you should be wary of anyone who says yes. One tutor can genuinely cover a science cluster, or Maths with Additional Mathematics 0606, or two languages, because the mark schemes and command words overlap enough to transfer. Asking for all IB and IGCSE subjects from one tutor in Mumbai across Maths, Physics, Economics and English means getting someone shallow in at least two of them. The arrangement most families end up with is one tutor for the Maths and science side and another for languages and humanities, with the two slots on different days of the week.

faqs.question: Do you have tutors for the IB Diploma after IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning that handover during Year 11 is worth the effort. The International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) is a different animal from Cambridge IGCSE: Internal Assessment (IA) coursework, the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Higher Level and Standard Level split all arrive at once in DP1. An IGCSE Extended Mathematics 0580 candidate has the foundation for Maths at Higher Level; a Core candidate generally does not. We match DP tutors across Mumbai, Thane and Navi Mumbai the same way, by component rather than by subject name, so a tutor is shortlisted for Physics Paper 2 at Higher Level and the IA, not for "Physics".

sections.heading: How IB Gram builds a shortlist for a Bombay International School family in Mumbai
paragraphs: The enquiry that arrives from a Babulnath family is almost never a request for a tutor in the abstract. It reads like this: our daughter is in Year 10, she has Chemistry and Additional Mathematics, school finishes in the afternoon, and nothing can start before half past six because of the drive back through Kemps Corner. The subject matters. The window is what decides whether a match holds for a full term. So the timetable is the first filter we apply, before qualifications, before experience, before anything else printed on a profile.

From there the filter narrows by board and by level. A parent asking for an IB or IGCSE home tutor for Bombay International School students in Mumbai is usually asking about one of two different things: the IGCSE years, where the work is syllabus coverage and past paper technique, or the Diploma Programme, where the tutor also has to understand internal assessment criteria and the pace of a two-year course that cannot be caught up in March. We do not treat those as the same request. Somebody excellent with a Year 9 group can be exactly the wrong person for a DP2 student three weeks from a draft deadline.

What comes back is a short list rather than a directory. Two or three profiles, each carrying the subjects that tutor has actually taught at this level, the syllabus codes they work with, the area they travel from, and the evening windows they can hold every single week. You see the travel origin because it predicts reliability better than anything a tutor writes about themselves. Somebody coming from Tardeo or Walkeshwar for a seven o'clock start will still be turning up in February. Somebody promising to cross the city from Andheri every Tuesday usually will not, and the arrangement quietly dies in week six.

Treat the first session as both a lesson and an interview. Sit in for the opening ten minutes if the household allows it. By the end the tutor should be able to say what the gap is in plain language: not that your child needs to work harder, but that she is dropping method marks because the intermediate line of working never gets written down, and that is several marks a paper. If the match is wrong, say so immediately. Changing tutors in week two costs you nothing. Changing in week nine costs a term.

sections.heading: IGCSE Years 9-11 and the IB Diploma Programme: what a two-stage pathway asks
paragraphs: Bombay International School, at Babulnath in South Mumbai, Maharashtra, runs a Cambridge International Education IGCSE pathway followed by the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP). That is public information about the school and the limit of what anybody outside it should claim to know. What it means for a family is that a student sits two assessment systems back to back, built on different philosophies, with roughly eight weeks between the end of one and the beginning of the other.

The IGCSE stage occupies Years 9 to 11 and ends in terminal papers. Several subjects are tiered: a Core paper and an Extended paper covering the same subject at different ceilings, with the Extended route carrying the full grade range and the Core route capped below it. Sciences add practical assessment or an alternative-to-practical paper. The grading rewards technique as much as knowledge, which is why a bright student can read the textbook twice and still lose marks on command terms such as describe, explain and suggest.

The Diploma Programme is a different machine. Six subjects, one from most groups, three taken at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL). Around those six sit the Core: the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK), and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment (IA) marked by the school against published criteria and then moderated. Nothing in IGCSE prepares a student for writing four thousand words of independent research while three IA drafts are due.

Tell any prospective tutor which board a sibling is on too, because Mumbai schools do not share one pathway. Some run Pearson Edexcel IGCSE, some run the Middle Years Programme (MYP) before DP, and criteria that look similar on paper are marked differently. A tutor who assumes the wrong variant will teach to the wrong mark scheme for a month before anyone notices.
bullets: IGCSE runs Years 9 to 11 and ends with terminal written papers
Core and Extended tiers change the paper sat, not the subject studied

sections.heading: Which subjects do IGCSE and IB DP families in Mumbai ask for most?
paragraphs: Mathematics and the sciences, in that order, then Economics and Business Management, then English when a first-language paper turns out harder than a bilingual household expected. Second languages arrive last, usually in DP1, when a student discovers that Spanish ab initio is a full subject with its own written and oral assessment rather than a soft sixth choice.

Mathematics splits early and the split matters. At IGCSE the question is Core or Extended, and then whether to add Additional Mathematics, which is the genuine bridge into Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. A student who skips it and walks into AA HL is meeting calculus, proof and exact-form answers at the same time as a new school structure. The alternative route, Applications and Interpretation, is not a lesser subject; it is a different one, built around modelling and technology, and it closes some university doors while opening others.

Here is the kind of thing a tutor fixes in one session. A Year 11 student is working an Additional Mathematics optimisation question: a closed cylinder of fixed volume, find the radius that minimises the surface area. She writes the surface area in terms of the radius, differentiates it correctly, sets the derivative to zero and produces exactly the right value. Full marks, she assumes. The mark scheme also wants proof that the stationary point is a minimum, through the second derivative or a sign test either side, and that mark disappears every time she answers one of these. The same cylinder returns in Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 1, this time without a calculator, with the answer required in exact form and the justification expected rather than prompted. That is the Higher Level step in a single question: not stranger ideas, fewer prompts.

The sciences follow a similar pattern. Co-ordinated Sciences keeps three disciplines alive in fewer timetable hours and suits plenty of students, though it leaves less content behind when Chemistry HL begins. In DP, each science carries a scientific investigation assessed against published criteria, and most of the marks that go missing go on methodology and evaluation rather than on the practical work itself. Economics students lose marks on the internal assessment commentaries for the same reason: real-world article, correct diagram, no evaluation. English A Language and Literature Paper 1 is unseen analysis against the clock, which is a trainable skill and almost never trained.

sections.heading: Where your tutor travels from: Mumbai coverage from South Mumbai to Thane
paragraphs: Babulnath sits at the middle of the island, with Malabar Hill above it, Napean Sea Road and Breach Candy to the west, Tardeo behind it and Grant Road below. Families attending the school live across all of those, plus Walkeshwar, and reach it from Grant Road and Charni Road stations on the Western Line. That central position is the practical advantage here: a tutor can arrive from four different directions, so the available pool is wider than for a school sitting at one end of the island. For mainstream subjects such as IGCSE Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Economics, availability is genuinely good. The honest constraint is not distance, it is the hour: the Peddar Road and Kemps Corner evening flow decides which slots can exist at all, and a tutor who says yes to both a 6pm and a 7.30pm booking on the same evening is making a promise the traffic will break.

Most matches for these families stay inside South Mumbai, where a pool runs from Colaba and Cuffe Parade through Worli and Tardeo. Moving north, the Western Suburbs hold a deep bench in Bandra, Khar, Santacruz and Juhu, and the Western Express Highway plus Metro Lines 2A and 7 make north-south travel along the line workable off-peak. Coming south in the evening is another matter. Metro Line 3 has changed the calculation for a tutor working between Worli, Bandra Kurla Complex and the island, and the Coastal Road has made the Worli to Babulnath run far more predictable than it was. No single tutor covers all IB and IGCSE subjects and any tutor in Mumbai who implies otherwise should be asked which syllabus codes they have actually taught.

The Central Suburbs run along the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR and no station of their own, so tutors there reach students by road from Ghatkopar or Andheri East. The Eastern Suburbs stretch from Chembur and Wadala up through Vikhroli to Mulund, and the Eastern Freeway makes the island city reachable from Chembur much faster than the map suggests, which is the one eastern corridor that genuinely works for a South Mumbai evening slot. The Harbour Line and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road fill in the rest.

Navi Mumbai works node to node, Vashi to Nerul to Kharghar along Palm Beach Road, and the Atal Setu has shortened the crossing to the island considerably. Thane spreads along Pokhran Road and Ghodbunder Road, served by the Central and Trans-Harbour lines. For a Babulnath family, neither is a realistic weekly home visit, and we will say so rather than book a tutor who resents the drive by October. Where a Navi Mumbai or Thane tutor is the right subject specialist, the sensible answer is online. We keep a pool deep enough to cover all IB and IGCSE subjects across IGCSE Years 9-11 with tutors in Mumbai spread across every one of these zones, and we match for the shortest honest journey.

sections.heading: The IGCSE and IB DP calendar that sets a Mumbai school year
paragraphs: Before the calendar, the boundary. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We are not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Bombay International School in any way, we have no access to its staff, its materials, its internal marks or its admissions, and any tutor who tells you otherwise is selling you something. What we work from is the same public information you have: the school is at Babulnath in South Mumbai and offers IGCSE and IB Diploma Programme pathways. Everything useful we can add is about those two boards, not about the institution.

The board calendar is what actually governs your term. School years here start around June, and the first stretch to the Diwali break is pure syllabus coverage, which is the cheapest time to fix a weakness and the time families most often skip. Mocks land either side of the break and into December. January and February are the compression point for DP2: internal assessment final submissions, the Extended Essay deadline and the Theory of Knowledge essay all converge while teachers are finalising predicted grades. March is revision and the last internal deadlines. The IB written examinations run from late April into May, the Cambridge June series overlaps them, and results arrive in July for the IB and August for Cambridge, with remark and retake decisions due within a very short window after that.

The practical consequence is that help booked in January is help booked in the worst month of the year. A DP2 student in February has no spare evening, and a tutor hired then spends the first three weeks learning the student rather than teaching. The families who get the most out of tutoring start in the June to September stretch, run one session a week through the quiet months, and increase only in the run-up to mocks. For a Year 10 student the equivalent logic applies: the work that protects an IGCSE grade happens a year before the paper, not six weeks before it.

Families here usually weigh a couple of other South Mumbai options when they first choose a school, most often Activity High School at Peddar Road, which follows an IGCSE route, and Aditya Birla World Academy at Tardeo, which offers IGCSE and the IB Diploma Programme. That is public context, nothing more. It matters to tutoring for one dull reason: a tutor working in this pocket of the city may have students at more than one of these schools, which affects which evenings they can hold, and that is a scheduling fact rather than any kind of relationship.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a Babulnath family?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default and for this part of the city it is also the right default. IB and IGCSE home tuition for Bombay International School students in Mumbai almost always means a tutor already living inside the island, arriving at the flat, working at the dining table with the actual exercise book rather than a photograph of it. The tutor sees how the student writes, where she stops, what she skips. That is worth a surprising amount in a subject where marks hang on written method.

The trade-offs are real and worth saying out loud. Travel time is built into the slot whether or not anybody itemises it, so a tutor who gives up ninety minutes of an evening to the road has fewer slots to sell and will defend the one you book. That is why a good arrangement is a fixed weekly time rather than a floating one. A home session also needs a workable room: a table with a plug point, away from the television, where a sibling is not doing homework three feet away. And a cancelled home session is harder to replace than a cancelled online one, because the tutor's evening has already been spent getting there.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai earns their place in three situations. The first is scarcity: Psychology, Computer Science, Economics at Higher Level, or a language that nobody within five kilometres teaches well. The second is time: a 9pm revision hour during exam leave that no tutor will drive across Kemps Corner for. The third is intensity, when a student needs three short sessions a week in March rather than one long one. Screen-shared past papers with a graphics tablet work well for mathematics and sciences. They work less well for a fourteen-year-old who needs somebody in the room to stop her drifting.

Hybrid is what most families settle into without planning it. One home session a week as the anchor, plus a short online check before a deadline: the night before an internal assessment draft goes in, or the evening after a mock paper is returned. It also absorbs the weeks when the city stops, which in practice means the heavy monsoon days and exam leave, when the student is at home all day anyway. Agree the hybrid pattern at the start rather than drifting into it, so the tutor prices and plans one arrangement instead of two.

sections.heading: How are IB and IGCSE home tutors in Mumbai checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Identity, qualification, teaching history and a subject screen, in that order, and all of it before a profile is shown to you. Every IB and IGCSE home teacher for Bombay International School students in Mumbai goes through the same sequence, and a tutor who will not complete it does not get listed. The checks are not a guarantee of chemistry with your child, which no process can supply, but they remove the categories of problem that waste a term.

Identity means a government photo document and a confirmed address, because a person coming into your home weekly should be somebody whose name you can verify. Qualification means the degree claimed, checked against the subject claimed, which matters more than it sounds: a mechanical engineering graduate can be superb at IGCSE Mathematics and completely unprepared for the evaluation demands of a DP Chemistry internal assessment. Teaching history means which boards, which levels, which years, and for DP tutors whether they have worked with students through a full two-year cycle rather than only coaching the final term. The subject screen is practical: here is a student's written answer, mark it, then justify the marks against the criteria. It exposes the gap between somebody who knows the content and somebody who knows the mark scheme.

Then there is the half you should do yourself, which is the more useful half. Ask which syllabus codes and which exam series they have taught, and listen for whether the answer is specific. Ask how they would handle a missed session, a late draft, or a student who stops doing the set work, and get the answer before you need it. Ask what the internal assessment criteria are for the subject in question and see whether they can name them without looking. Ask who else in the building or the area they teach, since a tutor already arriving on your road at six can hold your slot far more easily than one making a special trip.

Be sceptical of breadth. No single tutor covers all IB and IGCSE subjects and any tutor in Mumbai who implies they can should be asked, politely, to name the last three papers they marked in each. Two specialists are almost always better than one generalist, and for a student taking both a science and a language this is not a luxury. Be sceptical too of anybody promising outcomes in a first conversation. We do not guarantee grades, and neither should they.

sections.heading: Choosing HL and SL at the end of IGCSE: the decision that shapes DP2
paragraphs: The single most consequential academic decision a family at this school makes is taken in Year 11, usually in the same months the student is revising for IGCSE papers, which is the worst possible time to think clearly about anything. Three subjects will be taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, and that selection governs the workload, the stress profile and the university options of the following two years. Changing an HL subject in the first term of DP1 is possible. Changing it in DP2 is generally not.

What Higher Level adds is poorly understood. Families picture extra topics, and there are extra topics, but the harder half of the difference is a change in how questions are asked. HL papers prompt less. An SL question will often tell the student which method to use; the HL version of the same idea presents a situation and expects the student to choose. HL sciences add additional content and a longer, less structured paper. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level adds a further paper built on deeper problem solving, and the mathematics internal assessment is judged against the same criteria at both levels, which quietly penalises an HL student who picks a thin topic.

The IGCSE stage feeds this directly. Sitting Extended papers keeps the Higher Level door open; a Core entry narrows it, because the content assumed on day one of DP sits above the Core ceiling. Taking Additional Mathematics is the strongest single predictor of a comfortable first term in Analysis and Approaches HL. Then there are the external constraints: engineering routes generally expect Mathematics and Physics at Higher Level, medicine expects Chemistry and usually Biology, and several economics programmes abroad now ask for Mathematics at Higher Level specifically. A family choosing HL subjects by which teacher the child likes is choosing a degree shortlist without realising it.

This is where a tutor is genuinely useful, and where an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai should be willing to disappoint you. The honest process is short: give the student two or three Higher Level questions in the candidate subject, watch what happens, and have a frank conversation about effort and interest rather than ability alone. There is no single best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai for that conversation; there is the one who has taught the specific Higher Level subject and will say plainly that the student is not ready for it, or that she is ready and the family is underestimating her. Both of those sentences save a year.

HL adds content and removes prompting, and the prompting matters more

sections.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks of home tuition in Mumbai?
paragraphs: After four weeks you should have a diagnosis and one changed habit, not a changed grade. The diagnosis should be specific enough to repeat to a teacher: she is strong on content and loses marks on command terms, or he can do the algebra but cannot set up the problem. The habit is usually small and mechanical, such as writing the working line that earns the method mark, or reading the mark allocation before answering. If four weeks have produced only a general sense that sessions are going fine, that is a warning.

By the end of a term the evidence should be visible in school work rather than only in the tutor's opinion. Mock papers move, or specific question types that used to be skipped are now attempted. Internal assessment drafts go in on time, which for a DP student is often worth more than the content improvement itself, because a late draft costs feedback rounds that cannot be recovered. A student who was avoiding one topic entirely is now willing to start questions on it. Progress at this stage is rarely linear and often shows as a drop first, when a student starts attempting harder questions and scores worse before scoring better.

Across a full exam cycle the honest measure is whether predicted grades stop surprising everybody and whether the student walks into the hall with a workable strategy for each paper. That is as far as anybody responsible will go. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor, however good with past papers, can promise a result that depends on a student's work, a school's teaching, an examiner's judgement and a single morning in May. Anyone offering you a number is guessing or lying, and the ones who do it most confidently are the ones to avoid.

What can be promised is narrower and more checkable: a tutor who arrives on the agreed evening, marks to the published criteria rather than to a feeling, tells you the truth at the four-week mark even when it is unwelcome, and says clearly when the problem is not something tutoring solves. Sometimes it is sleep, or six subjects chosen badly, or a student who does not want this. A tutor who identifies that in month one has done more for the family than one who quietly bills through to March.

sections.heading: Starting home tuition in Mumbai: what to have ready for the first session
paragraphs: Three things make the first session useful instead of introductory. The subject list, with Higher Level and Standard Level intentions marked even if they are not final. The last two marked papers, with the teacher's comments still on them, because a marked script tells a tutor more in five minutes than a parent can in an hour. And two evening windows that survive a bad traffic day, not the ones that work in theory. If you want one request covering all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes across Mumbai for two children on different boards, say that at the start and we will build it as one schedule rather than two unrelated bookings.

For a DP student, add the internal assessment brief and the criteria sheet for the subject in question, plus the school's internal deadlines if you have them. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student, add the syllabus code if you know it, since Mathematics and Additional Mathematics are different animals and families frequently name the wrong one. If there has been a previous tutor, say what did not work. That is the most useful sentence in the whole conversation and the one parents most often leave out from politeness.

The household logistics are simple and worth settling before the tutor arrives. A table with a plug point, away from the television, where the session will happen every week. Add the tutor's name to the building's visitor list in advance so the first evening does not start with a fifteen-minute delay downstairs. Have somebody at home for the first session, which is normal practice and nothing to apologise for. And agree the cancellation rule in the first week: how much notice either side gives, and whether a missed slot is made up or forfeited.

The first session itself should produce something you can read. A short written diagnosis, a plan for the term that names topics rather than aspirations, and a clear statement of what the tutor expects the student to do between sessions. If you need a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai across a family, we will stagger the starts so you are not assessing three new people in one week. And if the first tutor is not right, tell us in the first fortnight and we will move, without a conversation about why.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Rates move with five things, and none of them is a fixed price list. Board and level first: a DP Higher Level subject costs more per hour than a Year 9 subject because the preparation and marking load is heavier. Then subject scarcity, which is why Psychology, Computer Science and the less common languages sit above Mathematics. Then travel, since a tutor crossing Kemps Corner in the evening is giving up a second slot. Then session length and frequency, where two shorter weekly sessions often cost more than one long one. Finally timing, because February availability is scarce and priced accordingly. Ask for the total monthly figure rather than an hourly one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor realistically reach Babulnath for an evening slot on a weekday?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor already lives inside South Mumbai. A tutor coming from Tardeo, Walkeshwar, Grant Road or Napean Sea Road can hold a 6.30pm or 7pm slot reliably through the year. The arrangements that break are the ones that assume a suburban tutor will cross into the island at peak hour every week; that holds in July and collapses by October. The Peddar Road and Kemps Corner flow is the real constraint, not the kilometres. If the only specialist for a scarce subject lives in Powai or Thane, book that one online and keep home sessions for subjects with a local pool.

faqs.question: Do you have tutors close enough for weekly home classes in South Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the strength of a central location. Most IB and IGCSE home classes for Bombay International School students in Mumbai are taught by somebody already working within the island, because Babulnath can be reached from Malabar Hill, Breach Candy, Tardeo and Grant Road in a short run. For mainstream subjects such as IGCSE Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English, the local pool is deep enough to offer a genuine choice rather than one available name. Scarcer subjects may need either a longer journey or an online tutor, and we will tell you which category you are in before you commit.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to Bombay International School in any way?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to the school. We have no access to its teachers, its internal assessments, its marking, its reports or its admissions process, and we would not use such access if we had it. What we work from is public information: the school is at Babulnath in South Mumbai and offers IGCSE and IB Diploma Programme pathways. Our tutors are matched on the boards and subjects they have actually taught. If any tutoring service claims a relationship with a school, ask them to put it in writing.

faqs.question: My child cannot choose between Analysis and Approaches at HL and SL. Can a tutor help decide?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most valuable single sessions a family can book. The method is practical rather than theoretical: the tutor sets two or three genuine Higher Level questions in the subject and watches how the student handles the ones with no method given. That reveals more than any report card. The conversation should then cover whether the student has taken Additional Mathematics at IGCSE, what degree routes are under discussion, and what the other five subjects demand in the same two years. A tutor willing to recommend Standard Level is more useful than one who agrees with the ambitious option.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for IB DP subjects?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma Programme subjects, yes, with conditions. Screen-shared past papers and a graphics tablet work well for Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, and online is often the only way to reach a specialist in Psychology, Computer Science or a less common language. It works particularly well for internal assessment feedback, where the real work is annotating a draft. It works less well for younger students who drift without somebody in the room, and it works badly at the end of a long day on a phone screen. Use a laptop, a quiet room and a fixed time, and online holds up through a full cycle.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three or four sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace them, without requiring you to justify the decision. Fit is not a moral judgement; a tutor who is excellent with a methodical Year 10 student can be wrong for a fast, impatient DP2 student. We ask for one specific detail, such as the pace being wrong or the sessions drifting into chat, purely so the next match is better. A replacement is normally arranged within the same week for mainstream subjects and takes a little longer for scarce ones. The expensive mistake is waiting: families who hold on until the mock results are three months behind for no reason.

faqs.question: We have seen no real progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask the tutor for the diagnosis in writing before changing anything. At four weeks there should be a specific statement of the problem and evidence of one habit changing, even if marks have not moved. If the tutor cannot produce that, the problem is the tutor. If the diagnosis is clear and credible but the marks are flat, the problem may be the gap between sessions, since one hour a week cannot outrun six days of nothing. Sometimes the honest finding is that the subject choice is wrong, or that sleep and timetable load are the real issue. A tutor who says that has earned the month.

faqs.question: Do we need separate tutors for IGCSE and for the IB Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: For two children at different stages, usually yes. The IGCSE years reward syllabus coverage and paper technique; the Diploma Programme rewards understanding of internal assessment criteria, independent research and a two-year pace. Plenty of tutors handle both within a subject, especially in Mathematics and the sciences, and a single tutor is simpler to schedule. Across subjects it is different: one person claiming every subject at both levels is a warning sign. For a single child moving from Year 11 into DP1, keeping the same subject tutor through the transition usually helps, provided that tutor has genuinely taught a full DP cycle.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: For the first session, yes, and it is standard rather than awkward. You are confirming who is in your home, how they work and whether the room arrangement functions. After that it is your call. Many families stay in the flat without sitting in the room, which is a sensible middle position. Two practical points: tell the building's security desk the tutor's name in advance so the evening does not start with a delay, and keep the session in a shared space rather than a bedroom. Most tutors prefer this too, because a visible working space removes ambiguity for everybody involved.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor help with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and with a clear boundary. A subject tutor can help a student structure an Extended Essay in that subject, sharpen the research question and understand the assessment criteria, which is where most essays are won or lost. The work itself must be the student's own, and the school supervisor remains the person guiding it formally. Theory of Knowledge is more specialised and is often better handled by a tutor who teaches it, since the essay rewards a particular kind of argument rather than subject knowledge. Say at the matching stage if you want this, because it changes who we shortlist.

We come back with two or three tutor profiles carrying syllabus codes, teaching history and the area each one travels from. You pick, the first session runs as a working diagnosis with you free to listen in, and if the match is wrong in the first fortnight we replace the tutor without a debate.

sections.heading: How do we match an IB and IGCSE home tutor for Cathedral and John Connon School students in Mumbai?
paragraphs: You send one message naming the board, the year group and the subject. Inside about a working day you get two or three tutor profiles: what each has taught, for how many years, which boards, and when they can reach your building. You choose one. The first session is a diagnostic rather than a lesson, and you are told in writing what it found before you commit to a term of anything.

What a request for an IB and IGCSE home tutor for Cathedral and John Connon School students in Mumbai tells us is mostly calendar. It says the child is on a Cambridge International Education IGCSE pathway that feeds into the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) inside the same institution, that the school day runs on a Fort timetable, and that the family probably lives somewhere on the island. It does not tell us the subject problem, so the first question back is always about the subject and the specific piece of work that went wrong.

Asking for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai is the wrong frame, and we say so early rather than politely agreeing. There is no single ranking. A Diploma Programme Economics teacher who writes excellent commentary feedback can be a poor fit for a Year 10 student who needs someone patient about algebraic manipulation. Fit is specific: subject, level, the student's actual gap, the hour of the evening they can still concentrate in, and whether they learn better by being questioned or by being shown.

Most parents start by typing IB and IGCSE tutors near me from somewhere in Mumbai, then discover that proximity is the least useful filter of the three that matter. A tutor fifteen minutes away who has never supervised a Diploma Programme Internal Assessment (IA) is worse than one forty minutes away who has marked a hundred of them. We weigh travel seriously, because a match that dies in November helps nobody, but we weigh it after subject and level, never before.

sections.heading: IGCSE into the IB Diploma Programme: the hinge year in a South Mumbai school
paragraphs: Cathedral and John Connon School runs an International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) pathway and an International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) pathway. That is public information and it is the reason this page exists. The structure matters far more than the names. IGCSE is taken across roughly Years 9 to 11 as a set of separate subject qualifications, each graded on its own and each capable of standing alone. The Diploma Programme that follows is one qualification assembled from six subjects plus a core, and a weak component drags the whole total.

Inside IGCSE the first real decision is tier. Mathematics, the sciences and several language subjects are offered at Core and Extended, and the Extended papers reach grades the Core papers are not able to award. Families often treat this as a confidence question about the child. It is closer to a Diploma Programme question about the next two years: a student who wants Higher Level (HL) Physics needs the Extended Mathematics content, because the Core syllabus never covers the algebraic manipulation that Higher Level Physics quietly assumes from the first week.

The Diploma Programme then asks for three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard Level (SL), one drawn from each of five groups plus a sixth that may be a second science, a second language or an arts subject. On top sit Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). A family can ask for help across all IB and IGCSE subjects in IGCSE Years 9-11 from one tutor in Mumbai, or split the load across two specialists once Diploma Programme Higher Level choices have hardened and the subjects stop overlapping.

The hinge sits at the end of Year 11. The IGCSE results that are meant to inform Diploma Programme choices arrive after the choices have largely been made, so the decision is taken on predicted grades, mock performance and what the student can stand doing for two more years. That is a conversation worth having with someone who has taught both halves and has watched the same student make the same choice badly before.
bullets: IGCSE grades each subject separately; the Diploma Programme grades one assembled package.
Core and Extended tiers cap different grades; Extended feeds Higher Level science.
Diploma Programme: three Higher Level, three Standard Level, plus TOK, EE and CAS.

sections.heading: Subject choice across both boards, and what each subject makes a student produce
paragraphs: Every subject on both boards ends in something the student has to produce, and the production is what tutoring is actually for. At IGCSE that is a set of timed papers, with a practical or coursework component in the sciences and the arts. In the Diploma Programme it is timed papers plus an Internal Assessment (IA) in every single subject, marked by the teacher against published criteria and then moderated externally, which means the criteria are the real curriculum for that piece of work.

The Internal Assessment is not one thing, and treating it as one thing is the commonest planning error we see. In Diploma Programme Mathematics it is an exploration of a mathematical idea the student chooses for themselves. In the sciences it is an individual investigation with its own research question and its own collected data. In Economics it is a set of commentaries on real news articles. In Language A it is an oral on a global issue, and in History it is a short investigation with a formal source evaluation section. A shortlist spans all IB and IGCSE subjects with one tutor in Mumbai per subject where the load genuinely justifies it.

At IGCSE the components are blunter and easier to prepare for, which is both the relief and the trap. A science subject typically carries a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper split by tier, and a practical component that is either a laboratory examination or an alternative-to-practical written paper. Mathematics has two papers at the chosen tier, with the Extended papers carrying the longer structured questions. English Language sits on reading and directed writing before any literary analysis appears, and candidates who are strong readers often lose marks on format rather than content.

Deciding how many subjects to tutor is its own problem and deserves a decision rather than a drift. Two subjects at two hours each is a realistic weekly load for a Year 11 student who still has school homework, a sport, and a daily commute into Fort. Four tutored subjects is usually a sign that something structural has gone wrong with the week, and the honest answer there is to fix the timetable and the sleep before adding a third tutor to it.
bullets: Every Diploma Programme subject carries an Internal Assessment; IGCSE mostly does not.

sections.heading: Where in Mumbai the families at this Fort school actually live
paragraphs: Fort is an office and institution district, so almost nobody tutored under this heading is tutored in Fort itself. The school sits there; the homes are spread down the island and up the lines. In practice IB and IGCSE home tuition for Cathedral and John Connon School students in Mumbai happens in a flat in Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Churchgate, Marine Drive, Walkeshwar or Nepean Sea Road, and the tutor is matched to that home address rather than to the school gate.

South Mumbai is short on distance and long on time, which catches out every tutor who has just moved down from the suburbs. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers a handful of kilometres and can still lose forty minutes at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. The Western Line ends at Churchgate and the Central and Harbour lines terminate at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), so a tutor living near either station reaches the Fort, Churchgate and Marine Drive belt without touching a highway. The Coastal Road has made the Worli run noticeably quicker.

Families move, and a share of this school's students now commute from much further out. The Western Suburbs run along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, so Bandra West and Khar sit one Bandra-Worli Sea Link crossing away, with Metro Lines 2A and 7 serving Malad and Kandivali further north. In the Central Suburbs, Powai and Ghatkopar are reached by JVLR and Metro Line 1 rather than by any station of their own. The Eastern Suburbs, meaning Chembur and Wadala here, are closer to Fort than the map suggests because of the Eastern Freeway. Navi Mumbai nodes such as Vashi and Nerul sit on the Harbour Line and Palm Beach Road, and the Atal Setu has shortened the Panvel approach considerably.

Thane is the honest limit of a weekday road match. A tutor living near Thane station reaches Pokhran Road and Majiwada quickly and Ghodbunder Road slowly, and none of them should be driving to Colaba for a ninety-minute evening lesson that starts at seven. Metro Line 3 now links Cuffe Parade to the Bandra Kurla Complex, which has made a small number of cross-city matches workable that genuinely were not before. Beyond that we match inside the zone and use online sessions for everything the road cannot sustain.

sections.heading: The assessment calendar a Cathedral and John Connon School family plans around
paragraphs: Before anything else, the boundary. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with Cathedral and John Connon School, not endorsed by it, and with no access to its staff, its internally set papers or its marking. We name the school because parents search for it and because its published board pathway sets the shape of the year. Anyone offering you inside knowledge of a Mumbai school's internal assessments is offering you something they should not have, and you should treat that offer as a reason to walk away.

The shape of the year is set by the examination boards, not by any tutor. Cambridge IGCSE sits its main series across May and June, with a smaller November window, so Year 11 spends the second term in mock season and the third term in the real thing. The Diploma Programme May session puts its examinations in the same window, which is why a single South Mumbai household can have a Year 11 child and a DP2 child both effectively unavailable through the same six weeks, with one set of parents trying to run two revision timetables.

The pressure points are predictable enough to plan around, which is the whole argument for starting early. August and September are quiet, and they are the cheapest time to repair a foundation gap because nothing is due. October into November is when Diploma Programme Internal Assessment drafts start landing and when Year 11 coursework stops being theoretical. December and January are mock months. February is when the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay deadlines tend to collide with everything else on the desk. March and April are revision, and by then a tutor is managing pace and nerves rather than teaching new content.

Families here often compare notes with parents at B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade and Bombay International School at Babulnath, both of which also run IGCSE and Diploma Programme pathways in South Mumbai. The calendars rhyme because the boards are the same, not because the schools coordinate anything. If a neighbour's child has a different mock week or a different coursework deadline, that is a school-level decision, and no tutor can or should predict it for you.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid when your child commutes into Fort from across South Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition first, online as cover, and hybrid as the arrangement most families settle into by the second term. A tutor at the dining table gets the one thing a screen cannot reliably get: the student's working, in pencil, as it happens. For a Year 11 sitting Extended Mathematics that is most of the diagnosis, because the error is almost never in the final answer and almost always three lines above it.

The commute shapes the weekly timetable more than the subject ever does. A child travelling into Fort from Bandra West or Chembur leaves early and is rarely home before six, so a weekday slot realistically starts at seven and should finish by half past eight if the next morning is going to work. Saturday mornings are the most reliable hour of the week in South Mumbai and the first slots to go. Most IB and IGCSE home classes for Cathedral and John Connon School students in Mumbai therefore run after seven on two weekdays plus a weekend morning.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai earns their place in two clear situations. The first is scarcity: Higher Level Chemistry, Diploma Programme Economics and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level have thin tutor pools, and insisting on travel can narrow a short list down to nobody. The second is examination season, when a thirty-minute question clinic the night before a paper is worth more than a cancelled ninety-minute visit. Against that, online loses the loose conversation at the end of a session, which is very often where a student finally admits what they did not understand.

Hybrid in practice means one visit a week and one screen session, or all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes across Mumbai during term with online cover through the monsoon and the examination weeks. It is less a compromise than an admission that July rain on the island is real and that a tutor stuck at Haji Ali is not teaching anybody. Agree the pattern in writing at the start, including what happens to a missed slot and who carries the cost of it.

sections.heading: How are IB and IGCSE tutors in Mumbai checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Every tutor gives us a degree certificate, a photo identity document, a verifiable teaching history and a recorded or live sample of them teaching a syllabus topic at the level they are claiming. We watch the sample ourselves rather than taking the claim on trust. A candidate who can describe the Diploma Programme Internal Assessment criteria in the abstract but cannot mark one sample student paragraph against them does not get listed, because marking against criteria is the job.

There are limits to verification and you should know exactly where they sit. We confirm qualifications and teaching history; we cannot confirm what grades a tutor's previous students went on to get, because that data is not ours and anybody quoting it to you is quoting something nobody can check. We also do not list anyone who claims a connection to Cathedral and John Connon School. A tutor who says they know what the school is about to set is either guessing or doing something improper, and both are reasons to pass on them.

Do your own three checks in the first session, because you will learn more in twenty minutes than any profile tells you. Ask the tutor to name the components of your child's subject without looking them up. Ask how they would mark one paragraph of your child's last piece of real work. Ask what they want the student to do between now and the next session. An IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai who cannot answer the second question is a lecturer rather than a tutor, and your child already has lecturers for six hours a day.

Ask about continuity as well, because it is the question nobody thinks to ask until it matters. Families arranging IB or IGCSE home tutoring for Cathedral and John Connon School students in Mumbai usually need it across two or three years, so a tutor planning to leave the city in June is the wrong match for a Year 10 student however good the trial lesson was. We ask tutors to state their horizon honestly, and we tell you when that horizon is short.

sections.heading: Why Year 11 is the year most Cathedral and John Connon School families start looking
paragraphs: Year 11 is the year two separate pressures land inside the same twelve months. The IGCSE terminal examinations arrive, and the Diploma Programme subject choice has to be made before the results of those examinations are known. A student is therefore picking Higher Level subjects on the strength of mock grades and teacher predictions, while simultaneously revising for the papers that were supposed to settle the question for them. Families notice the strain in January and start looking for help in February.

The second pressure is a change in what marking rewards, and it catches strong students hardest because their existing technique stops paying. IGCSE preparation is largely mark-scheme recall: there is an expected answer, the mark scheme lists it, and a disciplined student learns to produce it on demand. The Diploma Programme replaces much of that with criterion-referenced judgement, where a published descriptor asks whether the student has justified, evaluated or analysed, and an examiner decides which band the work belongs in. Take one concrete pair of tasks. An IGCSE alternative-to-practical paper might ask how to improve the reliability of a set of titration results, and 'repeat the titration until two titres agree within 0.10 cm3' takes the mark cleanly, because it is the expected response and the candidate does not have to mean it.

Now put the same student into Diploma Programme Chemistry, writing the Internal Assessment under Criterion B, Exploration. That same sentence earns very little there. The descriptor asks for a methodology that is described and justified in relation to the student's own research question, so they have to explain why concordant titres matter for the precision of the particular concentration being calculated, which sources of error are realistic in their own apparatus, and what they chose to control and why they chose it rather than something else. The chemistry knowledge is identical in both cases. The thing being assessed is not, and a student who has never been asked to justify a choice in writing will under-perform their real understanding for a full term before anybody diagnoses why.

The third pressure is load arriving all at once. In DP1 the Internal Assessments, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay all begin inside the same academic year, each with a different supervisor, a different deadline and a different set of criteria. None of them is difficult in isolation. All of them together, against a Fort timetable and an hour of commuting each way, is a project-management problem long before it is an academic one. A good tutor in this year spends as much time on sequencing and draft deadlines as on subject content, and says so.
bullets: Higher Level choices get made before IGCSE results confirm where the strengths are.
Mark-scheme recall stops paying; criterion descriptors reward justification instead.
Criterion B rewards why a control matters, not merely that it was applied.
Internal Assessment, Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay all start the same year.

sections.heading: What does progress look like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see process change rather than grade change: homework started earlier, a method written out instead of guessed at, fewer blank starts on a question. At one term you should see it reach school assessments, usually as a steadier floor rather than a higher ceiling. At one examination cycle you can judge the arrangement properly. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and anybody who does is selling you something they have no way of delivering.

The four-week mark is really a relationship check rather than an academic one, so ask your child rather than the tutor. Does the tutor make you do the work or do they do it in front of you. Do you know what you are supposed to do before the next session. Can you say what you were bad at four weeks ago and whether it has moved. If those answers come back vague after a month, the match is wrong, and the subject is very unlikely to be the reason it is wrong.

Some things move slowly and you should budget for it rather than be disappointed by it. A reading-speed problem in Diploma Programme English or History does not resolve inside a term. A student who has not written an extended piece of sustained argument since Year 9 will need most of a term before an Extended Essay chapter stops being painful to produce. Conversely, a Year 11 Mathematics student with one specific topic hole, trigonometric identities or algebraic fractions, can cross a grade boundary in six weeks, because the gap is narrow and the papers reward exactly that.

When it is not working, say so at week three rather than week ten. We arrange a replacement without argument and without asking you to build a case for it, and we ask the outgoing tutor for a short handover note so the incoming one does not spend a paid session repeating the diagnostic you already paid for. Most failed matches come down to pace or personality rather than competence, and nobody has to be blamed for it on either side.
bullets: Four weeks: process change, earlier starts, written method, fewer blank pages.
One term: a steadier floor in school assessments, rarely a dramatic ceiling.
One examination cycle: the first genuinely fair test of the arrangement.
