sections.heading: Starting with an IB and IGCSE home tutor in South Mumbai
paragraphs: Send three things and the match gets dramatically faster: the subject and level, your child's last two pieces of marked work, and the three evening windows that actually survive a Fort commute. The marked work does more than any description can, because a tutor reading a teacher's written comments alongside the student's answers can usually see the pattern inside twenty minutes and tell you what kind of help this is.

You do not need to decide the full scope before you start. Some families want a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai from day one, and most of those are better served beginning with a single subject and adding a second after a month of evidence. Others want six focused weeks of Extended Mathematics before the mocks and nothing afterwards. Both are entirely normal requests, and the tutor should be told plainly which of the two they are being hired for.

The first session is a diagnostic and should feel like one. The tutor works through a past paper question or a piece of the student's own coursework while asking them to narrate what they are doing, because the narration exposes the gap far faster than the final answer does. At the end you should get a short written note: what the gap is, which syllabus sections it touches, what the next four sessions will cover, and what the student has to do between them. If that note does not arrive, ask for it before the second session.

A few practical things are worth settling in the first week rather than the fourth. Decide where in the flat the session happens and that it is not the bedroom. Check whether building security needs a standing gate pass so the tutor is not held downstairs every Tuesday. Agree what happens when either side misses a session. And agree how the tutor will tell you something you do not want to hear, because settling that in September is what makes the honest conversation possible in February.
bullets: Send subject, level, two pieces of marked work and three workable evening slots.
Start with one subject; add a second only after four weeks of evidence.
Expect a short written diagnostic note after the first session, every time.
Arrange a standing gate pass so the tutor is not stopped at security weekly.
Agree the missed-session rule before the week you actually need it.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to Cathedral and John Connon School in any way?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform, not affiliated with Cathedral and John Connon School, not endorsed by it, and with no access to its staff, its internally set assessments or its marking. We name the school because that is the phrase parents type into Google, and we write about its board pathway because IGCSE and the Diploma Programme are public, published syllabuses that anybody can read. If a tutor ever tells you they know what the school is about to set, treat it as a reason to end the conversation there.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our home in Colaba or Cuffe Parade on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and South Mumbai addresses are among the easier ones to staff, because tutors who live on the island do not have to cross a highway to reach you. The practical constraint is the hour rather than the distance. Colaba and Cuffe Parade sessions usually start at seven, once the child is back from Fort and has eaten, and a ninety-minute slot finishing by half past eight holds up across a full term far better than a nine o'clock start ever does. Tell us the building and we match within realistic travel of it.

faqs.question: My child gets home from Fort at six. When can home tuition realistically happen?
faqs.answer: Seven to half past eight on two weekdays, plus a Saturday morning, is the pattern that actually survives a term. Fort empties into the evening peak and the trip back to Churchgate, Marine Drive or Worli is slower than the distance suggests, so a six o'clock start fails roughly one week in three, and after that the tutor and the family quietly start resenting each other. Book the later slot and keep it. One unhurried Saturday session is worth two rushed weekday ones once examination term begins.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we will not print a figure here because any figure printed here would be wrong for your case. Board and level come first, since Diploma Programme Higher Level work costs more than IGCSE Year 9. Subject scarcity comes second: Higher Level Chemistry and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches have far smaller tutor pools than English or Business Management. Then travel distance and time of day, because a tutor crossing the island in the evening peak is selling you two hours of their day for one of yours. Session length and whether you book a term block finish the list.

faqs.question: We are deciding between Core and Extended IGCSE Mathematics. Can a tutor help with that call?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the more valuable things a tutor does in Year 9 and Year 10. The decision usually gets framed as a question about confidence when it should be framed as a question about consequence. Extended papers award grades the Core papers cannot, and Higher Level Diploma Programme sciences assume Extended content that the Core syllabus never teaches. A tutor can test the specific gap, which is algebraic manipulation more often than not, then tell you honestly whether six focused weeks closes it or whether Core is the better-fitting plan for this student.

faqs.question: Is online as effective as home tuition for Diploma Programme subjects?
faqs.answer: For most subjects it is close, and for Internal Assessment supervision it can genuinely be better, because screen-sharing a draft with tracked comments beats two people squinting at one laptop at a dining table. Where online loses is early diagnosis and handwritten working in Mathematics and Physics, since the tutor cannot see the line where the error entered. The usual answer for a South Mumbai family is hybrid: run home tuition for the first month while the tutor learns the student, then move routine sessions online and keep one visit a fortnight.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: You tell us and we replace them, with no argument and no fee negotiation to get through first. We ask one question about what went wrong, not to challenge you but because the answer changes who we suggest next: pace, personality, communication style and subject depth are four different problems with four different replacements. The outgoing tutor writes a short handover note so the new one does not spend a whole session repeating the diagnostic. Most swaps happen inside the first month, which is exactly when they should happen.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we start with in Year 11?
faqs.answer: One, in almost every case. Parents arranging IB and IGCSE home tuition for Cathedral and John Connon School students in Mumbai often ask for three subjects at once in September, and that reliably produces a student who is busier rather than better. Start with the subject where the gap is widest or the stakes are highest, run it for four weeks, and then judge it. If the first subject is holding and there is still genuine room in the week, add a second in October before Internal Assessment drafting starts eating the calendar.

faqs.question: Do tutors help with the Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a firm boundary: a tutor teaches the skill and reads a draft, and the student writes every word of it. For an Internal Assessment that means working through the criteria together, testing whether a research question can actually be answered with the data the student can collect, and pointing at the paragraph that asserts something instead of justifying it. For the Extended Essay it is mostly scope control and source discipline. For Theory of Knowledge it is learning to state a claim and then argue against it properly. Supervisors check authenticity, and a tutor who offers to write any of it should be refused.

faqs.question: We live in Navi Mumbai but my child studies in Fort. Does that change the match?
faqs.answer: It changes the mode more than it changes the match. A Vashi, Nerul or Belapur address is best served by a tutor from the same node, because pulling somebody across the Atal Setu or along the Harbour Line for a weekday evening lesson looks workable in September and falls apart by November. The school being in Fort is irrelevant to the tutor's journey; your home address is the only thing that matters to it. For scarce Higher Level subjects we would suggest online from the start rather than a road match that will not hold.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both IGCSE and Diploma Programme years as my child moves up?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is worth asking for deliberately rather than hoping it happens. A tutor who has taught both halves understands why Extended Mathematics content matters for Higher Level Physics, and what changes in the marking once criterion descriptors replace mark schemes. Continuity also saves most of a term of getting to know a student. The thing to check is the tutor's own horizon: if they expect to leave Mumbai within the year, a Year 10 student is better off starting with somebody who will still be here in DP1.

faqs.question: Will a tutor have the school's own worksheets or past internal papers?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anybody who claims otherwise. School-set materials belong to the school, and a tutor circulating them is doing something that could cause your child real trouble. What a good tutor does have is the published syllabus, past board papers, the official assessment criteria and mark schemes, and years of experience of what examiners actually reward. That is more than enough to work with. Work set by the school arrives at the session inside your child's own folder, which is exactly how it should arrive.

sections.heading: How we match a home tutor to a Children's Academy family in Mumbai
paragraphs: A request for an IB and IGCSE home tutor for Children s Academy International students in Mumbai is treated as two questions, not one. The first is which course your child is actually entered for, by campus and by subject. The second is who can reach your gate on a weekday evening and keep doing it until March. Both get answered before a name is sent to you, because getting either one wrong wastes a term.

The first question is less obvious than it sounds. Children's Academy International School sits inside a group that runs more than one campus in Mumbai, and international streams change pathway and subject options between cohorts. A child in Year 9 at one campus and a child in Year 9 at another can be on different boards with different coursework obligations. So we ask for three things in writing: the campus, the board printed on the exercise book or the entry confirmation, and the subject option form your child filled in. If you do not have those, your first job is to get them from the school office, not from us.

The second question is pure logistics and we treat it as seriously as the academics. We take the pool of verified tutors who have taught the relevant board and subject, cut it to those whose own home is within a dependable evening reach of your building, and look at teaching record inside what remains. You then get two or three names with the corridor written against each, you call them yourself, and nobody visits until you have spoken to them.

The first visit is a working hour at your table with the child's last marked work open. By the end of it the tutor should be able to tell you which subjects are genuinely at risk, which are merely untidy, and what the next four visits will cover. You get that in writing the same night. If our honest view is that your child needs one subject fixed rather than the three you asked about, we will say so rather than sell you a timetable.

sections.heading: Two boards under one roof: establishing what your child is actually entered for
paragraphs: This is the single most useful thing on this page, so it comes early. International Baccalaureate (IB) programmes and the International General Certificate of Secondary Education are different systems with different assessment logic, and a school offering both will have children of the same age sitting under each. The International Baccalaureate runs the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and the Diploma Programme (DP); IGCSE is offered by Cambridge International Education and by Pearson Edexcel, each with its own subject codes. A tutor who assumes the wrong one will teach the wrong exam technique with total confidence.

Establish the pathway in three checks. Look at what is printed on the front of the exercise book or the school's subject outline: a Cambridge or Edexcel syllabus code means IGCSE, while MYP criteria labelled A to D mean the Middle Years Programme. Look at how the last report expressed the grade: a criterion-based level is MYP, a percentage or a letter grade against a syllabus is usually IGCSE. Then confirm it with the school. The coordinator or the examinations officer is the only reliable source for the entry, the series and the subject options, and no tutor and no website should be your authority on that.

The reason to be fussy is that the next decision depends on it. A child finishing IGCSE Years 9-11 and moving into the Diploma Programme faces a jump in independent writing and in deadline management that catches strong students out. A child already in MYP Year 4 or 5 is being assessed against criteria rather than a syllabus, and revision that ignores the criteria will not move the level. Requests that arrive worded as all IB and IGCSE subjects IGCSE Years 9-11 tutor Mumbai therefore get a follow-up question, because the phrase covers at least three different jobs.

An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai who works with families from a school running both systems is used to this and should ask you the same questions we do in the first five minutes. If a tutor does not ask which board, which year and which options before quoting you an hour, that is information about the tutor.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, Core and Extended, and the assessments underneath each
paragraphs: Subject choice at a school running both systems is where families make decisions they cannot easily reverse, and most of them are made in a rush around an option form. At IGCSE, several subjects are offered at two tiers, and the Core or Extended decision in Mathematics is the one that follows a student furthest: the tier a child takes shapes which Diploma Programme Mathematics course is realistic two years later. At Diploma level the Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) split is the equivalent fork, and three HL subjects chosen to look impressive is a heavier week than three chosen to match how the child actually works.

Underneath the subject names sits the assessment load, which is what families consistently underestimate. Diploma subjects each carry an Internal Assessment (IA), and alongside them sit the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK), all with their own school deadlines. The Middle Years Programme has its criterion-based tasks and the personal project. Some IGCSE subjects carry coursework or practical components and some do not. Add them up before choosing, because a combination that is academically sensible can still produce three major drafts due in the same fortnight.

This is what all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai can usefully cover actually means in practice: not every subject at once, but the two or three where the assessment load and the child's weakest skill overlap. A student who writes slowly should not be carrying two essay-heavy Higher Level subjects and an Extended Essay without support in place from the start of the year. A student strong in Mathematics and weak in written reflection needs help with the IA write-up rather than with the mathematics inside it.

What nobody should take from a page like this one is the structure itself. The IB revises subject guides on its own cycle, Cambridge and Pearson revise syllabuses on theirs, and schools change their option blocks between cohorts. Get the current component list, the tier definitions and the deadline calendar from the relevant subject guide and from your coordinator, and treat any number you read online about weightings or paper lengths as out of date until the school confirms it.
bullets: Core or Extended at IGCSE shapes which DP Mathematics course is realistic

sections.heading: Which Mumbai corridors families commute from, and what that does to a 6pm slot
paragraphs: Children's Academy International School draws most heavily from the Western Suburbs, and the commute pattern there is north and south along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway rather than across the city. Families in Malad East, Kandivali East, Borivali, Goregaon, Dahisar and Charkop are on the same spine, and Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made that spine far more usable in the evening than Link Road alone ever was. Tutors are matched along it: a tutor living in Borivali will hold a weekly slot in Kandivali East for a year, and will struggle to hold one in Chembur past November.

Beyond that spine the city behaves differently in each direction, and we cover all of it. In South Mumbai the distances are short and the evening signals at Peddar Road and Haji Ali are slow, so families in Tardeo, Parel, Worli and Marine Lines are matched within the island, helped now by the Coastal Road and by Metro Line 3. In the Central Suburbs, Powai and Chandivali have no station of their own and are reached by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar along JVLR, with the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway serving everything from Kurla upward and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road carrying tutors across.

The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund West on the Central and Harbour lines, with the Eastern Freeway making the trip down to South Mumbai quicker than the map suggests. Navi Mumbai is matched node to node, because Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel sit a short drive from one another on Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines and Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 alongside. The Atal Setu has made the crossing from the island city real, but we would not build a year-long weekday slot on it. Thane follows Pokhran Road, Majiwada and the long Ghodbunder Road run out to Kasarvadavali, and Thane tutors cover Thane.

All of which is why travel time, not distance, decides the shortlist. A search for IB and IGCSE tutors near me Mumbai returns names with no idea which side of the Sea Link anybody lives on, and that single omission is what turns a promising first month into a tutor asking to move to Sunday mornings. Mumbai, Maharashtra is a city where eight kilometres can cost forty minutes at the wrong hour, so we ask for your building name before we ask for the target grade. An IB and IGCSE home tutor for Children s Academy International students in Mumbai has to make the same trip fifty times, and the fiftieth one is the test.

sections.heading: The school's calendar and reporting rhythm, and reading it honestly
paragraphs: The rhythm at a Mumbai school running both systems is predictable in shape even when the dates move. A settling term, then interim feedback, then a cluster of internal assessments and mocks, then parent-teacher conferences, then the stretch where coursework and Internal Assessment deadlines land close together, then the external series. Families notice the external series and underestimate the deadline stretch, which is the part that actually determines the reports.

Reports from a school like this one can arrive in two languages at once, and parents are rarely told that. A Middle Years Programme subject reports a criterion level with a descriptor; an IGCSE subject reports a grade or percentage against a syllabus. The two are not comparable and should never be averaged in your head. Read the descriptor rather than the number: a criterion comment about communicating reasoning is a writing instruction, and it is more useful to a tutor than the level beside it. Ask your tutor after a month what the school's comments are consistently pointing at, across subjects. The pattern is usually one skill, not six.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We are not affiliated with Children's Academy International School, we hold no endorsement from it or from any other school mentioned here, and we do not guarantee grades. Naming the school is context so that families searching for it can find a tutor who understands the pathway question. Our tutors do not speak to schools on a family's behalf, do not name individual teachers in their session notes, and do not comment on school staffing.

What a tutor should do is work to the school's own paperwork. The task sheet the teacher issued, the rubric attached to it, and the teacher's written feedback on the last piece are the three documents that matter, and they beat any generic revision guide. If you can put those three things on the table for the first visit, the tutor can start from where the school already is instead of spending two sessions guessing. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai works best when it is unglamorously aligned with what the school asked for.

sections.heading: Home tuition in Mumbai first, then online, then a deliberate hybrid
paragraphs: An IB and IGCSE home tutor for Children s Academy International students in Mumbai is the lead booking here because most of the work is paperwork the student has to be sitting in front of. A task sheet, a rubric, a marked draft and a half-finished Internal Assessment plan spread across a dining table can all be seen at once, and a tutor can put a finger on the criterion and then on the sentence that fails to meet it. On a shared screen the student sees whichever document is on top.

The honest costs are travel and commitment. A tutor's evening journey is part of what you are paying for, which narrows who can reach you and on which day. Missed visits are hard to move because the slot after yours belongs to a family nearby. And the household has to supply a table, an hour and an open door, which in a flat with a younger child is an adult decision rather than a tutor's request.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai is genuinely the better option in four situations, and we will tell you when we see one: no verified specialist for that subject lives within sane reach of your node, the family is travelling, the child is unwell, or the external papers are a fortnight away and travel has become too expensive. What is lost online is small and real, mostly the pause before an answer and the ability to rotate a page and say read that line again.

Hybrid is where families carrying several Internal Assessments usually end up, and it works much better when planned than when drifted into. One weekly visit at the table for marking and planning, plus one short call before a draft is submitted, covers both the thinking and the deadline. Agree the pattern in week one. If a tutor booked for weekly home classes starts proposing calls instead, that is a travel problem and it is a week-three conversation rather than a week-twelve one.

sections.heading: What is checked before a tutor reaches your gate in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Five things, before any name reaches you. Government photo identity. An address proof that confirms the corridor the tutor claimed, because a tutor who says Kandivali and lives in Vasai will be late from February onward. A documented record of teaching the specific board and subject. A subject conversation with somebody who has read the relevant papers or guides. And references from families the tutor has worked with in Mumbai. That is the shortlist for an IB and IGCSE home tutor for Children s Academy International students in Mumbai, and it removes the obvious problems rather than certifying a person.

We also check board-specific experience rather than accepting a general claim. Diploma Programme Chemistry and IGCSE Chemistry are not the same teaching job, and a tutor comfortable with one may be guessing at the other. Where a tutor has strong technique in one system and limited exposure to the other, we say so on the shortlist and let you decide, because for some families technique matters more than coverage and for others the reverse is true.

Then there are checks only you can make, and they take one call and one session. Ask which year groups the tutor's last three students were in and what specifically changed. Ask the tutor to mark one of your child's returned pieces while you listen, and notice whether the rubric gets mentioned at all. Sit within earshot of the first hour. Be wary of anybody offering a guaranteed grade, because nothing stands behind that sentence. The best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai for a child who writes fluently but misses the criteria may be the most pedantic person on your list rather than the most reassuring.

At the door, two checks on the first visit. The person who arrives is the person in the profile we sent, and the name entered in the gate register matches. If a substitute ever turns up without prior notice, that is not a scheduling detail, and we want to know the same day.

sections.heading: How does a tutor work alongside your child's teachers rather than against them?
paragraphs: By teaching the school's method first and offering any alternative second. A tutor who tells a child that her teacher's approach is wrong has created a problem the child cannot solve, because she still has to submit work to that teacher. The rule our tutors work to is simple: the school's method is the one that gets practised for assessment, and a different technique is introduced as a second tool only once the first is secure.

The same restraint applies to assessed work, and on this there is no room for interpretation. A tutor does not draft, rewrite, restructure or supply content for an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a personal project or any piece of coursework. The IB has academic honesty requirements and the examination boards have their own rules on candidate authenticity, and a student whose submitted work is not her own is risking far more than a grade. What a tutor legitimately does is ask questions about the student's own draft, point at the criterion the draft has not met, teach the skill that gap needs, and hand the work back for the student to fix herself. A good tutor leaves fingerprints on the student's ability and none on the page.

Practically, alignment looks like this. The tutor reads the task sheet and the rubric before planning the session. The tutor uses the teacher's written feedback as the agenda rather than inventing one. If the school is running a mock in a fortnight, the plan bends towards it. If the school's deadline calendar puts two drafts in the same week, the tutor says so and reorders the work instead of adding to it. And where a tutor genuinely disagrees with how something has been marked, the message goes to the parent in plain language, for the parent to raise with the school if they choose. The tutor does not become a second voice in the child's academic life competing with the first.

Our tutors also keep the school out of their notes in one specific sense: no individual teacher is named, praised or criticised in a written session note. There is a practical reason beyond manners. Those notes get forwarded, screenshotted and quoted, and a sentence written casually about a named teacher can damage a relationship the family depends on for predicted grades and references. The note describes what the child did and what comes next. That is all a note needs to do. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families rely on is useful in proportion to how little friction they create with the school.

sections.heading: What should progress look like by the next Mumbai reporting cycle?
paragraphs: At four weeks, process rather than grades. The markers worth watching are whether your child reads the rubric before starting a piece, whether drafts now get planned instead of begun, and whether she can say in her own words which criterion her last piece missed. Grades at a school reporting on criteria or on syllabus assessments move across a reporting cycle, not across a month, and anyone claiming otherwise in week two is guessing.

By one full term, you should see a report comment that shifts, and your tutor should be able to name the specific skill that moved and the evidence for it. Across one external cycle, expect the gap between predicted and achieved to narrow, and expect the more durable change: a student who manages a deadline calendar without being chased. For a child moving from IGCSE Years 9-11 into the Diploma Programme, that habit is worth more than any individual subject gain, because the Diploma punishes poor scheduling harder than it punishes gaps in content.

The limits are worth stating plainly. We do not guarantee grades. A tutor who promises a particular result in the next series is describing a sales technique rather than your child. Attendance, whether anything happens between visits, and where in the course you start all cap what is possible: a Year 9 beginning after the monsoon has room to rebuild skills, while a Diploma student starting three months before papers is triaging, and we would rather say that in the first call.

If it is not working, raise it at visit three or four. Write to us with what you have actually seen: the hour is mostly conversation, the slot keeps moving, your child goes quiet when he arrives, nothing gets marked. We talk to the tutor first, because early mismatches are often about pace, slot or room rather than ability. If the person is genuinely wrong for your child, we arrange a replacement from the same shortlist without you starting a new search, and the diagnostic and notes go across so visit one is not a repeat of work already done.

sections.heading: Getting started: what to have ready before the first home classes session
paragraphs: One message to begin, with six things in it: the campus, your child's year group, the board printed on the entry confirmation or exercise book, the subject options, two evenings that are genuinely free, and your area and building name. If you are unsure about the board, say so and send a photograph of the last report instead. We would rather spend a message resolving that than send you a Diploma specialist for a Middle Years Programme student.

Before the first visit, put four documents on the cleared table: the most recent marked piece with the teacher's comments on it, the task sheet and rubric for whatever is currently due, the last report, and the school's deadline calendar if the coordinator has issued one. Those four give a tutor more in ten minutes than an hour of discussion. Add the tutor's name to your society's visitor list a day ahead, because the first visit is the one that gets held at the barrier.

The session itself is a working diagnostic. The tutor reads the marked piece, asks your child to talk through one answer or one paragraph, sets a short timed task, and marks it in front of her against the actual criteria rather than against a general impression. It closes with a verdict in plain words: which subjects are at risk, which skill is costing the most across all of them, and what the next four visits will do about it. That reaches you in writing the same night.

After that it should be dull and regular. Same evening, same table, a written note every week, and a short conversation at the door about what went wrong that day and what happens before the next visit. All IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Mumbai parents book through us run on that pattern. If you have doubts at visit three, say so then. Changing tutors costs you one conversation, and a term of being polite about an hour that is not working costs considerably more.

faqs.question: How do we confirm which board and which campus our child is actually registered under?
faqs.answer: Ask the school office or the programme coordinator in writing, and keep the reply. Three documents settle it: the entry or registration confirmation, the subject option form your child submitted, and the current subject outline the teacher issued. A Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel syllabus code on any of them means IGCSE; criteria labelled A to D mean the Middle Years Programme. Do not rely on what an older sibling did, because option blocks and pathways change between cohorts, and do not rely on a tutor's assumption. We ask for this before matching precisely because getting it wrong costs a term of the wrong exam technique.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Internal Assessment without crossing an academic honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clearer than most families expect. A tutor may explain the criteria, ask questions about the student's own draft, point out where the draft fails to meet a criterion, teach the underlying skill, and discuss structure in general terms. A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure or supply content, and may not generate the data or the analysis. The practical test is whether the words and decisions on the submitted page are the student's. If a tutor offers to tidy up a draft for you, decline, because the IB and the examination boards treat authenticity seriously and the student carries the consequence.

faqs.question: Our child does IGCSE now and moves to the Diploma Programme next year. Same tutor or a new one?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the tutor has genuinely taught the Diploma, and you should ask directly rather than assume. Continuity is valuable: a tutor who already knows how your child works saves a term of discovery. But Diploma subjects demand independent writing, research and deadline management that IGCSE does not, and a tutor who has only taught IGCSE will be learning alongside your child. We check Diploma teaching experience separately from IGCSE experience for this reason. Where a tutor is strong on one and thin on the other, we tell you on the shortlist and let you weigh continuity against expertise.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Five factors, and any page quoting you a figure is not being straight. Board and level matter, because a verified Diploma Higher Level specialist is a narrower pool than a general school-subject tutor. Subject scarcity matters, and some Diploma subjects have very few experienced teachers in any one corridor. Travel distance matters, because the evening a tutor spends on the Western Express Highway is time nobody can teach in. Session length and weekly frequency matter. So does documented experience with the specific board rather than the subject in general. Ask any tutor to justify a rate against those five and listen to the answer.

faqs.question: Should a parent be at home while the session runs?
faqs.answer: Someone adult should be in the flat, and the useful distance is the next room with the door open. You will hear whether your child is talking or being talked at, whether the rubric gets mentioned, and whether the tutor explains or merely corrects, and none of that appears in a written note. Sitting at the table changes how a teenager behaves and usually makes the hour less productive. For the first three or four visits we would ask a parent to be present in the house and at the door for the handover afterwards, after which many families step back entirely.

faqs.question: Will the tutor contact the school or the subject teacher directly?
faqs.answer: No. Our tutors do not contact schools, teachers or coordinators on a family's behalf, and they do not name individual teachers in their written session notes. Anything a tutor thinks the school should hear goes to you, in plain language, and you decide whether to raise it. There are two reasons. The relationship with the school belongs to the family, not to a tutor, and predicted grades and references depend on it. And a casual written remark about a named teacher has a way of travelling further than intended. The tutor's job stops at your door.

faqs.question: Core or Extended for IGCSE Mathematics? Can a tutor advise on that?
faqs.answer: A tutor can give you useful evidence, but the decision belongs to you and the school. What a tutor can do is set a few Extended-tier questions, watch how your child handles them, and tell you honestly whether the gap is a few weeks of work or a structural one. What the school knows, and a tutor does not, is how this cohort has been taught and what the department expects. The reason to take it seriously is that the tier shapes which Diploma Mathematics course is realistic later, so confirm the implications with the coordinator before the option form goes back.

faqs.question: What happens if our tutor's method contradicts what the teacher taught in class?
faqs.answer: The school's method wins for assessed work, and a good tutor says so out loud. A child told her teacher is wrong is stuck, because she still submits to that teacher. So our tutors teach the school's approach until it is secure, then offer an alternative as a second tool if it genuinely helps. Where a tutor believes something has been marked unfairly, the observation comes to you rather than to your child, and you choose whether to raise it. If a tutor repeatedly undermines the classroom in front of your child, tell us, because that is a match we will change.

faqs.question: Which months are hardest for a Mumbai family running both boards at once?
faqs.answer: The stretch where internal deadlines stack, which usually sits between the mock cycle and the external series rather than during either. Families watch the external dates and get ambushed by a fortnight holding an Internal Assessment draft, a coursework submission and two mocks. If you have children on both pathways, those fortnights rarely align, so build one shared calendar for the household. The quiet window after the monsoon settles is the best time to start a weekly tutor, because there is room to build habits before anything is at stake.

sections.heading: How a request for a DAIS tutor becomes a Mumbai shortlist
paragraphs: Every request for an IB IGCSE tutor for Dhirubhai Ambani International School BKC students in Mumbai arrives looking roughly the same: a year group, a subject, a deadline and a pin location. The useful information is in what parents leave out. What time the child actually walks back in through the door, whether a sibling is using the same room for an online class, how long the drive from Bandra Kurla Complex to your gate takes at half past five on a weekday, and whether the subject is in real trouble or just boring the child. We ask for those four things before opening a single profile, because a tutor who is excellent on Chemistry assessment criteria and arrives at a quarter past eight on a school night is not a match. He is a cancellation two weeks away.

The shortlist itself is deliberately short. Three names with a reason attached to each is more useful to a parent than thirty profiles sorted by a star rating. For a Year 10 student taking Cambridge Additional Mathematics alongside Coordinated Sciences, we look for someone who has taught the Extended tier and can describe how the question style shifts between the written papers, not someone who tutors school mathematics generally. For a first-year Diploma Programme student, we look for a tutor who has supervised an Internal Assessment (IA) in that exact subject, because the draft-and-feedback cycle is where a large part of the final mark is decided, and a tutor who has never read the current criteria for it will coach the content well and misread the write-up completely.

What happens next is ordinary and we keep it ordinary on purpose. You speak to the shortlisted tutor on the phone before anyone comes to the house. Ask what the last three students they taught were sitting, and what went wrong in each case. Then one paid session, at your dining table or online, with a single task set in advance: read the child's last test paper and describe the pattern in the lost marks. If the answer comes back as more practice is needed, that is a weak answer and you should say so on the call. If it comes back as she sets the equations up correctly and drops the last two marks on every long question because she stops writing units, you have found the right person and the rest is scheduling.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Dhirubhai Ambani International School, or with any other school named anywhere on this page. We do not guarantee grades, and no tutor on the platform is permitted to promise a specific mark to win the work. What we do control is how good the shortlist is, how fast it gets rebuilt when it is wrong, and whether the tutor who turns up is the tutor you spoke to.

sections.heading: Which programme is your child actually in, IGCSE or the Diploma Programme?
paragraphs: Families at a school that runs both pathways are usually at one of three stages, and each stage wants a different kind of tutor. Years 9 to 11 sit the International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) under Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, with Core and Extended tiers to choose between. Years 11 and 12 sit the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) decisions and three core requirements running underneath. Below that, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) marks work against its own criteria, which look nothing like a Cambridge grade boundary.

The confusion that costs families the most is treating the boundary between those stages as a continuation. It is not. An IGCSE grade is an exam grade with a small amount of coursework behind it, and preparation is largely about question technique under timed conditions. A Diploma Programme grade combines external papers with internally assessed work that is drafted, supervised and marked against published criteria months before the exam, and then moderated. A student who was comfortable in Year 11 can slide badly in the first DP term, not because the content got harder overnight but because nobody told her the work is now partly a writing project. A tutor who only ever taught IGCSE will keep drilling past papers while the Physics IA proposal sits untouched.

Parents sometimes type the entire thing into a search box. The phrase 'all IB and IGCSE subjects IGCSE Years 9-11 tutor Mumbai' is clumsy as English, but it describes the real request accurately: one person who understands both boards well enough to tell you when the tiers and levels your child picked are the wrong shape for what she wants to study later. That is the conversation to have in Year 9, not in Year 11 when a change means dropping a subject.

One warning about structure. Do not take paper counts, component weightings, durations or mark totals from a tutoring site, including this one. Cambridge and Pearson revise their syllabuses on their own cycles, and the IB revises subject guides by cohort, so the shape of an assessment can differ between your older child's year and your younger one's. Read the current subject guide for the syllabus your child is actually registered against, and put the structural questions to the school's examinations officer or the Diploma Programme coordinator, who hold the version that applies to that cohort.

sections.heading: Subject choice across two boards: HL, SL, Core and Extended
paragraphs: Subject choice is where tutoring either saves a year or wastes one. A family wanting all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai can carry alone is asking for something nobody honest sells: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and English A: Literature are not the same job, and the person who is strong at one is rarely the person you want for the other. What a single good tutor can do is sit with the option form and work backwards from where the child wants to apply. Engineering in the United States wants a particular mathematics route. Medicine in the United Kingdom wants Chemistry at Higher Level and usually Biology. Economics at a competitive university cares which mathematics course appears on the transcript.

At IGCSE the two decisions that matter most are tier and breadth. Extended Mathematics keeps the full grade range open and is the normal route for anyone heading towards a quantitative Diploma Programme course. Coordinated Sciences covers three sciences in a smaller timetable footprint, which suits a student loading up on languages, but separate Physics, Chemistry and Biology give a deeper base for Higher Level science later. Cambridge subjects such as Business Studies and Computer Science carry coursework or practical components, and those components are precisely where a home tutor is useful, because they are done over weeks at a desk rather than in an exam hall.

In the Diploma Programme every subject carries an Internal Assessment (IA), and they do not look alike. Physics and Chemistry want an investigation with a defensible research question and real uncertainty analysis. Mathematics wants an exploration, which is a short piece of mathematical writing and the single most commonly underestimated task in DP1. Economics wants commentaries built on recent news articles, which means the student has to be reading something other than the textbook from the first month. History wants a formal investigation with source evaluation. On top of all of that sit the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK), which are scheduled by the school and ignored by students until they collide with mock exams.

When a parent asks for a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai, what we usually build is two people rather than one: a sciences-and-mathematics tutor and a humanities-or-languages tutor, with the heavier one coming weekly and the lighter one fortnightly. It costs less than four separate single-subject tutors and it stops the week filling up with lessons at the expense of actual independent study, which is the thing the exam is measuring.

sections.heading: Where do Mumbai tutors travel from, and what does that cost you in time?
paragraphs: The pool we draw on for an IB IGCSE home tutor for Dhirubhai Ambani International School BKC students in Mumbai is not concentrated near the campus. It is spread across the whole of Mumbai, Maharashtra, and the only question that matters for a standing weekly slot is how far the tutor has to come at the worst hour of the day. In South Mumbai, families in Cuffe Parade, Colaba, Walkeshwar, Tardeo and Worli are served by tutors who live on the island, because a short distance here is a long journey: eight kilometres from Worli to Colaba can still cost forty minutes at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals. Matching along the line works and matching across it does not: Khar to Santacruz is nothing, Malad to Kandivali is nothing, and Bandra to Andheri at six in the evening is an argument waiting to happen. sections.heading: The BKC school calendar and the three months that hurt
paragraphs: Bandra Kurla Complex has become the densest cluster of international schooling in the city. Dhirubhai Ambani International School sits there alongside the American School of Bombay and Ascend International School, which is why the evening traffic around the complex is what it is and why so many tutoring requests from Bandra, Khar West, Worli and Santacruz West turn out to be for children who spend their day in the same few blocks. Families commute in from the island along the Bandra-Worli Sea Link, down the Western Express Highway from Andheri and Goregaon, and across the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road from Chembur and Powai, which means the child who gets home at four and the child who gets home at six are often classmates.

The rhythm of the year is what a tutor has to plan around, and it is broadly shared across Mumbai's international schools. The academic year opens after the summer break, settles through the monsoon, and produces its first real reporting moment in the autumn term, which is usually when parents discover that a subject is not going well. Mock examinations for IGCSE candidates fall in the cooler months, Diploma Programme internal assessment drafts queue up through the same window, and the final coursework deadlines arrive in the first months of the calendar year, just as revision should be starting. The May examination session then compresses everything that was postponed. The months that hurt are the autumn reporting window, the mock season and the fortnight when coursework deadlines and revision overlap.

A school with a reporting calendar this structured gives you something valuable: written evidence, in the teacher's own words, of where the marks are going. Use it. The comment that says the conclusion does not follow from the evidence presented is worth more to a tutor than the grade printed above it, and it is more useful than a parent's own summary of the problem. Bring the report, the last two marked assessments and, if there is one, the subject teacher's feedback on an internal assessment draft to the first session, and the tutor can skip the diagnostic guesswork entirely.

Two limits on what any tutoring platform can tell you. IB Gram has no relationship with the school, no inside knowledge of its internal deadlines, and no view of any individual teacher's marking, so anything specific to a particular cohort has to come from the school itself. And the exact dates shift year to year. Ask the examinations officer or the programme coordinator for the current calendar rather than working from a tutor's recollection of last year, especially if your child is sitting the November session rather than May.

sections.heading: Is home tuition in Mumbai better than online for a DAIS student?
paragraphs: For most Years 9 to 11 students, yes, and the reason has nothing to do with teaching quality. Most families who ask for an IB IGCSE home tutor for Dhirubhai Ambani International School BKC students in Mumbai mean somebody at the dining table on a fixed evening, and for a fifteen-year-old that physical presence is what makes the hour happen at all. A tutor in the room sees the exercise book, notices the three questions quietly skipped, and cannot be minimised behind a game. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai also solves a scheduling problem: the slot is in the house, so there is no second journey after a school day that already involved the Western Express Highway.

The honest cost of IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai arrangements is the travel. A tutor crossing the city in the evening peak is paying for that crossing with their own time, and it shows up as a narrower choice of slots, a higher rate, or both. It also makes cancellations contagious: one flooded underpass in July and the session is gone, because there is no fallback. Families who book all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes Mumbai evenings can genuinely sustain tend to be the ones who accepted a tutor from twenty minutes away over a slightly better-qualified tutor from an hour away.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai earns their place in three specific situations. The first is a scarce subject: Higher Level Economics, Psychology, Global Politics, Computer Science or a second language has a thin pool in any one suburb, and the right specialist may simply live in Thane or Navi Mumbai. The second is intensive work close to exams, where four short sessions a week are worth more than one long one and nobody can travel four times. The third is coursework feedback, where a shared screen and a marked-up document beat sitting side by side. The trade-off is real: online needs a wired-in student, a working camera, a quiet corner and a parent willing to notice when attention drifts.

Hybrid is what most families settle into by the second term, and it is a sensible default rather than a compromise. One home session a week to set the agenda, hold the child to account and read the body language, plus one or two short online sessions for drilling, doubt-clearing and draft review. During mock season the online half scales up without anyone adding a commute. Through the monsoon it keeps the week intact when the roads do not cooperate. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Mumbai families keep for two years is almost always one who agreed to work this way.

Travel narrows your slot choice and makes monsoon cancellations harder to absorb
Online opens scarce Higher Level subjects across Thane and Navi Mumbai
Short, frequent online sessions beat one long one near exams
Hybrid holds the week together when roads or deadlines go wrong

sections.heading: What is checked before a tutor is sent to your flat in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Before any IB IGCSE tutor for Dhirubhai Ambani International School BKC students in Mumbai appears on a shortlist, three things are verified and none of them is a certificate scan. Identity first: government photo identification matched against the name and the phone number, because a tutor who sends a substitute to your home is the single worst outcome in this business. Then teaching history: which board, which syllabus, which year groups, and the names of the papers or components they have actually prepared students for. A tutor who says IB Maths and cannot immediately distinguish Analysis and Approaches from Applications and Interpretation has not taught the Diploma Programme recently. Then a subject conversation with someone who knows the syllabus, built around a real marked script rather than a quiz.

There are checks only you can do, and they are the ones that catch the remaining problems. Watch the first session rather than leaving the house. Listen for whether the tutor is explaining or performing. Ask, at the end, what the plan is for the next four weeks and what they expect the child to do alone between sessions; a tutor with no answer to the second half of that question is planning to do the work for her. Ask what they will not take on, because a tutor who claims every subject in both boards at every level is describing a sales position rather than a teaching one.

Be wary of anyone who offers a guaranteed grade, or who talks about a guaranteed result in a first phone call. Nobody can see the question paper. What an experienced tutor can do is tell you which marks are currently reachable and what has to change for them to be reached, and that prediction gets more accurate as they see more of the child's written work. We do not guarantee grades and we do not allow tutors on the platform to advertise one. A tutor who promises a specific number is either inexperienced or counting on you not checking in March.

Academic honesty is the other thing to settle before the first session, and it matters more on both boards than most families expect. A tutor may teach the skills an Internal Assessment needs, read a draft and point at a weak research question. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply the data or rewrite paragraphs. Internal assessments are submitted with an authenticity declaration, and the consequences of breaching it land on the student, not on the tutor. Any tutor who is vague about that line should not be in your house.
bullets: Government photo identification checked against the name and phone number
Board, syllabus and year groups confirmed by paper, not by claim
Subject conversation run on a real marked script, not a quiz
You watch session one and ask what the child does between sessions
Coursework help stops at feedback; the writing stays the student's own

sections.heading: How a Mumbai home tutor works alongside school teachers, not against them
paragraphs: The most common way private tutoring fails a student at a strong international school is not weak teaching. It is a second syllabus. A tutor who starts from his own notes, his own notation and his own order of topics gives a fifteen-year-old two versions of every method and no way to choose between them. The child then writes the tutor's solution in a school assessment, loses marks for a step the department expects to see, and concludes that she is bad at the subject. A good home tutor opens the school exercise book first and teaches inside the conventions already in it: the same symbols, the same layout, the same sequence.

That alignment has to be concrete. The tutor should know which textbook or digital resource the department uses, where the class currently is in the scheme of work, and what the next assessment covers. If a Chemistry teacher insists on state symbols in every equation, the tutor insists on them too. If a Mathematics department marks method before answer, the tutor stops accepting correct answers with no working. On the written side, the tutor should be reading the subject teacher's actual comments on returned work rather than inventing a theory about the problem. The teacher has seen thirty scripts from the cohort and knows exactly what the class is getting wrong.

There is a boundary a tutor should not cross, and it is worth saying plainly. The tutor does not correct the school. Where a tutor genuinely believes something has been marked oddly, the move is to show the student the published criteria and encourage her to ask her teacher, not to tell her the teacher is wrong. Children repeat these conversations in class, and a student who arrives believing her department is incompetent has lost the single most important relationship she has for that subject. The tutor's job is to make the teacher's instruction land, not to replace it.

Used this way, a tutor fills gaps a classroom cannot. A class of twenty-five cannot stop for the one student who never properly learnt index laws three years ago, and that is exactly the hole a home tutor can close in four quiet sessions. A classroom cannot give an hour of silent, supervised past-paper work with an adult reading over your shoulder. A classroom cannot sit with one student and interrogate a weak Internal Assessment research question until it becomes answerable. Those are the jobs worth paying for, and they are additive rather than competitive.
bullets: Teach inside the school's notation and layout, never a parallel method
Know where the class is in the scheme of work before each session
Read the subject teacher's written comments instead of guessing the problem
Send disagreements about marking back to the teacher through the student
Spend tutor time on gaps and supervised practice a classroom cannot provide

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at grades at all. What changes first is behaviour: the child starts attempting the long questions instead of leaving them, brings her own list of doubts to the session, and stops saying she does not know where to begin. The tutor should by then be able to tell you in one sentence what the specific weakness is, in the language of the subject rather than in general terms. Not weak in Physics, but she can quote the definitions and cannot apply them to an unfamiliar situation, which is a different problem with a different fix. If after a month nobody can describe the problem precisely, the diagnosis never happened.

At one term, marks on school assessments should start moving, though rarely evenly and rarely in a straight line. Internal assessment work is where the clearest gains usually show first, because a drafted piece responds to feedback in a way that an exam technique does not. Written subjects move more slowly than calculation subjects, because the underlying skill is reading and structuring an argument and that takes longer to build than a method. A student who was failing is more likely to show a jump than a student already sitting comfortably in the middle, where moving up a band is a much finer piece of work.

At one exam cycle you find out what actually held. Some things that do not improve on any timetable are worth naming honestly. A child who will not do independent work between sessions will plateau, because one or two hours a week against a full syllabus is not enough on its own. A subject chosen against the child's grain stays hard whoever teaches it. A student carrying six subjects, an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and a sport has a time problem rather than a comprehension problem, and more tuition makes it worse. In that situation the right advice is to drop a commitment, which is not advice that sells lessons.

We do not guarantee grades and we would not trust anyone who did. What we will do is tell you when tutoring is the wrong tool. Sometimes the answer is a study-skills intervention rather than subject teaching, sometimes it is a conversation with the school about a learning-support assessment, and sometimes it is accepting that a Higher Level choice was a mistake and changing it while there is still time. A platform that only ever recommends more hours is not advising you.
bullets: Week four: behaviour and a precise diagnosis, not a better grade
One term: coursework responds fastest, written subjects move slowest
Mid-band students need finer work than students who are failing
No independent practice between sessions means a predictable plateau
Sometimes the honest recommendation is fewer commitments, not more hours

sections.heading: Booking an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Four pieces of information make the difference between a shortlist that fits and a week of wasted calls. The exact year group and board, written as the school writes it. The subject and, for the Diploma Programme, the level. Two or three time windows that genuinely work, allowing for the drive home. And your locality with the nearest landmark, because an IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai is matched on travel before anything else. If there is a report card or a marked paper, attach it. Nothing speeds up a match like the teacher's own sentence about what is going wrong.

The first session has a fixed shape and it is not a lesson. The tutor reads the most recent marked work, asks the child to attempt two or three questions unaided while watching how she starts them, and then talks to you for ten minutes about what the pattern is and what the next four weeks will cover. You should come out of it with a plan you could repeat to someone else, and the child should come out of it with one specific thing to do before the next session. A first session that is an hour of friendly revision has told you nothing.

People who search the phrase 'best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai' are usually asking something more practical than it sounds: which tutor will still be turning up in February. The answer is almost always the one whose journey is short enough to be boring, whose subject is genuinely theirs, and who was honest on the first call about what they could not do. So is the honest version of the question behind 'IB and IGCSE tutors near me Mumbai': near enough to be reliable, specialised enough to be useful.

If a tutor is not working out, say so in the first fortnight rather than the second month. There is no contract to exit and no notice period to serve. Tell us what specifically went wrong, because that sentence is what makes the replacement better: too fast, too passive, no structure, no written feedback, kept arriving late. We re-match within the same week where the subject pool allows it, and for scarce Higher Level subjects we will tell you honestly if the only realistic option is online.
bullets: Have the year group, board, subject and level written down exactly
Give two or three realistic time windows, not a general preference
Attach a report card or a recent marked paper if one exists

faqs.answer: Yes, and the practical limit is the tutor's own commute rather than willingness. faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and none of them is a fixed rate card. Board and level: Diploma Programme Higher Level costs more than IGCSE Core because the pool of people who can mark against current criteria is smaller. Subject scarcity: Mathematics and Physics tutors are everywhere, Higher Level Economics, Psychology and second languages are not. Travel distance and the hour of the day, which is the biggest single factor in Mumbai. Session length and frequency, where two short sessions usually cost more than one long one. And format, since online removes the travel component entirely. Ask each shortlisted tutor to quote on all of these rather than comparing a single number.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10 and wants Economics at Higher Level later. Can one tutor cover both stages?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and for Economics it is usually a good idea. IGCSE Economics and Diploma Programme Economics share enough of a conceptual base that continuity helps, and a tutor who already knows how your child argues on paper is worth a lot when the commentaries start. The thing to verify is that the tutor has actually supervised Diploma Programme commentaries recently, not just taught the content, because the marking is criteria-based and quite particular about the use of current news articles and diagrams. If the tutor has only IGCSE experience, plan to add or switch at the start of the first Diploma Programme year rather than mid-course.

faqs.question: Do we need a parent at home during the session, and where in the flat should it happen?
faqs.answer: Someone responsible should be at home, and the session should happen in a semi-open space rather than a bedroom. A dining table or a study with the door open works well: it is quiet enough to concentrate and visible enough that nobody is unsupervised. You do not need to sit in, and hovering tends to make a teenager perform rather than think. What helps is being within earshot for the first two or three sessions, then dropping back. Keep the room free of the television, the younger sibling's online class and the phone, and have the school textbook and exercise book already on the table.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out after three sessions. What happens?
faqs.answer: You tell us and we re-match, usually within the same week. There is no contract, no notice period and no obligation to continue with somebody your child has stopped talking to. The one thing we ask for is specifics, because a replacement chosen against a vague complaint tends to fail the same way. Too much talking and too little writing, no structure to the hour, no feedback on the work set, consistently late, or simply a personality mismatch are all useful and actionable. For a scarce Higher Level subject, re-matching can take a little longer and we will say so rather than sending a weaker fit to fill the slot.

faqs.question: Does online tuition really work for IGCSE Mathematics?
faqs.answer: It works well for some things and badly for others. Doubt-clearing, worked solutions, past-paper walkthroughs and marking feedback all transfer to a screen with no real loss, especially with a document camera or a tablet the student can write on. What does not transfer is supervised silent practice, which is where a lot of IGCSE Mathematics improvement actually comes from, and the tutor's ability to notice a student quietly skipping the questions she cannot start. For Years 9 to 11 we usually suggest one home session a week for accountability plus short online sessions for drilling, rather than going fully online.

faqs.question: We commute to BKC from Powai. Should the tutor be near the school or near us?
faqs.answer: Near you, always. The tutor comes to your home, not to the school gate, so the school's location affects only what time your child is free, not where the tutor should live. For Powai that means we look at Powai itself, Chandivali, Andheri East, Kanjurmarg, Ghatkopar and Vikhroli, because Powai has no railway station of its own and everything arrives by road along the Jogeshwari-Vikhroli Link Road or the Eastern Express Highway. A tutor who lives near Bandra Kurla Complex and would have to drive out to Hiranandani Gardens at seven in the evening is a worse bet than a Chandivali tutor ten minutes away.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week make sense during IGCSE mock season?
faqs.answer: For a single weak subject, two shorter sessions beat one long one, because the gap between them is where the practice happens. For two or three subjects under pressure at once, the honest answer is often to reduce rather than add: a student with five tuition slots a week has no time left to work alone, and solitary timed practice is what mock exams actually test. A workable mock-season pattern is one home session per weak subject, one short online review for each, and at least two evenings with no tuition at all. Protect those evenings even when the mock timetable looks frightening.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to Dhirubhai Ambani International School in any way?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation, partnership or arrangement with Dhirubhai Ambani International School, the American School of Bombay, Ascend International School or any other school mentioned on this page. We name schools only as local context, so that parents can see we understand the calendar and the commute their family deals with. We have no access to any school's internal deadlines, no view of any teacher's marking, and we do not speak to schools on a family's behalf. For anything official, including examination registration and coursework deadlines, the school's own office is the only reliable source.

faqs.question: Can we switch from home classes to online during the monsoon?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families should plan for it before July rather than improvising in it. Agree with the tutor at the outset that any session the weather cancels moves online the same evening instead of disappearing, and make sure the student has a device, a charged backup and a quiet corner ready so the switch takes two minutes. Mumbai loses a predictable number of evenings to waterlogging every year and the sessions nearest the exams are the ones most likely to go. Families who agreed on an online fallback in June keep their term intact; families who did not lose a fortnight.

faqs.question: Our building needs a gate pass for regular visitors. How is that arranged?
faqs.answer: You arrange it, and it is worth doing in the first week rather than after three arguments at the gate. Most Mumbai societies will issue a standing visitor pass or add a regular tutor to an approved-visitor list once a resident requests it in writing, and some ask for an identity document copy. Ask the tutor for the name as it appears on their identification so the register matches. Where a building insists on a fresh entry every visit, a fixed day and time makes it routine for the security desk. The small amount of paperwork removes a recurring reason for sessions to start fifteen minutes late.

faqs.question: What should we ask a tutor on the first phone call?
faqs.answer: Four questions, in this order. What were the last three students you taught sitting, and what went wrong for each of them? Which board and syllabus have you taught most recently, and can you name the papers or components? What will you expect my child to do between sessions? And what in this subject or level would you not take on? The answers tell you more than any qualification list. A tutor who answers the first question with specifics and the last one honestly is a tutor who has done the job. Vague answers to all four are the warning sign.

sections.heading: The IGCSE and IB Diploma pathway inside one Mumbai school
paragraphs: A family here deals with two assessment systems under one roof, and the switch between them is where most of the trouble starts. Cambridge IGCSE, taken across Years 9 to 11, is a terminal system. The grade comes from papers written at the end, in the May/June or October/November series, and a student who gets organised six weeks out can repair a mediocre year. Subjects are tiered: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits into Core and Extended, and the Extended tier is the one that keeps Higher Level Mathematics open in the Diploma Programme two years later.

The International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) works the other way round. A student takes six subjects, three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), plus the core: Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject is graded 1 to 7, the core contributes up to three bonus points, and 45 is the ceiling. A meaningful share of every subject grade is fixed long before the May examinations, in Internal Assessment (IA) work drafted in year one and finished in year two. No amount of revision repairs an IA that went in during January.

That structural difference is the real content of the Year 11 to Diploma Programme year one transition, and it catches strong students hardest. A student who scored well at IGCSE by revising late walks into DP1 with the same habit intact, then discovers in February that the Extended Essay supervisor wants a research question, the Theory of Knowledge teacher wants an exhibition commentary, and the Physics teacher wants a research design, all inside a fortnight. What is being examined at that point is scheduling at least as much as subject knowledge.

Tutoring across that join is therefore less about teaching new content than about changing how a student works. Useful support in Year 11 keeps the Extended tier and Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 on the table, because dropping either quietly closes doors at Higher Level. Useful support in DP1 gets the first Internal Assessment draft finished early, which buys room for everything that lands afterwards. Families who treat the two years as one continuous pathway, rather than two separate problems, spend far less on tuition overall.

sections.heading: Subject choice, Higher Level decisions and the internal assessment behind each one
paragraphs: Every Diploma Programme subject carries its own piece of internally assessed coursework, and those pieces are the quiet reason families call for a tutor. The sciences share one format: a single scientific investigation, around ten hours of work, marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and worth a fifth of the subject grade. Mathematics, in both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, carries an exploration marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Neither is rescued by last-minute effort, because both are graded on the thinking visible on the page.

The humanities and languages run on different clocks. History requires a historical investigation of roughly 2,200 words with an evaluation of sources section that most students underweight. Economics takes three commentaries of around 800 words, each pinned to a real news article and a different part of the syllabus. Language A students sit Paper 1 as guided textual analysis and Paper 2 as a comparative essay, and face an individual oral built on a global issue and two chosen texts, with an additional essay at Higher Level. Business Management, Psychology, Computer Science and Visual Arts each add their own coursework shape.

The IGCSE side is more familiar to most parents, but the choices still matter. Mathematics 0580 Extended, Additional Mathematics 0606, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, First Language English 0500, Economics 0455, Business Studies 0450 and Computer Science 0478 are the usual spine, with Coordinated Sciences 0654 taken by students who do not intend to carry three separate sciences. A Year 10 student who picks Core Mathematics because the Extended paper looks frightening may be making a Diploma Programme decision eighteen months before realising it.

A family wanting all IB and IGCSE subjects from one tutor in Mumbai should expect that to hold through Year 10 and break in DP1. A request for all IB and IGCSE subjects across IGCSE Years 9-11 tutoring in Mumbai is realistic, because the content is still broad and shallow. The same request at Higher Level is not. The honest answer at Diploma Programme level is usually two specialists, sometimes three, and a parent who insists on one generalist is buying thin coverage in half the timetable.

sections.heading: What the BKC school calendar does to a Mumbai tutoring year
paragraphs: To be plain about it before anything else: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Dhirubhai Ambani International School in any way. We have no access to its staff, its internal materials or its deadlines, and no tutor on this platform should ever claim otherwise. What we describe below is the ordinary public shape of an IB school year in Mumbai, Maharashtra, which parents already know from their own child's diary. Bandra Kurla Complex happens to hold several international schools within a few minutes of each other, including the American School of Bombay and Ascend International School, and families across all of them work to roughly the same rhythm.

That rhythm starts in June, in the monsoon, which is also when the first tuition requests of the year arrive. The term runs through to the Diwali break in October or November, with the first real assessments landing well before it. Diploma Programme year two mock examinations typically fall in January or February, Internal Assessment final submissions cluster in the same window, and the May examination session closes the whole thing out, with results in early July. IGCSE students in Year 11 sit the May/June series alongside them, so a household with two children can have both sets of pressure in the same fortnight.

The pressure points are predictable enough to plan a tutoring year around. September and October belong to the Extended Essay, because the first full draft and the Theory of Knowledge essay title selection both sit there for a May session cohort. November and December are when Internal Assessment drafts come back covered in supervisor comments and have to be rewritten properly. January and February are the worst month-and-a-half of the two years: mocks, final Internal Assessment submissions and university deadlines overlapping. March and April are pure examination technique, and by then a tutor should be marking past papers rather than teaching new content.

This is why starting tuition in January is usually a mistake, and why we say so to parents who ask in January. The highest-value months are the quiet ones. A tutor brought in during July or August of DP1 works on the Internal Assessment research question while there is still time to change it; the same tutor brought in during February is doing damage limitation on a draft that cannot now be redesigned. The Year 11 calendar rewards the same early start, because Cambridge IGCSE coursework and the Extended tier decision both arrive sooner than families expect.
