September to October: Extended Essay drafting and Theory of Knowledge essay titles
January to February: mocks, final Internal Assessments and university deadlines together

sections.heading: Home tutor, online or hybrid: which actually works for a BKC family?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default here and it is what most families ask for first. IB and IGCSE home tuition for Dhirubhai Ambani International School students in Mumbai usually means a tutor arriving between half past six and eight in the evening, after the school run and before dinner, in a flat in BKC, Bandra East or Santacruz East. The advantages are real and not sentimental: the student cannot drift off into another browser tab, the tutor sees the actual folder of marked work rather than a photograph of one page, and a parent can tell within three weeks whether anything is changing. The cost is travel, and travel is what breaks weekly slots.

Online is the honest answer for scarce subjects and for awkward geography. A Higher Level Economics teacher who lives in Thane is not driving to Bandra East on a Tuesday evening in July, but she will teach the same student every Tuesday for two years over a screen without missing one. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai also solves the February problem, when a student needs three short sessions in a week rather than one long one. Screen sharing suits mathematics and the sciences well, because the working can be written out live, and suits essay subjects even better, because both people can edit the same document.

Hybrid is what most families settle into without planning it. The standing weekly session happens at home, and the extra sessions before a mock or an Internal Assessment deadline happen online at short notice. Some families run one subject at home and another online purely because of who was available. Booking all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes across Mumbai sounds tidier than it is; insisting on in-person delivery for every subject usually means accepting a weaker tutor for at least one of them, which is a worse trade than it looks.

The trade-offs worth stating plainly: an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai coming to your home costs more per hour, because travel time is real time. Online costs less and is more reliable in the monsoon, but needs a desk, a decent connection and a door that closes. A student in Year 9 or Year 10 who still needs supervision usually does better in person. A Diploma Programme year two student working on an Extended Essay is often better served online, because what they need is a reader, not a presence.
bullets: Home tuition: best for Years 9 to 11 and for students who drift
Online: best for scarce Higher Level subjects and short pre-deadline sessions
Hybrid: standing weekly slot at home, extra sessions online before mocks
Travel time is billed time, so a nearby tutor is a cheaper tutor

sections.heading: How are IB and IGCSE tutors in Mumbai actually checked?
paragraphs: Before any tutor is shown to a family asking for IB or IGCSE tutoring for Dhirubhai Ambani International School students in Mumbai, we check three things and we check them in order. Identity comes first: a government photo identity document, a current address, and a working phone number that matches. Qualifications come second: the actual degree certificate, and for anyone claiming teaching experience, the school or college where it happened. Subject-specific experience comes third and matters most. Having a Physics degree is not the same as having taught Diploma Programme Physics, and the gap between the two shows in the first week.

The subject check is a conversation, not a form. We ask which syllabus version they teach to, how the Internal Assessment criteria are worded, what they would do with a student whose exploration question is too broad, and which past paper series they use for practice. A tutor who has genuinely taught the Diploma Programme answers all four without hesitating. A tutor who has read about it produces vague, confident sentences about concepts and skills. We also ask directly whether they have any relationship with the schools their students attend, and the only acceptable answer is that they do not.

That last point is worth dwelling on, because it is where the market gets dishonest. Nobody on this platform has access to any school's internal materials, nobody has been trained by any school, and nobody can tell you what is coming in an internal assessment. If a tutor hints at inside knowledge of a BKC school, that is a reason to end the conversation, not a selling point. IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation to any school named anywhere on this page, and a tutor who implies otherwise is misrepresenting both themselves and us.

There is also work for you to do, and it takes about twenty minutes. In the trial session, ask the tutor to mark one piece of your child's returned work in front of you and explain the mark against the criteria. Ask what they would prioritise over the next six weeks and why. Ask what they will send you after each session. Then ask your child one question afterwards: did that make sense. A tutor who is wrong for your child is usually obvious by the end of the first hour, and nobody benefits from waiting a month to say so.
bullets: Government photo identity, current address and a verified contact number
Degree certificate seen, plus the school or college where teaching happened
Syllabus-level questioning on criteria wording, past paper series and exploration design
Any hint of inside knowledge about a school is a disqualifier, not a credential
Your own check: ask the tutor to mark one returned script against the criteria

sections.heading: Why BKC tutors go deep on IB DP rather than wide across boards
paragraphs: Bandra Kurla Complex holds one of the densest concentrations of international schools anywhere in India, and that density has shaped the tutors who work there. A tutor based in Bandra East or Santacruz East can fill an entire week with Diploma Programme students without ever teaching a state board or CBSE lesson, which is simply not true of a tutor in most other parts of the country. The result is specialisation. Families asking about IB and IGCSE coaching for Dhirubhai Ambani International School students in Mumbai are drawing on a pool that has repeated the same syllabus year after year rather than one that covers four boards at once, and that repetition is the thing you are actually paying for.

Here is what depth looks like in practice, on one component. Take the Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level exploration, worth a fifth of the subject grade and marked out of twenty across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. A DP1 student in Bandra East proposes to explore the mathematics of basketball shooting. A generalist tutor says that sounds interesting and helps with the projectile equations. The student writes a competent piece and scores in the middle, because projectile motion at Higher Level is not Higher Level mathematics, and the use of mathematics criterion caps out immediately.

A specialist does something different in the first twenty minutes. She keeps the student's interest in basketball and changes the question, so that the investigation now models shot success as a function of release angle and uses optimisation with a constraint, then tests the model against the student's own recorded attempts. That single change opens the top band of the use of mathematics criterion, gives personal engagement something real to point at, and creates natural places for reflection, which is the criterion most students bolt on at the end as a paragraph of regret. None of that is harder teaching; it is knowing where the marks live.

The same instinct applies across the pathway. A specialist spots that a Year 11 student heading for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level should not drop Additional Mathematics 0606. She knows the Theory of Knowledge essay rewards an example the examiner has not seen forty times. She knows the sciences investigation is won in the research design section, weeks before the data is collected. Parents sometimes ask who the single best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai is; there is no such person, but there is a right person for one student on one pathway, and in BKC the pool is deep enough that they usually exist.
bullets: BKC tutors repeat the same Diploma Programme syllabus rather than covering four boards
The Mathematics exploration is scored out of twenty across five published criteria
Changing the research question early is worth more than months of content revision
Reflection and personal engagement are planned at the start, not added at the end
Depth matters most at Higher Level, where generalist coverage runs out fastest

sections.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks, one term and one exam cycle?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at grades at all, and any tutor who points at a grade after four weeks is managing you rather than teaching your child. What should have changed by then is behaviour: homework is being started earlier, the student can explain what a question is asking before attempting it, and the tutor is sending you a short note after each session saying what was covered and what was set. If your child still cannot tell you what they worked on last Tuesday, something is wrong and it is worth saying so in week four rather than week twelve.

At one term, roughly a June-to-Diwali or January-to-March block, you should see movement on the things that are actually marked. An Internal Assessment draft exists and has been through one round of supervisor comments. Past paper scores in the weak topic have moved, even if the overall grade has not, because an overall grade is an average that lags. The student has stopped avoiding the subject. For a Year 11 student, this is also the point at which the Core versus Extended question gets answered honestly rather than hopefully.

At one examination cycle, a mock series or the May session itself, you get the real reading. Here is the uncomfortable part: IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor should. A Diploma Programme grade is produced by two years of a student's own work, a school's teaching, an examiner's judgement and a set of internal assessments that were submitted months before the papers. Tutoring changes what a student brings into that room; it does not control the room. Anyone selling a guaranteed point gain is selling something they cannot deliver.

What tutoring reliably does is narrower and still worth paying for. It converts a student who does not know how to start into one who does. It gets coursework finished early enough to be revised rather than rescued. It replaces panic revision with marked past papers and a list of recurring mistakes. Families who get the most out of it treat the tutor as part of a system that includes the school and the student's own hours, not as a substitute for either, and they start the conversation in July rather than in February.
bullets: Four weeks: habits, session notes, and a student who can restate the question
One term: a real Internal Assessment draft and movement on weak-topic past papers
One cycle: honest reading against mocks, with no promised point gain
Grades are not guaranteed by anyone, and a tutor promising one is a warning
The biggest single variable remains the hours the student puts in alone

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition for Dhirubhai Ambani International School students in Mumbai
paragraphs: Getting started takes one message and about ten minutes of preparation. Before you send it, gather three things: the most recent report card or progress sheet, one piece of returned marked work in the subject that is slipping, and the two or three evening windows you can genuinely protect every week. The marked work matters more than the report card, because a report tells us a grade and a marked script tells us where the marks were lost. If your child is in Diploma Programme year one, add the subject and level combination and whether any Internal Assessment has been started.

The first session is diagnostic and should feel like one. The tutor works through the returned script with your child, finds the two or three things that are actually breaking, and sets a short piece of work to confirm the diagnosis. By the end of it you should have a plain answer to one question: is this a content gap, a technique gap or a scheduling problem. Those three need different treatment, and a tutor who starts teaching from chapter one without asking is not doing the job you are paying for.

After that, the normal pattern for a home tuition slot in BKC, Bandra East or Santacruz East is ninety minutes once a week per subject, rising to two sessions a week in the six weeks before mocks and in the final stretch before the May session. Fees depend on the board, the level, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels and how long the session runs, which is why we quote per tutor rather than publishing a rate card that would be wrong for most families.

If the match is not right, tell us in the first fortnight. Replacing a tutor early costs you one wasted session; replacing one in February costs a term. We re-shortlist against the same brief, you take another trial, and nothing carries over. That is the whole arrangement, and it is deliberately easy to leave, because a platform that makes you argue your way out of a bad match is not one worth joining in the first place.
bullets: Send: report card, one marked script, year group, subjects and levels
Name two or three evening windows you can protect for a full term
First session diagnoses content gap, technique gap or scheduling problem

faqs.question: What does tuition for a Dhirubhai Ambani International School student cost?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate, and anyone quoting one before knowing the subject is guessing. What an IB and IGCSE home tutor for Dhirubhai Ambani International School students in Mumbai charges depends on five things: the board and level, because Higher Level work costs more than Year 9 support; the scarcity of the subject, because Higher Level Economics teachers are rarer than Mathematics teachers; the distance travelled, since travel time is real working time; the session length; and whether delivery is at home or online. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai also move with the calendar, because February availability is tighter than July availability. We quote per tutor, in writing, before the trial.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to Dhirubhai Ambani International School in any way?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, approved by or connected to Dhirubhai Ambani International School, the American School of Bombay, Ascend International School or any other school named on this page. We have no access to any school's staff, internal materials, marking or deadlines. We name the school because parents search for it and because its board pathway is public information, and for no other reason. If any tutor suggests to you that they have an inside line to a school, please tell us, because that is grounds for removal from the platform.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our building in BKC on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the most common arrangement we set up in this part of Mumbai. Tutors matched to BKC, Bandra East and Santacruz East families are chosen partly because they already live or teach within that ring, so a half past six or seven o'clock start is realistic rather than aspirational. Give us your building and the gate protocol when you first write in, because a tutor who needs a pre-approved visitor entry or a resident's call at the gate each week needs to know before the first visit. Tutors carry photo identity for the register. A standing weekly slot with the same name is far easier for security than ad hoc timings.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, but you should be in the house for the first one. Being present for the trial lets you hear how the tutor explains something and how your child responds, which is the only real evidence you will get that early. After that, most families are in another room. For students in Years 9 and 10 we suggest staying within earshot, because younger students drift and a tutor is not a disciplinarian. For Diploma Programme students, presence usually makes things worse rather than better. What you should expect regardless is a short written note after each session saying what was covered and what was set.

faqs.question: My child is moving from IGCSE Year 11 into DP1. When should tuition start?
faqs.answer: Start in the summer before Diploma Programme year one, not in the first term of it. The transition from IGCSE to the Diploma Programme is a change in how work is assessed rather than only a step up in difficulty, and a student who scored well at IGCSE by revising hard in the final weeks will carry that habit into a programme where a fifth of each subject grade is settled by coursework written months before the exam. Two or three sessions in June and July spent on the Higher Level subject choices, the Additional Mathematics question and how the Internal Assessment calendar works prevent most of the problems we see in February.

faqs.question: Does online tuition really work for IB Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes, with two conditions. The first is subject fit: mathematics and the sciences work well online because the working can be written out live on a shared screen, and essay subjects work very well because tutor and student can edit the same document together, which beats passing a printout back and forth. The second is setup: a desk, a stable connection and a door that closes. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai is also often the only way to reach the right Higher Level specialist, since the best person for a scarce subject may be in Thane or Navi Mumbai and will never make a weekday evening journey to Bandra.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: You tell us and we re-shortlist, usually within a day or two. There is no contract, no notice period and no awkward conversation required with the tutor, because we handle that. Please do say it early rather than waiting for a term to end; three wasted sessions is a small loss, and a wasted term before mocks is not. It helps if you can describe what specifically did not work, whether the explanations were too fast, the tutor was teaching content when the issue was technique, or the personalities simply did not fit. That description makes the second match considerably better than the first.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for a written review rather than switching immediately. At four weeks, grades genuinely should not have moved, so the question is whether the underlying behaviour has. A reasonable tutor can tell you precisely what they have been working on, what the student can now do that they could not in week one, and what is still broken. If that account is vague, the problem is the tutor. If it is specific but your child is not doing the work set between sessions, the problem is not the tutor, and changing them will not help. We are happy to sit in the middle of that conversation.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all the subjects my child needs?
faqs.answer: Through Year 9 and Year 10, often yes. At Diploma Programme level, almost never. The content is deep enough by then that the same person is rarely strong at Higher Level Chemistry and Higher Level English Language and Literature, and a generalist who claims both is usually ordinary at each. The practical answer for most families here is one tutor for the subject that is genuinely failing, and a second only if a different subject becomes a problem later. Adding three tutors at once is expensive and gives a Diploma Programme student more evening commitments than study hours, which usually makes the term worse.

faqs.question: How does the Mumbai monsoon affect a weekly evening home tuition slot?
faqs.answer: It is the single biggest cause of cancelled sessions, and it is why we match on travel distance rather than on credentials alone. June to September evenings in Mumbai can turn a twenty-minute drive across the Western Express Highway into an hour, and a tutor who faces that twice a week will quietly start rescheduling by August. Two things help. Keep the slot with a tutor who lives inside your corridor rather than across the city, and agree in advance that heavy rain moves the session online rather than cancelling it. Most families here run exactly that arrangement and lose almost no sessions across the year.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can help a student narrow a research question, build a reading plan, structure an argument, understand what the assessment criteria are actually asking for, and read a draft critically. A tutor cannot write any part of it, cannot supply the content, and must not touch the student's reflection sessions with their supervisor, which belong to the school. The Extended Essay in particular is usually a scheduling failure rather than an intellectual one, and the most useful work a tutor does on it happens in September and October of Diploma Programme year two, not in December.

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Navi Mumbai to one family at this school
paragraphs: Almost every enquiry we receive about this school says the same three things: the board, the child's year, and the words Navi Mumbai. That is not enough to match anybody. D.Y. It is how many can reach your building at the hour your child is genuinely free, and keep doing it in late June when the roads are standing water and the Sion-Panvel Highway has slowed to a crawl. Three profiles that survive that test beat twelve that do not.

Timing of the request matters more than parents expect. An enquiry that arrives in April or early May, before the new academic year settles, draws a wider shortlist than the same enquiry in September, by which point the tutors who travel well have filled their weekday evenings. If you are reading this mid-term, say so plainly, and tell us which days are genuinely free rather than which days you would prefer. sections.heading: Two pathways under one roof: what IB and IGCSE actually ask of a student
paragraphs: D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, Navi Mumbai runs both an International Baccalaureate (IB) pathway and a Cambridge IGCSE pathway. That is public information about the school and it is the only kind of statement about it you will find on this page. What it means for tutoring is less obvious than it sounds. A child here can sit Cambridge IGCSE papers at the end of Year 11 and begin the IB Diploma Programme (DP) a few months later, and those are two different assessment cultures rather than two difficulty settings of the same one.

Cambridge IGCSE splits most of its subjects into Core and Extended tiers, and the tier is a decision with a ceiling attached: the Core papers cap the achievable grade, the Extended papers do not, and moving between them late in Year 11 is awkward because the content covered differs. A parent asking for help with all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 usually wants one tutor in Mumbai to hold the whole timetable, and for Years 9 and 10 that is sometimes workable. By Year 11 it rarely is, because tier decisions in Maths and the sciences need someone who has taught those specific papers.

The IB Diploma Programme is built differently. Six subjects, three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), plus the core: the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and Creativity, Activity, Service. HL is not SL with extra homework. It adds genuinely separate content and, in several subjects, an additional paper. Choosing three HLs that all carry heavy internal assessment work in the same term is the single most common self-inflicted problem we see in DP1, and the time to catch it is before the subject form goes in, not in February of DP2.

Some families at the school follow the Middle Years Programme (MYP) before the Diploma rather than IGCSE. The MYP marks against criteria with published descriptors and no past-paper bank, which is a different kind of preparation entirely. If your child is on that route, say so at the enquiry stage, because a strong IGCSE tutor is not automatically a strong MYP tutor and the reverse is equally true.
bullets: Core and Extended IGCSE tiers carry different grade ceilings and different content.

sections.heading: Which subjects do families at this school actually ask for help with?
paragraphs: Maths and the sciences account for most requests, followed by English and Economics. At IGCSE that means Cambridge Mathematics 0580 Extended, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610, and at DP it means Mathematics Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation at HL or SL, the three sciences, and Language A: Language and Literature. Second-language requests cluster around French, Spanish and Hindi, with ab initio students needing a very different tutor from Language B students. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects the tutor pool in Mumbai is deeper in Maths than in anything else, and thinnest in Music, Visual Arts and the less common second languages.

Here is a worked example of what subject-level experience buys you. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 Paper 6, the Alternative to Practical, is where careful students quietly leak marks. A typical question gives a table of pendulum lengths and the time for twenty oscillations, then asks the student to calculate the period, plot period squared against length, draw the best-fit line, find the gradient and state one precaution. Four separate things are being marked and only one of them is physics.

First, the calculated values have to be recorded to a consistent number of decimal places, justified by the raw data. Second, the axes must be scaled so the plotted points occupy more than half the grid in both directions, which is a drawing decision made before any point goes down. Third, the gradient triangle has to span at least half the drawn line, and the coordinates must be read from the line rather than lifted back out of the table. Fourth, the precaution: writing be careful while measuring earns nothing, while viewing the bob against a fiducial mark at eye level to avoid parallax earns the mark. A tutor who has marked that paper fixes all four in a single sitting. A tutor who merely knows pendulums fixes none of them.

The internal assessments deserve the same scrutiny. The DP sciences investigation, the Mathematics Exploration, the Economics commentaries built on real news articles and the Business Management project are each marked against published criteria that have been revised for recent cohorts. Ask any prospective tutor which version of the subject guide they last taught from and which criterion students most often lose marks on. A vague answer there tells you more than a long list of qualifications.

sections.heading: Where in Mumbai do these tutors actually travel from?
paragraphs: The honest answer is that for a family at this school, the tutor almost always comes from inside Navi Mumbai. The nodes are planned close together and linked by Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Harbour Line running Vashi to Panvel, the Trans-Harbour Line connecting Thane and Vashi, and the Navi Mumbai Metro running from Belapur towards Pendhar. Nerul station on the Harbour Line is the practical anchor for anyone travelling to the school's surroundings by train. Within this geography, Vashi, Sanpada, Nerul, Seawoods, CBD Belapur, Kharghar, Kamothe, Panvel and Ulwe are all node-to-node drives rather than expeditions.

IB Gram covers the rest of Mumbai, Maharashtra as well, and families sometimes ask whether a tutor from the island city can come across. In South Mumbai we match within the island, where Colaba and Cuffe Parade sit close to Fort and Worli but the Peddar Road signals and the Coastal Road decide the evening. The Western Suburbs run along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway, where Bandra and Khar, or Malad and Kandivali, match well along the line and badly across it, with Metro Line 1 from Versova to Ghatkopar and Metro Lines 2A and 7 filling the gaps.

The Central Suburbs hang off the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali reached by road along JVLR and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road because Powai has no station of its own. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi up through Vikhroli to Mulund, and the Eastern Freeway makes South Mumbai far closer from there than the map suggests. Thane sits apart again, spread from the station across Pokhran Road and Ghodbunder Road to Majiwada and Kasarvadavali, where the Ghodbunder stretch alone can double a journey after six.

All of which explains the rule we apply to this school. The Atal Setu and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link have genuinely changed weekend travel across the harbour, and a Saturday morning tutor from Chembur or Wadala to Nerul is now a reasonable proposition. A Wednesday 6pm tutor making the same trip is not, however willing they are in week one. We match inside the belt for weekday home classes and look outward only for weekend blocks or online work.

sections.heading: What the IB and IGCSE calendar does to a Mumbai family's week
paragraphs: IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform. We are not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to D.Y. Patil International School, and nothing here is published with the school's involvement. We describe the school only as public context: it is in Nerul, in Navi Mumbai, and it offers IB and IGCSE pathways. Families comparing options across the city look at other schools running the same boards, Ryan Global School among them, and the calendar pressure described below comes from the boards rather than from any one campus.

The shape of the year is consistent wherever these boards are taught. From late August into October the new timetable settles and the first formal assessments appear, which is when gaps from the previous year become visible. November and December bring the heavier internal assessment work and the first serious mock papers, immediately before a break that most families treat as rest and most DP2 students should not. January and February are the compression point: Extended Essay and internal assessment deadlines cluster, mocks are returned, and predicted grades take shape. March to May is the examination window itself.

There is a second rhythm layered on top, which is the Mumbai one. The monsoon from June into September rearranges every weekday evening in the belt, and a tutor travelling from Kharghar to Nerul in heavy rain will be late or will not come. December brings school events and travel. The practical consequence is that the useful months for building something, rather than patching something, are roughly July to October and the back half of May. A tutor engaged in January is doing damage control, which is legitimate work but a different job.

We do not have the school's internal calendar, its assessment schedule, its mark schemes or its reports, and no tutor on this platform has access to any of them. Nor have we placed tutors who taught at the school, and we would not claim it if we had. What a good tutor does instead is read your child's own diary and assessment sheets in the first session and build the plan from those, which is the only reliable source of dates any outsider can work from.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a Navi Mumbai school run?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default and it is what most families here want. IB and IGCSE home tuition for DY Patil International School students in Navi Mumbai works because the nodes are close: the tutor arrives, the child does not travel after a full school day, the parent can see what is happening, and the session holds its shape week after week. The cost is rigidity. A home slot is fixed to one tutor's road, so a cancelled evening is genuinely lost rather than shifted, and the pool narrows to people who can make that specific journey.

Online suits particular cases rather than particular families. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai, or outside it, becomes the right answer when the subject is scarce, when the child is in Panvel or Ulwe and the evening road makes travel unreasonable, or when the work is essay feedback, Extended Essay supervision or past-paper review that transfers cleanly to a screen. It is weakest for a Year 9 or 10 student who has not yet learned to work unsupervised, and for anything that depends on watching a hand write out a method and correcting it mid-line.

Hybrid is what we end up recommending most often in the outer nodes, and it is not a compromise so much as an acknowledgement of the road. One home session at the weekend, when travel is cheap and the household is calm, carries the teaching. One shorter online session midweek carries the follow-up, the marked work and the question the child could not ask on Saturday. Families in Kharghar, Kamothe and Panvel who try to force two weekday home classes instead usually lose one of them inside a month.

Whichever shape you choose, keep it stable for a full term before judging it. Switching from home tuition to online halfway through because one week went badly resets the relationship and costs more than the week you were trying to save. If you are unsure, start with home classes and add the online session later rather than the other way round, because a tutor the child has met in person teaches far better online than one they have not.

sections.heading: How do I know a tutor is who the profile says they are?
paragraphs: Every tutor listed with IB Gram goes through identity verification, a check of the qualifications they claim and a conversation about the boards and papers they have actually taught. Someone who says they teach IB Physics is asked which level, which internal assessment criteria and which paper they are strongest on. Someone who says IGCSE Maths is asked about 0580 Extended and the questions students lose marks on. The answers decide whether the profile goes out at all. We also record the areas a tutor genuinely travels to, because an aspirational travel radius is the most common reason a good match collapses in week three.

That is our half. Yours is the half that matters more, and it takes one conversation. Ask the tutor which board and which syllabus version they last taught. Ask them to talk through a single past-paper question in the child's subject, out loud, on the call. Ask what they would do in the first three sessions and what they would want to see from your child's school diary. A tutor who answers those three questions concretely is almost always the right one, and a tutor who answers in generalities is almost always not.

Ask the uncomfortable question too. No tutor on this platform has the school's internal materials, its mark schemes, its staff contacts or its report data, and anybody who implies otherwise is telling you something that is not true. Finding an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai who claims inside knowledge of a specific campus should make you cautious rather than reassured. The legitimate version of that claim is much smaller: this tutor has taught these papers to students at several schools in Navi Mumbai and knows what the boards reward.

Keep the practical checks as well. Confirm the tutor's full name and phone number before the first visit, tell your building security who is coming and on which day, and be at home for the first session. These are ordinary precautions for anyone entering your flat weekly, and no reputable tutor will find them unusual. IB Gram remains independent of every school named on this page, including D.Y. Patil International School, and our checks cover our tutors rather than any school's staff.

sections.heading: Same school, different answer: what is realistic from each Navi Mumbai node
paragraphs: There is no single answer to IB and IGCSE home tutoring for DY Patil International School students in Navi Mumbai, because the school is the anchor for the whole belt and its families are spread across it. Two children in the same class, with the same subjects and the same problem, have different options available on a Tuesday. From Nerul the child is home early and the local tutor supply is at its best, but the real constraint is the opposite of what parents assume: there is no decompression gap, and a 4pm start with a tired eleven-year-old is worse than a 6pm one. Nerul families should be choosing between early evening and after dinner, not rushing to fill the first free hour.

Seawoods is a short run down Palm Beach Road and the early slot genuinely exists there, which creates its own trap. Because the travel cost is so low, Seawoods parents tend to over-schedule, stacking two subjects on the same evening because both tutors can make it. One of those sessions is always the weaker one. Vashi and Sanpada sit twenty to twenty-five minutes up the same road and have the widest tutor pool in the belt, helped by the Trans-Harbour Line, but Vashi households are frequently juggling a second child at a different school, so the realistic shape there is one subject, one fixed weekday, defended against everything else.

CBD Belapur changes the question from travel to supervision. Parents here often work in the node itself and get home around seven, so the honest options are a post-dinner weekday slot with an adult present, or a longer ninety-minute weekend block, rather than a 5pm session the child sits through alone. Kharghar has plenty of tutors of its own, and its genuine gap is not distance but calendar: a local tutor may be excellent and still have no feel for the way IB and IGCSE deadlines stack, so insist they build the plan from your child's diary. Kamothe usually inherits whatever Kharghar and Panvel can spare, which makes an early commitment to a fixed slot more important there than anywhere else.

Panvel is where honesty saves everyone a wasted month. Forty-five minutes to an hour each way on the Sion-Panvel Highway in evening traffic means a weekday home tutor will be late, then later, then unavailable, and the family concludes that tutoring does not work when what failed was the schedule. A Panvel family should plan for a weekend home session plus midweek online from the start. Ulwe is similar, and while the Atal Setu has changed its connection to the island city, it has done nothing for the school run itself. Say your node at the first message and you skip this entire discovery process.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and anybody in this market who does is selling something they cannot deliver. What a good match reliably produces is visible and worth watching for. At four weeks you should see changed behaviour rather than changed marks: your child knows what the next assessment is, brings specific questions to the session instead of saying everything is fine, and has started attempting past-paper questions without being pushed into it. If none of that has shifted in a month, the match is wrong and you should tell us rather than waiting politely for a term to end.

At one term the marks usually start to move, and they move unevenly. A student weak across a subject often gains most on the paper that rewards technique, which at IGCSE is frequently the practical or data-handling paper rather than the theory one, because technique is simply faster to fix than two years of missed content. Expect the gain to show in one component before it shows in an overall grade. A term is also long enough to tell whether the tutor is teaching the subject or teaching the answers, and the difference is audible when you ask your child to explain something.

At one exam cycle the question changes from improvement to consistency: can the student produce the same standard under timed conditions, in the hall, on a bad day. That is a separate skill from knowing the material, and it is the main thing the final months are for. We cannot guarantee outcomes here either, and the variables that sit outside any tutor's reach are real: attendance, sleep, the child's own engagement, and how much ground there was to recover when you started.

When a tutor is not working out, say so early. Tell us what specifically is wrong, because the fix differs: a personality mismatch needs a different person, while a pacing problem or an unclear plan is often fixable in one conversation with the same tutor. If a replacement is the answer, we re-match from the same node and the new tutor receives a short handover of what has been covered, so your child is not re-diagnosed from zero. Most re-matches happen in the first month, which is exactly when they should.
bullets: Four weeks: behaviour changes first, marks later; judge the habit, not the score.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Four things make the first conversation useful. Your node, written plainly. The subjects and the board, with level or tier if the decision has been made. The two or three weekday slots that are genuinely free, after travel and after any other activity, not the ones you hope to free up. And the most recent piece of marked work you have, even if it is a single assessment sheet, because it says more in thirty seconds than a paragraph of description. With those four, a shortlist takes a day or two rather than a week.

The first session should not look like teaching. A tutor who starts lecturing in minute one has skipped the only part that is irreplaceable. Expect them to go through the child's diary and assessment dates, work through a past-paper question or a recent piece of marked work while watching how the child thinks, and identify where the marks are actually going. You should get a short plan at the end of it: what the next few weeks target, what the child does between sessions, and what you should see by the fourth week.

Set the practical terms at the same time. Agree the day and time and treat them as fixed. Agree how a cancellation on either side is handled and how far ahead it needs to be. Decide where in the flat the session happens, ideally a table in a room with a door rather than the dining table in the middle of the household. Give building security the tutor's name and the standing day, which saves a ten-minute argument at the gate every single week and is the most common small friction in Navi Mumbai societies.

Then leave it alone for a term. The strongest predictor of a tutoring arrangement working is not the tutor's credentials but whether the slot survives contact with real life for twelve consecutive weeks. Protect it, tell us early if something is wrong, and keep your own eye on the one thing no tutor can report accurately: whether your child is doing the work between sessions.
bullets: Have your node, board, subjects, free slots and one marked script ready.
A first session is a diagnostic: diary, past-paper question, plan, not a lecture.
Fix the day, the cancellation rule and the room before week one.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to D.Y. Patil International School in any way?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to D.Y. Patil International School, and this page is published without the school's involvement. We name the school because parents search for it, and we describe it only in public terms: it is in Nerul, in Navi Mumbai, and it offers IB and IGCSE pathways. A family hiring an IB and IGCSE home tutor for DY Patil International School students in Mumbai is engaging us, not the school, and any question about school policy, reports or internal dates belongs with the school directly.

faqs.question: Will a tutor really travel to my home in Kharghar on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, Kharghar is one of the easier nodes for weekday home tuition because it has a reasonable local tutor base of its own, so the person coming to you is usually travelling within the node rather than across the belt. What you should pin down is the slot. A 5.30pm or 6pm start held every week is sustainable; a 4.30pm start that assumes clear roads on the Sion-Panvel Highway is not. Ask the tutor where they are travelling from and what their journey looks like in heavy rain, and believe the answer they give about June rather than the one about November.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Rates are set by individual tutors and we will not publish a price list, because a single figure would be misleading for every family it did not fit. The variables are consistent though. Board and level matter most, with IB Diploma Higher Level costing more than IGCSE Years 9 and 10. Subject scarcity matters next: a Physics Higher Level or a Spanish tutor commands more than a Maths tutor simply because fewer exist. Then travel distance and session length, which is why an outer node often costs more per hour than Nerul or Seawoods. Online sessions remove the travel component entirely.

faqs.question: We live in Panvel. Is a weekday home tutor realistic for us at all?
faqs.answer: Honestly, often not, and it is better to know that now. The road from the inner nodes to Panvel in evening traffic runs forty-five minutes to an hour each way, so a tutor who agrees to a Wednesday 6pm slot in week one is frequently late by week four and gone by week eight. The arrangement that holds is a longer weekend home session, when the road is cooperative, plus a shorter midweek online session for marked work and follow-up questions. Panvel families who start with that shape stay with their tutor far longer than those who insist on two weekday visits.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all of my child's subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes at IGCSE Years 9 and 10, rarely at Year 11, and almost never at Diploma Programme level. A capable Maths and Physics tutor can usually hold Chemistry too at the lower years, which keeps the week simple and the cost down. Once tier decisions and internal assessments arrive, the work becomes paper-specific, and a tutor stretching across four subjects is being generically helpful in three of them. Booking all IB and IGCSE subjects as home classes in Navi Mumbai is rarely the right call. Two strong subject tutors beat one who covers everything adequately.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for the IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: For some parts of them, yes, and for others it is clearly weaker. Online handles theory explanation, past-paper walkthroughs, mark-scheme analysis and feedback on written answers perfectly well, and a document camera or tablet closes most of the gap on worked calculations. Where it struggles is the practical paper and any situation where the tutor needs to watch a hand write out a method and interrupt mid-line. If your child is in Year 9 or 10 and still needs the presence of an adult to stay on task, start with home classes and move parts of the work online once the habit exists.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out after three weeks. What happens now?
faqs.answer: Tell us immediately rather than waiting for the term to end, and be specific about what is wrong. If it is personality or communication, we re-match from the same node and you do not start the search again. If it is pacing, an unclear plan or too little written feedback, that is often repairable in one direct conversation with the same tutor and is worth trying first. A replacement comes with a short handover covering what has already been taught, so your child is not diagnosed from scratch a second time. Most re-matches happen inside the first month.

faqs.question: How does society gate access and visitor entry work for a regular tutor?
faqs.answer: It works best when you set it up once instead of weekly. Give your building security the tutor's full name, phone number and the standing day and time, and ask whether your society allows a recurring visitor entry or needs a fresh gate pass each visit, because practice varies widely across Navi Mumbai complexes. Some towers want the resident to approve each entry through an app, which fails quietly if you are in a meeting. Sorting this before the first session removes the single most common cause of a session starting fifteen minutes late.

faqs.question: What happens to sessions during the monsoon or on a bad traffic evening?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before you need it. Most tutors will tell you by early afternoon if the evening looks impossible, and the standard arrangement is that the session moves online at the same hour rather than being cancelled, which keeps the rhythm intact. From June to September across Nerul, Vashi, Kharghar and Panvel this will happen several times, and families who have no agreed fallback simply lose those weeks. Decide in advance how many rescheduled sessions carry forward and whether a late cancellation from either side is chargeable, then stick to what you agreed.

faqs.question: Do your tutors know the school's internal assessment schedule?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who claims they do. We have no access to the school's calendar, mark schemes, teaching materials, staff or report data, and we have not placed tutors on the basis of having taught there. What an experienced tutor does know is how the IB and Cambridge calendars behave across a year and which months compress. The reliable source of your child's actual dates is your child's own diary and assessment sheets, which a good tutor will ask to see in the first session and build the plan around.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in on sessions, and does a tutor need a separate room?
faqs.answer: Be present in the house, particularly for the first few sessions, without sitting in the room throughout. Most children work worse with a parent watching and better knowing one is nearby. On space, a table in a room with a door beats the dining table in the middle of household traffic, and it matters more than families expect for a ninety-minute evening session after a full school day. If the flat has no quiet corner, say so at the enquiry stage, because some tutors adapt to it well and others genuinely do not.

sections.heading: How we match an IB & IGCSE home tutor for Ecole Mondiale World School students in Mumbai
paragraphs: A request that names a school is a different request from one that names a subject. When a parent writes to us about a child at Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, the first question we ask is not which subject is slipping. It is which programme year the child sits in. A Grade 4 student in the Primary Years Programme (PYP), a Grade 9 student in the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and a Grade 11 Diploma Programme (DP) student need three different sorts of tutor, and only the last of those three is working towards an external examination.

That one answer changes everything after it. For a PYP child we look for a tutor who can sit with a unit of inquiry and build research and note-taking habits, not someone who drills sums for an hour. For MYP we look for fluency in criterion-based marking: a tutor who can read a task sheet, point at the command term, and show a student what separates a level 4 descriptor from a level 7 descriptor in that exact subject. For DP we look for subject depth, Internal Assessment (IA) supervision experience, and a realistic sense of how many drafts a student actually needs.

The sequence from your first message to a first lesson usually runs over a few days rather than a few hours, because the shortlisting step is the one that decides whether the match holds for a full term. We would rather spend two extra days finding a tutor who can hold a Tuesday evening slot in Juhu until March than send you someone free this week who drops the slot in November.

There are two things we do not do. We do not hold or claim access to any school's internal task sheets, mark books, teacher comments or assessment materials, and we do not approach school staff. Everything a tutor works from comes from you and your child: the report you received, the marked task that came home, the calendar the school publishes to its own parents. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai who offers you more than that is offering something no honest platform can supply.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: which stage is your child actually in?
paragraphs: Ecole Mondiale World School is, as a matter of public record, a full International Baccalaureate (IB) continuum school in Juhu offering the Primary Years Programme, the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma Programme. A continuum child can therefore move from the early years to Grade 12 without ever sitting an external board examination until the DP papers themselves. That single fact should shape what you ask a tutor for at every stage before Grade 11.

PYP is transdisciplinary. Children work through units of inquiry, gather evidence, and finish the programme with the Exhibition, a student-led inquiry presented to the school community. There is no external mark anywhere in it. MYP runs five years across eight subject groups, and every subject is marked against four published criteria, each out of 8, which are then converted to a 1 to 7 grade. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project, and Service as Action runs across the whole programme.

DP is the first programme with an external examiner at the end of it. Six subjects, usually three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), sit alongside the core: Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). Every subject carries an Internal Assessment marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB, and the written papers come in the May session of Grade 12.

Here is where the continuum advantage quietly becomes a continuum problem. A student who joins DP from an IGCSE school has already sat two years of timed external papers and knows what a three-hour morning feels like. A continuum student has usually never done it. In our experience that gap shows up in timing and in exam-condition writing stamina rather than in understanding, which is why we often suggest a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai start timed writing practice in MYP 5, a full year before DP begins.

sections.heading: Subject choice across both boards: HL, SL, Core and Extended, and what each one assesses
paragraphs: In MYP there is very little subject choice to make until the last two years, when language acquisition phases, and the arts and design options, start to separate students. What does need managing much earlier is criterion literacy. MYP Sciences marks Criterion A (knowing and understanding), B (inquiring and designing), C (processing and evaluating) and D (reflecting on the impacts of science). Mathematics uses knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Language and Literature marks analysing, organising, producing text and using language. A child can understand the content and still lose a band because nobody taught them what organising means to an MYP examiner.

DP choice is real and consequential. Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, each at HL or SL, and the wrong pick in Grade 11 is painful to undo in Grade 12. Sciences, Individuals and Societies and Language B all offer HL and SL routes, where HL means more content, usually an extra paper, and a longer leash on the Internal Assessment. A parent wanting cover across all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 looks for tutors in Mumbai who can hold two of those subjects well rather than six badly.

The IGCSE half of this page matters to a continuum family in two situations: your child joined from an IGCSE school, or you are considering a move to one of the IGCSE schools elsewhere in Mumbai. There the decisions are Core versus Extended tier, which caps the grades a candidate can be awarded, and whether the centre follows Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, since the coursework and practical arrangements differ. We cover all IB and IGCSE subjects with home tutors in Mumbai, but we match one tutor to one or two subjects, never a generalist to a whole timetable.

Internal assessment is the thread running through both boards. A DP Sciences IA, a Mathematics exploration, a History IA and a Business Management IA each have their own criteria and their own word limits, and each needs a different kind of help: a research question that is actually answerable, a data set that is actually collectable in Mumbai, and a draft submitted early enough for the teacher's one permitted round of written feedback to be worth something.

sections.heading: Home tuition in Juhu, JVPD Scheme, Vile Parle West and Khar West, and across Mumbai
paragraphs: Families at this school mostly live inside a small triangle: Juhu itself, the JVPD Scheme roads behind it, Vile Parle West on the other side of S.V. Road, and Khar West a short run down Linking Road. A few come from Santacruz West and Andheri West. In Mumbai, Maharashtra, that triangle is unusually tutor-friendly, because the whole of it sits between two Western Line stations, Vile Parle and Santacruz, and a tutor can reach most of it without ever touching the Western Express Highway.

The constraint is the clock, not the distance. Juhu Tara Road, Gulmohar Road and the JVPD Scheme internal roads are quiet at four in the afternoon and solid from about half past six, and school pickup around Juhu narrows them again in the early afternoon. A tutor living in Andheri West can be at a JVPD Scheme flat in fifteen minutes off-peak and forty in the evening peak, so we try to fix the slot and the direction of travel together. Metro Line 1 from Versova through Andheri to Ghatkopar, and Metro Lines 2A and 7 running down from Dahisar, widen the pool of tutors who can hold an early evening slot here without driving.

We also match for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai well beyond Juhu, because families move and siblings study elsewhere. In South Mumbai we cover Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Worli and Peddar Road, where the Coastal Road and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link now decide whether a Bandra tutor can take a 7pm slot at all. Across the Western Suburbs we cover Bandra West, Khar West, Santacruz, Andheri and Malad along the Western Line. In the Central Suburbs we cover Powai, Chandivali, Ghatkopar and Kurla, reached by JVLR and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road rather than by any station of their own.

The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Vikhroli up to Bhandup and Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines, with the Eastern Freeway and the Eastern Express Highway doing the heavy lifting. Navi Mumbai is matched node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur and Kharghar along Palm Beach Road, with the Atal Setu now making the island city reachable in a way it was not. Thane we match within Thane, from the station across Pokhran Road to Ghodbunder Road. For an IB and IGCSE home tutor for Ecole Mondiale World School students in Mumbai, though, we almost always stay inside the Juhu, JVPD Scheme, Vile Parle West and Khar West ring, because that is the match that survives the monsoon.

sections.heading: What the Mumbai IB calendar does to a continuum family's year
paragraphs: Check the calendar your own school publishes to parents, because dates differ by campus and we do not speak for any school. The shape below is what IB families in Mumbai generally plan around, and it is driven by one fixed point: the Diploma Programme examinations sit in the May session, and every internal deadline in the two years before them is reverse-engineered from that date.

November and December are the first pressure point, with MYP semester tasks landing together and DP1 internal examinations in the same weeks. January and February are the hardest stretch in the whole continuum: DP Internal Assessment final drafts, the Extended Essay, and the TOK essay all converge, and MYP 5 students are finishing the Personal Project report at the same moment. February and March bring DP mock examinations and then study leave. June and July belong to the monsoon, when travel is slowest and tuition demand is lowest, which makes them the easiest months to start a new tutor rather than the obvious ones.

Juhu complicates this for families with children at more than one school. Jamnabai Narsee International School and Utpal Shanghvi Global School are both in the Juhu area and both run IGCSE or IB DP pathways, and their assessment weeks do not line up with a continuum school's. A parent running a Grade 10 IGCSE candidate and an MYP 4 student in the same flat is running two calendars, two sets of deadlines and often two tutors on alternating evenings.

The practical consequence is about booking, not about panic. Demand for DP Sciences, Mathematics and Economics tutors in the Western Suburbs peaks just before the IA window, which is exactly when the good ones have no slots left. If you know your child will need help in January, the time to find a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is August or September, when a tutor can still choose your Tuesday at six rather than offering you a Sunday morning.

January and February: Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and TOK deadlines collide.

May: the external Diploma Programme papers for Grade 12.
June and July: monsoon travel, and the quietest month to start.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a Mumbai continuum student?
paragraphs: For PYP and MYP students, home tuition wins almost every time. A nine-year-old working on a unit of inquiry needs an adult in the room who can see the page, close the other tab, and notice when attention goes. An IB and IGCSE home tutor for Ecole Mondiale World School students in Mumbai also sees the things a camera hides: that the study table is in the living room, that homework starts at nine at night, that the laptop belongs to an older sibling until eight.

The honest cost of home tuition is time and fragility. A tutor travelling from Andheri West to JVPD Scheme spends an hour on the road for a ninety-minute lesson, which means fewer slots in their week and a strong preference for a fixed day. Monsoon weeks and a waterlogged S.V. Road cancel visits that online sessions would have survived. Agree the fallback in advance: a visit that cannot happen becomes an online session at the same hour, not a lost week.

IB and IGCSE online tutoring in Mumbai earns its place in two specific situations. The first is subject scarcity: HL Physics, HL Economics, Computer Science and the less common Language B options have thin tutor pools, and insisting on someone who can drive to Juhu on a Wednesday can mean waiting a month for a weaker match. The second is drafting. Reviewing an IA or an Extended Essay over a shared screen, with the examiner criteria open in a second window, is genuinely better online than hunched over one laptop at a dining table.

Hybrid is what most DP families here settle into by the second term: one home session a week for teaching, and a short online check midweek for drafts, corrections and a look at what was actually submitted. It keeps the relationship face to face while cutting travel out of the half of the work that does not need it, and it survives both exam leave and a week of heavy rain.
bullets: Home tuition suits PYP and MYP students who need supervision, not content.
Online suits scarce HL subjects and drafting work over a shared screen.
Hybrid keeps one weekly home session and a short midweek online check.
Agree in advance that a rained-off visit moves online, not away.
A door, a table and a charged laptop beat a bedroom corner.

sections.heading: How are tutors verified, and what should a Mumbai parent check for themselves?
paragraphs: We check three things before a tutor is introduced to you: government photo identity, documentary evidence of the qualification they claim, and subject knowledge screened by someone who has taught that subject at that level. We also ask for teaching history and references where a tutor has them. We will not pretend this is the same as a police background check. If you want one for somebody who will be in your flat weekly, say so and arrange it; it is a reasonable thing for a parent in Juhu to want and we will not be offended.

The checks you run yourself are the ones that actually predict the term ahead. Hand the tutor one returned MYP task with the criteria sheet stapled to it and ask them to explain, out loud, why the teacher awarded that level and what the next band needs. Ask what a command term like evaluate or justify requires in that subject. Ask how many IA drafts they will read and by what date. A tutor who answers those three questions concretely is worth more than one with a longer list of degrees.

One more check matters on a school page like this one. Parents who search for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai often end up talking to someone who hints at inside knowledge of a particular school: a copy of last year's task, a line to a teacher, an idea of what is coming. Treat that as a reason to end the conversation. It is either untrue or it is academic dishonesty, and both land on your child, not on the tutor.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We are not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Ecole Mondiale World School or any other school named on this page, and we have no access to their materials or their staff. What we offer is an IB and IGCSE home tutor for Ecole Mondiale World School students in Mumbai who understands the programmes your child is in, which is a different and more useful thing.
bullets: Photo identity and qualification evidence are checked before any introduction.
Subject screening is done by someone who has taught that subject.
Ask the tutor to mark one returned task against the published criteria.
Ask how many IA drafts they will read, and by when.
Treat any claim of inside school access as a reason to stop.

sections.heading: The PYP Exhibition and the MYP Personal Project: what a tutor can and cannot do
paragraphs: These two pieces are where a continuum education asks a child to work alone for the first time, and they are the two places where tutoring goes wrong most often. Both are assessed on process, both are supervised by school staff, and both have an academic honesty requirement that makes an undeclared tutor a problem rather than a help. Tell the school a tutor is involved. Supervisors expect it, and the student's own reflection is where the marks live anyway.

For the PYP Exhibition, the useful help is unglamorous. A tutor teaches a ten-year-old how to turn a central idea into lines of inquiry that can actually be researched, how to tell a usable source from a search result, how to take notes in their own words rather than copying, and how to plan backwards from the presentation date so the last week is rehearsal rather than panic. A tutor who supplies content, slides or sentences has broken the task. A tutor who sits through one rehearsal and asks three hard questions has done the job.

A worked example from MYP makes the point sharper. Take a Grade 9 Sciences investigation into how salt concentration affects potato cylinders, assessed on Criterion B, inquiring and designing, out of 8. Most students write: I will change the salt and measure the potato. That is a level 2 answer. It has no measurable independent variable, no stated control, and no reasoning. The level 7 version names the variable and its range (sodium chloride solution at five concentrations from 0.0 to 1.0 mol per cubic decimetre), states a hypothesis with osmosis and water potential as the reason, lists controlled variables with the method of control beside each one (same cork borer diameter, same immersion time, each cylinder blotted the same number of times), plans repeats, and draws the blank results table before touching a potato. Not one of those improvements is about potatoes. That is why we teach the criterion rather than the topic: one good session on Criterion B pays out on every investigation that student runs for the rest of the year.

The Personal Project works the same way, scaled up. It is marked on planning, applying skills and reflecting, and the process journal is the evidence for all three. The students who struggle are rarely short of ability; they are short of entries, because they did the work and forgot to record it. An IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai earns their fee here with a twenty-minute weekly check: what did you do, what went wrong, what did you change, write it down now. The product matters far less than most families expect.
bullets: Exhibition work needs source evaluation and a plan, not borrowed content.
Criterion B marks the variables table, not how the practical turned out.
One process journal entry per working session is the Personal Project backbone.
Declare the tutor to the supervisor; academic honesty rules require it.
One criterion taught well transfers to every task that year.

sections.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks, one term and one exam cycle?
paragraphs: After four weeks, expect a diagnosis and a habit, not a grade. A tutor who has seen four sessions of real work should be able to tell you something specific that you did not know: that your MYP 4 child understands the science and loses marks on Criterion C graphs, that the DP1 student is reading the question but answering a different one, that nothing is wrong academically and the problem is a nine-thirty start to homework. One changed habit, like a variables table written before the practical, is a good four-week outcome.

After one term, a criterion band or a predicted grade can move, and often one does. It can also sit still while the underlying work improves, especially in MYP where a single weak criterion drags the converted grade. We do not guarantee grades and no honest tutor will, because the tutor controls perhaps two hours of a week that contains thirty hours of school. What a term should produce is a child who can say what their current level is and what the next one needs.

Across one full exam cycle, the realistic wins are timing, completeness and drafting discipline: fewer unattempted marks at the end of a paper, an IA finished early enough to use the teacher's feedback, an Extended Essay that did not eat the February holidays. For continuum students specifically, the thing most worth buying in DP1 is exam-condition practice, because it is the one skill the previous eleven years did not require.

When it is not working, tell us in week three rather than month three. Nobody at IB Gram is offended by a re-match; we would rather replace a tutor in October than defend one in March. Tell us what is wrong in behavioural terms, like the child goes quiet, or the tutor talks for fifty minutes, and we will shortlist again from the brief. There is no charge for the shortlist and no argument about it.
bullets: Four weeks: a specific diagnosis, one habit change, and a question list.
One term: one criterion band, or a steadier predicted grade.
One exam cycle: better timing, fewer unattempted marks, calmer drafting.
We do not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor will.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home classes in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Three documents make the first session four times more useful. Send the most recent report, two pieces of marked work with the teacher's comments still on them, and the assessment calendar the school already gives you as a parent. If your child uses a school portal, have the login to hand so the tutor can see the actual task sheet rather than a description of it. We never ask for anything the school has not already given you.

The first session is a diagnostic, and it should feel like one. The tutor works through the marked task with your child, finds where the marks were lost, checks whether the cause is content, criterion understanding or timing, and ends with a written plan: what we will cover in the next four sessions, what your child does between them, and what you should see by week four. If a tutor wants to start teaching Chapter 1 instead, that is a signal.

Then fix the logistics once and stop thinking about them. Agree a standing day and time, the room, and whether an adult is home. Arrange a standing gate pass with your society office rather than a visitor entry every week, because in most Juhu and JVPD Scheme buildings the second week is when the lift queue eats ten minutes of the lesson. A tutor can take all IB and IGCSE subjects through home classes in Mumbai only when the slot itself is boring and predictable.

Tell us the programme year, the subjects, your area and two time windows that genuinely work, and we will come back with a shortlist rather than a sales call. IB Gram remains an independent platform with no affiliation to Ecole Mondiale World School, and the only promise we make is about the match and the process, not about the grade at the end of it.
bullets: Send the last report and two pieces of marked work.
Send the assessment calendar the school already gives parents.
Agree the weekly slot, the room, and who is home.
