faqs.question: My child is at the Worli campus. Will you send a tutor from the suburbs?
faqs.answer: Usually not for a weekday evening slot. Worli and Prabhadevi enquiries are matched from inside the island city first, which in practice means Lower Parel, Mahalaxmi, Dadar, Tardeo, Cuffe Parade and Colaba, with Bandra at the outer edge. A tutor crossing the Bandra-Worli Sea Link or coming down the Coastal Road from the Western Suburbs can make a weekend block work reliably, but a 7pm Tuesday tends to start slipping by week four. If the subject is scarce enough that the only strong tutor lives in the Western Suburbs, we will say so and recommend online or a weekend slot instead of pretending the travel will hold.

faqs.question: We are at the Kandivali campus. How do you find someone for weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: By matching inside the Link Road corridor, which is the main advantage of being in the north-west. Tutors who live in Kandivali West, Kandivali East, Borivali, Malad, Goregaon or Dahisar reach you without crossing the city, and Metro Lines 2A and 7 plus the Western Express Highway make a late finish workable for them. That gives genuinely deep weekday availability for IGCSE Mathematics and the Sciences, and for DP Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology. The honest exception is the top end of the Diploma Programme, where a Higher Level Economics or second-language specialist may not live in your corridor at all.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we will not quote a figure because any number on a page like this would be wrong for half the people reading it. Fees move with the board and level, since Diploma Programme Higher Level work costs more than IGCSE Year 9 support. They move with subject scarcity, because there are far fewer experienced Theory of Knowledge or Higher Level Economics teachers than Mathematics teachers. They move with travel distance and the time of day, which is why a 7pm slot across the city prices differently from a 5pm slot in your own lane. They move with session length and frequency, and with whether the format is home, online or hybrid. Ask any tutor to break their rate down along those five lines.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all my child's subjects?
faqs.answer: Almost never, and you should treat the offer as a warning rather than a convenience. Across the two boards and the levels involved, nobody teaches every subject to examination standard. What works is one tutor for the subject that is genuinely failing, a second if a different subject is also in trouble, and occasional short blocks for a language, Theory of Knowledge or an Internal Assessment. Two tutors doing a narrow job well cost less in wasted sessions than one generalist doing a broad job adequately. If you want a single point of contact, that is what the matching platform is for.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for IB and IGCSE, or is it a compromise?
faqs.answer: It works well for specific situations and poorly for others, so the answer depends on the student. Online is genuinely the better choice when the subject is scarce, when you want three short technique sessions a week rather than one long block, when a Diploma Programme student is revising late at night, and through the monsoon when evening travel is unpredictable. It is weaker for younger IGCSE students who need supervision to stay off their phone, and for diagnostic work where a tutor is reading hesitation and body language. Most families end up hybrid by the second term, which is a sensible destination rather than a halfway house.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: You tell us and we replace the match. There is no argument, no notice period to serve out and no need to justify the decision in detail, though the detail is useful because it makes the next match better. Saying the explanations are too fast, or that the sessions keep drifting into content revision when the problem is examination technique, lets us filter differently rather than sending a near-identical profile. Three sessions is a reasonable point to judge. One is too early, because a diagnostic session is deliberately uncomfortable, and a full term is too late to recover cheaply.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask the tutor one specific question before changing anything: name the marks being lost and show me the evidence. A tutor doing the job will answer with something concrete, such as your child loses the method marks because working is not written down, and will show you the scripts. If the answer is general encouragement about confidence and effort, the match is wrong and should change. Also check what is realistic: four weeks produces a diagnosis and one mechanical fix, not a grade jump. Topic test scores typically move before examination grades, and they move unevenly from unit to unit.

faqs.question: Do your tutors have past papers or materials from the school itself?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should tell you otherwise. No tutor on IB Gram has access to Ryan Global School's internal question papers, mark schemes, teaching materials or staff, and we are not affiliated with the school in any way. What a good tutor works from is public: the published IB subject guides, the Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel syllabuses and specimen papers, past papers, mark schemes and examiner reports. That material is more than enough, because the external examination is what actually sets the grade. Anyone claiming insider access to a school's assessments is either exaggerating or describing something you do not want to be part of.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session, and what space is needed?
faqs.answer: Someone should be at home, though they do not need to be in the room. For students under sixteen we recommend an adult present in the flat as a matter of ordinary caution, with the session happening in a space that is visible rather than behind a closed bedroom door. The practical requirements are small: a table, two chairs, a plug point and enough quiet that nobody has to repeat themselves. Clear the gate access in advance, because a tutor who argues with security every week will eventually stop accepting the slot, and that is the commonest reason a good match quietly dies.

faqs.question: My child is in IGCSE Year 9 and has to pick subjects. Can a tutor help decide?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a short block of two or three sessions is usually better value than a term of teaching. The decisions that matter are the Core versus Extended tier, since the tier caps the grade available in Year 11, and which combination keeps the Diploma Programme options open at Higher Level two years later. A tutor who teaches the subject can tell you what the Extended paper actually demands compared with Core, and where your child currently sits against that. The school's own guidance counsellor should lead the decision; an external tutor is a second opinion on the subject-level reality.

sections.heading: The IB pathway at Singapore International School, and where tutoring actually earns its keep
paragraphs: Singapore International School at Dahisar East offers International Baccalaureate (IB) programmes, so a family there sits somewhere on the Primary Years Programme (PYP), Middle Years Programme (MYP) and Diploma Programme (DP) continuum rather than on a board that examines externally every year. That changes what tuition is for. The IB continuum defers external examination until the end of DP2 and fills the years before it with continuous internal assessment, so what needs support early is method, written communication and deadline discipline, not exam drilling.

Parents searching for an IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai-wide are usually holding two boards in their head at once, and reasonably so. Siblings land at different schools. A child may sit International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) papers with Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel at one school and then move into DP at another, and transfers between the two in Years 9 to 11 are ordinary here. A tutor who knows only one board teaches the other one wrong without noticing: IGCSE Extended Mathematics rewards clean method marks on short structured questions, while MYP Mathematics is marked against criteria that include communication and application to a real context. A student drilled for one bleeds marks in the other.

The MYP 5 into DP1 step is where most of the damage is done. Up to MYP 5 a capable student can be carried by classwork and a good memory. DP1 then starts three Higher Level (HL) subjects, three Standard Level (SL) subjects, Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and an Internal Assessment in nearly every subject, all at the same time. A tutor brought in during the second half of MYP 5 can fix note-taking and method while there is still room to fix them. A tutor brought in during January of DP2 is doing damage control on a timetable that no longer bends.

On the Cambridge side the earlier decision is Core versus Extended. Families often want all IB and IGCSE subjects across IGCSE Years 9-11 with one tutor in Mumbai, and through Years 9 and 10 that is frequently workable, because one strong generalist can hold five or six subjects at that level. Core papers cap the top grade available while Extended papers do not, so stepping down from Extended because a term went badly is a decision with a ceiling attached to it. Make that call on evidence from marked work, not on one bad set of results in the monsoon term.

sections.heading: Which subjects need a Higher Level specialist and which need a steady generalist?
paragraphs: Here is the test. A subject needs a Higher Level specialist when the HL syllabus contains content the Standard Level course never meets at all. A subject needs a steady generalist when HL only adds depth, volume and speed on the same material. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, Physics, Chemistry and Biology fall in the first group. English, History, Business Management and most language subjects fall in the second.

Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL is the clearest case. It carries topics an SL student never sees: proof by induction, complex numbers in modulus-argument and Euler form, Maclaurin series, vectors and planes, differential equations and the harder integration techniques. It also carries a third paper that SL candidates do not sit. Paper 3 is a long guided investigation in two extended parts, and a student who has only ever answered short structured questions will freeze on it even when the underlying mathematics is well known. No amount of goodwill makes a general maths tutor useful on that paper in the term before exams.

The sciences split the same way. Physics and Chemistry at HL add additional higher level material layered onto every topic, and the HL question papers ask for multi-step reasoning that the SL papers do not. The internal assessment in each science is a single scientific investigation of the student's own design, and the marks live in the quality of the research question, the control of variables and the treatment of uncertainty, not in the write-up length. That is a skill a subject specialist coaches in two or three sessions and a generalist often cannot coach at all, because he has never marked one against the published criteria.

On the other side, English A Language and Literature HL, History HL and the language acquisition subjects are depth subjects. HL adds an extra text, an extra essay, wider comparative range and a tighter standard on the same skill. A strong, well-read generalist who marks drafts seriously and makes the student rewrite is worth more there than a nominal specialist who only talks. Every DP subject also carries its own Internal Assessment with published criteria, and a tutor who cannot name the criteria for your child's subject is not the right tutor for it.

sections.heading: Home tuition across Dahisar, Borivali and Mira Road, and the rest of Mumbai
paragraphs: Home sessions for these families happen inside a tight band: Dahisar East, Dahisar West, Borivali East, Borivali West and, across the district line, Mira Road. That band is served by Dahisar station on the Western Line, by Metro Lines 2A and 7 running above the Western Express Highway, and by the highway itself, which is the one road in this stretch that still moves after half past seven. An IB and IGCSE home tutor for Singapore International School students in Mumbai is drawn, in practice, from that band and no further.

Each part of it contributes something different. Borivali East and Borivali West hold the largest resident pool of experienced school teachers in the far north, which is why most weekday evening slots in Dahisar are filled from there. Mira Road sits outside the municipal boundary but is close in road terms, and it widens the pool without adding a single highway crossing, which matters because every crossing is where a weekly slot eventually dies. Kandivali East and Malad add reach for weekend sessions when nobody is fighting the evening peak. None of this is theoretical: a tutor who has to come down from Dahisar at six in the evening and back up at nine will cancel by the fourth week, and the student loses a month.

IB Gram works across Mumbai, Maharashtra, not only in this band, and the same matching logic applies everywhere. In South Mumbai, tutors in Colaba, Cuffe Parade and Worli are matched inside the island using Metro Line 3 and the Coastal Road rather than brought down from the suburbs. Across the Western Suburbs, Bandra, Juhu, Andheri and Malad are matched along the line and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link rather than across it. In the Central Suburbs, Powai and Chandivali are reached by road from Ghatkopar or Andheri East over JVLR, with Mulund on the Central Line. In the Eastern Suburbs, Chembur, Vikhroli and Bhandup run off the Eastern Express Highway, with the Eastern Freeway making South Mumbai closer than it looks.

Navi Mumbai is matched node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur and Kharghar along Palm Beach Road, with the Harbour Line and the Atal Setu linking back to the island. Thane is matched within Thane, from the station across Pokhran Road and out along Ghodbunder Road towards Majiwada and Kasarvadavali. Parents typing IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai are really asking whether a tutor's weekly route survives the evening peak, and the honest answer depends entirely on which side of a highway or a creek both parties live.

sections.heading: The Mumbai IB calendar and the months that squeeze a Singapore International School student
paragraphs: Take your dates from the school, not from this page. IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation to Singapore International School and no access to its internal calendar, its staff, its materials or its reporting. What follows is the shape of the IB year as it runs across Mumbai generally, which is enough to plan tuition around, and you should check every internal deadline against what the school itself sends you.

The academic year here starts into the monsoon, and the first term is quieter than it feels. This is the cheapest term to fix things in and the one families most often skip. By the second half of it the first serious internal assessments land, and in DP1 that usually means a science practical, a Mathematics exploration proposal and the first properly marked essays. The Diwali break in October or November is the last genuine gap in the year; after it the calendar compresses hard.

From December into February the pressure points stack. Mock examinations, final Internal Assessment deadlines, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay all fall inside one short stretch, and because schools set internal dates ahead of the IB's own submission deadlines, the version your child must finish is earlier than the date published by the IB. A DP2 student in Dahisar East sitting the May session will typically be finishing a Physics investigation, a Mathematics exploration and a TOK essay inside the same fortnight as mocks. That fortnight is why tuition that starts in January is so often too late to change anything.

The northern suburbs give families a second useful reference point. JBCN International School, Borivali runs IB and IGCSE a short way down the Western Express Highway, and Thakur International School at Kandivali East and Ryan Global School at Kandivali sit in the same corridor, so tutors working this stretch are generally handling several calendars at once. That is an argument for booking a weekday evening slot early in the year rather than in December, when every family in Dahisar, Borivali and Kandivali is looking for the same hours.

sections.heading: Home tuition in Dahisar East plus an online HL specialist: how the split works
paragraphs: Home tuition is the right default here, for a reason that has nothing to do with teaching quality. A tutor sitting at your dining table in Dahisar East or Borivali East watches the working happen. He sees the student skip a line of algebra, reach for a calculator on a non-calculator paper, or write a conclusion that never refers back to the recorded data. On a screen share of a finished answer, all of that is invisible, and it is exactly where the marks go. Home classes also impose a routine that a teenager cannot quietly opt out of.

The honest cost of insisting on home tuition for everything is choice. Holding a home-only line narrows the pool to tutors willing to come to the northern end of the Western Express Highway on a weekday evening, and at Higher Level that pool is close to empty. Families who hold the line anyway usually end up with a capable generalist teaching HL Physics, which is a worse outcome than an online specialist by a wide margin. The generalist is not the problem; being asked to teach content he has never taught is.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai, or in another city entirely, removes the travel constraint, and that is the whole point of using one. It buys access to people who have actually taught and marked Maths AA HL or Physics HL. The trade-offs are real and worth stating: the student needs a tablet or a document camera pointed at the working rather than just a webcam, a connection that survives the monsoon, a desk rather than a bed, and enough maturity to stay engaged for ninety minutes unsupervised. Below Year 9 it generally does not hold.

Hybrid is what most of these families settle on, and it is not a compromise: it is the correct structure. IB and IGCSE tutoring for Singapore International School students in Mumbai works best as one strong local home tutor carrying breadth and routine, plus one or two online specialists carrying the subjects where depth decides the grade. The local tutor holds the week together and watches the working. The specialist handles the two subjects where content gaps, not habits, are the problem. The worked example in the next section shows exactly how that is arranged across a week.

sections.heading: How is a tutor checked before reaching your Mumbai home, and what should you check yourself?
paragraphs: Every IB and IGCSE tutor for Singapore International School students in Mumbai goes through the same checks before a parent sees the profile: government photo identity verified against the name on the profile, degree and teaching qualifications seen rather than claimed, and a subject conversation at the level requested. That last one does most of the work. Someone who has taught Chemistry HL can describe how the additional higher level content changes the Paper 2 questions; someone who has not will talk about chemistry in general.

References from previous families are checked where they exist, and so is the specific claim that matters most on this page: that the tutor has taught the level being asked for. A tutor who has taught Mathematics Applications and Interpretation SL for years is not an Analysis and Approaches HL tutor, and IB Gram treats those as different qualifications because the papers are different papers. For an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai working across both boards, the same rule applies to Cambridge and Edexcel, which examine the same subject differently.

There are also claims IB Gram does not make and you should be suspicious of anywhere. No tutor here has access to any school's internal materials, mark schemes, predicted grades, report comments or staff. Nobody on this platform works inside Singapore International School, and nobody can tell you what a particular teacher expects. Any tutor who says otherwise is either exaggerating or describing something that would be a serious problem if true. Good tutoring works from the published syllabus, past papers and the IB's own assessment criteria, all of which are available to any competent teacher.

Do your own checks in the first two weeks. Ask which syllabus version the tutor is teaching from, since subject guides change and an out-of-date one quietly teaches removed content. Ask to see a piece of your child's work the tutor has marked, with comments, not just a tick. Ask directly how the tutor handles Internal Assessment support, because the correct answer is coaching on structure, method and criteria while the student writes every word. A tutor who offers to draft any part of an IA is putting your child's diploma at risk and should be ended that day.

sections.heading: The Higher Level specialist gap in the northern suburbs of Mumbai
paragraphs: Singapore International School is the northernmost IB school in this corpus, and that single fact creates a problem worth naming plainly rather than hiding. Good general subject tutors exist in Dahisar, Borivali and Mira Road in reasonable numbers. A Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL or Physics HL specialist who will travel to Dahisar East on a weekday evening largely does not exist. Specialists at that level are few, they are booked early, and they live mostly between Bandra and Powai. Pretending otherwise produces the familiar failure: a well-meaning tutor is appointed in July, struggles with HL content by September and leaves in November, which costs a term.

Here is a worked example of the alternative. A DP1 student lives in Borivali East and her school day ends at Dahisar East. Her subjects are English A Language and Literature HL, History HL, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL, Physics SL, Economics SL and Hindi B SL. Two problems: she is losing ground in Maths AA HL on the non-calculator paper and on proof, and her History HL essays run long without arguing anything. Everything else is fine but drifting, because nobody is holding her to deadlines.

The split that works runs like this. A local home tutor comes to the flat in Borivali East twice a week, Tuesday and Friday evenings. He covers Physics SL and Economics SL, reads her History drafts and makes her rewrite them, checks the Hindi B written tasks, and spends the last ten minutes of every Friday on one page: what is due, what is started, what has not been looked at. That is the breadth and routine job, and it needs presence in the room more than it needs rare expertise. Alongside him, an online Maths AA HL specialist takes a single ninety-minute session on Sunday mornings, working through proof by induction, complex numbers and Paper 3 style investigations, and sets a short non-calculator set that the local tutor checks on Tuesday.

Three things make that arrangement hold. The two tutors share the same one-page tracker, so the Sunday specialist knows what Tuesday found. The parent books the Sunday slot around the specialist's availability rather than around the family's convenience, because that is the scarce resource. And the parent accepts that one subject is taught by someone who will never see the dining table. On cost, two online specialists plus one local tutor is usually not more than three local tutors, because what you pay a premium for is a Higher Level teacher willing to cross Mumbai, and that is precisely the thing you have stopped buying.

sections.heading: What progress should look like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not expect a grade to move, and if someone tells you it has, ask to see the marked evidence. What you should see by then is narrower and more useful: the student can say what the question is asking before answering it, homework is finished before the session rather than during it, and the tutor can tell you in one sentence what the specific weakness is. If after four weeks nobody can name the weakness, the diagnosis failed and the tutor is working blind.

At one term, with one set of marked assessments behind you, the picture should be concrete. Internal assessment drafts should be arriving ahead of the school's internal dates rather than on them. In a HL science you should see the uncertainty treatment and the research question tightening. In a maths subject you should see method marks being picked up on questions where the final answer is still wrong, which is where the first real gains always show. Movement of a whole grade band inside one term happens, but it is not what you plan on.

At one exam cycle, judged across mocks and the final session, you are looking for consistency rather than a single good paper. A student who scores well in one mock and badly in the next has not learned the subject; she has learned one paper. The honest limits are worth saying out loud. Tutoring cannot replace attendance, it cannot fix a subject choice that was wrong from the start, and it cannot compress two years of HL content into the stretch between mocks and May, although every year some family asks it to.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Singapore International School or with any other school named here, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades. What can be promised is the structure: a tutor whose level was verified, a written diagnosis you can read, a tracker you can see, and a replacement if the match is wrong. Anyone offering more certainty than that in an IB subject is selling something.

sections.heading: Starting with an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai: what to send and what happens first
paragraphs: Send four things and the shortlist comes back far better. First, the year group and the full subject list with levels marked, because HL and SL change which tutor is even eligible. Second, the two subjects that actually worry you, named honestly rather than diplomatically. Third, photographs of the last two pieces of marked work, including the teacher's comments, since those comments usually diagnose the problem before any tutor does. Fourth, the days and times your household can genuinely hold every week for a term.

That last one is where most matches fail before they start. A slot that works in July because the evenings are free and fails in October because of a sports commitment is not a slot. Pick the hour you will defend. For families in Dahisar East and Borivali East, a weekday evening after seven usually travels better than six, because the Western Express Highway has thinned by then, and Sunday mornings are the easiest hour in the week to hold for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai.

The first session covers the diagnostic and nothing else, and it should feel slightly uncomfortable. The tutor works through the marked papers with the student present, asks her to redo one question out loud, identifies whether the issue is content, method or exam technique, and writes it down. No syllabus is taught in that hour. The output is a plan: which topics in what order, how many sessions a week, and whether one of the subjects needs an online specialist rather than the person sitting in your living room.

After that, the rhythm is simple and you should insist on it. A standing weekly slot, a shared one-page tracker the parent can see, a short written note after each session, and a review at four weeks against what the diagnostic said. If the tutor is wrong for your child, say so at that review. Changing a tutor in week five costs a few sessions. Changing in February costs a grade, and by then there is nothing anyone can do about it.
bullets: Send the subject list with HL and SL marked against each subject
Send photos of two marked papers including the teacher's written comments
Name the hour you can defend every week for a full term

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to Singapore International School in any way?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Singapore International School. We have no access to its staff, its internal materials, its mark schemes, its predicted grades or its reports, and no tutor on this platform should ever claim otherwise. The school is named here only as public context: it is at Dahisar East in Mumbai and it offers International Baccalaureate programmes. Everything tutors work from is the published subject guide, past papers and the IB's own assessment criteria, which any competent teacher can access. IB Gram also does not guarantee grades.

faqs.question: Will a tutor really come to Dahisar East for a weekday evening session?
faqs.answer: Yes for most subjects, and that is why the local pool is drawn from Borivali East, Borivali West, Mira Road and Kandivali rather than from further south. A tutor living within that band reaches Dahisar East using the Western Express Highway or Metro Lines 2A and 7 without a long cross-city run, and a slot after seven in the evening travels better than one at six. What does not hold is a Higher Level specialist coming up from Bandra or Powai; that arrangement typically collapses inside a month, which is why those subjects are better taught online.

faqs.question: Why use an online tutor for Maths AA HL instead of finding a local one?
faqs.answer: Because the content is the constraint, not the convenience. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level carries proof by induction, complex numbers, Maclaurin series and a Paper 3 investigation that Standard Level students never sit, and a tutor who has not taught and marked that paper cannot prepare a student for it, however close he lives. Online opens the pool to people who have. Keep the rest of the week local: the home tutor sees the working, checks the non-calculator sets the specialist assigns, and holds the deadlines. You lose almost nothing by moving one subject to a screen and gain the only thing that matters in it.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and no honest page quotes a figure. Board and level come first: Higher Level Diploma Programme subjects cost more than IGCSE Years 9 to 11 because fewer people can teach them. Subject scarcity comes second, which is why a Physics HL specialist prices differently from an English tutor. Travel distance is third, and it is unusually heavy for Dahisar East because few tutors come this far north. Session length and frequency are fourth. Mode is fifth: online removes the travel component entirely. Ask any tutor to break the quote down against those five and compare like with like.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a separate room, or is the dining table fine?
faqs.answer: The dining table is fine and often better than a bedroom. What a home session needs is a hard surface wide enough for a past paper, a textbook and a notebook open at the same time, a chair at the right height, decent light and no television in earshot. A bedroom with the student on the bed produces exactly the posture that produces careless work. Keep phones out of the room, including the tutor's. If you are running online sessions for one subject, the same table works, with a tablet or a document camera pointing at the paper rather than at the student's face.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP 5 and moves into DP next year. When should tutoring start?
faqs.answer: Start in the second half of MYP 5, not in DP1. The jump into the Diploma Programme brings three Higher Level subjects, three Standard Level ones, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and an Internal Assessment in nearly every subject, all beginning at once. A student who arrives with weak note-taking or untidy method gets no quiet term in which to fix it. Six months of work on method before DP1 starts is worth considerably more than the same six months spent firefighting in DP2. It is also the point at which Higher Level choices are still reversible.

faqs.question: The tutor has been coming for a month and nothing has changed. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Raise it at the four-week review rather than waiting, and be specific about what has not moved. Ask the tutor to state the weakness in one sentence and show the marked work supporting it. If that answer is vague, the diagnosis never happened and a replacement is the right call. Tell IB Gram what went wrong, in detail, because the second match is only better if the first failure is understood: wrong level, wrong subject expertise, wrong personality fit or a slot the student was always too tired for. A new tutor restarts with the diagnostic session, not mid-syllabus.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all our subjects, or do we need several?
faqs.answer: Through IGCSE Years 9 and 10, one strong generalist can usually carry five or six subjects well. Past MYP 5, all IB and IGCSE subjects with one tutor in Mumbai stops being realistic, because Diploma Programme Higher Level subjects need people who have taught those specific papers. The practical structure is one local tutor holding breadth, routine and deadlines, plus one or two specialists for the Higher Level subjects where content depth decides the grade. Families who want all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes in Mumbai under one person past DP1 almost always end up adding a specialist by the second term anyway.

faqs.question: We live in Mira Road and the school is at Dahisar East. Do you match from our side?
faqs.answer: From your side, always, because the tutor comes to your home rather than to the school. Mira Road sits outside the municipal boundary but is close in road terms to Dahisar and Borivali East, so the pool available to you is effectively the same one. The useful consequence is that a Mira Road address adds its own local teachers to the shortlist rather than subtracting from it. The thing to avoid is a tutor who has to cross the Western Express Highway twice in an evening peak, whichever side of the boundary he starts from.

faqs.question: What happens when a home tuition session is missed because of rain or traffic?
faqs.answer: It is rescheduled, and you should agree the rule in week one rather than after the first cancellation. Mumbai gives you a monsoon that closes roads and an evening peak on the Western Express Highway that no one controls, so a home tutor who never misses a session is a tutor you are not being told the truth about. For home tuition the workable arrangements are a fixed backup slot later in the same week, or a short online session covering the same ground when travel fails. Agree which one applies, agree how the society gate will admit the tutor at the later hour, and agree how many reschedules in a month is too many.

faqs.question: Can you guarantee a 7 in Higher Level Physics?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody can. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and a tutor who offers you a specific point score is telling you something he cannot know. What a Higher Level Physics specialist can realistically do is close content gaps in the additional higher level topics, coach the scientific investigation against the published criteria, and drill the multi-step reasoning the Higher Level papers demand. The outcome also depends on attendance, on the work done between sessions and on how early you started. Judge a tutor on marked evidence of movement over a term, not on what he promised in the first phone call.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring good enough for a Year 10 IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: Usually yes for one subject, rarely as the whole arrangement at that age. A Year 10 student can hold an online session when the subject is well defined and the tutor sets written work that gets checked, which is why an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai works well for a single scarce subject. What online does badly at this age is supervision of habits: posture, skipped steps, phone drift and homework that was never started. That is the job of a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai sitting in the room twice a week, and it is hard to replicate through a screen.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram shortlist an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai for a Thane family?
paragraphs: You send three things: the subjects, the year group, and the part of Thane you live in. IB Gram filters for verified tutors who already teach within a short run of that address, and two or three profiles come back to you, usually inside a working day, carrying qualifications, syllabus experience and the evenings each tutor still has free. You choose one. Nobody is assigned to you, and no tutor turns up at your door before you have read their profile and agreed a time.

The address matters far more than most parents expect. Asking for an IB and IGCSE tutor for Smt Sulochanadevi Singhania School students in Mumbai is asking for a standing weekly commitment that has to survive a monsoon week, a bad evening on the arterial roads, and an exam fortnight when the Thursday slot shifts to Sunday morning. A tutor whose own flat sits fifteen minutes away absorbs all of that without complaint. A tutor driving up from Andheri or Chembur absorbs it twice over, once in each direction, and the booking quietly starts to wobble. Geography is therefore the first filter applied, ahead of price and ahead of headline credentials.

The second filter is the syllabus, not the subject. After the first session you tell IB Gram whether the fit worked. If the answer is no, you say so in a sentence and a different profile is shortlisted. sections.heading: IGCSE Years 9 to 11, and where the International Baccalaureate fits afterwards
paragraphs: Smt Sulochanadevi Singhania School is a Thane school offering Cambridge IGCSE pathways, and the structure that follows from that is public and predictable. Cambridge International Education runs IGCSE as a two-year course, normally examined at the end of what Indian families call Class 10. Year 9 is the foundation year where subject choices are made and the habits that decide the final grade are formed. Year 10 is where coursework and tiering decisions bite. Year 11, for schools that run the full three-year shape, is the examination year itself.

Two examination series exist each year: May and June, and October and November. The May and June series is the one most Indian schools enter, which means the real work happens between the start of the academic year in June and the mocks that land in the winter. The October and November series exists mainly for retakes, for students who joined late, and for candidates sitting a single subject out of step with their cohort. Knowing which series your child is entered for changes the entire shape of a tutoring plan, because it moves the deadline by five months.

The International Baccalaureate (IB) usually enters the picture after IGCSE, when a student moves to a Diploma Programme (DP) school for Classes 11 and 12. In the Thane and Mulund belt, NES International School in Mulund West is the nearest well-known option offering both IB and IGCSE pathways, which makes it a common crossover destination for families who want to stay on this side of the city. IB Gram covers all IB and IGCSE subjects across IGCSE Years 9-11 with a tutor in Mumbai who has actually taught the level in question, and also covers the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and the Diploma Programme for families who switch boards.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Higher Level or Standard Level: the decisions that set the ceiling
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE tiers the harder subjects, and the tier decision is the single most consequential academic choice of Year 10. In Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 the Core tier caps the achievable grade at a C and the Extended tier opens the full range up to an A star. Sciences work the same way. A student placed on Core because of one weak term in Year 9 can be stuck behind a ceiling that then disqualifies them from Higher Level (HL) Mathematics in the Diploma Programme two years later. IB Gram lists all IB and IGCSE subjects and matches a tutor in Mumbai for each one, and tier review is a standard part of the first month's work in a tiered subject.

A worked example makes the difference concrete. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 Paper 6, the Alternative to Practical, routinely asks a candidate to find the resistance of a length of wire from a table of voltage and current readings. Most students in Thane can rearrange the formula and reach a number. The marks they lose sit elsewhere: plotting the points to fill more than half the grid, drawing a single best-fit line rather than joining the dots, choosing two widely separated points on that line for the gradient rather than two raw data points, and quoting the answer to a sensible number of significant figures with ohms attached. A tutor who has marked that paper spends the session on those five habits, not on the physics, because the physics was never the problem.

Language subjects carry a different trap. Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 and English as a Second Language 0510 are different qualifications with different reading demands, and a student entered for the wrong one wastes a year. On the IB side, every Diploma subject carries an Internal Assessment (IA), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) runs alongside, and the Extended Essay (EE) sits on top; the Higher Level and Standard Level (SL) split changes both the syllabus content and the assessment weighting. Tutors are matched to the exact combination your child is sitting.

sections.heading: Thane first, then the rest of Mumbai: where these tutors actually live
paragraphs: Thane spreads west to east from the station, and the places a Singhania School family is likely to live are the places tutors live too: Thane West around the station, the Pokhran Road corridor, the Ghodbunder Road stretch running north, Majiwada at the junction of the two, and Hiranandani Estate further up. Thane station itself sits on the Central Line and is the terminus of the Trans-Harbour Line to Vashi, which is why Thane connects more easily to Navi Mumbai than to the Western Suburbs. We cover all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes across Mumbai, but the Thane pool is deep enough that a Thane request almost never needs to leave the district.

Outside Thane, the city divides into zones that behave like separate tutor markets. South Mumbai covers Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Fort, Babulnath and Worli, served by the Western Line to Churchgate, the Harbour Line to CSMT, Metro Line 3 and the Coastal Road. sections.heading: Which months does a Thane IGCSE calendar actually squeeze?
paragraphs: The pressure months for a Cambridge IGCSE student in Thane are November to January and then March to May, and both squeezes come from the examination calendar rather than from anything peculiar to one school. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Smt Sulochanadevi Singhania School; everything described here comes from the published Cambridge assessment timetable and from how the Indian academic year is normally arranged, not from inside knowledge of any school.

The first squeeze arrives with mock examinations. Indian schools running the May and June series typically hold mocks in the winter, which collides with the Diwali break, the first serious cold-weather illness of the year, and any coursework still outstanding from Year 10. Students who coasted through the first term discover in one week that they are two chapters behind in three subjects at once. This is the month when most families start looking for help, and it is also the month when good tutors in Thane are already full, which is why a request made in September is matched far more comfortably than one made in December.

The second squeeze is the run-in to the written papers themselves, roughly March to May. By then nothing new can be taught usefully; the work is past papers, timing, and the specific technique each component rewards. A student doing four hours of revision without ever sitting a full paper under timed conditions is rehearsing the wrong skill. A tutor's job in those weeks is to force whole papers, mark them honestly against the published mark scheme a candidate can obtain themselves, and then spend the session on the five marks that keep going missing. We never claim access to a school's internal materials, mark schemes, teachers or report data, and any tutor who claims otherwise is telling you something that should worry you.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: which actually works for a Thane IGCSE student?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the lead service and the right default for Years 9 and 10. A tutor sitting at your dining table sees the things a camera hides: the page the student skipped, the calculator used for arithmetic they should do in their head, the handwriting that will cost marks in a graph question, the phone face-down but still buzzing. IB and IGCSE home tuition for Smt Sulochanadevi Singhania School students in Mumbai is also the mode that survives a bad week, because the tutor arriving at the door removes every excuse to postpone.

Online is genuinely good for some things and genuinely weaker at others, and it is worth being plain about which. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai can be excellent for a scarce subject where the only person who has taught Cambridge IGCSE Economics or a Diploma Programme Higher Level language lives in Kharghar or Dahisar. Screen sharing suits essay feedback, worked algebra and mark-scheme walkthroughs. It is weaker for practical technique, for a student who needs someone physically present to stay on task, and for the first few sessions of any relationship, before the tutor knows how the child reacts to being stuck.

Hybrid is what most families settle into without planning it. The weekly session happens at home, and a short online call is added before a test or when a question comes up mid-week. In the examination run-in some families flip the ratio: two online paper reviews and one longer session at home every week. There is no single correct answer, and the honest trade-off is that each online hour costs less in travel and attention from the tutor, while each hour at home buys supervision that no video call reproduces.

We cannot confirm that they will get on with your particular fifteen-year-old, that their explanation style suits a child who thinks in pictures, or that they will keep the same energy in week twelve that they had in week one. That is what the first session is for, and it is why the replacement process exists and why we ask for feedback after it rather than at the end of the term.

There is also a check you should run yourself, and it takes ten minutes. Ask the tutor which syllabus code they are teaching to and listen for a number rather than a subject name. Ask what the Internal Assessment criteria are for the subject if it is an IB student, or which paper carries the practical skills if it is Cambridge IGCSE. Ask how they would handle a student who is two chapters behind. Finally, be wary of anyone who claims a relationship with your child's school, access to its staff, its internal materials or its report data. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named on this page, and no honest tutor in Thane will tell you otherwise. sections.heading: Why a Thane family should stop searching for a Mumbai tutor and search locally instead
paragraphs: Thane runs its own self-contained tutor market, and this is the single most useful thing a Singhania School parent can know. The tutors who teach Cambridge IGCSE here live here, work here and build their weekly timetables around Thane addresses. They are not a spillover from the island city. In practice that means IB and IGCSE home classes for Smt Sulochanadevi Singhania School students in Mumbai are almost always delivered by somebody whose own address is a few kilometres from yours. Yet parents in Thane routinely type the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai into Google, get results pointing at Bandra, Powai and Juhu, and start negotiating with someone who will need ninety minutes of their evening to reach Pokhran Road and ninety more to get home.

Those bookings fail in a recognisable pattern, usually around week four. Week one the tutor is early and enthusiastic. Week two they are twenty minutes late and apologetic. Week three a session is moved to the weekend because of something at their end. Week four the rescheduling begins in earnest, and by week six the family is searching again, now in December with the mocks arriving. Nothing dishonest has happened. A person who crosses the city twice a week for one lesson is simply running an arrangement that does not pay for itself in time, and the arithmetic catches up with them.

The same arithmetic explains fees. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on the board, the level, how scarce the subject is, how long each session runs and how far the tutor travels, and that last factor is not a line item you will see quoted; it shows up instead as a tutor who will only offer you Saturday, or who wants two hours rather than one to make the trip worthwhile. A local match removes the travel premium from the negotiation altogether. When parents search for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai, near is doing far more work in that phrase than they realise, and in Thane it should be read literally.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one Cambridge series
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not expect a grade to have moved, and any tutor promising that is overselling. What you should see by week four is diagnostic: the tutor can tell you exactly which topics are weak and why, your child can explain what they got wrong in the last test rather than just that they got it wrong, and homework is being started without a fight on at least some evenings. If none of that has happened after four sessions, the match is wrong and it is worth changing early rather than waiting politely until the term ends.

At one term, roughly three months, the marks should start to move in the subject being tutored, and the movement is usually uneven. A Cambridge IGCSE Physics student often gains on the structured theory paper before the Alternative to Practical catches up, because graph and measurement technique takes longer to rebuild than content recall. A student moved from Core to Extended in Mathematics 0580 may see marks dip first, which is normal and not a failure: they are now sitting a harder paper against a higher ceiling.

Across a full series, from the start of the academic year to the May and June papers, the realistic outcome of consistent weekly work is a meaningful shift in the subjects tutored and better exam technique across all of them. IB Gram does not guarantee grades. No tutor can, and the ones who say they can are either inexperienced or are counting on you not checking afterwards. What a good tutor controls is preparation, honest marking and the removal of avoidable mistakes; the rest sits with the student on the day, which is uncomfortable but true.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home classes in Mumbai for a Singhania School student
paragraphs: Have four things ready before you send the enquiry and the first session will be worth twice as much. First, the subjects and the year group. Second, the most recent report or test papers, including the ones that went badly, because those are the useful documents. Third, two or three evening windows that genuinely work every week, not the ones that work in theory. Fourth, your locality within Thane, so the shortlist is drawn from tutors who can reach you in minutes rather than hours.

The first session is diagnostic and should feel like it. A good tutor spends most of it watching your child attempt work rather than lecturing: a past paper question, a graph, a piece of writing, whatever exposes the gap fastest. They should finish by telling you, in plain language, what the actual problem is. Sometimes the answer is not academic at all; a Year 10 student who understands the chemistry perfectly but loses marks to unreadable working needs a different intervention from one who never learned moles.

Finding a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is rarely the right ambition anyway. Most families start with the one subject that is causing the most trouble, see whether the arrangement holds for a month, and add a second only if it does. That is cheaper, easier to schedule around a Thane evening, and far easier to judge honestly than booking three subjects at once and never knowing which of them is working.

sections.heading: IGCSE Years 9 to 11 and the IB Diploma Programme on one campus
paragraphs: The IGCSE side runs across Years 9 to 11, with the two-year syllabus usually taught in Years 10 and 11 and Year 9 used to build toward it. Cambridge International Education syllabuses report grades A* to G; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports 9 to 1, and families sometimes notice the difference only when they compare a report card with a cousin at another school. The tier decision is the one with teeth: Core and Extended candidates sit different papers, and the Core route caps the grade available, so a student capable of Extended Maths but entered for Core papers has a ceiling nobody mentioned at the parent meeting. A parent asking for all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 with a tutor in Mumbai who understands both tiers is asking a reasonable question.

The IB Diploma Programme is a different animal. Six subjects, one from each group, usually three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, with Higher Level carrying more teaching hours and more syllabus. On top of the six sit the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS), none of which are optional. Subject grades run one to seven, the EE and TOK together contribute up to three bonus points, the maximum is forty-five and twenty-four points is the floor for the award of the diploma, with further conditions about minimum grades. Mumbai schools sit the May examination session, so DP2 students are writing papers from late April while their IGCSE siblings are still revising.

The join between the two programmes is this page's real subject. Where a school runs IGCSE into the DP on one campus, as Thakur International School publicly does, most of the DP1 intake arrives from an IGCSE background rather than from the IB Middle Years Programme (MYP). An MYP student has lived inside criterion-referenced marking for years; an IGCSE student has lived inside mark schemes. Both can do well in the DP, but they fail differently in the first term, and a tutor who has only taught MYP-fed DP classes will misread what an IGCSE-fed student needs. A slice of every Year 11 also leaves after IGCSE for A Levels or an Indian board, which is why the DP decision gets made on incomplete information in the middle of mocks.

sections.heading: Subject choice, Core or Extended, Higher or Standard: where the decisions bite
paragraphs: Subject choice is where both boards hand a family a decision that looks administrative and is not. At IGCSE the choices with consequences are Extended rather than Core Maths, separate sciences rather than a combined route, and which second language starts in Year 9, because each of them decides what is available two years later. Extended IGCSE Maths is the realistic route into Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a student arriving from Core papers into AA HL spends DP1 repairing algebra while also learning what a DP question is asking for. Separate sciences make a Group 4 Higher Level choice far less painful than a combined-science background does, mostly because the practical work and the quantitative treatment are already familiar.

At DP level every subject carries an internal assessment (IA), and they do not queue politely. The sciences require a scientific investigation the student designs; Mathematics requires an exploration; Language A requires an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay on a literary work; Economics requires a portfolio of commentaries on published articles; History requires a historical investigation; Business Management requires a research project; Visual Arts requires a comparative study alongside the exhibition. Each has its own criteria, its own internal deadline set by the school, and its own failure mode. The commonest DP2 crisis in Kandivali East is not one impossible IA; it is three competent drafts falling due in the same fortnight as the first mock papers.

A worked contrast makes the gap concrete, and the pendulum works because both boards use it. In Cambridge IGCSE Physics, an alternative-to-practical question hands the student a table of lengths and times for ten oscillations and asks them to complete the period column, plot the points, draw a line of best fit, find the gradient and state one precaution. Every step has an expected answer, and a tutor can teach the pattern inside two sessions. In DP Physics the same pendulum becomes a scientific investigation the student designs: they choose the research question, decide what to vary and control, justify the range and the number of repeats, carry the uncertainty in length and timing through to error bars, and write an evaluation naming the weakness that actually limited the conclusion. No step has an expected answer. The marking asks whether the design was justified and whether the evaluation is honest, which is why a student who collected A grades by learning mark schemes can produce a tidy DP report and still land mid-band.

sections.heading: What does the Kandivali East school calendar demand, month by month?
paragraphs: The academic year opens in June and the first pressure is logistical rather than academic: the monsoon. July and August are the weeks when a 6pm session in Kandivali East becomes a 6:40pm arrival, and the families who keep momentum are the ones who agreed in advance that a washed-out evening moves online instead of disappearing. September and October are when internal assessment work lands properly. DP1 students meet criteria-marked laboratory and essay tasks for the first time, DP2 students are deep in final IA drafts, and Year 11 starts its run of timed papers under something close to exam conditions.

The Diwali break in late October or November is the most useful fortnight of the year and the most routinely wasted. Nothing is due, so nothing gets done, and then December arrives with DP2 internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay final submission and the first full mock papers inside the same three weeks. January and February are the hardest stretch in any Mumbai IB and IGCSE school: mocks for Year 11 and DP2, the Theory of Knowledge essay written against a prescribed title, predicted grades being settled, and university deadlines sitting on top of all of it. March closes out IGCSE practical and coursework components, which is a quieter month on paper and a tired one in practice.

Examinations land in a narrow band: IB DP papers from late April into May, the IGCSE series through May and June, IB results in early July and Cambridge results later in the summer. Two consequences follow. First, tutor availability across Kandivali East, Borivali East and Malad East tightens in the same weeks for every school in the corridor, because Ryan Global School, JBCN International School in Borivali, Witty International School in Malad and Singapore International School in Dahisar East sit the same windows, so a family looking for an IB and IGCSE home tutor for Thakur International School students in Mumbai in January is competing with every other family in the north-west. Second, the cheap months are June to September, when good tutors have space and nothing is due. IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation to Thakur International School or to any school named here; this calendar is the public examination calendar, not inside information.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for Thakur International School students in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition first. Many families here live within a kilometre or two of the school, so a 4:30pm or 5pm weekday slot is genuinely reachable for a tutor who lives in the corridor, which is not true across most of Mumbai. Online comes second, for scarce Higher Level subjects and for the monsoon. Hybrid, meaning home sessions through term and online in deadline weeks, is where most DP families end up by the middle of DP1.

The reason home tuition works around Thakur Complex is scheduling rather than geography. A tutor finishing in one lane can take the next slot a few buildings away without a vehicle, so an IB and IGCSE home tutor for Thakur International School students in Mumbai working this corridor can hold three consecutive evening slots and still arrive on time for the third. The real constraint is the band, not the distance: almost every family wants 6pm to 9pm, and a tutor has at most three of those hours to sell. Families who accept a 4:30pm start on two days a week end up with a better tutor than families who insist on 7:30pm and take whoever is left. Younger students in Years 9 and 10 also work better in home classes, where a parent is in the next room and the phone is not within reach.

Online is worth being honest about. For an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai, a DP Economics commentary or a Mathematics exploration review is as good on screen as in person and often better, because the document is shared and annotated live while the student watches. Scarce subjects make online the only real option: Computer Science HL, Psychology, Spanish ab initio and Analysis and Approaches HL have small tutor pools in this city, and insisting on a home visit narrows the shortlist to whoever lives nearby rather than whoever can teach it. What online loses is the handwriting. You cannot watch a Year 10 student's working build up on paper, and a DP Physics uncertainty calculation typed on a tablet hides exactly the slips you wanted caught. Hybrid resolves most of this, and an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai should be willing to run both patterns rather than defending the one that suits their own commute.

sections.heading: How IB Gram checks IB and IGCSE home tutors before they reach a Mumbai doorstep
paragraphs: Every IB and IGCSE home tutor on the platform goes through the same checks, and the checks for an IB or IGCSE tutor for Thakur International School students in Mumbai are no different from the checks for any other family. Before an introduction, IB Gram verifies government photo identity and evidence of the degree claimed, and asks the tutor to describe their board experience by component rather than in general terms: which syllabus, which papers, which internal assessment, and when they last taught it. Syllabuses are revised, and a tutor who taught DP Physics under an older guide should say so rather than discover it in front of your child. References come from previous families, and the questions are about reliability and communication as much as results, because a tutor who cancels twice a month fails for reasons that have nothing to do with subject knowledge.

Then there is what you should check yourself, in the trial session, in about ten minutes. Ask the tutor to explain how the conclusion criterion differs from the evaluation criterion in a DP science investigation, or what changes between Core and Extended papers at IGCSE; a tutor who answers in general praise instead of specifics has not worked at that level recently. Ask which syllabus version they last taught and what changed in it. Ask for the first month's plan in writing. Ask how they will mark your child's work, because a tutor who writes a criterion band and a reason on a draft is worth more than one who says it looks good. Watch whether they ask your child questions or lecture at them for fifty minutes.

What IB Gram will not do is worth stating plainly. We never present a tutor as having taught at Thakur International School, we have no access to the school's materials, mark schemes, predicted grades or report comments, and we are not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to the school in any way. We also hold the academic honesty line, because it protects your child: an internal assessment, an Extended Essay and a Theory of Knowledge essay are submitted as the student's own work, and a tutor who offers to draft any of them is creating a problem rather than solving one. Home sessions run in a common room with an adult in the house, not behind a closed bedroom door, and a tutor who resists that arrangement is not the right tutor.

sections.heading: Why does DP Year 1 shock students who spent IGCSE at the same Mumbai school?
paragraphs: Because the building stays the same while the demand changes completely. A student who sat IGCSE at Thakur International School walks into DP1 through the same gate, past the same noticeboards, with the same friends, and meets criterion-referenced internal assessment, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Higher Level depth inside a single academic year. Continuity of campus hides a real discontinuity of demand, and it is the commonest reason parents in Kandivali East ask for help in October of DP1 rather than in June.

The four changes arrive together, which is the problem. Marking stops being a checklist: an IGCSE A often came from learning what a mark scheme accepts, while a DP criterion asks whether the method was justified and whether the evaluation is honest, so a student with no practice at that reads a middling band as unfair rather than as information. The Extended Essay is the first piece of independent research anybody has asked them for, with a supervisor, a research question of their own invention and a four-thousand-word limit, where IGCSE coursework arrived with a task sheet. Theory of Knowledge has no content to revise, which hurts the diligent students most, because revision has been their entire method since Year 9. Higher Level is not the same subject with more questions on the end; it brings extension topics and a different paper, and the step from Extended IGCSE Maths to Analysis and Approaches HL is the one families underestimate most reliably.

The fix is timing rather than intensity, and it belongs in Year 11. In January of Year 11, read the published assessment criteria for one likely DP subject with your child and let them notice that the descriptors describe judgements, not answers. In the gap between the last IGCSE paper and the first DP1 lesson, which is the cheapest preparation window in the whole two years because nothing is due, have them write one piece of four or five hundred words from a research question they invented, reference it properly, and carry uncertainties through one calculation end to end. That is perhaps six sessions of work, and it converts the DP1 shock into a nuisance. Parents often ask who the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai is for this transition; the more useful question is whether the tutor has taught both boards and can show you, inside one session, the practical difference between a mark scheme and a criterion.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks, expect behaviour to change rather than grades. The markers that actually predict a good term are small ones: your child attempts homework before being asked twice, can say in their own words what a question or a criterion is looking for, starts a hard problem instead of waiting for the session, and brings a specific doubt rather than a general complaint. A good tutor will also have told you by week four what the real gap was, and it is frequently not the one you booked for. The Physics problem turns out to be algebra, the Economics problem turns out to be command terms, and the English problem turns out to be reading speed.

At one term, progress should be visible on school work and not only inside the sessions. A Year 11 student should be finishing an Extended structured paper inside the time allowed instead of running out before the last question. A DP1 student should have an IA draft with a method section that survives being questioned, and should be able to say which criterion their draft is weakest against and why. At one exam cycle grades do move, but they move in company: subject choice, attendance, the amount of independent work and whatever else happened that term all sit inside the same result. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and any tutor who does is guessing with your child's name on it.

The honest limits matter as much as the plan. A home tutor cannot repair a subject choice that was wrong at the start, and an HL that should have been SL will keep costing points through DP2 whatever happens in a weekly session. A tutor cannot attend school for your child, cannot write an internal assessment, and cannot compress two years of reading into the fortnight before the Theory of Knowledge essay is due. What a tutor can do is make the next task tractable and the standard visible, week after week, until the student can see it without help. If nothing has moved by week four, we change the plan or we change the tutor, and the written plan from the first match travels to the new one so your child does not start again.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home classes in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Have five things ready and the first session stops being an interview. The last school report with the teacher comments, not only the grades, because the comments usually say whether the problem is understanding or output. The subject list with each level written out: Core or Extended at IGCSE, Higher or Standard in the DP, and which Mathematics route. The school's assessment deadline sheet, which tells the tutor what to work on first instead of guessing. Two or three evening windows you can genuinely hold for a term rather than the ones you hope for. And the gate rule for your building, so the first visit does not stall at reception while your child waits upstairs.

The first session is a working session, not a test. A good tutor opens the task your child has due next, watches them attempt it, and stops at the first place the method breaks rather than at the first wrong answer. By the end there should be one page: what the gap is, what the next four weeks cover, what your child does between sessions, and what you should be able to see by week four. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai does not exist at DP level, so if you need several subjects, say so at the start and we schedule them back to back instead of scattering them through your week.

After that the pattern is deliberately dull. One standing weekly slot per subject, a review at four weeks against the written plan, and a louder conversation in the months the calendar makes hard: December, January and February. Families who want a single provider for all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes across Mumbai get a small coordinated team rather than one heroic person, arranged so the DP child and the IGCSE child are not both losing their Saturday. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Thakur International School, so what you are buying is tutoring and a plan, not access to anybody inside the school.

faqs.question: My child did IGCSE at the school and starts DP1 next term. What changes first?
faqs.answer: The marking changes first, before the content gets harder. In IGCSE your child learned to produce what a mark scheme accepts; in the DP, a lab report, an essay or an exploration is judged against criteria descriptors that reward justified design and honest evaluation. The second change is the volume of self-directed work, because the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the first internal assessment drafts all arrive inside twelve months. Most DP1 students who struggle are not weaker than they were in Year 11; they are being asked a different kind of question.

faqs.question: When should we start preparing for the IB Diploma Programme if my child is in Year 11 now?
faqs.answer: January of Year 11 lightly, then seriously in the June gap once the IGCSE papers are finished. Light work in January means reading the assessment criteria for one likely DP subject and writing one short piece from a research question your child chose. The June gap is the cheapest window in the two years because nothing is due: a handful of sessions on command terms, referencing and uncertainty handling puts a student ahead of a cohort that starts DP1 cold. Waiting until October of DP1 means learning the format during the first graded tasks.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building inside Thakur Complex on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the internal layout is why. Buildings in the Thakur Complex area sit on short internal lanes, so a tutor already teaching in Kandivali East reaches you on foot or with a short auto ride instead of crossing the Western Express Highway. The practical limits are the slot band and the gate. faqs.question: We live in Borivali East. Will a tutor come that far for home tuition?
faqs.answer: Yes, Borivali East sits inside the normal travel radius for this corridor. Magathane and the lanes off the Western Express Highway are a short run from Kandivali East, and Metro Line 7 makes that trip predictable in a way the highway stops being after 6pm. faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and level first, then scarcity, travel and session length. Higher Level DP subjects cost more than IGCSE Core work because the teaching pool is smaller and the preparation per session is longer. A subject with few qualified tutors in this city, such as Computer Science HL or a Group 2 language, prices differently from IGCSE Mathematics. Travel distance matters because a tutor crossing Mumbai loses an hour each way, and so does whether you want ninety-minute or two-hour sessions, one subject or four, and internal assessment support close to a deadline. faqs.question: Does online tutoring work as well as home classes for a DP Chemistry internal assessment?
faqs.answer: For the internal assessment itself, online is often better than home classes. The work is a document: a research question, a method, a data table, an uncertainty treatment and an evaluation, and a shared screen with live annotation beats two people leaning over one laptop. Online is weaker at the earlier stage, when your child is still learning to handle apparatus and read a scale, and at the exam-technique stage, where a tutor wants to watch handwritten working appear. Most DP Chemistry families run home sessions through term and move online for the fortnight around the deadline.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out after two sessions. What happens?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we change the tutor, with no debate about who was right. We ask one question first, because the answer changes the replacement: is the problem reliability, explanation or fit? A tutor who arrives late needs replacing with someone who lives closer. A tutor whose explanations do not land needs a different teaching style, not a better degree. A clash between a brisk tutor and a quiet fifteen-year-old is nobody's fault and is the easiest of the three to fix. The new tutor receives the written plan from the first match, so your child does not repeat the diagnostic.

faqs.question: There is no visible progress after a month. Should we change the tutor?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, but you should ask for evidence this week. At four weeks the honest markers are behavioural: does your child attempt homework unprompted, can they say what a criterion is asking for, do they start a question instead of staring at it? If those are moving, grades usually follow within a term. If none of them have moved, something is wrong with the plan or the match, and we run a three-way conversation with you and the tutor before replacing anybody. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and one month is too early to judge a grade anyway.

faqs.question: Do tutors help with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, or only subjects?
faqs.answer: Both, inside the academic honesty rules the school and the International Baccalaureate enforce. A tutor can help your child narrow a vague Extended Essay topic into an answerable research question, build a reading plan, understand what the criteria actually reward and rehearse the supervisor meetings. For Theory of Knowledge, a tutor can work on choosing exhibition objects and on structuring an essay against a prescribed title. What a tutor must never do is write or rewrite any part of it. The EE and the TOK essay are submitted as your child's own work, and a tutor offering to draft them is a risk, not a shortcut.

faqs.question: Our society gate will not admit an unregistered visitor. How is that handled?
faqs.answer: It gets handled at matching, not at the gate on the first evening. Many societies in Kandivali East and Borivali East require the resident to register a visitor in an app, add a name to a list at the main gate, or take a call before entry. Tell us which applies and the tutor arrives with the right expectation and photo identity, and you register them once for a standing weekly slot instead of every week. Where a society refuses recurring visitors outright, the usual answers are the clubhouse study room or a hybrid pattern with some sessions online.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all IB and IGCSE subjects for two children in the same house?
faqs.answer: Usually no, and a tutor who says yes is telling you something useful. A request for all IB and IGCSE subjects needs more than one tutor in Mumbai as soon as DP Higher Level work is involved, because nobody teaches HL Physics and Language A English to the same standard. What does work is pairing: one tutor across Mathematics and the sciences for the IGCSE child, another for the DP child's two weakest subjects, scheduled back to back so your evening carries one disruption instead of two. For a Year 9 or Year 10 child, a single strong generalist is often the better answer.
